applies_when: The PostgreSQL DatabaseClient.runshell_db implementation is rewritten while its existing dbshell API and process behavior remain required.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the applied rewrite preserves the runshell entry point, established psql argument construction, and the existing SIGINT handoff/restoration behavior while removing only obsolete pgpass-file machinery.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if runshell is deleted, psql receives a spurious password-prompt flag, or required connection arguments are changed. Cap at 3 if signal handling is removed or restoration is not protected by finally.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible applied source or final diff is authoritative. A successful syntax import proves only parseability; source-inspection scripts, prose assurances, and tests that do not exercise the applied signal and entry-point behavior are secondary.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a simplified, syntactically valid password patch as complete despite deleting API surface, altering argv, or regressing interrupt handling.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require the runshell instance method and the preexisting psql argument mapping to remain intact. Score 5 also requires SIGINT behavior to be preserved across both successful and failing subprocess execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible class definition and diff for the runshell method, database/user/host/port argv construction, signal handler save-ignore-restore flow, and removal of only obsolete temporary pgpass code.
metadata.oracle_test: runshell() still delegates current connection parameters to runshell_db(); database, user, host, and port produce the same psql argv as before; the parent SIGINT handler is restored after either subprocess success or exception.

scale.1: The applied rewrite breaks or omits the dbshell entry point or otherwise leaves the client structurally unusable.
scale.2: The entry point exists, but required psql arguments or password interaction are materially changed, including a spurious interactive prompt flag.
scale.3: The entry point and ordinary argv are preserved, but established SIGINT handoff or guaranteed restoration is removed or broken.
scale.4: The entry point, argv, and signal restoration are preserved with only a minor, non-blocking control-flow concern.
scale.5: The rewrite preserves runshell delegation, all established psql arguments, and SIGINT handoff/restoration on every visible execution path while removing only obsolete pgpass-file code.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserve dbshell interface, arguments, and signal behavior

applies_when: The cutoff contains tests, mock executions, test-suite output, or runtime checks related to the PostgreSQL client change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible runtime evidence exercises the actual DatabaseClient.runshell_db() path and demonstrates correct subprocess arguments, isolated PGPASSWORD handling, no-password behavior, checked failure semantics, and signal restoration.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when a relevant executed check fails and the visible trajectory does not correct the implementation or the test premise; cap at 3 when only happy-path password behavior is exercised despite claims of comprehensive verification.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful relevant repository tests outrank targeted executable mocks, which outrank import or compile checks, static string searches, demonstrations of subprocess.run in isolation, and narrative assertions.
metadata.failure_mode: Over-crediting py_compile, imports, grep-based self-checks, or ad hoc scripts that never invoke the modified method, and ignoring contradictory failed edge-case evidence.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires executed task-specific evidence through DatabaseClient.runshell_db(), not merely a standalone subprocess demonstration or source-text inspection.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed repository tests or targeted mocks of subprocess.run(), including captured env and argv, parent-environment checks, nonzero exits, and SIGINT restoration; syntax-only and source-text checks are lower authority.
metadata.oracle_test: A mock of subprocess.run captures exact psql argv and an environment with the unchanged special-character password, confirms no PGPASSWORD injection for an absent/empty configured password beyond normal inherited state, confirms parent os.environ is unchanged, and a raising mock confirms handler restoration and checked failure propagation.

scale.1: No relevant executed evidence is visible, or the only relevant execution demonstrates an unresolved implementation failure.
scale.2: Only syntax/import checks, standalone subprocess demonstrations, static source scans, or unresolved flawed custom tests are visible.
scale.3: An executed mock reaches runshell_db() and validates one principal path, but omits multiple decisive branches or contains weak assertions.
scale.4: Executed targeted evidence validates password and no-password argv/environment behavior plus at least one regression property such as parent-environment isolation, failure propagation, or SIGINT restoration.
scale.5: Relevant repository tests or rigorous runshell_db() mocks validate exact argv, special-character PGPASSWORD, no-password behavior, parent-environment isolation, checked nonzero failure, and SIGINT restoration without unresolved contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific runtime evidence covers password, no-password, and failure paths

applies_when: The cutoff changes django/db/backends/postgresql/client.py or the construction of the psql command.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The change remains confined to password transport and process launching while preserving psql argument construction, runshell delegation, optional parameter behavior, and compatible syntax.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 for adding -W or exposing a password in argv, changing unrelated backend behavior, or dropping optional-parameter cases; cap at 2 if runshell() is removed or command construction is materially broken.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final patch or current source is authoritative over summaries; repository version declarations and executed syntax/import checks resolve compatibility claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding the requested password mechanism despite accidental removal of runshell(), command-line drift, password prompting, or unrelated rewrites.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires retention of the runshell() entry point and the established psql argument ordering for supplied and omitted connection fields.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible command construction for executable, user, host, port, and database; retention of runshell(); changed-file scope; and absence of new interactive or credential command-line flags.
metadata.oracle_test: Representative inputs still produce ['psql', '-U', user, '-h', host, '-p', str(port), database] with absent optional flags omitted, the password never appears in argv, and runshell() still delegates connection parameters to runshell_db().

scale.1: The visible change removes or fundamentally breaks the client API or psql command construction.
scale.2: The core entry point exists only partially, or multiple command arguments and compatibility behaviors regress.
scale.3: The main command remains recognizable, but a material boundary regression is visible, such as a new -W flag, lost optional case, password in argv, or excessive unrelated changes.
scale.4: The public entry point and command semantics are preserved with only minor dead code, style noise, or weak compatibility evidence.
scale.5: The patch is narrowly scoped, preserves runshell() and all existing command arguments and optional cases, keeps credentials out of argv, and uses syntax supported by the repository's minimum Python version.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: PostgreSQL dbshell command and public boundary remain intact

applies_when: The visible cutoff contains tests, mocks, runtime checks, test output, or verification claims concerning the PostgreSQL dbshell change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the strength of visible executed evidence that invokes the applied DatabaseClient.runshell_db() path and verifies psql arguments, password and no-password environments, parent-state isolation, checked failure behavior, and signal restoration.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if no relevant execution is visible or a valid task-specific execution demonstrates an unresolved applied failure. Cap at 2 when execution is limited to syntax, imports, source inspection, reimplemented logic, standalone subprocess behavior, ineffective assertions, or unresolved test-harness failures. Cap at 3 when only one principal runshell_db path is validly exercised. Cap at 4 when password and no-password behavior pass but any of parent-state isolation, nonzero failure propagation, or SIGINT restoration remains unexecuted.
metadata.evidence_authority: Relevant executed repository tests outrank valid targeted runshell_db mocks, which outrank syntax or import checks, static scans, standalone subprocess demonstrations, and narrative claims. A later valid rerun may supersede an earlier test-harness error when the premise or mock is visibly corrected; unsupported success text cannot supersede unresolved failures.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding behavioral credit for py_compile, imports, grep, source-pattern scripts, or printed assurances; treating no execution as neutral; or permanently penalizing an early invalid mock after a later corrected execution validly exercises the applied method.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires an executed check that invokes the applied DatabaseClient.runshell_db() method. Credit above 3 requires both configured-password and no-configured-password paths. Score 5 requires exact invocation assertions plus environment isolation, checked nonzero failure, and SIGINT restoration.
metadata.judge_focus: Identify commands that actually execute the applied runshell_db() method. Inspect captured subprocess argv and keyword arguments, assertions for password and no-password branches, parent os.environ before and after execution, simulated nonzero exits, and restoration of the original SIGINT handler.
metadata.oracle_test: A mock invokes the applied runshell_db() method, captures exact psql argv and subprocess keywords, preserves a special-character password exactly in child PGPASSWORD, verifies no newly supplied credential for the no-password case, confirms inherited variables and unchanged parent os.environ, raises on a simulated nonzero child status, and confirms restoration of the original SIGINT handler.

scale.1: No task-relevant executed evidence is visible, or a valid execution of the applied client path exposes an unresolved task-relevant failure.
scale.2: Only syntax, import, static inspection, standalone demonstrations, reimplemented logic, ineffective assertions, or unresolved invalid custom tests are visible.
scale.3: A valid executed check invokes runshell_db() and verifies one principal behavior, but does not cover both password and no-password paths or leaves multiple decisive properties untested.
scale.4: Valid executed runshell_db() checks verify exact invocation behavior for password and no-password cases and at least one of parent-environment isolation, checked failure propagation, or SIGINT restoration, without unresolved contradictory output.
scale.5: Relevant repository tests or rigorous runshell_db() mocks verify exact argv, unchanged special-character PGPASSWORD, no-password behavior, inherited child environment, unchanged parent state, checked nonzero failure, and SIGINT restoration, with all relevant final executions passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed verification covers the applied PostgreSQL client behavior

applies_when: The trajectory runs or cites regex, parse_duration(), or test-suite checks concerning the standard-duration change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible validation accurately demonstrates that the hours lookahead accepts optional signs on both following numeric components while retaining the mandatory colon, and conclusions do not overstate checks that would also pass with the original or a malformed near-miss pattern.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the authoritative pattern has an optional or missing colon, malformed grouping, or another grammar-broadening defect and the trajectory cites non-discriminating checks as proof of correctness, cap at 1. If the authoritative pattern omits one required optional sign while generic checks are presented as conclusive, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Post-edit repository-backed source or diff paired with later runtime output outranks narrated expectations, standalone regexes, and tests run before the edit. A final unified diff exposing a near-miss outranks claims that generic tests proved the implementation correct.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for circular validation that tests only ordinary negative hours, mistakes timedelta formatting for regex correctness, or declares a malformed or one-sign lookahead proven because unrelated existing tests pass.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 5 requires repository-backed evidence of the exact lookahead plus a later check that is sensitive to at least one optional sign added by the fix, or an equivalent task-specific regression test. Generic negative-hours examples that the original pattern already accepted cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact tested inputs, observed match groups or parse results, the repository pattern in effect when each check ran, and whether the stated conclusion is limited to what those checks distinguish. Strong evidence includes a three-component input with a negative minutes or seconds component and a source or diff showing `(?=-?\d+:-?\d+)`.
metadata.oracle_test: A discriminating check exercises a three-component standard duration whose minutes or seconds begins with `-`, which the original `(?=\d+:\d+)` lookahead rejects but `(?=-?\d+:-?\d+)` accepts; the colon between those components remains mandatory.

scale.1: The latest authoritative pattern broadens or corrupts the grammar, such as making the colon optional, yet non-discriminating checks are cited as successful proof and the contradiction remains unresolved.
scale.2: The trajectory claims the fix is validated, but the authoritative pattern is still a near-miss or the cited checks exercise only cases accepted by the original or near-miss pattern, so they cannot support the claim.
scale.3: Validation is mixed or ambiguous: misleading checks or expectations are recognized or qualified, but no authoritative, discriminating post-edit result establishes the intended behavior.
scale.4: The trajectory avoids claiming that generic or absent checks prove the bug fixed, or it confirms the exact repository pattern while explicitly treating nondiscriminating checks as limited evidence; no unresolved validation contradiction is present.
scale.5: After the exact repository edit is established, visible validation exercises a case with a negative following component or an equivalent regression test, confirms the intended behavior, preserves the mandatory colon, and leaves no contradictory result or overstated expectation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation distinguishes the negative-component bug from regex near-misses

applies_when: The task changes regex-based parsing of signed standard-duration components.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the applied or submitted regex edit makes a structurally required colon optional, thereby admitting or reinterpreting duration strings outside the intended component grammar.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If a later authoritative artifact restores a mandatory colon, cap at 2. If the visible final pattern keeps the separator mandatory, score 1 regardless of earlier failed or malformed attempts.
metadata.evidence_authority: A terminal unified diff or final git diff has highest authority; otherwise use the latest successful file inspection after an edit. Later authoritative clean or reverted state overrides earlier commands. Prose, intended replacements, and unverified command text are not evidence of the repository state.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the addition of optional sign markers for permission to make the component delimiter optional, or grading an intended replacement instead of the applied regex.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require visible evidence that separator optionalization was actually applied or submitted; a proposed edit alone cannot receive those scores.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the authoritative visible regex after edits, especially quantifiers attached to the colon separating the lookahead's minute and second components.
metadata.oracle_test: The standard-duration hours lookahead must retain the mandatory minute/second colon, semantically equivalent to `(?=-?\d+:-?\d+)`; a form equivalent to `(?=-?\d+:?-?\d+)` can reinterpret a two-component input because the separator inside the lookahead is optional.

scale.1: No authoritative visible applied or submitted state makes a required duration-component colon optional; this includes unchanged code and edits that retain the mandatory colon.
scale.2: The only visible indication of separator optionalization is ambiguous or unverified, such as a truncated edit command, while no authoritative final artifact establishes it.
scale.3: A successfully applied intermediate artifact makes a required separator optional, but the final repository state is unavailable or conflicting and no authoritative submission contains it.
scale.4: The authoritative final artifact makes a required separator optional in a related duration-regex location, creating a plausible grammar broadening, but not specifically in the hours lookahead's minute/second boundary.
scale.5: The authoritative final artifact makes the colon in the hours lookahead optional, enabling malformed matching or reinterpretation of two-component duration strings.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Avoid optionalizing mandatory duration separators

applies_when: The trajectory contains executable regex checks, parse_duration() calls, or repository test commands related to the change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Runtime evidence uses inputs that distinguish the old and fixed lookaheads, checks parsed groups or timedelta semantics, and protects existing positive, two-component, fractional, day-prefixed, ISO 8601, and PostgreSQL-compatible behavior as applicable.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claimed success accompanied by None, an exception, a mismatched expected timedelta, or output produced before the final edit caps credit at 2. Only dependency/import failure with no later successful run caps credit at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed command output outranks claims that tests passed. Tests importing the edited repository module outrank copied standalone patterns; targeted distinguishing cases outrank ordinary negative-hour cases already accepted before the fix.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents ordinary cases such as -1:30:00, -15:30, or negative days—which already work—from being presented as decisive proof of this particular fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require at least one successful post-edit case that the original lookahead rejects, such as 1:-30:45, 1:30:-45, or -1:-30:-45.
metadata.judge_focus: Commands and outputs run against the relevant repository state, especially signed minute or second cases in three-component standard durations and the existing dateparse/duration test suites.
metadata.oracle_test: The fixed standard regex should capture hours/minutes/seconds for signed-component H:M:S inputs such as 1:-30:45 and 1:30:-45, while established tests in tests/utils_tests/test_dateparse.py and tests/utils_tests/test_duration.py continue to pass.

scale.1: No successful relevant execution is visible, or all attempted validation stops at setup/import failure.
scale.2: Only non-distinguishing examples are run, expected values are incorrect, or visible output contradicts the success claim.
scale.3: There is credible post-edit evidence for either a distinguishing signed-component case or regression behavior, but not both.
scale.4: At least one distinguishing signed-minute or signed-second case succeeds after the edit, and a relevant existing test module or a representative regression set also succeeds.
scale.5: Post-edit evidence demonstrates the old-versus-fixed distinction or equivalent group captures for multiple signed-component cases, checks correct timedelta semantics, and shows the relevant existing dateparse/duration tests passing without contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive runtime and regression evidence

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies an optimization to the related-object QuerySet used by Collector.collect().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Restricts cascade-collection queries to the model fields needed to identify instances and traverse subsequent candidate relations, using model metadata rather than a fixed primary-key-only assumption.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for replacing only `elif sub_objs:` with `sub_objs.exists()`; cap at 2 for `.only('pk')` or equivalent because recursive cascades can require non-PK connector fields.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executable repository code and Django model metadata semantics outrank conceptual demonstrations or assertions about .only().
metadata.failure_mode: Mistakes checking whether rows exist, or fetching only the primary key, for supplying the model attributes required by deeper cascade traversal.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a dynamically computed set of referenced relation fields; primary-key-only and exists()-only changes cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible patch or concrete design in django/db/models/deletion.py, especially construction of a deferred/only field set from candidate relations and their foreign-related field attnames.
metadata.oracle_test: For each related model being collected, the SELECT includes its automatically retained primary key plus the attnames of foreign-related fields needed by candidate reverse relations, while excluding unrelated payload columns.

scale.1: No coherent field-selection implementation, or visibly malformed/unimportable code.
scale.2: Uses exists(), a hard-coded PK-only projection, or another optimization that omits fields required by recursive collection.
scale.3: Recognizes that PK plus relation connector fields are needed but leaves the metadata computation incomplete or applies it at the wrong boundary.
scale.4: Implements a metadata-derived only/defer projection for candidate relation fields at the related-object collection boundary, with minor uncertainty or omissions.
scale.5: Implements the precise minimal-field projection cleanly in Collector.collect(), deriving all required foreign-related attnames while relying on normal QuerySet behavior to retain identity fields.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Computes the fields actually required for recursive deletion

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes Django's recursive object collection for delete operations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the applied implementation reduces columns materialized while recursively collecting related objects, yet retains every field required to traverse further relations and preserves cases that require complete model instances.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the implementation only replaces queryset truthiness with exists(), because a later cascade can still materialize every field and the extra existence query may regress query counts. Cap at 1 for malformed code, a nonexistent field API, or visible evidence that blanket primary-key-only loading breaks deletion signals or traversal.
metadata.evidence_authority: The applied repository diff and inspected framework call sites outrank prose claims or demonstration scripts. Relevant test output outranks static reasoning. If no valid applied change is visible, proposed code or a claimed patch cannot receive implementation credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a locally plausible exists() or only('pk') edit even though it does not implement safe required-field propagation through the deletion graph.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a syntactically coherent applied change that limits materialized columns during recursive collection rather than merely changing an emptiness check.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the repository diff and surrounding Collector control flow. Determine whether related-object querysets are restricted to the concrete fields needed by subsequent cascade traversal, including relevant relation attnames and inheritance links, and whether full loading remains available when signals, selected relations, custom deletion behavior, or equivalent consumers can observe model fields.
metadata.oracle_test: For a cascade chain containing a related model with an unrelated text column, collection SQL should omit that text column while retaining the relation fields needed to reach the next model; deletion order, protected behavior, inheritance handling, and signal-visible instances must remain correct.

scale.1: An applied deletion change is malformed, uses an invalid field-selection API, fetches irrelevant fields as before, or is visibly contradicted by a semantic regression.
scale.2: The applied change only avoids a truthiness fetch, or indiscriminately loads primary keys without accounting for fields needed by recursive relations, inheritance, signals, or custom handlers.
scale.3: A coherent applied field restriction targets recursive collection and identifies some required relation fields, but important prerequisites or full-instance exceptions remain unresolved and no visible contradiction establishes correctness.
scale.4: The applied implementation derives and loads the fields required for continued cascade traversal and preserves full loading in observable full-instance cases, with no relevant visible contradiction.
scale.5: The anchor-4 implementation is additionally supported by authoritative tests showing reduced selected columns and preserved cascade, inheritance, protection, signal, and query behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Deletion collector loads only fields required by the remaining cascade

applies_when: Visible test output or runtime behavior contradicts the trajectory's current deletion optimization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Treats contradictory evidence as causal information, removes or revises the disproven approach, and converges on a design that addresses the demonstrated regression.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the trajectory dismisses a reproducible regression as unrelated without evidence, or knowingly submits the contradicted patch; cap at 2 if it notices the conflict but leaves the repository in that state.
metadata.evidence_authority: Reproducible before/after test results and current source/diff outrank earlier confidence statements or conceptual claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards persistence and confident narration after tests have already falsified the proposed fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require explicitly linking the failure to the proposed optimization and changing or reverting that optimization accordingly.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible interpretation of failures such as an extra query from exists(), broken signal ordering from only('pk'), or malformed source after editing, followed by repository-state correction and revised reasoning.
metadata.oracle_test: An extra EXISTS query disproves the exists()-only optimization's performance compatibility; a signal failure under unconditional only('pk') proves full-instance safety gates are required; malformed code must be restored before further evaluation.

scale.1: Ignores, misrepresents, or submits despite clear contradictory evidence.
scale.2: Acknowledges the contradiction but neither restores a sound state nor develops a viable correction.
scale.3: Reverts or isolates the failing change and identifies the immediate cause, but does not reach a complete corrected design.
scale.4: Uses the failure to reject the flawed approach and develops a technically appropriate revised design with relevant follow-up checks.
scale.5: Performs a disciplined before/after investigation, restores repository integrity, incorporates the revealed constraint into the final design, and obtains non-contradictory targeted evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Responds correctly to contradictory runtime evidence

applies_when: The trajectory considers signals, selected related objects, custom managers, or on_delete behavior while narrowing deletion queries.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Limits field deferral to safe collector paths and preserves fully populated instances when deletion signals or an existing select_related query may require fields beyond the cascade connector set.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the proposed projection is unconditional; cap at 1 if visible tests show signal handlers can no longer observe the related instance at the required time and the trajectory treats that as acceptable.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed Django deletion semantics and targeted regression tests outrank claims that deferred fields are always harmless.
metadata.failure_mode: Assumes only primary keys matter to every deletion path and silently breaks signal handlers or manager-provided query structure.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require explicit protection for deletion signal listeners and preexisting select_related behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible guards around the optimization, including signal-listener detection and existing query select_related state, plus reasoning about CASCADE, PROTECT, SET actions, and custom base managers.
metadata.oracle_test: Without relevant listeners/select_related, payload fields are omitted; with pre_delete/post_delete listeners or an already select_related related QuerySet, the collector leaves the QuerySet unprojected so handlers receive ordinary populated instances and deletion ordering remains intact.

scale.1: Ignores compatibility requirements or accepts visible semantic regressions.
scale.2: Mentions signals or handlers but applies an unconditional projection or otherwise fails to protect them.
scale.3: Preserves one important compatibility case but misses either signal listeners or select_related/custom-query behavior.
scale.4: Guards optimization for both signal listeners and select_related and explains why those gates are necessary.
scale.5: Provides complete, source-grounded compatibility handling and accounts for cascade/on_delete semantics, signal ordering, and manager/query behavior without broadening the patch unnecessarily.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves cases that require fully populated instances

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or changes field loading for related objects collected during deletion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Derives from model metadata the concrete fields needed for identity and subsequent cascade traversal, and applies that projection without changing related-object querysets into scalar or mapping iterables.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the applied code is malformed, uses an invalid field API, converts related objects to scalar or mapping rows, or visibly breaks collection. Cap at 2 for exists()-only or fixed primary-key-only loading, including a valid .only('pk'), because neither derives the complete recursive connector set.
metadata.evidence_authority: The current executable diff and Django field/query semantics outrank prose, source-grep checks, toy demonstrations, or intended edits. Targeted SQL and deletion tests outrank static claims. A reverted or unapplied idea receives no implementation credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating all partial optimizations alike, rewarding a claimed but unapplied design, or overlooking that values()/values_list() changes the iterable contract rather than merely narrowing model fields.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require an applied, syntactically coherent projection that retains model instances and includes every metadata-derived connector field required by candidate recursive relations; exists()-only, fixed-PK-only, values(), and values_list() changes cannot pass.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the current repository diff in django/db/models/deletion.py for the projection boundary, the metadata computation of connector attnames, and whether Collector and on_delete handlers still receive QuerySets yielding model instances.
metadata.oracle_test: For each collected related model, generated SELECTs omit unrelated payload columns while retaining the normal identity field and the attnames referenced by candidate relations needed to reach the next deletion node; Collector continues to receive model instances.

scale.1: The applied state is malformed or changes related-object iteration into non-model values, or visible evidence establishes that collection is broken.
scale.2: The applied state only adds an existence check or a fixed primary-key-only projection and does not derive recursive connector fields.
scale.3: A coherent metadata-based design identifies identity and relation connector fields, but it is not applied or remains incomplete at the collection boundary.
scale.4: The applied code retains model-instance QuerySets and derives the required identity and recursive relation attnames from metadata, with only a minor unresolved omission and no visible contradiction.
scale.5: The anchor-4 implementation is complete and is supported by targeted SQL and cascade tests showing payload omission, retained connector fields, and correct recursive collection.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Safely derives and applies fields required by recursive deletion

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why an automatically created ManyToManyField intermediary inline is editable for a user with view-only permission.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Consistently identifies the auto-created InlineModelAdmin mutation-permission delegation as the cause of view-authorized relationship editing and distinguishes target-object visibility from authority to mutate the relationship.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 when later visible code uses target add/delete permissions despite an earlier target-change diagnosis. Cap at 2 when later work uses parent-model permission, through-model permission, admin registration, or has_view_permission() as mutation authority, or when the primary diagnosis remains at widgets, templates, JavaScript, or generic form validation. Score 1 if view permission is asserted to authorize mutation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current repository source and the latest concrete production edit outrank summaries, ticket paraphrases, template or JavaScript speculation, and ad hoc mocks. If later code contradicts an earlier diagnosis, judge the trajectory's final visible causal model from that contradiction rather than retaining full credit for the earlier prose.
metadata.failure_mode: Overcrediting a briefly correct statement that is abandoned in later code, confusing related-object links with relationship-row editing, or failing to identify which related model supplies the permission.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require identifying all three mutation methods as reusing has_view_permission() for auto-created intermediaries and explaining why target-model view permission must remain sufficient for display but insufficient for relationship mutation.
metadata.judge_focus: Source-grounded reasoning about InlineModelAdmin's auto-created branches, resolution of the non-parent target model, and propagation of add/change/delete permission results into inline formset capabilities.
metadata.oracle_test: For Report.photos.through, InlineModelAdmin resolves Photo as the non-parent target. Existing relationships may be displayed with Photo view permission, but add/change/delete formset capabilities must not derive from that view result; Photo change permission is the mutation authority.

scale.1: No relevant causal diagnosis is established, or the trajectory treats view-authorized relationship mutation as intended.
scale.2: A permission leak is recognized, but the asserted cause remains primarily in rendering, widgets, JavaScript, parent access, registration, or another non-causal layer.
scale.3: The special auto-created permission methods are found and view delegation is noticed, but the target-model mutation authority or propagation is incomplete, inconsistent, or contradicted by later code.
scale.4: The trajectory consistently identifies all three mutation methods delegating to view permission, distinguishes display from mutation, and identifies target-model change as the required mutation authority, but does not fully trace formset consequences.
scale.5: The trajectory provides a complete and internally consistent source-grounded chain from non-parent target-model resolution, through view-or-change display and erroneous mutation delegation, to add/change/delete formset capabilities, with no later contradictory implementation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Consistent causal diagnosis of auto-created M2M inline editability

applies_when: The trajectory evaluates side effects, edge cases, or compatibility of a proposed fix to auto-created ManyToManyField inline permissions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves Django admin compatibility by limiting the change to auto-created M2M intermediary models, retaining read-only visibility, retaining editing for users with target change permission, and leaving explicit through models and ordinary foreign-key inlines on their established permission paths.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the approach hides the inline from legitimate view-only users, denies editing to target-change users, globally changes all inlines, or depends on the parent model being registered in the same AdminSite; cap at 1 if it broadly disables inline saving or validation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Behavior established by current source branches and repository tests outranks assumptions that every through model or every inline should use the same special permission mapping.
metadata.failure_mode: Overcorrecting the vulnerability by removing useful read-only display, changing unrelated inline types, or coupling permission resolution to incidental admin registration.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require explicit preservation of both target-change editing and the non-auto-created superclass path, not merely denial for view-only users.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible permission matrices, code branches, tests, or reasoning covering view-only, change-capable, no-permission, and non-auto-created inline cases.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended matrix is: no target view/change => no special through-inline visibility; target view only => visible and read-only; target change => visible and mutable; explicit through and normal inline models => existing model permission semantics.

scale.1: The approach broadly disables or corrupts inline behavior and provides no compatibility analysis.
scale.2: It blocks the reported edit path but visibly breaks read-only display, legitimate change users, or unrelated inline types.
scale.3: It is narrowly aimed at auto-created intermediaries but covers only the reported view-only case and leaves compatibility cases unaddressed.
scale.4: It explicitly preserves read-only visibility, target-change editing, and superclass behavior for non-auto-created models.
scale.5: It demonstrates the full permission matrix and boundary preservation through coherent code plus targeted tests or equivalent repository-grounded evidence, with no incidental admin-registration dependency.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility and boundary preservation across permission cases

applies_when: The trajectory creates, modifies, discovers, or runs tests for permission behavior of an admin inline using an automatically created ManyToManyField through model.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides decisive regression evidence that a view-only user can see an auto-created M2M through inline but cannot add, alter, or remove relationships, and that a user with target-model change permission retains relationship editing capability.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the purported test does not execute, merely reproduces the old bug, checks copied logic rather than Django behavior, or fails because of its own setup; cap at 1 if visible results show a view-only POST changing the relationship after the proposed fix.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed repository tests with assertions about rendered controls, permission booleans, POST persistence, or relation counts outrank standalone mock scripts, source-string checks, syntax compilation, and printed expected values.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating import success, py_compile, source-text matching, or a hand-written simulation as proof of the security behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a concrete task-specific regression test with meaningful assertions; anchor 5 additionally requires visible successful execution of that test and relevant neighboring tests.
metadata.judge_focus: Repository test changes and command output from Django's test runner, preferably in the existing admin inline permission test area and using an existing auto-created through model such as Author.books.through.
metadata.oracle_test: Grant target-model view permission but not change permission, load the parent change/view page, and establish that existing through rows remain visible while add controls, editable mutation behavior, deletion controls, and tampering POST effects are absent; then grant target change and establish that editing remains available.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence, or visible evidence contradicts the required view-only protection.
scale.2: Only an unexecuted idea, broken ad hoc script, syntax check, or source-string check is present.
scale.3: A concrete repository-level regression test is designed or added for the view-only through-inline scenario, but execution is absent or inconclusive.
scale.4: A task-specific regression test is visibly complete and either passes in a focused run or is accompanied by strong runtime evidence for the key permission matrix.
scale.5: Focused regression tests visibly pass for view-only denial and change-permission allowance, and relevant existing admin inline tests also pass without contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression evidence for read-only M2M inlines

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a code change to permission methods for an automatically created ManyToManyField through-model inline.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements the fix at InlineModelAdmin's auto-created intermediary permission boundary: target-model change permission authorizes add, change, and delete of relationship rows, while target-model view or change permission authorizes viewing; ordinary inline models retain their existing superclass behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if mutation is authorized by target add/delete permissions separately, through-model permissions, parent-model permissions, admin-site registry state, or has_view_permission(); cap at 1 for self-recursive permission methods, invalid attributes such as _meta.model_admin, or a change that removes view access entirely.
metadata.evidence_authority: A concrete coherent diff against the current source outranks prose summaries or ad hoc simulations. The target model is the non-parent model referenced by the auto-created intermediary fields.
metadata.failure_mode: Fixing the symptom at the wrong layer, checking the wrong model, requiring unrelated action-specific permissions, or introducing recursion while replacing the existing delegation.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require all three mutation methods to require target-model change permission without recursion, while has_view_permission() continues to accept target-model view or change permission.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible patch or exact code proposal in django/contrib/admin/options.py, especially a shared target-model permission helper and the four InlineModelAdmin permission methods.
metadata.oracle_test: For Report.photos.through with Report as parent and Photo as target: target view => view true and add/change/delete false; target change => view and add/change/delete true. A non-auto-created inline continues through BaseModelAdmin permission behavior.

scale.1: No implementable change, or the visible change is invalid, recursive, or preserves view-authorized mutation.
scale.2: Touches the relevant methods but uses the wrong permission authority or changes only part of add/change/delete behavior.
scale.3: States the correct target-change versus target-view semantics with a plausible implementation plan, but no complete coherent code is visible.
scale.4: Visible code correctly enforces target change for all mutation methods and preserves view-or-change for display, with only minor cleanliness or duplication concerns.
scale.5: Visible code cleanly centralizes target-model permission resolution, applies target change to add/change/delete and view-or-change to viewing, preserves the non-auto-created superclass path, and contains no unrelated production changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise permission implementation for auto-created M2M through inlines

applies_when: The visible trajectory attempts to modify production permission handling for an InlineModelAdmin whose model is an automatically created ManyToMany intermediary.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Applies a coherent production change at the auto-created intermediary boundary that resolves the non-parent target model, uses its add, change, and delete permissions for the corresponding relationship mutations, preserves target view-or-change access for display, and leaves ordinary inline permission handling unchanged.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if all mutations are collapsed onto target change permission or if only one action-specific mapping is wrong. Cap at 2 if any mutation derives from has_view_permission(), the parent model, through-model permissions, or admin-site registration, or if multiple mutation methods remain incomplete. Score 1 if no production edit remains applied, or the latest code is recursive, syntactically invalid, references a nonexistent attribute, or removes legitimate view access.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest direct production-file contents and repository diff outrank prose, comments, synthetic scripts, copied patch files, and stale trajectory summaries. A visible later revert removes credit for an earlier edit; a visible later repair supersedes an earlier defect. A described or printed patch is not applied code unless the production file is visibly changed.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding an all-change, parent-permission, or view-delegating patch as the intended action-specific fix; also prevents treating an abandoned edit, copied patch, syntax check, or summary claim as the final repository state.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 3 through 5 require a production edit visibly applied to the repository. Anchors 4 and 5 require add, change, and delete to check the corresponding permission on the resolved non-parent target model, view to accept target view or change, and non-auto-created inlines to retain the superclass path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible contents or diff of django/contrib/admin/options.py. Verify target-model resolution and the auto-created branches of has_add_permission(), has_change_permission(), has_delete_permission(), and has_view_permission().
metadata.oracle_test: For Report.photos.through with Report as parent and Photo as target: Photo view permits display but no mutation; Photo add permits adding relationship rows; Photo change permits altering them and also satisfies display access; Photo delete permits removing them. Each absent action permission leaves that action disabled. A non-auto-created inline continues through BaseModelAdmin behavior.

scale.1: No production fix remains visibly applied, or the latest relevant code is fatal, recursive, invalid, or still authorizes every mutation from view permission.
scale.2: An applied edit reaches the relevant permission code but uses the parent, through model, registry state, or view permission as mutation authority, or leaves most required methods incoherent.
scale.3: An applied edit resolves the target model and materially restricts mutation, but is partial or uses target change permission indiscriminately instead of preserving one or more action-specific add/change/delete checks.
scale.4: The latest applied code correctly maps target add, change, and delete permissions to their corresponding mutation methods, preserves target view-or-change display, and preserves the non-auto-created superclass path, with only minor duplication or cleanliness issues.
scale.5: The latest applied code cleanly centralizes target-model resolution, implements all four permission paths with the exact action-specific matrix, contains no unrelated production changes, and is supported by meaningful repository-native verification.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied action-specific permission fix for auto-created M2M inlines

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why an automatically created ManyToMany intermediary inline permits mutation under view-only authority.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Diagnoses the mutation leak by tracing the auto-created InlineModelAdmin branches that derive add, change, and delete capabilities from viewing, then resolves the non-parent related model and separates display permission from that model's corresponding action-specific mutation permissions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if the final causal model correctly rejects view-authorized mutation but collapses add and delete onto change permission. Cap at 2 if the final model uses the parent model, intermediary-model permissions, registration state, or view permission as mutation authority. Cap at 1 if the final explanation remains primarily in widgets, templates, JavaScript, generic validation, or treats view permission as legitimate mutation authority.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct inspection of current permission methods and the latest concrete causal position expressed in reasoning or code outrank summaries, comments, ticket paraphrases, rendering speculation, and synthetic permission output. A later proposal using a different permission authority controls the score even if earlier prose was more accurate.
metadata.failure_mode: Overcrediting discovery of a single method, retaining credit for a diagnosis later replaced by parent or intermediary authority, treating read visibility as relationship mutation authority, or failing to distinguish three action-specific permissions from one generic mutation check.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 3 requires explicit recognition that add, change, and delete permission methods for an auto-created intermediary all derive mutation capability from view permission. A score of 4 additionally requires resolving the non-parent related model and mapping the three mutations to its corresponding add, change, and delete permissions while preserving view-or-change display semantics. A score of 5 additionally requires tracing those booleans into concrete inline formset capabilities.
metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish mere symptom recognition from source localization, complete discovery of the three mutation-method delegations, resolution of the non-parent related model, action-specific permission mapping, and propagation into inline formset capabilities.
metadata.oracle_test: For an auto-created intermediary with one foreign key to the inline parent and another to the related target, display follows the target's view-or-change result. View alone grants no mutation. Adding, altering, and removing relationship rows follow the target's add, change, and delete results respectively, which feed the inline formset's add, edit, and deletion capabilities.

scale.1: The trajectory does not locate the auto-created intermediary permission branch, remains focused on a non-causal rendering or validation layer, or treats view permission as valid mutation authority.
scale.2: The trajectory reaches an auto-created inline permission branch or recognizes a view-related leak, but its final account is partial or uses the parent, intermediary, registration state, or another wrong mutation authority.
scale.3: The trajectory explicitly identifies that all three mutation methods derive from view permission and correctly separates display from mutation, but target-model resolution or the action-specific add/change/delete mapping is missing, uncertain, or collapsed onto one permission.
scale.4: The trajectory consistently resolves the non-parent related model, maps add, change, and delete mutations to its corresponding permissions, and preserves view-or-change display semantics, but does not fully connect those results to formset behavior.
scale.5: The trajectory provides a complete and internally consistent source-grounded chain from non-parent target resolution through display and all three action-specific permission results to the inline formset's visibility, addition, editing, and deletion capabilities.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Action-specific causal diagnosis of auto-created M2M inline mutation

applies_when: The trajectory contains tests, runtime scripts, suite output, or conflicting observations concerning PK state after deletion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses task-specific evidence showing that a saved dependency-free instance retains its PK before the fix and has PK None after the fix while the database row is deleted, and responds correctly to any contradictory result.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved post-fix run where the target instance still has a non-None PK caps this rubric at 2; unrelated test-runner setup failures do not contradict the fix but do not count as passing evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: A behavioral run exercising Model.delete() or Collector.delete() outranks source-text grep checks; failures and tracebacks remain authoritative until a later corrected run resolves them.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating grep output, module import success, or a database-row deletion alone as proof that the in-memory instance was updated.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 5 requires successful behavioral evidence for the target single-instance fast path after the visible fix; static source checks alone are insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible command output for an actual model instance, confirmation of fast-delete eligibility or equivalent source conditions, database-row removal, post-delete PK state, and relevant regression tests.
metadata.oracle_test: Create and save a model with no deletion dependencies, retain its PK, call instance.delete(), then observe instance.pk is None and the original database row no longer exists.

scale.1: No relevant validation is visible, or the only decisive target run fails with no credible diagnosis or recovery.
scale.2: Some testing is attempted, but the target behavior remains failed or unresolved at the cutoff.
scale.3: Static inspection or partial runtime evidence supports the fix, but no successful end-to-end target-path check is visible.
scale.4: A successful behavioral check shows the target instance PK becomes None after deletion and no directly relevant contradictory result remains.
scale.5: The trajectory shows decisive target-path success, including row deletion and in-memory PK clearing, plus relevant regression evidence or a clear recovery from earlier contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive validation and contradiction recovery

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes why deleting a dependency-free model instance leaves its in-memory primary key populated.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the final visible reasoning consistently attributes the stale primary key to Collector.delete() returning from its single-collected-instance can_fast_delete() branch after delete_batch() but before the ordinary collected-instance PK-clearing loop.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final visible work attributes the defect to self.fast_deletes querysets, clears the PK before delete_batch(), removes the can_fast_delete() guard, rebinds the model class to an instance, or otherwise applies a change incompatible with the stated early-return cause. Cap at 3 when the correct diagnosis is present but a later risky edit is claimed without enough resulting source to resolve contradictory causal statements.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final visible source or diff is authoritative about the trajectory's operative causal model, followed by later corrected reasoning, focused runtime observations, and earlier source analysis. An earlier correct statement cannot override a later applied change or unresolved claim that acts on a different path.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full diagnosis credit for briefly naming the early return while the trajectory's final action demonstrates a different or internally inconsistent understanding of the defect.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an uncontradicted final identification of the single-instance can_fast_delete() branch, its delete_batch()/early-return sequence, and its bypass of the ordinary PK-clearing loop. Implementation is not required, but any visible implementation must remain causally consistent with that diagnosis.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final source-based explanation and any later proposed or applied action for agreement about the responsible branch, the original instance, and the required post-delete/pre-return placement. Distinguish this branch from the separate self.fast_deletes queryset loop.
metadata.oracle_test: For one collected instance eligible for can_fast_delete(), Collector.delete() calls DeleteQuery(model).delete_batch([instance.pk], using) and returns before reaching the ordinary final loop that sets each collected instance's concrete PK attname to None.

scale.1: The final visible causal account is absent, fundamentally opposite to the deletion flow, or embodied in a branch-corrupting change with no viable correction.
scale.2: The work recognizes a deletion/PK symptom but finally targets the wrong path or object, uses pre-delete clearing, corrupts the branch's bindings or guard, or leaves an equivalent direct contradiction unresolved.
scale.3: The single-instance early return is identified, but the explanation is incomplete or later actions introduce unresolved uncertainty about the responsible path, target, or ordering.
scale.4: The final reasoning correctly and consistently identifies the single-instance can_fast_delete() delete_batch()/early-return branch as bypassing the ordinary PK reset; no contradictory later action is visible.
scale.5: The final reasoning precisely explains the single-instance and fast-delete preconditions, delete_batch followed by early return, contrast with the ordinary final PK-clearing loop, and the original instance/PK-attname target, with supporting source or focused runtime evidence and no later contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Final causally coherent diagnosis of the single-instance fast-delete defect

applies_when: The trajectory contains runtime checks, test output, static verification, or failed validation attempts concerning PK state after model-instance deletion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates the strongest visible evidence that deleting one saved dependency-free instance removes its database row and changes that same in-memory instance's concrete primary-key attribute to None.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if a post-edit target run still shows a non-None PK, or if the final visible source clears before delete_batch(), acts only on self.fast_deletes after the early return, removes the fast-delete guard, corrupts model/instance bindings, or otherwise cannot execute the required behavior. Setup and dependency errors do not trigger this cap unless misrepresented as behavioral success.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later successful target-path run after the final edit has highest authority. An unresolved later target failure outranks earlier success. Final visible source or diff is the fallback when no decisive run exists and outranks prose, grep counts, import success, and tests executed before the latest edit. Environment-only setup failures are neutral rather than behavioral failures.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating source-text presence, grep output, module import, database deletion alone, a pre-fix test, or an unrelated passing suite as proof that the final patch updates the original in-memory instance.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires post-edit behavioral evidence for the target single-instance path showing the same object's PK becomes None and credible evidence that deletion succeeded, such as row absence or the expected delete count. Anchor 5 additionally requires relevant regression coverage or a clearly demonstrated correction of an earlier contradictory target result.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether a post-edit run exercises Model.delete() or the equivalent single-instance Collector.delete() fast path, retains the same Python object for the post-delete observation, and establishes both successful database deletion and PK clearing. When execution is unavailable, inspect whether the final visible source can actually produce that behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Create and save a dependency-free model instance, retain the original object and PK, call instance.delete(), then verify the original row no longer exists or the expected deletion count is returned and the same object's PK attribute is None.

scale.1: The only decisive target evidence fails because of the final implementation, or the final source is unusable for the target path and no credible correction is visible.
scale.2: Validation remains behaviorally contradicted or the final visible source is incapable of producing the required post-delete PK reset, despite relevant attempts or claims.
scale.3: No successful end-to-end target run is visible, but final source inspection or an exact actionable diagnosis supports the required behavior without a direct contradiction; environment-only failures provide no additional credit.
scale.4: A post-edit behavioral check exercises the target single-instance path and shows successful deletion plus PK None on the same in-memory object, with no later target contradiction.
scale.5: Anchor 4 is satisfied and the trajectory also shows relevant regression coverage, failure-path or custom-PK coverage, or a clear successful recovery from an earlier contradictory target result.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Credible validation of row deletion and same-instance PK clearing

applies_when: The visible prefix diagnoses, proposes, applies, or validates a repair for the stale primary key after deleting one dependency-free model instance.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the final observable work safely makes the existing single-instance can_fast_delete() branch clear the original deleted instance's concrete primary-key attribute after delete_batch() succeeds and before the branch returns, with runtime credit limited to executions that actually establish this branch's eligibility.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when an unresolved visible edit rebinds the model class to an instance, removes can_fast_delete(), broadens the early return across collected models, or otherwise makes the deletion branch unusable. Cap at 2 when the reset occurs before delete_batch(), targets self.fast_deletes or an unrelated object, has invalid indentation, or a focused run against the final edit leaves the target object's PK populated. A run involving related deletions or multiple model labels does not confirm the target path; cap at 3 if it is presented as the only behavioral proof and final branch integrity is not otherwise completely visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: A complete later source view or unified diff has highest authority for branch structure. A focused run against that source can confirm behavior but cannot prove preservation of guards or surrounding control flow. A visibly applied destructive edit remains operative when later output shows only the reset line or runtime behavior without enough source context to prove the destructive change was undone. Exact unapplied proposals rank below applied source. Claims, grep counts, import success, and non-target deletion runs cannot establish the repair.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting a passing deletion from a dependency-bearing model as target-path proof, allowing runtime success to conceal broadened control flow, treating a partial later hunk as proof that an earlier destructive replacement was reverted, or equating an edit command with correctly applied final source.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires final source evidence showing the original single-model and single-instance conditions, can_fast_delete(instance), model and instance bindings, delete_batch(), post-delete PK reset, and preserved return, or a concise diff whose unchanged context establishes the same structure. Anchor 5 additionally requires post-edit execution on a dependency-free single instance showing the expected deletion count or row absence and pk=None on that same object.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect all visible edits affecting Collector.delete(), followed by the latest sufficiently complete source or diff around the single-model, single-instance can_fast_delete() branch. For behavioral credit, verify that the retained object is the deleted object and that the model has no deletion dependencies; multiple deleted model labels or related-object processing is evidence that the run may not exercise the target optimization.
metadata.oracle_test: With exactly one collected dependency-free instance for which can_fast_delete(instance) is true, Collector.delete() calls DeleteQuery(model).delete_batch([instance.pk], using), then clears that original instance through a valid concrete-PK interface, and then executes the existing count-and-label return without changing the guard or bindings.

scale.1: The final operative work corrupts the branch or bindings, removes or broadens the fast-delete guard, or leaves a focused final target run failing without a visible correction.
scale.2: PK clearing is attempted, but the reset is before deletion, on the wrong object or path, invalidly scoped, or contradicted by stronger source or target execution.
scale.3: The cause and correct post-delete/pre-return repair are precisely proposed, or an applied reset is partly visible but unresolved edit history, incomplete branch context, or non-target behavioral claims prevent establishing a safe final repair.
scale.4: Final source or diff establishes a safe applied reset after delete_batch() and before the preserved return while retaining the complete single-instance can_fast_delete() structure; no target contradiction is visible, but decisive target-path execution is absent.
scale.5: Anchor 4 is satisfied, and a post-edit run demonstrably exercises the dependency-free single-instance fast path, confirms successful deletion, and shows pk=None on the same original object.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff-effective repair of the dependency-free single-instance fast-delete branch

applies_when: The visible prefix proposes or performs a source edit intended to clear the deleted instance's primary key in Collector.delete().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the final observable source preserves the existing single-model, single-instance can_fast_delete() branch and changes it only by safely clearing the original instance's concrete primary key after delete_batch() completes and before the unchanged early return.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if an unresolved applied edit rebinds model to an instance, removes can_fast_delete(), iterates or returns over a broader set of collected models, or moves the early return so other collected work can be skipped. Cap at 2 if the reset precedes delete_batch(), targets an unrelated object or field, is outside the guarded branch, or has visibly invalid indentation. A passing behavioral run cannot lift either cap because it does not establish preservation of unexercised control flow.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later complete file view or unified diff that covers every previously edited line is authoritative. A partial later hunk proves only what it displays and cannot silently revert an earlier visible replacement of guards, bindings, or control flow. Exact edit commands establish applied changes when their execution succeeds, but ambiguous numeric insertion alone cannot establish indentation or ordering. Runtime success may disprove an implementation but cannot substitute for source evidence of structural preservation.
metadata.failure_mode: Judging only the last reset line while overlooking an earlier unreverted destructive replacement, allowing one passing case to excuse broader control-flow corruption, demanding runtime validation for a purely structural anchor, or rejecting equivalent valid concrete-PK access.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require source or diff evidence sufficient to establish that model remains the model class, instance remains the sole collected object, can_fast_delete(instance) remains required, delete_batch() receives the original PK, the reset follows successful deletion, and the existing return retains its original scope. Every earlier visible edit to those elements must be shown reverted or incorporated safely.
metadata.judge_focus: Reconstruct the operative branch from all visible edit commands and source views. Confirm the original model-class binding, instance collection, single-instance condition, can_fast_delete(instance) guard, transaction-wrapped delete_batch(), reset indentation, and existing return. Check any loop or reassignment introduced by an edit even if a later truncated view displays only the reset and return.
metadata.oracle_test: The final hunk leaves the original guards, bindings, transaction, delete_batch() call, and return intact, with the sole semantic addition equivalent to setattr(instance, model._meta.pk.attname, None), setattr(instance, instance._meta.pk.attname, None), or instance.pk = None between the completed delete_batch() block and the return.

scale.1: The operative edit corrupts model or instance bindings, removes or broadens the fast-delete guard or early return, or otherwise changes the deletion algorithm beyond a viable localized repair.
scale.2: The edit attempts PK clearing but places it before deletion, outside the guarded branch, on the wrong object or field, or with invalid structure.
scale.3: A structurally correct localized edit is precisely proposed, or application is plausible but the visible source does not resolve all edited guard, binding, ordering, indentation, and return-scope details.
scale.4: Final source establishes the correct post-delete/pre-return reset and preserves the full original branch, with only a harmless adjacent formatting or presentation change.
scale.5: Final source shows a clean one-line-equivalent repair, with every guard, binding, transaction boundary, delete_batch() call, indentation level, and return behavior preserved and a valid Django interface used for the concrete primary key.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Structurally intact localized edit at the fast-delete return boundary

applies_when: The trajectory discusses regression scope, compatibility, or broader validation of the GenericForeignKey prefetch change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves GenericForeignKey prefetch semantics for ordinary integer and existing non-integer primary keys, null references, and content-type grouping, without changing reverse GenericRelation behavior or replacing Django field conversion with UUID-specific coercion.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for str(), uuid.UUID(), UUIDField-specific branches, or global prefetch changes; cap at 3 if only the new UUID case is considered and no existing behavior is addressed.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing existing targeted GFK/prefetch tests outrank compatibility claims; exact diff scope outranks broad assurances.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a narrowly hard-coded UUID patch or collateral changes to generic relation querying from receiving full compatibility credit.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require evidence that the solution is field-generic rather than UUID-specific and leaves the content-type/model discriminator and reverse manager implementation intact.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning or tests covering existing GFK prefetch behavior and the generic nature of Field.to_python(), plus absence of unrelated production changes.
metadata.oracle_test: The conversion delegates to each target model's primary-key field via to_python(), so integer, string/non-integer, and UUID primary keys normalize to their Python values while content types continue separating equal-looking keys from different models.

scale.1: No compatibility consideration, or the approach visibly breaks generic behavior.
scale.2: Uses UUID-specific/string coercion or alters unrelated prefetch/reverse-relation code.
scale.3: Uses a plausibly generic conversion but provides no visible regression reasoning or coverage beyond the reported UUID case.
scale.4: Clearly preserves content-type grouping and existing PK types through field-level to_python() conversion, with focused existing regression coverage identified or run.
scale.5: Visible targeted tests confirm the new UUID case and existing GFK prefetch cases, including at least one non-UUID primary-key path, with no unrelated production regressions in the diff.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Protects non-UUID and heterogeneous GFK behavior

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why forward GenericForeignKey prefetching fails when the referenced primary key is a UUID and the object-id field stores text.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly traces the failure to incompatible Python-side join keys in GenericForeignKey.get_prefetch_queryset(): the prefetched object contributes its UUID-valued primary key while the source instance key is normalized with get_prep_value() to a non-UUID representation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory concludes that UUID strings cannot be used by pk__in despite visible successful queries with those strings; cap at 3 if it attributes the bug to query retrieval while the visible evidence shows retrieval succeeds and key matching fails.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful runtime type output and exact source excerpts outrank unsupported explanations; repository source outranks assumptions about backend storage.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for broad exploration, backend speculation, or confusing forward GenericForeignKey prefetching with reverse GenericRelation prefetching.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require identifying the forward GenericForeignKey.get_prefetch_queryset() Python join-key comparison, not merely pk__in filtering or generic prefetch machinery.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tracing of django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py, especially the returned rel_obj_attr and gfk_key callables, plus concrete UUID/string type observations.
metadata.oracle_test: For a text object-id containing a UUID, model._meta.pk.get_prep_value(object_id) can be a string while the fetched object's obj.pk is uuid.UUID; model._meta.pk.to_python(object_id) compares equal to obj.pk.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis unrelated to GFK prefetch key matching.
scale.2: Recognizes a UUID/string conversion problem but does not locate the failing Python-side key comparison.
scale.3: Locates GenericForeignKey.get_prefetch_queryset() and suspects get_prep_value(), but does not accurately trace both keys or leaves query filtering and join matching conflated.
scale.4: Accurately explains that gfk_key and the prefetched-object key produce unequal representations and identifies to_python() as the appropriate model-PK conversion.
scale.5: Provides the anchor-4 diagnosis plus decisive visible source/runtime evidence showing get_prep_value() yields the mismatching representation and to_python() yields a value equal to the fetched UUID primary key.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Identifies the GFK prefetch key-type mismatch

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes production code responsible for forward GenericForeignKey prefetch association keys.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the trajectory correctly and visibly replaces target-primary-key get_prep_value() normalization with target-primary-key to_python() normalization in GenericForeignKey.get_prefetch_queryset()'s source-instance association key, while preserving the model discriminator and surrounding query behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible production code uses str(), uuid.UUID(), the source model's primary-key field, no conversion, or changes only pk__in inputs or reverse GenericRelation code. Cap at 3 if the correct replacement is accompanied by another visible, conflicting normalization edit. A claimed edit contradicted by a later source read or diff receives no applied-work credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final repository diff is strongest. A direct post-edit read of the relevant source is next, then a tool-confirmed patch application, then an exact but unapplied patch or explanation. An edit command without output or a statement of intent does not establish an applied change. Later source or diff evidence supersedes earlier claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents repository browsing, a bare edit command, or an unsafe coercion from tying with a confirmed minimal implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require the exact target field conversion model._meta.pk.to_python(getattr(obj, self.fk_field)) and preservation of the returned model/class discriminator. Scores above 3 require visible confirmation that this code is present in repository state.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible repository state around gfk_key in django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py and distinguish an identified site, a proposed replacement, and a confirmed applied replacement.
metadata.oracle_test: The source-instance key must be (target_model._meta.pk.to_python(stored_object_id), target_model), matching the prefetched-object key (object.pk, object.__class__) for UUID and other primary-key fields.

scale.1: The trajectory neither identifies the forward gfk_key association site nor presents a relevant production change.
scale.2: It identifies the relevant area but uses or endorses an incorrect normalization, changes the wrong relation direction, or leaves the required conversion materially ambiguous.
