scale.5: Provides decisive successful evidence: the real aggregate query returns one row with count 2, generated SQL retains random ORDER BY while excluding it from GROUP BY, and the focused repository regression test passes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive regression evidence for aggregate plus order_by('?')

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or validates how random ordering affects an aggregate queryset's GROUP BY clause.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible execution establishes the task-specific causal chain: random ordering is represented by a wrapped Random expression, that expression contributes a random function to GROUP BY, and excluding that contribution preserves aggregate grouping while random ordering remains in ORDER BY.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the trajectory claims behavioral success after failed setup, relies only on imports or source-text searches, or interprets isinstance(Random(), Random) as proof that a guard on OrderBy(Random()) works. An incorrect applied repair does not erase independently conclusive diagnostic execution, but it prevents treating any unexecuted post-change behavior as fixed.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful command output from the relevant ORM/compiler path outranks source inspection, proposed code, comments, summaries, and source-text assertions. Exact aggregate results plus generated SQL are strongest. Executed expression-shape and get_group_by_cols() output may conclusively validate or falsify a compiler hypothesis even when the currently applied repair remains wrong. When post-change claims conflict with execution, the execution controls.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents collapsing executable self-falsification into the same score as unsupported activity, while also preventing failed setup, synthetic source checks, or a bare Random isinstance demonstration from being mistaken for task validation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful execution that either demonstrates the task-shaped result-and-SQL behavior or decisively establishes the wrapper-to-grouping chain, including that the outer ordering expression is OrderBy rather than Random and that its derived grouping contribution contains Random.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect successful task-shaped ORM executions, generated SQL, and executed expression introspection. Distinguish exact failure reproduction, post-change confirmation, and a focused executable check that proves OrderBy(Random()) defeats a bare isinstance(expr, Random) guard.
metadata.oracle_test: With one parent and two related rows, aggregate ordering yields one row with count two; relationship ordering may split the groups; random ordering must yield one row with count two. RANDOM()/RAND() may remain in ORDER BY but not GROUP BY. The compiler ordering expression is OrderBy(Random()), whose grouping derivation exposes Random, so checking only the outer expression against Random is ineffective.

scale.1: No successful task-causal execution; only navigation, unsupported claims, unrelated commands, or repeated setup failures.
scale.2: Some relevant code or classes are identified, but execution is generic, failed, or misinterpreted and does not establish how Random reaches GROUP BY.
scale.3: A successful focused execution establishes one causal fact, such as Random.get_group_by_cols() returning Random or an aggregate query exhibiting suspicious behavior, but does not connect the ordering wrapper, grouping contribution, and SQL/result consequence.
scale.4: Successful execution establishes most of the causal chain or decisively falsifies a proposed expression-layer check, but lacks either the complete task-shaped result-and-SQL pair or complete post-change confirmation.
scale.5: Conclusive execution shows either the exact aggregate failure or repair with both queryset results and GROUP BY SQL, or an equally decisive wrapper-level chain showing OrderBy(Random()), its Random grouping contribution, and why a bare outer-expression check cannot remove it.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed causal proof of random-order grouping behavior

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or edits Django ORM compiler logic to prevent random ordering from contributing to aggregate GROUP BY clauses.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Targets only order-by-derived grouping in SQLCompiler.get_group_by(), excludes Random from the wrapped ordering expression's grouping sources, and preserves grouping contributions from ordinary non-reference ordering expressions while retaining aggregate and select-reference handling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for a bare isinstance(expr, Random) guard when expr is visibly OrderBy(Random()), for filtering get_group_by_cols() in a way that cannot reach the wrapped Random, or for malformed/duplicated compiler code. Cap at 3 if all non-reference ordering expressions are skipped, changing documented grouping semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible syntactically coherent diff is strongest; exact code shown in commands is next. Comments, self-authored text searches, and claims that a fix is present do not establish an applied implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistakes a bare Random for the actual compiler expression, or fixes the symptom by suppressing every ORDER BY contribution and thereby regresses legitimate grouping behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires wrapper-aware filtering of Random from the order-by expression's source expressions, or an equivalently demonstrated implementation that excludes the generated random function without dropping valid ordering columns.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible patch or exact proposed code in django/db/models/sql/compiler.py, especially treatment of expr.contains_aggregate, is_ref, expr.get_source_expressions(), and Random.
metadata.oracle_test: The order-by loop should continue to add ordinary source columns that affect grouping (such as ordering by a related field), skip select references and aggregate orderings as appropriate, and omit the Random source inside OrderBy(Random()).

scale.1: No concrete implementation boundary, or changes unrelated code.
scale.2: Attempts the compiler change but uses an ineffective bare-Random check, malformed edit, or otherwise visibly incorrect logic.
scale.3: Excludes random ordering but over-broadly drops valid ordering-derived grouping, or presents a plausible wrapper-aware approach without a coherent applied diff.
scale.4: Shows a coherent wrapper-aware compiler change that removes Random while preserving ordinary ordering sources and reference handling, with only minor uncertainty about aggregate handling or code integration.
scale.5: Shows the precise, minimal, syntactically coherent get_group_by() change: aggregate and reference cases are preserved/skipped correctly, wrapped source expressions are used, Random alone is filtered, and no unrelated compiler behavior is altered.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise compiler fix boundary for random ordering

applies_when: The task concerns an aggregate queryset whose GROUP BY is affected by random ordering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge whether the visible work establishes and preserves the task-specific invariant that random ordering may remain in ORDER BY but must not contribute RANDOM()/RAND() to GROUP BY, while ordinary order-by expressions continue contributing their required grouping columns.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible applied code checks only isinstance(ordering_wrapper, Random) when random ordering is wrapped by OrderBy, drops all order-by grouping expressions, is malformed or duplicated, or a post-change query still places RANDOM()/RAND() in GROUP BY. Failed setup attempts do not validate behavior. Temporary scripts, source-text searches, imports, and assertions that do not execute the relevant compiler path are non-evidence for a fix.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed command output and readable applied file content outrank thoughts, summaries, proposed patches, comments, and synthetic checks that only search source text. An executed task-shaped ORM query and its SQL outrank generic imports or isinstance demonstrations. When evidence conflicts, the latest visible applied code and genuine execution result control.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding code-location activity, claimed success after failed test setup, direct Random checks against the wrong expression layer, and broad removal of legitimate order-by grouping columns.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires either a successful task-shaped reproduction with both aggregate behavior and SQL-level causal evidence, or an applied wrapper-aware change that removes Random from the derived grouping expressions while retaining non-random grouping expressions.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executed ORM results, generated SQL, expression introspection, and the exact applied compiler edit. Credit exact reproduction showing one aggregated row for aggregate ordering, split groups for relationship ordering, and erroneous split groups or RANDOM()/RAND() in GROUP BY for random ordering. For edits, inspect whether the code removes the Random grouping contribution through the actual OrderBy expression shape rather than merely checking the outer wrapper.
metadata.oracle_test: For an entity with two related rows, annotate Count(related), then values(id, count): ordering by the count yields one row with count two; ordering by the related field may split grouping; ordering randomly must still yield one row with count two. Its SQL may contain RANDOM()/RAND() in ORDER BY but not in GROUP BY. Internally, random ordering is represented through an ordering wrapper whose grouping columns include a Random expression.

scale.1: No task-causal evidence: only repository navigation, repeated setup failures, unsupported claims, or an applied change that is malformed or clearly violates the grouping invariant.
scale.2: The relevant compiler path and Random involvement are identified, but evidence remains conceptual or generic; alternatively, an applied attempt is contradicted by the visible expression shape or cannot affect the Random grouping contribution.
scale.3: Meaningful executable diagnosis is present, such as inspecting Random or OrderBy grouping behavior or partially reproducing the aggregate query, but the full result-and-SQL causal chain is not established and no clearly correct applied repair is shown.
scale.4: A wrapper-aware, narrowly scoped repair is visibly applied and preserves ordinary order-by grouping contributions, but relevant post-change behavior is not executed; or the exact behavioral failure is reproduced without complete SQL-level confirmation.
scale.5: Conclusive visible evidence establishes the task-specific cause through an exact successful reproduction with both result and GROUP BY SQL evidence, or shows a wrapper-aware applied repair followed by relevant execution confirming that random ordering remains while Random is excluded from GROUP BY, with no contradictory applied code.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal validation of the random-order aggregation repair

applies_when: The trajectory executes or applies task-specific work concerning random ordering contributing to an aggregate queryset's GROUP BY clause.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the strongest visibly established causal milestone: reproducing the aggregate failure, proving how OrderBy-wrapped Random contributes a volatile grouping key, applying a narrow source-aware repair, or confirming the repaired query behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A failed setup is non-evidence rather than a behavioral failure. A visible bare isinstance(expr, Random) guard against an OrderBy(Random()) expression, malformed code, or code that skips every mixed ordering source cannot count as a repair. A post-change query still containing RANDOM()/RAND() in GROUP BY caps repair credit at 2, but it does not erase independently successful failure reproduction or wrapper diagnosis. Claims of success never override execution.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful task-shaped execution controls behavioral claims. Readable post-edit diff or resulting compiler code controls implementation claims. Executed OrderBy(Random()) and get_group_by_cols() inspection outranks unsupported explanation. Proposed commands, update messages, source searches, imports, and bare isinstance(Random(), Random) checks do not establish an applied repair or query behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equating one synthetic Random fact with a task-shaped reproduction, treating a failed repair as successful, missing the OrderBy wrapper, or discarding valid non-random ordering sources, while preserving credit for conclusive diagnostic execution that correctly falsifies an attempted repair.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires at least one of: an exact successful failure reproduction with both duplicated counts and random GROUP BY SQL; an executed complete wrapper-to-grouping trace; or readable applied code that reaches Random beneath the ordering wrapper while retaining non-random grouping sources. Score 5 requires two causally connected milestones, including either wrapper proof paired with exact reproduction or an applied narrow repair paired with successful post-change behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect successful ORM results and SQL, executed ordering-expression introspection, and readable resulting compiler code. Distinguish an isolated Random fact from the exact aggregate failure, a complete OrderBy(Random()) grouping trace, an applied source-aware repair, and successful post-change confirmation.
metadata.oracle_test: For one parent with two related rows, annotate Count(related) and project id plus count: random ordering must retain one row with count two. RANDOM(), RAND(), or the backend equivalent may remain in ORDER BY but not GROUP BY. The compiler ordering expression is OrderBy(Random()), and its grouping derivation exposes Random; ordinary ordering sources such as a related-field column must remain eligible to affect grouping.

scale.1: No successful task-causal execution and no coherent applied repair; evidence is limited to navigation, unsupported claims, repeated setup failures, or malformed work.
scale.2: Establishes only a conceptual or isolated fact, or applies an ineffective outer-OrderBy Random check; no exact aggregate failure, complete wrapper chain, or source-aware applied repair is established.
scale.3: Successfully establishes exactly one partial milestone, such as suspicious aggregate behavior, Random grouping behavior, or a coherent but unexecuted source-aware repair with unresolved integration or over-broad mixed-expression handling.
scale.4: Establishes exactly one decisive milestone: the exact duplicated-count failure with random GROUP BY SQL, a complete executed OrderBy(Random()) to Random grouping-contribution trace, or readable applied code that narrowly removes Random while preserving non-random ordering sources; no second connected decisive milestone is established.
scale.5: Establishes at least two connected decisive milestones: exact failure reproduction plus complete wrapper-level causal proof, or a readable narrow applied repair plus successful post-change results and SQL showing random ordering retained only in ORDER BY.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal progress from reproduction to verified random-grouping repair

applies_when: A production edit to SQLite DatabaseWrapper.check_constraints() is visibly applied
SQLite's supported PRAGMA foreign-key-check branch is the task-triggered path
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether the applied implementation produces valid quoted identifiers for both table-specific PRAGMA statements on the supported SQLite constraint-check path, with backend-aware quoting preferred over manually embedded delimiters.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assign 1 when malformed Python or an unavailable receiver such as self.connection.ops prevents the supported path from reaching SQL. Assign at most 2 when Python executes but either required PRAGMA remains raw or composes a malformed identifier. SQL in a feature-disabled fallback branch does not cap credit unless visible conditions select it.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible source or unified diff controls. Generated SQL or direct execution from that same state may confirm composition. A standalone SQLite query cannot override an unavailable receiver or malformed applied source.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding quote_name text attached to the wrong object, while also preventing inactive fallback rewrites or unrelated test-harness failures from obscuring a correct supported-path implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visibly applied, executable repair that makes both table-specific PRAGMAs valid for a keyword identifier. Credit of 5 requires use of DatabaseWrapper's available backend operation, self.ops.quote_name(), with no concrete contradiction on the supported path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest applied expressions constructing PRAGMA foreign_key_check(table) and PRAGMA foreign_key_list(table), including the quote_name receiver and the resulting identifier placement. Inspect other edited source for definite syntax failures, but do not infer failure from an unselected compatibility branch.
metadata.non_evidence: Proposed but unapplied edits, comments, successful raw sqlite3 demonstrations detached from the applied wrapper code, test setup failures unrelated to SQL construction, and conditional fallback SQL not reachable in the visible task environment.
metadata.oracle_test: In DatabaseWrapper.check_constraints(), table_name='order' must compose as valid identifier-bearing SQL for both PRAGMA foreign_key_check("order") and PRAGMA foreign_key_list("order"); DatabaseWrapper exposes the quoting operation as self.ops.

scale.1: The latest applied supported path has malformed Python, uses an unavailable quoting receiver, or otherwise fails before SQL construction.
scale.2: The applied Python executes, but one or both required table-specific PRAGMAs remain unquoted or visibly compose invalid identifier SQL.
scale.3: No relevant production edit is visibly applied, or the visible state is too incomplete to determine both PRAGMA constructions.
scale.4: Both required PRAGMAs visibly compose valid quoted keyword identifiers, but the implementation manually embeds SQLite delimiters rather than using the backend operation.
scale.5: Both required PRAGMAs use self.ops.quote_name(table_name) and the supported task path has no concrete visible syntax, receiver, or SQL-composition contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete executable quoting on the supported SQLite PRAGMA path

applies_when: A production edit affecting SQLite DatabaseWrapper.check_constraints() is visibly applied
The visible prefix permits determining whether production SQL construction beyond the two task-triggered PRAGMAs was changed
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether the applied repair is confined to quoting the table-name arguments of the two task-triggered SQLite PRAGMAs, or instead introduces unnecessary production SQL rewrites and their associated semantic risk.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assign 1 if any changed production statement has malformed Python, uses an unavailable receiver, or visibly composes malformed SQL. Assign at most 2 when collateral edits visibly double-delimit an identifier or alter unrelated production behavior without evidence establishing the prerequisite or necessity. Do not penalize test-only setup or unapplied proposals.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source, unified diff, or successfully applied edit followed by source inspection controls. A repository summary reporting no changed files does not override later visible applied source. Direct SQL execution may confirm a changed expression but cannot establish that unshown collateral edits are absent.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating broad speculative SQL rewrites as equivalent to a precise repair merely because both required PRAGMAs contain quote_name.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit of 5 requires both required PRAGMAs to use the available self.ops.quote_name(table_name) operation and requires the production behavior change to be limited to those two identifier substitutions. Any additional production SQL-construction change precludes 5.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the complete visible production diff, not merely occurrences of quote_name. Determine whether the implementation changes only PRAGMA foreign_key_check(table) and PRAGMA foreign_key_list(table), or also rewrites SELECT statements, compatibility branches, column quoting, unrelated backend operations, or other production behavior.
metadata.non_evidence: Unapplied plans, comments about possible additional quoting, standalone sqlite3 demonstrations, temporary test scripts, dependency failures, and edits outside production source that do not alter the repair's scope.
metadata.oracle_test: The minimal task-causal patch replaces the raw table_name interpolation in PRAGMA foreign_key_check(%s) and PRAGMA foreign_key_list(%s) with self.ops.quote_name(table_name). The reported loaddata parse failure does not require rewriting later SELECT diagnostics, feature-disabled fallback SQL, or unrelated backend operations.

scale.1: The applied production state contains a definite syntax error, unavailable quoting receiver, or malformed changed SQL expression.
scale.2: The two PRAGMAs may be addressed, but collateral production edits visibly double-delimit identifiers or alter unrelated SQL behavior without an established prerequisite; no level-1 failure is shown.
scale.3: No production repair is visibly applied, the repair is only proposed, or the visible state is too incomplete to determine whether the change is contained.
scale.4: Both PRAGMAs have an executable quoted-table repair, but other production SQL construction or compatibility behavior is also changed; those additional edits have no concrete visible defect.
scale.5: The executable production repair uses self.ops.quote_name(table_name) for both required PRAGMAs and is otherwise confined to those two task-causal identifier substitutions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Contain the repair to the task-triggered PRAGMA identifier defect

applies_when: The task concerns MiddlewareNotUsed during construction of a mixed synchronous/asynchronous middleware chain.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards an applied implementation that treats handler adaptation and middleware construction transactionally, so a skipped middleware leaves both the accumulated handler chain and its declared async mode unchanged while a successfully constructed middleware receives the required adapted callable.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible code resets to the original base get_response and thereby discards previously loaded middleware, changes handler_is_async to the skipped middleware's mode, passes an unadapted callable where adaptation is required, corrupts indentation or control flow, or leaves duplicate exception blocks. Cap at 3 if the correct approach is only proposed or simulated outside the repository.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository file contents and a visible git diff outrank narrative claims. Executed inspections of the modified block outrank pseudocode. If summaries conflict with command output, use the latest visible repository inspection or diff.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a mode flag update, a reset to the base view handler, or instantiation with the unadapted handler for preservation of the accumulated middleware chain.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires visible applied source changes. A score of 5 additionally requires that the applied control flow preserves the prior handler and handler_is_async on MiddlewareNotUsed while committing the candidate state only after successful construction.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible patch or current file contents around BaseHandler.load_middleware. Track handler and handler_is_async across adaptation, middleware construction, the MiddlewareNotUsed exception path, and successful construction.
metadata.oracle_test: For each middleware iteration, define the pre-iteration pair as (handler, handler_is_async). Construct a candidate callable adapted for that middleware. If construction raises MiddlewareNotUsed, the next iteration must observe the unchanged pre-iteration pair. If construction succeeds, the middleware must have received the correctly adapted callable and the committed pair must represent the new middleware instance and middleware_is_async.

scale.1: Visible applied code is malformed or clearly violates chain construction, such as discarding previously loaded middleware, duplicating broken control flow, or committing an incompatible handler state.
scale.2: The overwrite is discussed, but the applied remedy is causally wrong or contradicted by visible execution; examples include changing only handler_is_async, resetting to get_response, or moving adaptation so the middleware receives the wrong callable.
scale.3: The correct transactional invariant is explained or demonstrated in pseudocode, but no coherent repository change is visible; alternatively, an applied preservation change remains materially ambiguous on either the exception or success path.
scale.4: A coherent applied change preserves the prior handler state on MiddlewareNotUsed and retains normal successful-chain construction, but exact mixed-mode behavior is not yet established by strong visible evidence.
scale.5: The applied code unambiguously uses a temporary candidate or equivalent rollback so both handler and handler_is_async remain unchanged on MiddlewareNotUsed and are committed correctly after successful middleware construction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves middleware-chain state when middleware is skipped

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes Django's BaseHandler.load_middleware() handling of MiddlewareNotUsed in an ASGI middleware chain.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that adapt_method_mode() may replace the current handler before middleware construction raises MiddlewareNotUsed, so continuing leaves an adapter for a skipped middleware in the chain while handler_is_async still describes the pre-adaptation handler.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims MiddlewareNotUsed itself changes handler_is_async, occurs during request-time __call__, or that sync-only middleware is inherently unsupported by ASGI. Cap at 3 if later visible evidence disproves the stated mechanism and the trajectory does not revise it.
metadata.evidence_authority: Directly displayed source and concrete execution traces outrank paraphrases of the issue report; a trace demonstrating callable mode or awaitability outranks unsupported assumptions.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards noticing the nearby continue statement without explaining the coupled handler/handler_is_async invariant or the resulting await mismatch.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires connecting the mutation on the exception path to inconsistent handler mode state or incorrect behavior of a subsequent middleware under ASGI.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning tied to django/core/handlers/base.py: the ordering of handler adaptation, middleware factory invocation, the MiddlewareNotUsed exception path, and handler_is_async.
metadata.oracle_test: A skipped middleware must be observationally absent from chain construction: both the handler callable and its declared async-mode state presented to the next iteration must match the state before attempting that middleware.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis centered on unrelated settings, debug-toolbar behavior, or ASGI's general inability to use synchronous middleware.
scale.2: Locates load_middleware() and MiddlewareNotUsed but gives a materially incorrect or vague account of the side effect.
scale.3: Correctly states that handler is adapted before the exception and remains changed after continue, but does not trace the mode-state mismatch or effect on later middleware.
scale.4: Correctly traces the skipped iteration, unchanged handler_is_async, later adaptation decision, and resulting sync/async mismatch such as an HttpResponse being awaited.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal account in both callable and mode-state terms, grounded in displayed code or a focused trace, and accurately distinguishes construction-time skipping from request-time middleware execution.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of middleware-chain poisoning

applies_when: The attempted fix can affect async/sync middleware adaptation or the MiddlewareNotUsed exception path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards executable validation that places a constructor raising MiddlewareNotUsed next to middleware with different sync/async capabilities, exercises the resulting ASGI chain, and accurately interprets both focused regression and broader test results.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when the trajectory labels a run successful despite a visible target TypeError, unawaited coroutine, syntax error, invalid import path, or unrelated setup exception preventing the target path. Cap at 2 when tests only instantiate or load the chain without exercising the async response path. A failing valid regression does not itself reduce evidence quality if the failure is recognized and used to reject the patch.
metadata.evidence_authority: Completed command output and test-runner results outrank stated conclusions. An official repository test invocation outranks an ad hoc script for broader compatibility, while a focused executable regression outranks unrelated existing tests for reproducing this bug. Tracebacks and warnings override unsupported PASS messages.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating middleware loading, callable type printing, mocked adaptation, or a script blocked by unrelated configuration errors as proof that the reported ASGI request failure is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires an actually executed, valid test that reaches the MiddlewareNotUsed mixed-mode path. A score of 5 requires both focused task-specific coverage and a relevant repository test run with results interpreted consistently.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect test code, commands, exit status, tracebacks, warnings, and assertions. Confirm that middleware paths are importable, MiddlewareNotUsed is raised during factory construction, ASGI execution is awaited through the correct interface, and the test checks the returned response or chain behavior rather than only successful loading.
metadata.oracle_test: In ASGI mode, configure an importable middleware factory that is selected as sync-only or otherwise forces adaptation and raises MiddlewareNotUsed in __init__, alongside a subsequent usable middleware of a mode that exposes poisoning. Execute the resulting request path with proper awaiting and verify that the response is an HttpResponse rather than producing an await/type mismatch. Relevant existing middleware tests should also remain green.

scale.1: Visible validation is invalid or its claimed conclusion directly contradicts the observed traceback, warning, syntax failure, import failure, or target TypeError.
scale.2: Only superficial or blocked checks are run, such as source inspection, chain loading, wrong-interface calls, or tests that never reach the mixed-mode MiddlewareNotUsed path.
scale.3: A valid component-level reproduction or instrumentation reaches relevant adaptation behavior and its result is interpreted accurately, but the resulting ASGI request path is not exercised end to end.
scale.4: A valid focused regression executes the mixed-mode MiddlewareNotUsed ASGI path and accurately establishes whether the candidate passes or fails, but no relevant broader repository test run is completed.
scale.5: A valid focused ASGI regression and relevant repository tests are both executed, with assertions covering response awaitability or type and all visible results interpreted without contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validates the skipped-middleware ASGI regression with authoritative evidence

applies_when: A source change or concrete implementation plan modifies BaseHandler.load_middleware() around handler adaptation and MiddlewareNotUsed.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Makes each middleware-loading iteration transactional: the middleware factory receives the correctly adapted downstream handler, but if construction raises MiddlewareNotUsed, neither that adapted callable nor a corresponding mode change is committed to the chain.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the implementation instantiates middleware with the unadapted handler and only adapts afterward, resets to the base get_response and discards already loaded inner middleware, updates handler_is_async to the skipped middleware's mode, or visibly breaks syntax/control flow. Cap at 3 if temporary state is restored incompletely or successful middleware no longer receives normal conversion/update behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: A syntactically coherent displayed diff and its control flow outrank prose claims. Repository tests or focused runtime evidence outrank comments saying the fix works.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistakes moving adapt_method_mode() after middleware construction for a fix, even though middleware factories must be constructed with a callable already adapted to their declared mode.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires preserving both requirements: middleware(handler) receives the adaptation required by middleware_is_async, and a skipped middleware leaves the prior handler state intact.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible patch or exact code plan preserving the pre-iteration handler on MiddlewareNotUsed while retaining normal adaptation, middleware hooks, exception conversion, and handler_is_async updates for successfully constructed middleware.
metadata.oracle_test: Equivalent valid forms include saving and restoring the current handler on MiddlewareNotUsed, or computing an adapted temporary handler and committing it only after successful factory construction; existing inner middleware must remain in the downstream chain.

scale.1: No implementation boundary is identified, or the visible change is unrelated to middleware loading.
scale.2: A concrete change is attempted but violates the transactional invariant, damages the chain, or is visibly malformed.
scale.3: The change preserves the prior handler on the exception path but leaves a significant ambiguity or defect in factory adaptation, successful-path updates, or surrounding control flow.
scale.4: A coherent minimal change preserves the old handler on MiddlewareNotUsed and keeps the successful middleware path semantically intact.
scale.5: A precise, minimal, syntactically coherent implementation makes adaptation provisional until successful construction, preserves all previously loaded inner middleware, and leaves handler_is_async and hook registration behavior correct on both paths.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Transactional implementation of skipped middleware loading

applies_when: The trajectory executes or adds checks intended to validate MiddlewareNotUsed behavior in a mixed sync/async middleware chain.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards valid executable evidence that first reaches construction-time MiddlewareNotUsed with mixed middleware modes, then verifies preservation of the accumulated handler state, and ultimately exercises an awaited ASGI response path and relevant repository tests.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if success is claimed despite a visible syntax error, import failure, invalid settings setup, wrong interface call, unawaited coroutine, target TypeError, or failed assertion. Cap at 2 if execution proves only that load_middleware() returns or that a chain object is callable. Cap at 3 if a valid state probe never executes the resulting ASGI response. A recognized failing regression remains valid evidence of the candidate's failure and is not itself a false-success contradiction.
metadata.evidence_authority: Completed command output outranks PASS text and narrative conclusions. A focused executable target-path check outranks unrelated passing tests for this defect. Official repository test results establish broader compatibility but do not by themselves prove the mixed-mode skip regression. Tracebacks, warnings, and failed assertions override claimed success.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating successful middleware loading, callable-type printing, mocked adaptation that never constructs the target chain, a blocked script, or unrelated green tests as proof that the ASGI request regression is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires execution that actually reaches a middleware factory raising MiddlewareNotUsed under a mode configuration capable of adaptation. A score above 3 requires an awaited request or equivalent execution through the final ASGI middleware chain. A score of 5 requires both focused target-path evidence and a relevant repository test run.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect test code, importability, middleware capability declarations, where MiddlewareNotUsed is raised, commands, exit status, tracebacks, warnings, assertions, and whether execution stops at loading, probes the construction transition, or awaits the actual ASGI response path.
metadata.oracle_test: Use importable middleware factories with explicit sync_capable and async_capable declarations. One factory must raise MiddlewareNotUsed during construction after its downstream callable would require adaptation; neighboring middleware must expose an incorrect retained adapter. At component depth, assert that the next iteration observes the same pre-skip handler and mode. At request depth, await the ASGI chain and assert an HttpResponse is produced without an await/type mismatch.

scale.1: The attempted validation is invalid or its claimed conclusion contradicts visible errors, warnings, failed assertions, or the target await/type failure.
scale.2: Executable checks are absent, blocked, or limited to syntax, source inspection, middleware loading, chain existence, or another path that never reaches a valid mixed-mode MiddlewareNotUsed construction.
scale.3: A valid executable component probe reaches construction-time MiddlewareNotUsed with relevant mode adaptation and accurately inspects or asserts the handler transition, but it does not execute the final awaited ASGI response path.
scale.4: A valid focused regression awaits the resulting ASGI request or equivalent final chain, checks response type or awaitability, and interprets the result accurately, but no relevant broader repository test run is completed.
scale.5: Both a valid focused awaited ASGI regression and relevant repository tests complete, with task-causal assertions and all visible results interpreted consistently.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validates the skipped-middleware transition at increasing execution depth

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why a local foreign-key attname remains blank after the cached related object's target value changes.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly traces assignment of the related object's initial blank target value into the local foreign-key attname, recognizes that the cached object later holds a nonempty target value, and identifies save preparation's `is None` guard as the reason the blank local value is not resynchronized.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory applies or continues to endorse a repair in relation assignment, `_save_parents()`, SQL generation, or constraint handling after evidence establishes that the cached related object has the updated value and save preparation owns resynchronization. Cap at 4 for unconditional mismatch-based resynchronization because it can overwrite a deliberate nonempty local value.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source excerpts and coherent value tracing are authoritative whether established statically or by execution. Runtime output strengthens but is not required for the causal diagnosis. An applied wrong-layer change is stronger contradictory evidence than an unsuccessful attempt to run a reproduction.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing the expected assignment-time snapshot with the save-time defect, penalizing correct source analysis merely because an ad hoc execution failed to initialize, or treating an overbroad mismatch rewrite as equivalent to an empty-value-bounded repair.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visibly identifying the `is None` guard in `_prepare_related_fields_for_save()` and explaining why it excludes a blank string. Credit at 5 requires a save-preparation correction bounded to the local field's defined empty values and visible focused validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the trajectory's account of the assignment-time snapshot, the cached related object's later target value, and the condition in `Model._prepare_related_fields_for_save()` that controls resynchronization.
metadata.oracle_test: After assignment, the local attname may contain `''`; after the cached related object's target becomes `'foo'`, save preparation must recognize the local value as field-defined empty and copy `'foo'`, while a deliberate nonempty local value is not classified as empty.

scale.1: No coherent account of the stale local foreign-key value, or an account contradicted by visible source or value evidence.
scale.2: Observes some relevant state but endorses an incorrect causal layer or applies a wrong-layer repair, without establishing save preparation as the resynchronization point.
scale.3: Correctly traces the complete stale-state transition from blank assignment-time snapshot to a nonempty cached target value, but does not identify the precise `is None` save-preparation guard.
scale.4: Identifies the `is None` guard and explains why it misses the blank string, but does not both apply and validate a field-empty-value-bounded correction; an unconditional mismatch rewrite cannot exceed this level.
scale.5: Identifies the complete causal chain, applies resynchronization in save preparation using the local field's defined empty values, and visibly validates the delayed-target sequence without overwriting an already nonempty local value.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Source-grounded diagnosis and bounded save-time repair of stale foreign-key state

applies_when: A diagnosis, implementation, or concrete patch could alter synchronization or cache behavior for ForeignKey or OneToOneField relations outside the reported delayed character-key sequence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Demonstrates that the repair is limited to field-defined empty local values and preserves preinitialized targets, deliberate nonempty local values, unsaved-object protection, and target-field resolution.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the final implementation changes descriptor assignment globally, assumes every target is the related primary key, or overwrites every nonmatching local value without acknowledging that compatibility risk. Cap at 3 when a broad mismatch implementation passes only the reported example, or when the condition hard-codes '' rather than using field semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible predicate determines the semantic boundary. Observed focused assertions outrank compatibility claims, while source-grounded analysis of adjacent unsaved-object and cache logic outranks generic assurances. field.empty_values is authoritative over hard-coded string checks; target_field is authoritative over assumptions that every relation uses obj.pk.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding compatibility credit by default, treating one successful reproduction as regression safety, or overlooking that unconditional mismatch synchronization changes which side of an inconsistent cached relation is authoritative.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires examining the actual synchronization condition and naming a concrete unaffected path. Credit above 3 requires a field-empty-value boundary plus explicit protection of deliberate nonempty local state. Credit at 5 requires an applied narrow condition and observed compatibility checks.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact final synchronization predicate and visible reasoning or tests for preinitialized target values, nonempty local mismatches, unsaved related objects, nullable clearing, and foreign keys using a non-primary target field.
metadata.oracle_test: A preinitialized related key continues to save unchanged; a deliberate nonempty local foreign-key value is not replaced merely because a cached object differs; a related object without a usable key remains rejected; and alternate target fields continue to use their configured target value.

scale.1: No visible compatibility consideration, condition inspection, or unaffected-path evidence.
scale.2: Mentions compatibility only generally, or visibly uses a descriptor rewrite, primary-key-only assumption, or unconditional mismatch rule without examining its effect on existing relation semantics.
scale.3: Examines at least one concrete unaffected path or observes the reported case under a broader repair, but still uses a hard-coded blank check, lacks protection for deliberate nonempty local state, or provides no field-semantic boundary.
scale.4: Uses or precisely specifies field-defined empty-value synchronization and explains preservation of deliberate nonempty local state plus at least one additional path such as preinitialized keys, unsaved-object rejection, nullable handling, or alternate targets, but lacks observed compatibility tests.
scale.5: Visibly applies the field-empty-value-bounded condition and observes focused checks for the preinitialized-key path and at least one additional safeguard, with adjacent unsaved-object and cache-consistency behavior left intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Demonstrated compatibility boundary for foreign-key resynchronization

applies_when: The proposed diagnosis or change could affect existing ForeignKey or OneToOne synchronization and relation-cache behavior beyond the empty character-primary-key case.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves established behavior for relations whose local FK is already nonempty, preinitialized primary keys, nullable relations, unsaved-object rejection, and foreign keys targeting non-primary fields by limiting synchronization to field-defined empty values.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the implementation synchronizes whenever `obj.pk != local_fk`, changes all descriptor assignments, or assumes every relation targets the related model's primary key; cap at 3 if compatibility is asserted without examining the actual condition.
metadata.evidence_authority: The semantics of the final visible condition and focused compatibility tests outrank broad assurances; `field.empty_values` is authoritative over hard-coded string checks or unconditional mismatch synchronization.
metadata.failure_mode: Passing the reported example by introducing a broader relation-authority rule that silently overwrites intentional scalar FK state or mishandles `to_field` relations.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicit protection of nonempty mismatch/cache behavior and at least one unaffected path such as a PK supplied before assignment, `None`, or `to_field`.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, source boundary, or tests showing the change does not replace arbitrary nonempty local values and does not alter descriptor assignment or target-field resolution.
metadata.oracle_test: Only empty local values are repaired. A relation assigned with `Product(sku='foo')` continues to save normally; unsaved related objects with no usable PK remain prohibited; nonempty mismatches retain existing cache-invalidating behavior.

scale.1: No compatibility consideration, or visible changes indiscriminately alter relation behavior.
scale.2: Uses a broad mismatch or descriptor rewrite that risks nonempty FK, cache, or `to_field` semantics.
scale.3: Keeps the change relatively local but checks only `None`/`''` ad hoc or provides no concrete analysis of unaffected paths.
scale.4: Uses field empty-value semantics and explicitly explains preservation of nonempty mismatch and at least one unaffected relation path.
scale.5: Combines the narrow semantic condition with visible focused evidence covering the working preinitialized-PK path and relevant safeguards such as unsaved-object rejection, nullable handling, or alternate target behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility preservation for nonempty relations and alternate targets

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why a cached related object whose primary key changes after assignment leaves the owning model's foreign-key attname stale.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that relation assignment initially copies the related target value into the local `*_id` attribute, a blank `CharField` primary key yields `''`, and the decisive defect is the save-preparation logic only resynchronizing when that local value is `None`.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory continues to locate the fix primarily in `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.__set__()`, `_save_parents()`, SQL preparation, or database constraint handling after visible evidence shows the save-preparation guard.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source excerpts and runtime values from the task sequence outrank speculative explanations; evidence from save preparation outranks assignment-only hypotheses once the cached object is shown to hold the new primary key.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the expected assignment-time snapshot or the deferred constraint failure for the root defect, and consequently editing the wrong ORM layer.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires connecting the stale empty string to the `is None` guard in `_prepare_related_fields_for_save()`, not merely observing descriptor assignment.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tracing of `order.product_id`, the cached `order.product`, and `Model._prepare_related_fields_for_save()` before persistence.
metadata.oracle_test: Immediately after assignment the local FK may be `''`; after setting and saving the related `Product`, its cached `sku`/`pk` is `'foo'`; saving `Order` must synchronize the empty local FK from that cached object.

scale.1: No relevant causal account, or an account contradicted by visible source/runtime evidence.
scale.2: Recognizes a stale foreign-key value but attributes it only to generic descriptor, database, or primary-key behavior without locating the save-time guard.
scale.3: Traces assignment of `''` and later mutation of the cached related object's primary key, but does not identify the precise defective condition in save preparation.
scale.4: Locates `_prepare_related_fields_for_save()` and explains that its `is None` condition misses the empty-string local FK, with only minor uncertainty about the intended empty-value abstraction.
scale.5: Precisely explains the complete causal chain and why save preparation must treat the local field's defined empty values, including `''`, like `None` while retaining the cached related object.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of stale foreign-key attname during save preparation

applies_when: The task concerns a local ForeignKey or OneToOneField value becoming stale after the cached related object's non-auto primary key or target-field value changes before the owning object is saved.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge whether the trajectory correctly establishes and addresses the save-time failure to synchronize the owning model's stored foreign-key attribute with the cached related object's now-valid target value.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory applies an assignment-time workaround that skips or rewrites empty keys without repairing save-time synchronization, confuses ordinary ForeignKey handling with multi-table inheritance, or visibly breaks clearing a relation, nullable behavior, custom to_field behavior, or unsaved-related-object safeguards. Cap at 3 if the correct change is merely proposed or applied without observed behavioral verification.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest direct repository observations, working-tree code, and executed test output outrank summaries and narrated claims. A passing focused reproduction is authoritative only for the behavior it actually asserts; repository tests outrank ad hoc print-based checks for regression safety. Proposed commands, intended edits, and unexecuted tests are not applied evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents over-credit for merely rediscovering that descriptor assignment copied an empty string, for treating the database constraint failure as the root cause, or for changing descriptor assignment even though the required causal correction is re-evaluating the cached relation during owner save preparation.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a visible applied change at the save-preparation path and an observed focused test showing that an initially empty non-auto related key is later copied into the owner's foreign-key attribute before persistence. Score 5 additionally requires durable regression coverage and an observed relevant suite pass.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect direct traces of the cached related object, the owner's local foreign-key attname, ForwardManyToOneDescriptor assignment, and Model._prepare_related_fields_for_save(). Credit a repair only when it refreshes the local value from the cached related object when the two values differ, while preserving unsaved-related-object protection and relation-cache behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: For an owner assigned a cached related instance before a non-auto CharField primary key is populated, then given a key and saved, owner.save() must synchronize the local foreign-key attname to that key. Assignment with the key already populated must remain correct, and genuinely unsaved related objects without a usable key must retain Django's data-loss protection.
metadata.stage: early diagnosis through initial implementation validation

scale.1: No reliable task-causal progress: setup or exploration never establishes the stale local-versus-related value, or the trajectory commits to a visibly incorrect locus or behavior contradicted by the inspected code or tests.
scale.2: Establishes the reproduction or correctly traces assignment-time copying and the stale cached relation, but does not identify the save-preparation mismatch guard as the required repair; no correct applied fix is visible.
scale.3: Correctly identifies that save preparation must refresh the owner's foreign-key attname whenever it differs from the cached related object's current target value, and gives a concrete compatible change, but the change is only proposed or lacks observed focused verification.
scale.4: Applies the correct save-time mismatch-based synchronization and observes a focused reproduction pass, while preserving the existing unsaved-object guard; durable regression coverage or broader relevant validation is still absent or incomplete.
scale.5: Applies the correct save-time synchronization, adds durable regression tests covering the delayed non-auto key case and the already-populated-key case, checks relevant edge behavior such as clearing or custom target fields where applicable, and observes the focused and relevant existing test suites pass.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Save-time foreign-key resynchronization diagnosis and repair

applies_when: A trajectory investigates or changes owner-save handling after a cached related object's configured target value changes from initially empty to usable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures progress from establishing the stale local foreign-key state through applying and validating a save-preparation correction that refreshes only field-defined empty local values from the cached related object's configured target field.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final endorsed or applied repair remains in descriptor assignment, _save_parents(), SQL generation, or constraint handling after the cached object is shown to contain the usable target value. Cap at 4 if the applied predicate hard-codes only the reported empty string or synchronizes every mismatch. Cap at 3 when a correct edit is only proposed or when no executed focused check verifies the applied edit.
metadata.evidence_authority: Later displayed source or a repository diff establishes applied code; narrated edits and unexecuted commands establish only proposals. Direct source excerpts and coherent value traces can establish diagnosis without a successful reproduction. Executed output establishes only the asserted behavior, and repository tests outrank ad hoc scripts for regression confidence. The relation's target_field and the local field's empty_values define the relevant semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating assignment-time copying as the repair point, confusing a proposed command with an applied edit, accepting a passing reproduction that never asserts the persisted foreign key, or making the cached object authoritative over every deliberate nonempty local mismatch.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a complete stale-state trace and localization to save preparation. Credit above 3 requires a visibly applied save-preparation edit. Credit at 5 requires field-defined empty-value gating plus observed checks for both delayed-target synchronization and preservation of a preexisting nonempty local value.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible local attname value at assignment and owner save, the cached related object's configured target value, the guard in Model._prepare_related_fields_for_save(), the final applied predicate, and the exact assertions exercised by executed checks.
metadata.oracle_test: After relation assignment copies an initially empty configured target into the owner's local attname, changing and saving the cached related object must cause owner save preparation to copy its now-usable target value when the local field classifies the current local value as empty. An already nonempty local value must remain outside that repair boundary, and target_field rather than an assumed primary-key attribute supplies the copied value.
metadata.stage: causal localization through focused implementation validation

scale.1: No reliable stale local-versus-cached state is established, or the visible account is contradicted by source or runtime evidence.
scale.2: Establishes only a reproduction or partial stale-state observation, or ends with a wrong-layer diagnosis or repair; save preparation is not coherently established as the resynchronization point.
scale.3: Completely traces assignment of an initially empty target, later mutation of the cached target, and the still-stale local attname, and identifies the save-preparation empty-value guard or specifies the correct correction, but no applied and focused-verified edit is visible.
scale.4: Visibly applies a save-preparation correction and observes the delayed-target case succeed, but the predicate is hard-coded or mismatch-wide, or focused evidence does not show preservation of an already nonempty local value.
scale.5: Visibly applies synchronization gated by the local field's defined empty values, reads the cached object's configured target field, and observes focused checks proving delayed-target synchronization and preservation of nonempty local state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied and verified empty-value resynchronization during owner save preparation

applies_when: The visible trajectory encounters a failed semantic test, syntax error, API mismatch, backend-capability mismatch, or other evidence contradicting its current approach.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Responds to contradictory evidence by identifying its cause, reverting or revising the invalid approach, and preserving only conclusions supported by subsequent source or runtime evidence.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the trajectory calls a fix successful after a visible failing semantic test or leaves known malformed code in place; cap at 2 if it notices the contradiction but continues building on the disproven approach.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed exceptions, assertion results, git diff/source state, and backend feature flags override earlier claims that a fix is correct; a clean rollback outranks continuing from corrupted code.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating setup failures as product failures, ignoring a failing post-fix reproduction, or claiming correctness immediately after syntactic/API breakage.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires the contradiction to change the implementation hypothesis or test setup, not merely trigger unrelated exploration.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible acknowledgement of failures such as unchanged raw IDs, malformed patches, expression.output_field errors, wrong connection objects, unsupported bulk-return behavior, or broken test setup, followed by targeted correction or rollback.
metadata.oracle_test: After evidence disproves direct Field use with backend converters, an invalid connection lookup, or an unexercised RETURNING path, the trajectory revises toward valid column-expression/compiler semantics or a correctly configured test and rechecks the affected behavior.

scale.1: Ignores or misrepresents decisive contradictory evidence and continues with a known-broken conclusion.
scale.2: Acknowledges the contradiction but neither isolates its cause nor restores a sound code/test state.
scale.3: Correctly identifies the immediate cause and rolls back or proposes a targeted correction, but does not re-establish semantic evidence.
scale.4: Revises the hypothesis or implementation in direct response, restores coherent code/test setup, and obtains relevant follow-up evidence.
scale.5: Level 4 plus uses the contradiction to uncover a deeper task-specific requirement—such as expression compatibility, converter ordering, complete return-branch coverage, or backend feature gating—and validates the revised approach.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from contradictory runtime and API evidence

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes values returned by model inserts or bulk inserts for fields with database converters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that INSERT-returned values are raw cursor values assigned to model attributes without the normal database-converter pipeline, and traces both ordinary save/create and supported bulk_create behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory attributes conversion to model descriptors, to_python(), get_prep_value(), or ordinary attribute access despite visible source showing SELECT conversion in the SQL compiler; cap at 3 if it diagnoses only one affected insert pathway.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed source inspection and reproducible runtime observations outrank unsupported narrative; compiler and call-site code outrank guesses based only on backend operation names.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking direct setattr() as the root implementation boundary rather than the downstream symptom of unconverted INSERT result rows.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires recognizing that create/save and bulk_create share INSERT-returned rows and that conversion must occur before those values are assigned to instances.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tracing from Model.save()/QuerySet.bulk_create() through _insert() and SQLInsertCompiler.execute_sql(), contrasted with SQLCompiler.get_converters()/apply_converters() on SELECT results.
metadata.oracle_test: A BigAutoField subclass whose from_db_value() wraps non-None values yields the wrapper after a normal SELECT but a raw integer immediately after create() and, on capable backends, bulk_create().

scale.1: No task-specific causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by the inspected insert/result code.
scale.2: Recognizes that returned insert values are raw or directly assigned, but does not connect this to Django's converter pipeline or follows only an incidental call site.
scale.3: Correctly contrasts INSERT return handling with SELECT converter handling and explains one affected creation path.
scale.4: Correctly traces both create/save and bulk_create to unconverted SQLInsertCompiler result rows, with relevant source evidence.
scale.5: Provides the complete trace in level 4 plus decisive runtime evidence showing raw-on-insert versus converted-on-SELECT behavior and correctly distinguishes field preparation from database-result conversion.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of the insert-return conversion gap

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates why a database-generated value returned by an INSERT has different Python semantics from the same value loaded by a SELECT.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Establishes, with visible source or runtime evidence, that INSERT-returned cursor rows bypass the normal database-converter pipeline before save/create or bulk_create assigns them, and localizes the missing step to the shared insert compiler result boundary.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when the asserted cause is directly disproved and not revised. Cap at 2 when the trajectory continues to attribute result conversion to descriptors, to_python(), get_prep_value(), or ordinary setattr() after inspecting the SELECT compiler pipeline. Cap at 3 when it establishes only a caller assignment symptom without localizing the shared upstream boundary.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful or failing runtime observations and exact inspected source control the score. A type comparison or converter-call observation outranks a hypothetical example. Compiler conversion contracts outrank assumptions about descriptors, to_python(), preparation hooks, or backend method names.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking repository browsing volume for causal evidence, treating assignment as the root boundary, requiring unsupported bulk-return behavior from the active backend, or crediting a claimed reproduction whose output does not exercise INSERT RETURNING.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicit evidence that the missing operation belongs between fetching INSERT-returned rows and caller assignment, rather than at attribute access or field preparation. Credit of 5 requires mutually supporting source and runtime evidence and capability-aware treatment of ordinary and bulk insert paths.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect concrete source reads and command output connecting SQLInsertCompiler returned rows, SQLCompiler.get_converters()/apply_converters(), and downstream assignment. Distinguish a direct setattr() symptom from the upstream absence of conversion, and distinguish executed observations from unsupported summaries.
metadata.oracle_test: A field whose from_db_value() wraps non-None values receives a raw value immediately from an INSERT-returning path but a wrapped value after SELECT; source inspection shows SELECT rows use backend-plus-field converters while SQLInsertCompiler returns unconverted rows that are subsequently assigned by save/create or supported bulk_create.

scale.1: The work provides no relevant causal evidence or maintains a materially false explanation despite decisive contrary evidence.
scale.2: The symptom or a direct assignment site is identified, but the explanation remains speculative or invokes the wrong conversion mechanism.
scale.3: Visible source or runtime evidence correctly establishes either the INSERT-versus-SELECT conversion difference or the missing compiler conversion step, but not the complete fetch-to-convert-to-assignment boundary.
scale.4: Concrete evidence localizes the gap between SQLInsertCompiler's raw returned rows and downstream assignment and relates it correctly to SQLCompiler's converter pipeline; either runtime confirmation or supported-path coverage remains incomplete.
scale.5: Source tracing and executed runtime evidence jointly establish the raw INSERT result, the absent ordered converter step, and downstream assignment for ordinary creation and capability-supported bulk creation, with no unresolved contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-backed localization of the INSERT conversion gap

applies_when: The visible trajectory proposes or applies a code change intended to convert values returned by INSERT operations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements an executable, centralized conversion step for rows returned by SQLInsertCompiler, using expression-compatible returning columns and Django's ordered backend-plus-field converter machinery before callers assign values to model instances.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if known malformed code remains in the visible repository state. Cap at 2 if execution shows a wrong connection object, a bare Field passed where expression.output_field is required, unchanged raw INSERT values, or another semantic failure that has not been corrected and rechecked. Cap at 3 for assignment-site conversion, manual from_db_value-only loops, duplicated caller logic, or a compiler patch that leaves a visibly applicable return branch raw.
metadata.evidence_authority: A syntactically valid applied diff and executed post-change behavior outrank prose or an unexecuted patch sketch. Inspected SQLCompiler and backend API contracts outrank guessed signatures. A visible exception, malformed diff, unchanged raw value, or failing focused test overrides a claim that the patch works.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding an attractive proposal as though it were applied, treating direct setattr() as the proper conversion boundary, manually invoking only field converters, passing Field objects to backend APIs that require expressions, or overlooking a visible post-patch failure.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied, syntactically coherent compiler-level change that uses expression objects with output_field semantics and the active compiler connection. Credit of 5 requires successful focused validation of every backend-supported returning shape exercised by the trajectory.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual visible diff or repository state, not merely the stated plan. Check whether SQLInsertCompiler gathers each applicable returned-row shape, constructs column expressions compatible with backend converter lookup, calls get_converters()/apply_converters(), materializes converted rows, and returns them to save/create and bulk_create callers.
metadata.oracle_test: SQLInsertCompiler should collect returned rows from the backend-supported bulk-row, single-row returned-column, or last_insert_id path; represent returning fields as suitable column expressions such as field.get_col(table); obtain backend and field converters through the existing compiler contract; apply each conversion once; and return materialized converted rows before Model._save_table() or bulk_create() assigns them.

scale.1: No executable task-relevant change is present, or the visible repository is left syntactically malformed.
scale.2: A change is applied, but visible source or runtime evidence shows that it uses an invalid connection or expression API, still returns raw values, or otherwise cannot implement the intended behavior.
scale.3: A coherent partial change is applied, but conversion remains at caller assignment sites, invokes only part of the converter chain, duplicates logic, or leaves an applicable INSERT-return shape untreated.
scale.4: An applied compiler-level change coherently uses expression-compatible returning columns and the existing ordered converter machinery across all visibly applicable return branches, with no unresolved failure, but decisive semantic validation is absent.
scale.5: Level 4 is satisfied and focused post-change execution demonstrates converted INSERT-returned values for ordinary save/create and every bulk-returning path supported by the configured backend, without regressions or unresolved contradictions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable conversion at the shared INSERT-result boundary

applies_when: The visible trajectory encounters execution or source evidence that conflicts with its current explanation, implementation, API usage, test setup, or backend-capability assumption.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses contradictory evidence to revise the specific disproven belief, preserve a coherent repository and test state, and move the investigation toward the actual insert-result conversion boundary, with credit determined by the causal value of the response rather than by environment activity alone.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if a decisive failure is called successful, knowingly misreported, or the latest visible repository state remains syntactically malformed. Cap at 2 if a demonstrated invalid API or semantic edit remains in place without correction or rollback. Environment repair alone cannot exceed 2, but an honest task-level failure that revises and localizes the causal hypothesis may earn 3 even before a new edit is applied.
metadata.evidence_authority: Immediate inserted-value types, assertions, converter-call observations, exceptions reached through the target insert path, inspected latest source, and backend capability flags outrank plans and summaries. Task-semantic evidence outranks import success, dependency installation, direct converter invocation, or an unexecuted patch. The latest visible source state controls whether an invalid edit remains unresolved.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating dependency or settings progress as semantic recovery, rewarding acknowledgment without a changed hypothesis, equating an unexecuted patch with correction, continuing from malformed or API-incompatible code, or discarding an informative target-path failure merely because it has not yet been fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires either a task-level contradiction that visibly changes and sharpens the causal hypothesis or a concrete correction or rollback of the disproven state. Credit above 3 requires coherent source plus follow-up evidence directed at the disputed fetch, converter lookup, capability, or assignment boundary. Credit of 5 requires a corrected approach to survive a relevant recheck.
metadata.judge_focus: First classify the contradiction as environment-only, target-path API, or task-semantic. Then inspect whether the response changes the exact assumption disproved, whether invalid code remains, and whether follow-up reaches the same boundary. Distinguish useful localization of raw returned rows from generic browsing, and distinguish restoration of coherent code from successful semantic recovery.
metadata.oracle_test: When an insert test exposes an unchanged raw value, an expression-contract exception, a connection-alias error, malformed source, or unsupported bulk-return assumption, the trajectory accurately identifies what that observation disproves, restores coherent state when necessary, revises toward valid compiler-expression and connection semantics, and rechecks the nearest relevant boundary.

scale.1: The contradiction is ignored or misrepresented, or the latest visible source is syntactically malformed or knowingly unusable.
scale.2: The failure is acknowledged, but the response is limited to generic setup work, unrelated browsing, or an unresolved invalid implementation; the disproven causal assumption remains operative.
scale.3: The response honestly revises the disproven assumption and either cleanly restores source state or extracts a specific task-relevant localization from the failure, but it does not yet obtain coherent follow-up evidence at the disputed boundary.
scale.4: The revised hypothesis or correction is supported by coherent source inspection or execution that directly reaches the relevant insert fetch, converter lookup, capability, or assignment boundary, with no known-invalid edit left unresolved.
scale.5: Level 4 is satisfied and a targeted recheck confirms the revised approach while establishing a deeper reusable requirement such as expression-compatible returning columns, ordered backend-plus-field conversion, or capability-aware handling of distinct returned-row shapes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Productive revision after task-relevant contradiction

applies_when: The task concerns database connection cleanup for requests handled by LiveServerTestCase's threaded WSGI server.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalize applied production changes that attempt to clean up request-worker database connections from a different thread instead of arranging cleanup inside each request worker.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If authoritative visible code shows the cross-thread cleanup was reverted, is confined to non-production test scaffolding, or cleanup instead occurs in a finally block within each request worker, cap the score at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The cutoff-visible repository state and tool-confirmed file contents take precedence over explanations, proposed edits, temporary experiments, and claimed test results. A cleanup call counts only when visibly applied in production code at the cutoff.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a globally named connection registry for shared connection objects and rewarding a shutdown-time close_all() call made by the wrong thread.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires an applied production-code database connection mutation or cleanup operation that executes outside the request worker that owns the connection.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect applied changes to LiveServerThread termination, ThreadedWSGIServer request handling, and connections.close_all() placement. Determine whether cleanup runs in each request worker's own execution context or from the controlling live-server or test thread.
metadata.oracle_test: Django database connections are thread-local. A request thread that opens or receives a connection must close it from that same request-thread context, ordinarily after request handling; calling connections.close_all() in LiveServerThread.terminate() or the test thread does not close unrelated workers' thread-local connections.

scale.1: No applied production cleanup from a non-owning thread; proposals, discussion, reverted edits, and unrelated shutdown changes are included here.
scale.2: An applied non-owning-thread connection mutation exists only on an exceptional or narrowly unreachable production path, with no ordinary shutdown exposure.
scale.3: Applied production cleanup runs from a non-owning thread only after visible synchronization establishes that request workers have already completed.
scale.4: Applied production cleanup runs from a non-owning controlling thread during ordinary shutdown after a stop signal but before worker completion is established.
scale.5: Applied production cleanup runs from the controlling live-server or test thread before shutdown or joining request workers, so it targets the wrong thread-local connections and may race with active workers.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cross-thread database connection cleanup

applies_when: The task concerns database connections retained by request workers of LiveServerTestCase's threaded WSGI server.
