reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate the causal quality of the cutoff-applied production change for ensuring that each threaded live-server request releases its database connections before test database teardown.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If an ordinary production shutdown path calls connections.close_all() or otherwise mutates request-worker connections from the controlling live-server or test thread before shutdown has begun or before any worker-quiescence step, cap the score at 1 unless that path is visibly removed or superseded by worker-owned cleanup. Tests, comments, and synchronization claims cannot lift this cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Cutoff-visible repository contents and a terminal applied diff take precedence over explanations, planned edits, temporary experiments, generated patch files not applied to the repository, and claimed test results. When code paths conflict, the ordinary request and shutdown paths govern; a targeted test may increase credit only after its asserted production mechanism is visibly present.
metadata.failure_mode: Equating no applied implementation with a task-causal but incomplete lifecycle change, or treating shutdown coordination as equivalent to worker-owned connection cleanup.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires an applied production change that causally affects threaded request handling, worker completion, or connection cleanup. A score above 3 requires database cleanup to execute in the request worker that owns the thread-local connection on every normal and exceptional request exit.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the cutoff-applied production diff and resulting code for changes to request-worker execution, ThreadedWSGIServer shutdown or worker-waiting behavior, server selection, and database cleanup placement. Determine whether the change is absent, actively races shutdown, only improves lifecycle coordination, or closes connections in each request worker.
metadata.oracle_test: Django connections are thread-local. The complete mechanism wraps each ThreadedWSGIServer request worker so connections.close_all() runs in that same worker in a finally path after request handling. Waiting for workers or changing daemon/server policy can reduce shutdown races but does not itself close each worker's connection.

scale.1: An applied ordinary production path performs database cleanup from a non-owning controlling thread before shutdown starts or before any worker-quiescence attempt, creating a direct wrong-thread race.
scale.2: No applied production change causally affects threaded request lifetime or connection cleanup; only investigation, proposals, tests without a production mechanism, reverted edits, inert attributes, or unrelated changes are visible.
scale.3: An applied production change causally alters server threading, worker waiting, server selection, or post-shutdown cleanup, but it does not guarantee cleanup in every connection-owning request worker.
scale.4: Applied production code closes database connections in each request worker on normal and exceptional exit, but targeted regression coverage for threaded live-server cleanup is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: Applied production code closes database connections in each request worker through an unconditional finally-style path, with a targeted regression test that exercises threaded request cleanup and teardown ordering.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied request-connection lifecycle quality

applies_when: Tests, runtime probes, or a concrete test plan address Q combined with Exists or another boolean conditional expression.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evidence covers Q and Exists in both operand orders and demonstrates valid query semantics, not merely successful object construction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the latest visible Q-left test still raises TypeError, NotImplementedError, an object-not-subscriptable error, or returns Value(Exists(...)). Cap at 3 when only construction/repr is tested without query evaluation or expected-result assertions.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful targeted Django test-runner results with assertions outrank ad hoc repr-only scripts; the latest failing rerun overrides earlier success claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a non-exceptional repr, a hand-written mock, or the already-working Exists-left order as sufficient proof of the fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires observed successful execution of the formerly failing Q-left case or a committed repository test with a task-specific expected result.
metadata.judge_focus: Repository tests or runtime output for Q(...) & Exists(...), Exists(...) & Q(...), and corresponding OR behavior, preferably through QuerySet.filter() with asserted rows or SQL semantics.
metadata.oracle_test: Filtering with Q(predicate) & Exists(subquery) yields the same logical result as Exists(subquery) & Q(predicate), and the analogous reversed OR expression also evaluates correctly.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence exists, or all relevant probes fail before exercising the operator behavior.
scale.2: Only the original failure or the already-working Exists-left order is demonstrated, or the latest Q-left probe visibly fails.
scale.3: Both orders are exercised at object-construction level and appear valid, but there is no repository-level query assertion or the OR case is omitted.
scale.4: The formerly failing Q-left AND case and at least one complementary order or connector pass in relevant tests, with meaningful expected structure or query behavior.
scale.5: Targeted repository tests visibly pass for reversed AND and OR combinations, include non-empty Q predicates, and assert equivalent query results or otherwise decisive ORM semantics for both operand orders.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive semantic coverage for both operand orders

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the operand-order asymmetry between Q and a boolean conditional expression.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The diagnosis traces the two Python operator paths, identifies conditional capability as the operand boundary, and explains why merely admitting the expression still leaves the empty-Q branch unsafe.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 for an account centered only on a missing Q.__rand__ or for claiming that Q-left invokes the reflected method first. Cap at 2 if the latest account continues to endorse reflected-only repair, arbitrary operator delegation, resolve_expression eligibility, or Value wrapping after contrary evidence. Cap at 3 if it identifies the direct Q-left guard and conditional protocol but does not correctly explain the empty-Q branch.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source excerpts and reproduced call traces outrank speculation. Later TypeError, NotImplementedError, Value-wrapped output, or object-not-subscriptable output invalidates any earlier causal claim that cannot explain that result. Edits count as diagnostic evidence only when the trajectory states or demonstrates the mechanism they address.
metadata.failure_mode: Stopping at the operand-order dispatch asymmetry or strict guard and therefore missing the second failure caused by Q-only identity handling.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires correctly stating that the Q-left operation invokes Q.__and__ or Q.__or__ and reaches Q._combine() before reflected fallback can repair it. Credit above 3 requires correctly mapping the object-not-subscriptable failure to the empty-self branch attempting Q-style deconstruction or reconstruction of a non-Q conditional operand.
metadata.judge_focus: Explicit source-backed reasoning about Q.__and__ and Q.__or__, Q._combine(), the expression-side conditional combination path, and the branch selected when an empty Q is combined with a non-Q conditional expression.
metadata.oracle_test: For Q() combined with Exists, Python enters Q.__and__ or Q.__or__ and then Q._combine(); for Exists combined with Q, the expression-side operator recognizes both operands as conditional and constructs Q-compatible nodes. Once Q._combine() admits conditional operands, an empty self must not deconstruct the Exists operand as if it were a Q lookup node.

scale.1: The account is absent or fundamentally misstates which operator method handles the Q-left expression.
scale.2: The asymmetry or strict Q check is noticed, but the latest explanation still relies on reflected methods, broad expression capability, or another mechanism contradicted by source or runtime output.
scale.3: The diagnosis correctly traces the direct Q-left path to Q._combine() and explains the expression-left conditional path, but does not correctly identify why the empty-Q case can fail after the guard is loosened.
scale.4: The diagnosis also maps the empty-Q failure to unsafe deconstruction or reconstruction of the non-Q conditional operand, with only a minor omission about the opposite identity branch or connector symmetry.
scale.5: The account precisely distinguishes both dispatch paths, conditional eligibility, the two identity cases, and normal nonempty tree construction, explaining why the narrow repair must change both the acceptance boundary and branch-safe copying for AND and OR.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Source-backed diagnosis of dispatch, eligibility, and empty-Q failure

applies_when: The trajectory encounters a failed target probe, conflicting operator-dispatch evidence, or an edit that introduces a new exception or damages source structure.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory uses each visible contradiction to retire the mechanism it disproves, applies a narrower revision, removes obsolete edits, and checks the revised coherent source with a discriminating follow-up probe.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest source is malformed, truncated, duplicated, or still contains orphaned code. Cap at 2 if the trajectory repeats a disproved reflected, delegation, wrapping, or broad-protocol mechanism, or blames tooling after the same target failure recurs. Cap at 3 if it reaches the correct causal lesson or restores clean source but does not both apply the corresponding revision and probe it afterward. A latest known target failure caps at 3 unless another visible revision and follow-up occur after that failure.
metadata.evidence_authority: Exception traces and runtime output outrank verbal success claims. The latest complete source view or diff determines whether abandoned code remains. A source restoration proves integrity only; it does not prove recovery of the target behavior. A follow-up probe counts only when it exercises the visibly revised state.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking activity, source restoration, or a correct verbal observation for recovery without retiring the contradicted code and testing the replacement.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a specific contradicted mechanism to be removed or replaced in coherent source and a subsequent discriminating probe against that revision. Credit of 5 requires the latest targeted evidence to agree with the final narrow mechanism.
metadata.judge_focus: The sequence from each failure to the next hypothesis, edit, cleanup, source inspection, and probe: reflected methods after Q.__and__ raises first, broad wrapping after Value or object-not-subscriptable results, and empty-Q handling after nonempty combinations succeed while the empty case fails.
metadata.oracle_test: After reflected dispatch is disproved, reflected edits are removed and attention moves to Q._combine(); after wrapping causes Value or object-not-subscriptable behavior, wrapping is removed and the relevant empty branch is isolated; the resulting coherent source is then probed on the case that distinguished the old and new hypotheses.

scale.1: Contradictions are ignored or compounded, and the latest source is broken or incoherent.
scale.2: A failure is noticed, but the disproved mechanism is repeated, broadened, or left in the latest source without a coherent replacement.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly eliminates at least one hypothesis and leaves coherent source or a narrower plan, but the corresponding revision is absent or lacks a later discriminating probe.
scale.4: A contradicted mechanism is removed, a materially narrower revision is applied, and a later probe validates the revised causal step or exposes one new localized blocker; final validation or cleanup remains incomplete.
scale.5: Successive failures retire reflected, broad-wrapping, and unsafe empty-Q mechanisms as encountered; obsolete edits are removed; the final source is coherent; and later targeted evidence supports the resulting narrow approach.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Verified recovery from contradicted Q–expression approaches

applies_when: The proposed change broadens the operand types accepted by Q logical combination.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory protects existing Q/Q behavior and rejection of non-conditional operands while avoiding unrelated changes to expression bitwise semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if F expressions, integers, arbitrary objects, or any resolve_expression object are accepted as logical conditions; also cap at 2 if generic Combinable.__rand__/__ror__ semantics are globally weakened without task-specific necessity.
metadata.evidence_authority: Concrete regression test output and the final operand guard override general assurances that the patch is minimal.
metadata.failure_mode: Fixing the reported pair by silently broadening Q into a container for every expression or by regressing established Q identity and connector behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evidence that unsupported operands remain rejected and ordinary Q-to-Q combinations still work.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tests or source reasoning for Q & Q, Q | Q, empty and non-empty Q operands, non-conditional expressions or ordinary objects, and unchanged bitand()/bitor() behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Boolean conditional expressions such as Exists are accepted; Q/Q AND and OR retain their established connector and empty-node behavior; unsupported operands still raise TypeError and arithmetic/bitwise expression APIs remain unchanged.

scale.1: The change visibly breaks ordinary Q combinations or indiscriminately accepts unrelated objects.
scale.2: Compatibility is largely unaddressed, and source or runtime evidence shows at least one serious over-acceptance or Q/Q regression.
scale.3: The implementation appears narrow and Q/Q smoke checks pass, but unsupported-operand rejection or empty-Q behavior is not demonstrated.
scale.4: Q/Q AND and OR plus unsupported operands are visibly covered, with only a minor gap such as absent subclass or negation coverage.
scale.5: Regression evidence covers non-empty and empty Q/Q combinations, both connectors, unsupported non-conditional operands, and confirms no unnecessary change to generic expression bitwise behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression protection for Q and non-conditional operands

applies_when: A visible edit or concrete patch plan changes logical combination involving Q and non-Q operands.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The implementation admits boolean conditional operands at the Q combination boundary while preserving Q/Q identities, rejecting unsupported operands, and avoiding global or arbitrary operator delegation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when the latest source is syntactically malformed, structurally corrupted, or cannot execute the edited path. Cap at 2 when it accepts arbitrary objects, all resolve_expression objects, or all operands exposing an operator; delegates directly to another operand's operator; wraps conditions in Value; or globally weakens Combinable bitwise behavior. Cap at 3 when the guard is narrow but an empty-Q branch still deconstructs, reconstructs, or indexes a non-Q conditional operand as though it were Q data.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest complete source view or diff determines implementation scope. Targeted runtime results outrank assurances, but construction-level success cannot excuse a visibly broad guard or unsafe identity branch. A malformed or partially applied source view overrides earlier clean snippets.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating successful object construction as proof of compatibility despite over-acceptance, unsafe empty-Q reconstruction, arbitrary delegation, or unrelated changes to expression operators.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible narrow conditional-capability guard and branch-safe behavior for an empty Q combined with a non-Q conditional operand. Credit of 5 additionally requires visible checks that ordinary Q/Q behavior and unsupported-operand rejection remain intact.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest coherent Q._combine(), Q operator methods, and any expression-operator edits for the acceptance predicate, both empty-operand branches, connector preservation, copying behavior, and rejection of non-conditional operands.
metadata.oracle_test: A conditional expression such as Exists is accepted by Q._combine(); an empty Q returns or copies the conditional operand without Q-only deconstruction; ordinary empty and non-empty Q/Q combinations retain their identities and connectors; integers, F expressions, and arbitrary objects remain unsupported; generic expression bitand and bitor behavior is unchanged.

scale.1: The latest implementation is malformed or visibly breaks the edited operator path or ordinary Q combination.
scale.2: The implementation uses a broad or unrelated mechanism that can admit unsupported operands or alter generic expression operator semantics.
scale.3: The implementation has a narrow conditional boundary, but empty-Q copying or another identity branch remains unsafe or unresolved.
scale.4: The latest coherent implementation narrowly accepts conditional operands and safely handles Q identities for AND and OR, while source evidence preserves unsupported-operand rejection; regression execution is limited.
scale.5: The narrow branch-safe implementation is present and visible tests confirm both connectors, empty and non-empty Q/Q behavior, conditional expressions, and rejection of representative unsupported operands without generic operator changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Narrow, branch-safe Q conditional implementation

applies_when: Visible work adds or modifies tests for Q.deconstruct() behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible tests encode the new positional-args behavior for a lone lookup child and a lone non-subscriptable boolean expression, while checking reconstruction and existing connector or negation cases.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A test that continues to require Q(x=1) to deconstruct into kwargs caps credit at 2; a test that merely uses a generic mock without checking args and kwargs caps credit at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository test code with exact assertions outranks temporary scripts, printed values, or prose descriptions of proposed tests.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting source-only experimentation while leaving existing regression tests committed to the superseded serialization format.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require visible repository test changes that no longer assert the obsolete kwargs representation for a single lookup child.
metadata.judge_focus: Changes in tests/queries/test_q.py or equivalent committed tests, with exact assertions for args, kwargs, no exception, and Q(*args, **kwargs) round trips.
metadata.oracle_test: Tests should expect Q(x=1) to yield args=(('x', 1),), kwargs={}, and Q(Exists(...)) to yield one positional expression argument and reconstruct equivalently without TypeError.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence is visible, or tests encode behavior unrelated to Q.deconstruct().
scale.2: Only the old single-child kwargs expectation is retained, or a proposed test checks merely that no exception text was printed.
scale.3: A temporary or repository test covers the non-subscriptable child and checks useful output, but does not update the lone-lookup contract or reconstruction.
scale.4: Repository tests visibly cover both the new lone-lookup args shape and the non-subscriptable child, with at least one reconstruction or metadata assertion.
scale.5: Focused repository tests comprehensively assert the new args/kwargs contract, Exists or an equivalent real boolean expression, round-trip reconstruction, and connector/negation preservation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression tests encode the new serialization behavior

applies_when: The task concerns deconstructing a Q object whose sole child may be an ORM expression rather than a lookup pair.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible reasoning identifies the single-child kwargs special case as the causal defect and adopts the intended contract that every Q child, including a lone lookup tuple or Exists expression, is serialized through positional args.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Reasoning that retains kwargs serialization for a lone 2-tuple, checks hasattr(__getitem__), or accepts lists/dicts as lookup pairs is capped at 3; denying the child[0]/child[1] cause is capped at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct inspection of Q.__init__() and Q.deconstruct(), followed by observed deconstruct results, outranks speculation about subscriptability or backward compatibility.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a backward-compatible tuple guard as equivalent to the requested removal of the undocumented single-child special case.
metadata.hard_gate: Higher anchors require recognizing that the intended fix removes the single-child kwargs distinction rather than merely broadening which child types qualify for it.
metadata.judge_focus: Reasoning about self.children, the child[0]/child[1] crash, and the intended serialization shape for both Q(x=1) and Q(Exists(...)).
metadata.oracle_test: After the intended change, Q(x=1).deconstruct() has args=(('x', 1),) and kwargs={}, while Q(Exists(...)).deconstruct() has args=(exists_expression,) and does not raise TypeError.

scale.1: No correct causal diagnosis is visible, or the trajectory attributes the crash to unrelated query combination or settings behavior.
scale.2: The trajectory locates Q.deconstruct() or reproduces the TypeError but does not establish the serialization contract needed to fix it.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly explains the unsafe child indexing but chooses or endorses a tuple-length/subscriptability guard that preserves the old single-lookup kwargs behavior.
scale.4: The trajectory clearly concludes that the special case should be removed and that lone children belong in args, but incompletely explains reconstruction or metadata preservation.
scale.5: The trajectory precisely derives the defect and intended contract from code and runtime behavior, covering lone lookup tuples, non-subscriptable expressions, reconstruction, and connector/negation metadata.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of the Q.deconstruct() contract

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes Q.deconstruct() for a sole child that may be an ORM expression or another non-lookup object.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge whether visible reasoning identifies the unsafe single-child indexing assumption, derives that deconstruction must retain rather than merely stop crashing on the child, and validates the intended contract that every child is serialized through positional args.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Denying that child[0]/child[1] causes the failure caps credit at 1. If visible output has empty args and kwargs for a nonempty Q, or otherwise omits the sole child, cap at 3 even when the trajectory calls the result successful. Retaining any tuple, length, subscriptability, list, or dictionary test that converts a lone lookup child to kwargs caps credit at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source or unified diff determines the selected contract. Executed deconstruct and Q(*args, **kwargs) observations are next strongest. A concrete executable regression assertion that would fail when the child is omitted is stronger than prose but weaker than execution. Plans, claimed success, and assertions that only check absence of an exception are non-evidence for retention.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding location of the failing line without checking that the child survives, treating an empty deconstruction as successful crash avoidance, or treating a compatibility guard as equivalent to removal of the undocumented single-child representation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires either visible execution retaining the arbitrary child as a positional argument or a concrete executable regression assertion that checks its retention. Credit above 3 requires visibly adopting and applying the uniform all-children-in-args contract. Credit of 5 requires visible round-trip evidence and connector or negation preservation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect reasoning about self.children and child[0]/child[1], the selected serialization contract for both Q(x=1) and an Exists-like child, and visible outputs or assertions showing whether the sole child remains in args. Also inspect reconstruction, connector, and negation checks when present.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended diagnosis predicts Q(x=1).deconstruct() with args=(('x', 1),) and kwargs={}, and Q(exists_expression).deconstruct() with args=(exists_expression,) without an exception. Reconstructing Q(*args, **kwargs) must preserve the child structure, nondefault connector, and negation.

scale.1: The trajectory does not identify the unsafe single-child indexing cause, or attributes the failure to unrelated query, model, or settings behavior.
scale.2: The unsafe child indexing is correctly identified, but visible work neither retains the arbitrary child nor authors an executable assertion that would detect its omission; this includes accepting empty args and kwargs as success.
scale.3: The cause and retention requirement are established by direct execution or a concrete regression assertion, but the selected implementation remains shape-dependent, is visibly contradicted by omission, or has not yet adopted the uniform positional contract.
scale.4: The trajectory visibly adopts and applies the uniform all-children-in-args contract and demonstrates positional serialization for both a lone lookup tuple and an arbitrary non-subscriptable child, but round-trip or metadata validation is incomplete.
scale.5: The trajectory derives, applies, and validates the uniform positional contract, including retained non-subscriptable and lookup children, successful Q(*args, **kwargs) reconstruction, and preservation of nondefault connector and negation metadata.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Diagnosis and validation of Q.deconstruct() child retention

applies_when: A visible patch or source edit changes the implementation of Q.deconstruct().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge the latest applied Q.deconstruct() implementation by whether it retains every child, avoids broad shape or subscriptability assumptions, preserves metadata and path normalization, and preferably removes the single-child representation distinction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A branch that leaves args and kwargs empty for a nonempty Q, indexes a child after merely checking len() or __getitem__, or loses path, _connector, or _negated handling caps at 1. Treating lists, dictionaries, strings, or arbitrary subscriptable objects as lookup pairs caps at 2. Any remaining exact-tuple single-child kwargs conversion caps at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or unified diff overrides prose and earlier edits. Provenance-confirmed execution is supporting evidence for branch behavior. Temporary outputs from code that was subsequently restored or replaced are non-evidence for the final implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Equating all defensive guards, overlooking a branch that silently drops the child, or accepting broad duck-typing that converts arbitrary positional objects into keyword arguments.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 1 requires that every nonempty Q path retains its children. Credit above 2 requires either an exact built-in tuple of length 2 as the sole compatibility classification or removal of shape-based classification entirely. Credit above 3 requires unconditional positional serialization of all children. Credit of 5 requires a minimal clean implementation preserving path, connector, and negation logic.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact final branch structure and initialization of args and kwargs. Check behavior implied for an Exists-like object, a lookup tuple, a string, a list, a dictionary, an unusual-length tuple, a nondefault connector, and negation.
metadata.oracle_test: The canonical implementation is semantically equivalent to args = tuple(self.children); kwargs = {}; add _connector only for a nondefault connector; add _negated only when true; return the normalized path, args, and kwargs.

scale.1: The applied edit is malformed, can omit a child, still indexes an arbitrary child, or loses required path or metadata behavior.
scale.2: The edit avoids the reported example but uses a broad len(), __getitem__, list, dictionary, string, or similar predicate that can misclassify other positional children.
scale.3: A complete compatibility implementation converts only an exact length-2 tuple to kwargs and reliably places every other child in args while preserving path and metadata.
scale.4: All children are unconditionally serialized through args and required path and metadata behavior is preserved, but the patch contains avoidable duplication, unrelated changes, or unclear initialization.
scale.5: A minimal, clean applied implementation unconditionally derives args from self.children, initializes kwargs independently, and preserves path normalization, nondefault connector, and negation semantics.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Safe and precise implementation in Q.deconstruct()

applies_when: Visible work executes, adds, or modifies checks for Q.deconstruct() behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge how effectively visible checks expose loss of a sole arbitrary child, distinguish the intended lone-lookup positional representation from the obsolete kwargs representation, and verify reconstruction plus connector or negation metadata.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If a check labels empty args and kwargs successful for a nonempty Q, or otherwise accepts loss of the sole arbitrary child, cap at 1. A check that only confirms no exception without exposing args and kwargs caps at 2. Checks that explicitly require lone-lookup kwargs serialization cap at 3 even if they correctly verify arbitrary-child retention. Failures solely from unchanged assertions for the superseded lone-lookup representation do not invalidate otherwise correct canonical checks.
metadata.evidence_authority: Exact repository test assertions are strongest. Executed temporary assertions and deterministic executed comparisons or complete printed args and kwargs are next, provided the output visibly reveals whether the child was retained. Unexecuted assertions follow. Generic PASS labels, exception-only checks, plans, and prose descriptions are weakest and cannot override displayed omission or a contradictory assertion.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating no exception as a retention test, overlooking output that visibly contains empty serialization for a nonempty Q, refusing all credit to precise executed observations merely because they are temporary, or treating tests of the obsolete lone-lookup kwargs form as canonical contract coverage.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 1 requires visible inspection of args and kwargs for an arbitrary sole child without accepting omission. Credit above 2 requires an assertion, equality comparison, reconstruction check, or complete executed observation that makes child retention observable. Credit above 3 requires visible checks of the canonical positional form for both a lone lookup and an arbitrary child, plus reconstruction or metadata behavior. Credit of 5 requires durable repository regression tests covering the full contract.
metadata.judge_focus: Read the exact assertions, comparisons, and displayed values. Determine whether omission would be detected, whether Q(x=1) is expected in positional args with empty lookup kwargs, whether the same arbitrary child survives in args and reconstruction, and whether nondefault connector and negation metadata are checked.
metadata.oracle_test: Checks should establish Q(x=1).deconstruct() as args=(('x', 1),) with kwargs={}, establish an Exists-like object as the sole positional argument of its deconstruction, reconstruct equivalent children with Q(*args, **kwargs), and verify conditional _connector and _negated metadata.

scale.1: No relevant serialization result is inspected, or visible checks accept or celebrate omission of a sole arbitrary child.
scale.2: Checks reproduce the case or display relevant output but only establish crash avoidance, provide incomplete values, or do not make retention of the specific arbitrary child reliably observable.
scale.3: Executed checks make arbitrary-child positional retention observable and may cover reconstruction or metadata, but the lone-lookup contract is absent or explicitly remains in kwargs.
scale.4: Visible executable checks enforce or unambiguously demonstrate positional serialization for both a lone lookup and an arbitrary child and also cover reconstruction or connector/negation metadata, but durable repository coverage or one semantic case is incomplete.
scale.5: Durable repository regression tests assert both positional forms, arbitrary-child retention, round-trip reconstruction, nondefault connector handling, and negation handling.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable checks expose Q.deconstruct() retention and representation errors

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes Q.deconstruct() for a sole child that may be an ORM expression or another non-lookup object.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge whether the trajectory correctly traces the failure to unconditional indexing of a sole child, applies a repair that retains that child, and validates the selected serialization contract, with explicit precedence for the latest visible implementation and a strict distinction between compatibility guards and uniform positional serialization.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the latest visible implementation can still index an arbitrary sole child, leaves a nonempty sole child out of both args and kwargs, or visibly reconstructs a materially different Q object, assign 1 regardless of earlier successful output or prose. If a later restoration removes the repair, applied-work credit is unavailable. Any type, length, subscriptability, list, dictionary, or tuple-shape branch that still converts a lone lookup child to kwargs caps the score at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or unified diff determines which contract is applied and overrides earlier edits, summaries, and executions. Repository-root executions of that source are next strongest, followed by exact executable assertions and then observed deconstruct outputs. Success labels, plans, and expected results cannot override contradictory source or output.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting diagnosis despite visible child loss, treating absence of TypeError as proof that the child survived, relying on execution performed before a later source restoration, or rewarding a well-tested compatibility guard as equivalent to removal of the single-child special case.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 1 requires a correct causal diagnosis and no authoritative evidence of child omission. Credit above 2 requires a visibly applied repair that necessarily retains arbitrary sole children. Credit above 3 requires the applied source to serialize every child positionally without a shape-dependent lone-child kwargs branch. Credit of 5 additionally requires visible round-trip validation and preservation of nondefault connector and negation metadata.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest Q.deconstruct() body first. Determine whether a sole arbitrary expression is retained in args, whether a lone lookup tuple also remains in args, and whether reconstruction, nondefault connector, and negation checks were actually performed against the applied source.
metadata.oracle_test: For both a lone lookup and a lone non-subscriptable expression, deconstruct() should return the child as the sole positional argument and no lookup kwargs. Q(*args, **kwargs) should reconstruct equivalent children, while _connector appears only for a nondefault connector and _negated only when true.

scale.1: The cause is misidentified, the authoritative implementation remains unsafe, or visible behavior drops or materially corrupts a sole child.
scale.2: The unsafe child indexing is correctly diagnosed and a plausible repair is discussed or attempted, but no authoritative applied repair establishes retention of an arbitrary sole child.
scale.3: A visible applied compatibility repair safely retains arbitrary sole children positionally, with at least direct output or an omission-sensitive check confirming retention, but a shape-dependent lone-lookup kwargs branch remains.
scale.4: The visible applied implementation removes the special case and serializes all children positionally, with observed or executable evidence covering both a lone lookup and an arbitrary sole child, but round-trip or metadata validation is incomplete.
scale.5: The uniform positional implementation is visibly applied and validated for lone lookup and arbitrary children, Q(*args, **kwargs) reconstruction, nondefault connector metadata, and negation metadata.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis and applied validation of Q.deconstruct() child retention

applies_when: A visible source edit or executable check concerns recognition of BigAutoField or SmallAutoField descendants as AutoField subclasses.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the applied AutoFieldMeta implementation transitively recognizes descendants of BigAutoField and SmallAutoField while preserving ordinary AutoField subclass behavior, unrelated-field rejection, and the existing AutoField instance-check contract.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if visible applied code leaves a required BigAutoField or SmallAutoField descendant rejected, accepts an unrelated field, breaks AutoField identity or normal subclasses, makes __instancecheck__ invalid by changing _subclasses to a non-class/non-tuple value, or is syntactically invalid. Cap at 2 when only Options._get_default_pk_class or another individual caller is broadened while the shared AutoField issubclass contract remains false.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final unified diff or post-edit source read has highest authority. Later successful executable checks against the edited source are next, followed by an edit command or rewrite script that visibly targets the correct method. Prose claims and pre-edit tests have no authority over contradictory applied source. Successful descendant checks do not override a visible regression in another metaclass method.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents preferring one exact source expression over equivalent correct implementations and prevents awarding high credit to a descendant-only fix that silently corrupts _subclasses or __instancecheck__.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires evidence of an applied edit at AutoFieldMeta rather than only a caller-specific validation change. Credit above 3 requires preservation of the superclass fallback or demonstrably equivalent ordinary AutoField behavior, plus no visible type-contract break between _subclasses and __instancecheck__.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the effective definitions of AutoFieldMeta._subclasses, __subclasscheck__, and any edited __instancecheck__. Accept equivalent tuple-based, explicit-class, generator, loop, or MRO implementations when their visible semantics satisfy the full contract.
metadata.oracle_test: The effective code must make arbitrary-depth descendants of BigAutoField and SmallAutoField satisfy issubclass(..., AutoField), keep AutoField and its ordinary subclasses accepted, reject unrelated fields such as CharField, and keep instances of the designated compatible AutoField classes usable with isinstance(..., AutoField).

scale.1: Visible applied code is invalid or contradicts at least one oracle condition, including a broken _subclasses/__instancecheck__ interface.
scale.2: A concrete change is applied only at a caller-specific boundary, or the shared metaclass edit visibly remains insufficient to establish the required descendant relationship.
scale.3: An AutoFieldMeta edit is visibly applied and plausibly addresses descendants, but the resulting source is incomplete or materially ambiguous about transitive recognition, superclass fallback, unrelated-field rejection, or instance-check preservation.
scale.4: The visible implementation satisfies the full metaclass contract but includes harmless redundancy, unnecessary compatible adjacent edits, or relies on strong executable confirmation where the final source presentation is incomplete.
scale.5: A focused, visibly valid AutoFieldMeta change satisfies every oracle condition; semantically equivalent explicit-class, tuple, generator, loop, and MRO formulations receive equal credit when they preserve the surrounding contracts.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression-safe AutoFieldMeta subclass contract

applies_when: A visible implementation changes DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD validation or enumerates accepted field classes outside AutoFieldMeta.__subclasscheck__.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory introduces a wrong-layer workaround that accepts custom automatic fields only at a particular validation site while leaving issubclass(custom_auto_field, AutoField) false or duplicating the accepted-class list.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If final source instead confines the semantic fix to AutoFieldMeta.__subclasscheck__ and preserves the generic Options check, this rubric is fixed at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible diff and direct issubclass results outrank statements that a workaround is equivalent; later removal of the workaround removes the penalty.
metadata.failure_mode: Overlooks an apparently successful DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD workaround that leaves other callers of issubclass(..., AutoField) inconsistent and creates duplicated maintenance boundaries.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a visible final wrong-layer change, not merely discussion or an abandoned edit.
metadata.judge_focus: Changes to django/db/models/options.py, new BigAutoField or SmallAutoField imports there, duplicated explicit checks, and runtime evidence that the metaclass contract remains broken.
metadata.oracle_test: Options should continue asking only issubclass(pk_class, AutoField); AutoFieldMeta should define which compatibility classes and descendants satisfy that generic contract.

scale.1: No visible final bypass or duplicated accepted-class validation exists.
scale.2: A bypass is proposed or temporarily attempted but is absent from the latest visible source.
scale.3: The final change includes minor redundant class-specific logic outside AutoFieldMeta, but the metaclass contract is also visibly corrected.
scale.4: The final implementation changes Options or another caller to enumerate BigAutoField and SmallAutoField instead of repairing AutoFieldMeta, although the immediate reported setup may succeed.
scale.5: The wrong-layer workaround is definitive and broadens or otherwise damages validation, such as accepting unrelated classes, removing generic rejection, introducing import coupling, or leaving contradictory runtime behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Bypass of the AutoField virtual-inheritance contract

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes URLValidator behavior for URLs containing LF, CR, or tab characters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Applies a narrowly scoped change to URLValidator.__call__ that preserves its non-string ValidationError path and rejects every original string containing LF, CR, or tab immediately after the type guard and before scheme handling or URL parsing.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if membership, iteration, or another string-only operation may execute before the non-string guard, if the condition references the wrong variable, or if the visible code is syntactically invalid. Cap at 3 if any forbidden character is omitted, the check uses a parsed or normalized value, occurs after scheme handling or parsing, or changes the configured ValidationError contract. Later visible removal or breakage overrides earlier successful source views and tests.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository diff is authoritative for whether the change is applied and narrowly scoped. A later current-file view can establish executable content but, without a corresponding diff or equivalent before-and-after evidence, does not establish unchanged surrounding production code. Test output corroborates visible source but cannot replace it or override malformed, unsafe, removed, or partial code.
metadata.failure_mode: Avoids granting top credit to proposed or transient edits, test-only evidence, checks placed after other URL processing, unsafe pre-type-guard membership operations, malformed variable references, partial character coverage, or broader normalization changes outside URLValidator.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires a visible repository diff showing that URLValidator.__call__ retains the non-string guard first, checks all three characters '\n', '\r', and '\t' in the original value immediately afterward, and raises ValidationError with self.message, self.code, and params={'value': value} before scheme extraction, regex validation, urlsplit(), reconstruction, or normalization. Score 4 requires the same executable ordering in a current-file view when complete patch scope is not established.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible repository diff and current URLValidator.__call__ content for the non-string guard, an immediately following check covering LF, CR, and tab in the original value, the configured ValidationError arguments, and the absence of unrelated production changes.
metadata.oracle_test: In URLValidator.__call__, None and integer inputs follow the existing configured ValidationError path; an original string containing LF, CR, or tab anywhere raises the same configured ValidationError before any other URL processing; strings without those characters continue through the existing scheme, regex, IDN, IPv6, and hostname logic unchanged.

scale.1: No relevant applied source change is visible, or the visible change targets another validation or normalization layer instead of URLValidator.__call__.
scale.2: A relevant edit is visible but is unsafe for non-string inputs, syntactically invalid, references the wrong value, or otherwise cannot preserve the established ValidationError behavior.
scale.3: The edit is executable and relevant but omits a forbidden character, checks a processed value, occurs after scheme handling or parsing, or changes the configured ValidationError contract.
scale.4: Current executable source visibly preserves the non-string guard and immediately rejects LF, CR, and tab in the original value with the configured ValidationError, but the visible evidence does not fully establish the applied patch's scope or unchanged surrounding production code.
scale.5: An authoritative repository diff visibly applies the minimal URLValidator.__call__ change immediately after the non-string guard, rejects LF, CR, and tab in the original value with the configured ValidationError, and leaves all unrelated production validation behavior unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Persisted safe rejection of URL control characters

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or changes URLValidator behavior affected by URL parsing that removes carriage return, line feed, or tab characters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory applies a focused URLValidator change that rejects raw URL strings containing carriage return, line feed, or tab before parsing can remove them, while preserving valid URL handling and the validator's established behavior for non-string inputs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 when a visible relevant test still accepts a raw control-character URL or reveals a regression and the trajectory does not resolve and recheck it. Cap at 2 for a visibly malformed edit, a subset-only check, or a check placed before an unguarded type prerequisite that can raise TypeError for existing non-string cases.
metadata.evidence_authority: An inspected repository diff or source listing outranks prose claims. Repository-native validator test results outrank ad hoc scripts; focused direct executions are supporting evidence. If tests and claims conflict, the observed test result wins.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for merely explaining bpo-43882, trusting post-normalization parser components, testing only trailing newline, or introducing a superficially correct control-character check that breaks the existing input-type contract.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an applied, syntactically valid source change that covers carriage return, line feed, and tab without evaluating string membership on a non-string value.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible source edit or diff in URLValidator.__call__, its position relative to the string-type guard and urlsplit-dependent logic, coverage of all three parser-stripped characters, and directly observed validation results for invalid and unaffected inputs.
metadata.oracle_test: URLValidator must raise ValidationError for any raw string containing '\r', '\n', or '\t' before urllib parsing can erase those characters; corresponding clean URLs remain valid, and non-string inputs continue to raise ValidationError rather than an incidental TypeError.

scale.1: No applied relevant change is visible, or the applied change is clearly unusable and no successful direct behavior is demonstrated.
scale.2: An applied attempt exists but is incomplete or unsafe: it misses one or more of carriage return, line feed, and tab; contains a visible syntax/runtime defect; or can process non-string input with string-membership logic before the type contract is enforced.
scale.3: A plausible applied check covers the raw control characters, but source placement or contract preservation is not established, verification is only partial, or a relevant contradictory result remains unresolved.
scale.4: The visible source change correctly rejects all three characters at a safe point before parser-dependent validation, preserves clean URLs and non-string ValidationError behavior, and focused checks show no relevant contradiction.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and is additionally confirmed by the repository's relevant validator tests, including the reported newline cases and focused regression coverage for carriage return, tab, valid counterparts, and non-string inputs.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly reject parser-stripped URL control characters

applies_when: The trajectory runs tests or reproductions concerning the URLValidator behavior changed by bpo-43882.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces reliable visible evidence that the reported newline URLs and all relevant stripped control characters are rejected after the change, while ordinary hostname and IPv6 URLs remain accepted.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible post-change evidence shows either reported URL is accepted. Cap at 3 if an official test run fails or does not execute and only ad hoc checks pass. A URLField result does not contradict direct URLValidator evidence because form cleaning may normalize input before validators run.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successfully completed repository validators test suite outranks focused framework tests, which outrank correctly configured direct URLValidator checks; failed setup commands and self-authored print-only scripts are weaker evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Treats unexecuted claims, dependency/setup failures, mislabeled expectations, or URLField normalization behavior as proof that URLValidator itself is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires successful post-change evidence for both reported newline inputs plus at least one valid URL; anchor 5 additionally requires the repository validators test target or equivalent assertions covering LF, CR, tab, and compatibility.
metadata.judge_focus: Commands and outputs for the existing validators suite or direct URLValidator calls, including exact input representations, expected exceptions, and exit/pass status.
metadata.oracle_test: URLValidator raises ValidationError for 'http://www.djangoproject.com/\n' and 'http://[::ffff:192.9.5.5]\n'; direct checks should also reject embedded or trailing '\r' and '\t', while accepting the corresponding clean hostname and IPv6 URLs.

scale.1: No relevant executed evidence, or only assertions about expected behavior without output.
scale.2: A reproduction is attempted but setup fails, expectations are mislabeled, or visible results still show the reported defect.
scale.3: Correctly configured ad hoc post-change checks pass for the reported cases and at least one clean URL, but no authoritative repository test completes.
scale.4: Both reported cases and clean hostname/IPv6 controls pass in reliable post-change checks, with no contradictory relevant result.
scale.5: The repository validators test target completes successfully after the change, and visible focused evidence also demonstrates rejection of LF, CR, and tab with preservation of representative clean URLs.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive validator test evidence

applies_when: The trajectory discusses the cause of URLValidator accepting URLs containing LF, CR, or tab on affected Python versions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that affected urllib.parse.urlsplit() versions remove LF, CR, and tab characters before component parsing, allowing URLValidator's later parsing and fallback paths to validate a sanitized representation rather than reject the original input.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims the characters reach URLValidator only after external application code strips them, or otherwise attributes the failure to the URL regex without reconciling observed urlsplit() behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct runtime output from urlsplit() and URLValidator on the original strings outranks speculation; repository source and existing test expectations outrank general URL-policy assertions.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards reproducing acceptance without understanding why Python-version-dependent parsing changes the result.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require an explicit causal link between preprocessing by urlsplit() and loss of the forbidden characters before URLValidator's component checks.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection or runtime evidence connecting the original URL, urlsplit() output, and URLValidator's acceptance of the two reported newline cases.
metadata.oracle_test:
On an affected Python, urlsplit('http://www.djangoproject.com/
').path is '/' and urlsplit('http://[::ffff:192.9.5.5]
').netloc excludes the newline, while the original strings still contain '
'.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by visible source/runtime evidence.
scale.2: Recognizes a newline-related URL validation problem but gives an incomplete or materially confused account of where stripping occurs.
scale.3: States that urlsplit() strips relevant whitespace on affected Python versions, but does not connect this behavior clearly to URLValidator's validation flow or reported cases.
scale.4: Correctly connects urlsplit() removal of LF, CR, and tab to the reported URLValidator bypass and supports it with relevant source inspection or reproduction.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal account with direct original-versus-split runtime evidence for the reported hostname and IPv6 forms, and explains why validation must consider the untouched input before parsing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of bpo-43882 validation bypass

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes URLValidator behavior for raw URLs containing line feed, carriage return, or tab characters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Applies a focused change in URLValidator.__call__ that retains the existing non-string ValidationError path and rejects the untouched input when it contains LF, CR, or tab before scheme extraction or parser-dependent processing.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible implementation performs membership, iteration, splitting, or another string-only operation before the non-string guard; references the wrong variable; is syntactically invalid; or visibly removes the rejection. Cap at 3 if a required character is omitted, the check uses a parsed or normalized value, occurs after scheme extraction, or raises without preserving self.message, self.code, and params={'value': value}. Passing tests cannot lift an applicable source cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository diff hunk with enough surrounding context to identify URLValidator.__call__ is authoritative for the applied edit and its local scope; it need not display the entire file. A current-file view can establish executable ordering and behavior when it visibly includes the type guard, control-character check, and following scheme logic. Tests corroborate source but do not prove an omitted condition or override a later malformed, unsafe, moved, or removed edit. Later relevant source evidence supersedes earlier evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Avoids equating a merely truncated display with a defective implementation while withholding high credit from proposals, test-only claims, unsafe pre-guard checks, post-scheme checks, stale edits, wrong-variable conditions, and malformed source.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 or 5 requires visible executable source establishing that the non-string guard runs before any string-only operation and that the original value is checked for all of '\n', '\r', and '\t' before scheme extraction. Score 5 additionally requires a repository diff hunk or equivalent before-and-after evidence showing the focused production edit and unchanged adjacent URLValidator flow.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible URLValidator.__call__ source and repository diff context for the non-string guard, the control-character condition, its position before scheme handling, the value passed to the check, and the configured ValidationError arguments.
metadata.oracle_test: None and integer inputs continue through the configured ValidationError path; any original string containing '\n', '\r', or '\t' is rejected before scheme, regex, IDN, IPv6, hostname, or urlsplit processing; and strings without those characters retain the existing validation flow.

scale.1: No relevant applied production change is visible, or the latest visible source shows that the control-character rejection is absent or removed.
scale.2: The latest relevant code is malformed, references the wrong value, performs string-only work before the non-string guard, or otherwise visibly breaks the established input-type behavior.
scale.3: A relevant applied attempt is visible, but its exact executable ordering or full character coverage is not established, or it omits a required character, checks a processed value, occurs after scheme extraction, or changes the configured ValidationError contract.
scale.4: Visible current source establishes that the existing non-string guard runs first and that the untouched string is then checked for LF, CR, and tab with the configured ValidationError before scheme handling, but authoritative before-and-after patch scope is not shown.
scale.5: A visible repository diff hunk or equivalent before-and-after evidence establishes the focused URLValidator.__call__ edit: the non-string guard remains first, LF, CR, and tab are rejected in the untouched value with the configured ValidationError, and adjacent URL processing remains unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Safely applied URL control-character rejection

applies_when: The cutoff contains a test, test design, or runtime scenario for applying and then unapplying a squashed migration while its replaced migration modules remain available.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Exercises the existing squashed-migration fixture with replacement files present and asserts persistent applied-migration state before and after unapplication, including removal of the squash key and all replaced keys.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when a relevant test reaches its assertions and shows the squash key remains applied or another migration record is wrong. Import, settings, or dependency failures are not behavioral proof and cap at 3 unless followed by valid repository-native evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing focused repository-test output and explicit recorder assertions outrank ad hoc script output, table-existence checks alone, or assertions against an executor loader created before migration.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents accepting schema-only tests that pass even while django_migrations retains the stale squash row, and prevents false confidence from stale loader data.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an assertion that the squashed migration key is absent after backward migration; credit of 5 additionally requires a demonstrated relevant test pass.
metadata.judge_focus: A repository test under tests/migrations, preferably extending executor coverage, that queries MigrationRecorder or an equivalent fresh persistent-state view rather than only checking schema tables or a stale loader cache.
metadata.oracle_test: Using test_migrations_squashed, apply 0001_squashed_0002, establish that its applied state is recorded, migrate migrations to None/zero, then assert 0001_squashed_0002, 0001_initial, and 0002_second are all absent from fresh MigrationRecorder.applied_migrations().

scale.1: No relevant regression scenario is present, or the scenario cannot exercise replacement migration bookkeeping.
scale.2: Mentions or tests squash unapplication but checks only table removal, the plan, or replaced keys and therefore misses the reported stale squash key.
scale.3: Defines the essential apply-then-unapply scenario and squash-key assertion, but it is incomplete, not integrated, or not successfully executed.
scale.4: Provides a repository-integrated test that checks the squash key and replaced keys through persistent recorder state, with no contradictory completed result.
scale.5: Provides the complete focused regression test and visible successful execution with the replaced migration files still present.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression test for recorder state with replacement files present

applies_when: The visible trajectory proposes or performs a code change for unapplication bookkeeping of a migration with a nonempty replaces list.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Specifies or implements a change in MigrationExecutor.unapply_migration() that retains deletion of every key in migration.replaces and also deletes the replacement migration's own app/name recorder key, while preserving ordinary-migration and schema-reversal behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the adopted change removes only replaced keys, changes only the ordinary else branch, targets loader or graph state instead of the recorder boundary, or says the replacement's own key should not be removed. Cap at 3 if the own-key deletion is only general intent, branch placement is ambiguous, replaced-key deletion is lost, or the proposal remains mixed with unresolved incompatible implementations. An unnecessary application-side change prevents a 5 but does not erase an otherwise coherent backward fix.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final visible source change or diff is strongest. An exact executable patch, edit command, or unambiguous code-level specification is sufficient to establish the implementation design even if the final file is not displayed. Such evidence receives credit only when the trajectory's adopted explanation has the same polarity; a later reversion or endorsed contrary explanation controls.
metadata.failure_mode: Separates a complete code-level solution from mere method discovery, while avoiding false credit for an exact-looking patch whose surrounding reasoning gives it the opposite purpose or later rejects it.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an exact call or equally precise executable specification that record_unapplied(migration.app_label, migration.name) executes for a replacement migration in addition to the retained loop over migration.replaces. A contradictory claim that the replacement key should remain recorded prevents credit above 2.
metadata.judge_focus: The proposed or visible form of the migration.replaces branch in django/db/migrations/executor.py::unapply_migration(), including the complete set of record_unapplied calls, their branch placement, and the trajectory's stated purpose for them.
metadata.oracle_test: For replacement S of R1 and R2, the specified replacement path must request record_unapplied for R1, R2, and S; for ordinary migration N, the ordinary path must continue to request it once for N.

scale.1: Provides no actionable change at the persistent unapplication recording boundary.
scale.2: Locates relevant code but proposes an incorrect, reversed, contradictory, or out-of-scope change that does not reliably delete the replacement's own recorder key.
scale.3: States the correct remedy in general terms or gives a partially specified call, but does not establish complete branch placement and preservation of all replaced-key deletions.
scale.4: Gives a coherent exact implementation, whether proposed or performed, that deletes all replaced keys and the replacement's own key while preserving the ordinary branch and reversal flow.
scale.5: Shows the minimal correctly placed final source change with no unnecessary application-side, loader, graph, schema, planning, fake-mode, or callback modifications.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct replacement-unapply recorder change

applies_when: The cutoff contains reasoning about how a squashed migration and its replaced migrations are represented in django_migrations during backward migration.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that unapplying a replacement migration deletes the records named in migration.replaces but leaves the squashed migration's own recorder row behind, even though check_replacements may previously have created that row.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims the existing replacement branch already removes the squashed key, that check_replacements removes stale rows, or that only the replaced migrations should become unapplied; cap at 3 if it never distinguishes persistent recorder state from loader-local state.
metadata.evidence_authority: Directly quoted repository control flow and observed MigrationRecorder contents outrank assumptions based on method names, local in-memory applied_migrations sets, or migration-file presence alone.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad discussion of graph planning or file discovery that misses the persistent stale row responsible for the bug.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires identifying both the surviving squashed key and why deleting only the replaced keys does not delete it.
metadata.judge_focus: A code-grounded trace through MigrationExecutor.unapply_migration(), record_migration(), check_replacements(), and MigrationLoader's replacement-state synthesis, distinguishing actual recorder rows from loader-derived applied state.
metadata.oracle_test: After a squash replacing 0001_initial and 0002_second has been applied, django_migrations can contain all three keys; migrating the app to zero must leave none of those three keys applied.

scale.1: No relevant causal account, or an account centered on an unrelated subsystem.
scale.2: Recognizes that replacement migrations are special but gives an incorrect or internally inconsistent explanation of which records remain applied.
scale.3: Correctly states that the replacement branch removes the replaced migration records but not the squashed migration's own record.
scale.4: Also explains how check_replacements or loader replacement handling caused the squashed key to be considered and recorded as applied, and why the current unapply path leaves it stale.
scale.5: Provides a complete, code-grounded state transition from application through backward migration, explicitly separating database recorder rows, loader-synthesized applied state, and the presence of replacement files.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of the stale squashed-migration record

applies_when: The cutoff contains commands or observations presented as runtime evidence about squashed migration application or unapplication.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses Django's repository-native test environment or a correctly configured equivalent, treats setup failures as non-evidence, and updates conclusions when runtime results conflict with the proposed causal model.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if import errors, missing settings, missing migration nodes, empty recorder output from a misconfigured app, or a script that never reaches migration execution is claimed as proof. Cap at 3 if repeated invalid attempts are not replaced by valid evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successfully discovered Django test run using tests/runtests.py and fresh database state outranks standalone scripts; setup exceptions and empty results from misconfigured applications have no semantic authority.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding conclusions drawn from ModuleNotFoundError, NodeNotFoundError caused by bad setup, stale executor loaders, or no-op migration configurations.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one successfully executed repository-native migration test or an equivalently valid configured reproduction that reaches migration operations and assertions.
metadata.judge_focus: Command provenance, successful test discovery, actual assertions reached, freshness of recorder/loader state, and whether failed imports or misconfigured apps are interpreted cautiously.
metadata.oracle_test: The reliable command is a focused migration executor test through Django's own test runner; evidence is meaningful only after the intended migrations app and test database are loaded and recorder assertions execute.

scale.1: Runtime claims rely on invalid setup, or contradictory output is ignored.
scale.2: Attempts execution but repeatedly treats setup or discovery failures as behavioral evidence.
scale.3: Correctly recognizes invalid or inconclusive runs as non-evidence and refines the setup or reasoning, but no valid task-specific execution is reached.
scale.4: Successfully runs repository-native migration coverage and interprets its scope accurately, without claiming that an existing broad test proves the new recorder assertion.
scale.5: Successfully runs a focused reproduction or regression assertion for the stale squash record and reconciles all earlier contradictory or invalid observations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reliable runtime evidence and recovery from invalid reproductions

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates or changes applied-state bookkeeping for unapplying replacement migrations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the trajectory establishes the recorder-level cause of the stale squashed-migration status and converges on the minimal backward-bookkeeping correction without unnecessarily changing forward migration semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if the trajectory finishes by denying that the squashed row must be removed, reverses the requested behavior, or proposes changing forward application or loader graph semantics without a demonstrated need. Resolved and reverted experiments do not trigger the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Cutoff working-tree contents and git diff outrank earlier attempted edits; executed test output outranks claimed verification; direct observations of executor and loader code outrank speculative explanations. A final clean tree means temporary edits are evidence of reasoning only, not an applied fix.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for merely finding replacement-related code, confusing graph membership with persisted recorder state, treating a proposed edit as completed work, or adding a symmetric forward-recording change that the bug does not require.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require correctly identifying that the replacement branch removes the replaced migration records but can leave the squashed migration's own recorder row present. Score 5 additionally requires a source-grounded account of how that own row can be recorded or maintained.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect source reads, reasoning, cutoff-visible file contents, and tests concerning MigrationExecutor.unapply_migration(), record_migration(), check_replacements(), and the recorder rows for a replacement migration and its replaced migrations.
metadata.non_evidence: Repository browsing volume, repeated restatement of the issue, failed environment setup, unexecuted test scripts, and assertions about behavior unsupported by source or command output are not independently creditworthy.
metadata.oracle_test: With the squash file and the files it replaces all still available, after the replacement has been represented as applied and is migrated backward, the recorder must contain neither the replacement migration key nor any of its replaced migration keys. Forward recording behavior should remain otherwise unchanged.
metadata.stage: early trajectory diagnosis and patch planning

scale.1: No coherent task-causal diagnosis is reached, or the final position confidently asserts the opposite bookkeeping behavior.
scale.2: Finds migration replacement code but remains materially confused about which records persist, primarily pursues unrelated graph or environment theories, and gives no viable focused remedy.
scale.3: Identifies a likely asymmetry in replacement-migration recording or proposes deleting an additional record, but leaves the persisted-state mechanism unresolved, retains significant contradictions, or proposes unnecessary production-code scope.
scale.4: Correctly explains that backward handling removes replaced records while failing to remove the squashed migration's own record and identifies the focused unapply-side remedy, but lacks either the full source chain, a clear scope boundary, or reliable validation.
scale.5: Correctly and consistently traces the full invariant: replacement application records the replaced statuses, replacement maintenance can record the squash key, and the replacement unapply branch currently deletes only the replaced keys; it therefore targets deletion of the squash key as well, avoids unrelated forward-semantic changes, and any claimed implementation or validation is supported by cutoff-visible evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly diagnoses squashed-migration unapply bookkeeping

applies_when: The visible trajectory proposes, executes, or inspects a source change to recorder bookkeeping when backward-executing a migration with a nonempty replaces list.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements or precisely specifies the replacement path in MigrationExecutor.unapply_migration() so that it records every replaced migration key and the replacement migration's own key as unapplied, while leaving ordinary backward execution and forward recording unchanged.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the adopted design deletes only replaced keys, deletes only the replacement key, puts the own-key call only in the ordinary path, removes the replaced-key loop, or changes loader or graph state instead of recorder state. Cap at 3 when the own-key remedy is endorsed but its placement or preservation of the replaced-key loop remains materially ambiguous. A later visible incompatible source state overrides an earlier proposed edit.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible final source excerpt or diff is strongest. A successfully executed exact edit command, complete replacement snippet, or unambiguous code-level specification is also authoritative for the adopted design when its surrounding explanation endorses the same change.
