reference_golden_rubrics.title: Strength of regression and compatibility protection

applies_when: The trajectory inspects or changes the Python interpreter arguments used to start Django's autoreloader child process.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible applied production implementation reconstructs each parent sys._xoptions entry from its value, places valid CPython -X arguments in the common interpreter prefix before the module or script target, preserves warning options and launcher control flow, and verifies the resulting child semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when malformed -X reconstruction is also copied into or substituted for special launcher fallback branches, creating multiple inconsistent command prefixes or bypassing their intentional executable selection. Cap at 2 when the active code places -X arguments after the execution target, emits one argv element containing an embedded '-X ' prefix, or a real child invocation rejects or fails to preserve the generated option. Cap at 3 when the common-prefix implementation correctly handles only one of valueless True and explicit non-True values.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible applied source or unified diff outranks earlier edits, generated patch files, simulations, and narrative claims. Read the actual condition used by the serializer: testing the option value is authoritative, while testing whether '=' occurs in the option name does not establish value preservation. Execution of the exact argv produced by the active get_child_arguments() implementation outranks list inspection. Existing launcher control flow is authoritative for determining whether special executable fallbacks were preserved.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for a serializer that appears value-aware because it iterates over items but actually branches on key spelling, for key-only propagation that discards explicit values, for True rendered as name=True, for embedded-space or post-target arguments, and for duplicating malformed prefix logic across launcher branches. It also prevents hand-built formatting examples from being treated as execution of the active production command.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require visible applied production code that branches on each sys._xoptions value, emits a valueless argument when the value is exactly True, emits name=value for an explicit non-True value, and performs this work at the common interpreter-prefix boundary without reconstructing special launcher branches. Score 5 additionally requires semantic child-process verification of both forms.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final get_child_arguments() source or diff and identify the exact expression controlling serialization. Correct logic distinguishes value is True from an explicit value; logic such as '=' in key, iteration over keys alone, or a generic truthiness check is insufficient. Confirm that the resulting options follow the Python executable and existing interpreter options but precede -m, the script path, and application arguments, and that Windows executable or script-entrypoint fallbacks were not rewritten merely to inject the options.
metadata.oracle_test: For sys._xoptions equal to {'utf8': True, 'example': 'value'}, the common Python prefix must be semantically equivalent to [sys.executable, '-Xutf8', '-Xexample=value'] before any -m or script target. Separate pairs ['-X', 'utf8'] and ['-X', 'example=value'] are acceptable when real CPython execution validates them. The child must report {'utf8': True, 'example': 'value'}, existing -W options must remain, and intentional launcher-executable fallbacks must remain unchanged.

scale.1: An applied propagation attempt combines incorrect serialization with branch-specific duplication or replacement of launcher command construction, causing inconsistent prefixes or risking ordinary child startup and executable fallback behavior.
scale.2: The change is localized or otherwise avoids broad launcher corruption, but its active argv is invalid or misplaced: a real child rejects or loses an option, an argument embeds '-X ' as one string, options follow the module or script target, or neither True nor explicit values is reliably reconstructed.
scale.3: The applied common-prefix change preserves existing launcher and -W behavior and correctly supports one sys._xoptions form, but not both; examples include forwarding keys while dropping explicit values or preserving explicit values while serializing True as name=True. Uncorroborated final repairs and formatting-only demonstrations remain here.
scale.4: Visible applied production code branches on option values, correctly serializes both valueless True and explicit non-True entries in the common interpreter prefix, preserves -W handling and existing launcher branches, but lacks decisive execution of the active generated argv covering both forms.
scale.5: Meets score 4 and visibly executes the active get_child_arguments() argv, or an equivalent focused repository test, with a real child interpreter reporting both the valueless and valued sys._xoptions entries while existing argument paths remain covered.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Value-aware and branch-safe reconstruction of CPython -X options

applies_when: The trajectory inspects or changes the construction of the Python child-process command used by Django's autoreloader.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible applied production change preserves the parent interpreter's sys._xoptions in the reloader child command with valid CPython syntax, correct interpreter-option ordering, and no regression to existing module, script, warning-option, or Windows launcher paths.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible code emits a valueless True entry as name=True, places -X arguments after -m or the script path, or a real subprocess rejects or fails to preserve the option. Score 1 if the change also rewrites or duplicates launcher branches in a way that drops arguments, changes the selected executable, or otherwise regresses ordinary child startup.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied repository code and observed diffs outrank explanations. A real child-interpreter invocation showing sys._xoptions outranks a test that merely searches the constructed list. Existing control flow in get_child_arguments() is authoritative when assessing whether Windows executable and script-entrypoint fallbacks were preserved.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for proposed-only fixes, key iteration that silently loses explicit values, invalid boolean serialization such as -Xutf8=True, single argv elements containing an embedded '-X ' prefix, post-script option insertion, and broad launcher rewrites masked by optimistic manual-test claims.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require an applied production-code change that correctly handles both sys._xoptions values equal to True and explicit non-True values while placing interpreter options before the execution target.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied diff or observed source for get_child_arguments() and any altered launcher branches. Verify that -X arguments occur immediately after the Python executable and before -m, a script path, or application arguments; valueless entries are emitted as -Xname or as the two arguments -X and name; valued entries are emitted as -Xname=value or as -X and name=value.
metadata.non_evidence: Exploration volume, completion claims, generated patch files, syntax-only checks, tests that mutate sys._xoptions and only assert string presence, and statements that a format works without child-interpreter output are not evidence of semantic propagation.
metadata.oracle_test: For a parent state such as sys._xoptions == {'utf8': True, 'example': 'value'}, the child Python prefix must be semantically equivalent to [sys.executable, '-Xutf8', '-Xexample=value'] before the module or script target. The child must observe {'utf8': True, 'example': 'value'}, existing -W options must remain present, and unrelated Windows entrypoint behavior must remain intact.

scale.1: No relevant production change is visibly applied, or the active change structurally regresses child startup by corrupting executable selection, duplicating argument construction, dropping existing arguments, or breaking launcher fallback branches.
scale.2: A localized production change attempts propagation but is semantically invalid or misplaced, such as serializing a valueless True entry as name=True, constructing an argv element with an embedded '-X ' prefix, or appending interpreter options after the module or script target.
scale.3: A localized applied change places -X options before the execution target and preserves existing control flow, but only forwards option names and therefore drops explicit sys._xoptions values; it handles the motivating valueless flag but not the full observable contract.
scale.4: The applied change correctly serializes both valueless True entries and explicit values, places them before the execution target, and preserves warning, module, script, and launcher behavior, but lacks decisive task-relevant execution evidence covering both forms.
scale.5: Meets score 4 and includes focused visible verification in which a child interpreter receives both a valueless and a valued -X option and reports the corresponding sys._xoptions, or an equivalent repository test proves the same behavior while covering existing argument paths.

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or modifies code that forwards Python -X options through Django's autoreloader.

scale.2: A forwarding attempt is visible but is at the wrong boundary, has invalid ordering or serialization, or breaks the existing interpreter argument construction.

applies_when: The reported AttributeError arises while a function decorator is used through Django's method_decorator().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Observable analysis correctly traces the failure to _multi_decorate() passing a functools.partial of the bound method into the user decorator, where code such as func.__name__ cannot access ordinary function metadata.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory continues to assert that the principal failure occurs in _update_method_wrapper() or because functools.wraps raises while copying attributes after visible evidence shows the exception occurs inside the user's wrapper closure.
metadata.evidence_authority: A reproduced traceback or runtime inspection showing the decorator receives functools.partial outranks unsupported explanations about the decorator itself, _update_method_wrapper(), or wraps() failing during decoration.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a partial decorator, a decorator-returned partial, or outer wrapper metadata propagation for the actual partial bound-method argument captured by the user's decorator.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires locating the runtime source at bound_method = partial(method.__get__(self, type(self))) followed by dec(bound_method), not merely observing that partial lacks __name__.
metadata.judge_focus: Traceback, runtime type inspection, and reasoning that connects partial(method.__get__(...)) to the decorator's captured func and the failing func.__name__ access.
metadata.oracle_test: In the reported logger example, the first decoration-time call may receive _update_method_wrapper's dummy function, but the invocation-time call receives functools.partial(<bound method Test.hello_world ...>); accessing that object's __name__ raises AttributeError.

scale.1: No causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis unrelated to the observed AttributeError.
scale.2: Recognizes that functools.partial lacks __name__ but attributes the failure to the wrong call site or mechanism.
scale.3: Connects the failure generally to _multi_decorate() passing a partial into the decorator, without a complete runtime trace.
scale.4: Accurately traces construction, decoration, closure capture, and invocation of the partial-bound method, supported by relevant source inspection or runtime evidence.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis in 4 and explicitly distinguishes invocation-time bound_method handling from _update_method_wrapper's dummy-decoration metadata path, resolving any earlier contradictory hypothesis.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly identifies the runtime partial-metadata failure

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a change intended to prevent decorators used through method_decorator() from receiving a metadata-deficient callable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible repair supplies the invocation-time decorator input with the original method's standard wrapper assignments while retaining a callable, per-instance-bound, attribute-assignable adapter and the existing decorator composition behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for a change confined to `_update_method_wrapper()` when the invocation-time decorator input remains metadata-deficient. Cap at 3 for exposing only `__name__`, passing the raw bound method without addressing decorators that assign attributes, decorating the unbound method in a way that alters binding or timing, or unwrapping the partial without demonstrating equivalent call and composition semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed targeted reproductions and repository tests against the applied code outrank claimed behavior. Source semantics of `partial`, bound methods, `update_wrapper`, and the decorator loop outrank passing examples that omit decorator attribute assignment or composition.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating disappearance of the single AttributeError as sufficient even though the patch copies only one attribute, changes when decorators run, loses instance binding, prevents decorator attribute assignment, or disrupts multiple-decorator behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied change on the invocation-time callable path that preserves the full standard wrapper-assignment contract rather than only synthesizing `__name__`; credit 5 additionally requires visible checks of both the reported failure and existing method-decorator behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the proposed or applied change at `_multi_decorate()` and any demonstrations of the object passed to decorators. Check preservation of standard wrapper assignments, bound invocation, decorator-added attributes, multiple-decorator order, arguments, and return behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: The semantic reference is an attribute-assignable callable for the current instance that invokes `method.__get__(self, type(self))`, carries the original method's normal `functools.WRAPPER_ASSIGNMENTS` before user decorators inspect it, accepts decorator-added attributes, and is then processed in the existing decorator order.

scale.1: No repair relevant to the invocation-time decorator input, or only edits the example decorator to avoid metadata access.
scale.2: Attempts a repair at the dummy metadata-copy path or another non-causal location, leaving the runtime decorator input deficient.
scale.3: Targets the causal invocation path but remains incomplete or semantically risky, such as copying only `__name__`, using a raw bound method, changing decoration timing, unwrapping the adapter, or presenting an unapplied idea without compatibility evidence.
scale.4: Applies a general wrapper-assignment-preserving invocation adapter and demonstrates the reported logger case, while leaving broader decorator assignment or composition compatibility unverified.
scale.5: Meets 4 and visibly verifies preserved invocation arguments and result behavior together with decorator-added attributes and single or multiple decorator compatibility using relevant existing or focused tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repairs the decorator input while preserving binding and wrapper semantics

applies_when: The reported AttributeError occurs while a function decorator is invoked through Django's method_decorator().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible analysis consistently explains that `_multi_decorate()` creates a partial around the instance-bound method, passes that partial into the user decorator, and the returned wrapper later fails because its closure accesses function metadata on the captured partial.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 while the latest reasoning still treats `_update_method_wrapper()`, a partial decorator, a decorator-returned partial, or `wraps()` attribute copying as the principal cause despite visible evidence that the exception occurs in the user's invocation-time closure. Cap at 2 if the trajectory acts on that contradicted diagnosis without revising it.
metadata.evidence_authority: A reproduced invocation traceback and runtime inspection of the object received by the user decorator outrank speculative readings of `functools.wraps`, decorator return types, or `_update_method_wrapper()`. Later evidence-backed corrections outrank earlier hypotheses only when the trajectory stops relying on the contradicted hypothesis.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full diagnosis credit for merely observing that partial lacks `__name__`, or for a late correct sentence embedded in an unresolved sequence of mutually incompatible explanations.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires both the source-level construction-and-decoration chain and a settled distinction between `_update_method_wrapper()` decorating a dummy function for attribute discovery and `_wrapper()` decorating the per-instance partial during invocation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest causal explanation together with source excerpts, tracebacks, and runtime type observations connecting `partial(method.__get__(self, type(self)))`, `dec(bound_method)`, closure capture, and the later `func.__name__` access.
metadata.oracle_test: In the logger example, `_update_method_wrapper()` can call the decorator with an ordinary dummy function without triggering the reported failure. On method invocation, `_wrapper()` constructs `functools.partial(method.__get__(self, type(self)))`, passes it to the decorator, and the resulting closure later evaluates `func.__name__` where `func` is that partial.

scale.1: No relevant causal account, or the account is incompatible with the visible traceback and source.
scale.2: Recognizes missing function metadata on a partial but locates the principal failure in the wrong object, phase, or call path.
scale.3: Identifies the invocation-time partial and `dec(bound_method)` path, but the trace is incomplete or the latest reasoning still retains a contradictory `_update_method_wrapper()`/`wraps()` explanation.
scale.4: Provides a coherent and currently stable construction-to-closure-to-failure trace and distinguishes the dummy metadata path from invocation, but lacks either direct runtime corroboration or an explicit resolution of earlier contradictory claims.
scale.5: Provides the stable trace in 4, corroborates it with both relevant source and runtime or traceback evidence, and explicitly resolves any earlier competing diagnosis without later regression.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Establishes and retains the invocation-time partial-metadata diagnosis

applies_when: Runtime or test evidence exercises a metadata-reading decorator through method_decorator().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible tests or runtime output demonstrate that a wraps-based decorator can read the decorated method's assignments, invoke the method with correct binding, and return the expected result without the reported AttributeError.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the purported test avoids reading the decorator input's metadata, decorates a normal function rather than invoking a method through method_decorator(), or returns the wrong value. Cap at 3 if later output from the same relevant test still raises the original exception.
metadata.evidence_authority: Post-change test output from the repository implementation outranks standalone simulations; explicit assertions outrank success messages or printed output alone.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating absence of an exception in an altered or weakened reproduction as proof that wrapper assignments and method binding are preserved.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible post-change execution of the reported method_decorator path and evidence that the observed name is the original method name, not dummy, inner, or a fallback string.
metadata.judge_focus: A focused regression test or faithful reproduction using method_decorator(), a decorator that observes func.__name__ or related assignments, and an actual instance-method call.
metadata.oracle_test: A class method such as hello_world decorated with method_decorator(logger) must execute successfully, the logger closure must observe func.__name__ == 'hello_world', and the call must preserve normal self binding and the method's return value.

scale.1: No relevant runtime or test evidence is visible.
scale.2: Only pre-change reproduction, partial-object experiments, or an invalid or unfaithful test is visible.
scale.3: A focused post-change example runs without the original exception, but metadata identity or return and binding behavior is not decisively asserted.
scale.4: A faithful post-change test visibly confirms the original method name and successful bound invocation with the expected result.
scale.5: A repository regression test or equally rigorous asserted test confirms the reported behavior, including method identity and return and binding semantics, with visible passing output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Demonstrates the reported behavior with decisive runtime evidence

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the AttributeError raised by a decorator used through method_decorator().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the latest visible causal account consistently identifies the invocation-time partial passed to the user decorator as the metadata-deficient object captured by the returned wrapper.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest account or applied remedy treats _update_method_wrapper(), functools.wraps() copying from the dummy function, a partial decorator, or the final exposed method as the principal failure. Also cap at 2 if a later edit passes the raw bound method, unwraps to .func, or changes only _update_method_wrapper() while claiming that this follows from the diagnosis, unless the conflict is explicitly recognized and corrected. Cap at 3 when the correct path is stated but an incompatible hypothesis remains unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: A faithful invocation traceback or runtime observation of the object received by the user decorator outranks speculation. Relevant source inspection outranks general statements about partial. Later edits and explanations determine whether an earlier correct diagnosis was retained; a later incompatible action is stronger evidence than an unreconciled earlier sentence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents full diagnosis credit for merely noticing that partial lacks __name__, for a correct sentence embedded in unresolved competing theories, or for reasoning that is contradicted by the trajectory's own next implementation step.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicit localization to the invocation-time bound_method construction and dec(bound_method) handoff, together with a closure or call-time explanation for the eventual metadata access.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest reasoning, traceback or runtime inspection, relevant _multi_decorate() source, and any subsequent edit for a consistent chain from partial(method.__get__(...)) through dec(bound_method) to the later metadata access in the decorator closure.
metadata.oracle_test: During method invocation, _wrapper() creates an attribute-settable partial around method.__get__(self, type(self)), passes that partial to the user decorator, and the returned closure later accesses metadata such as func.__name__ on the captured partial. The dummy function used by _update_method_wrapper() is a separate attribute-discovery path.

scale.1: No relevant causal account is visible, or the latest account is incompatible with the observed exception and source path.
scale.2: The trajectory observes missing metadata on a partial but assigns the principal failure to the wrong object or phase, or later acts on such an incompatible diagnosis without correction.
scale.3: The invocation-time partial and decorator handoff are identified, but closure capture, call timing, or the distinction from the dummy metadata path remains incomplete or contradicted by unresolved later reasoning.
scale.4: The latest account coherently traces partial construction, dec(bound_method), closure capture, and call-time metadata access, and no later visible action contradicts that account.
scale.5: The stable account in 4 is directly corroborated by relevant source plus faithful runtime or traceback evidence and explicitly distinguishes the invocation path from _update_method_wrapper()'s dummy-decoration path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Retains the correct invocation-time partial diagnosis

applies_when: The trajectory executes tests, reproductions, or runtime experiments concerning method_decorator() and callable metadata.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate the strongest visible executable evidence from the latest repository state that the decorator receives the original method metadata while bound invocation and return behavior remain correct.

Cap at 2 if the purported validation avoids method_decorator(), avoids reading metadata on the decorator input, uses a defective reproduction whose own unrelated error prevents the target behavior from being observed, or the latest faithful run still raises the original exception or misbinds self. Credit 5 requires relevant repository regression tests and broader wrapper-contract evidence.

scale.1: No usable executable evidence is visible, or the attempted command or test is invalid, unrelated, or visibly misreported.
scale.2: Only the pre-change failure, an isolated partial experiment, or an unfaithful or still-failing post-change scenario is visible.
scale.3: A useful causal experiment is visible without an applied repair, or an applied focused scenario runs successfully but lacks decisive assertions for metadata identity, binding, or result behavior.
scale.4: Against the visibly applied change, a faithful focused test or reproduction confirms that the decorator observes the original method metadata and that bound invocation returns the expected result.
scale.5: Meets 4 and also shows passing relevant repository tests plus asserted coverage of the broader wrapper contract, such as standard assignments, decorator-added attributes, or multiple-decorator compatibility.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Builds decisive executable evidence for the metadata repair

applies_when: The task requires a source-code or test change in the repository.

Repository status or git diff outranks prose summaries of changes. An explicit execution-stopping error establishes blockage only when no later visible step resumes productive work.

scale.1: No explicit execution-stopping failure is visible at the cutoff.
scale.2: An execution-stopping failure occurred, but later visible work clearly recovered and resumed productive implementation or verification.
scale.3: An execution-stopping failure remains unrecovered, but a usable task-relevant applied diff or complete patch was already visible before it.
scale.4: An execution-stopping failure remains unrecovered before any usable artifact, but the visible prefix preserves a complete, actionable, task-correct edit plan identifying both the required behavior and the concrete code location.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unrecovered execution blockage before a usable repository artifact

applies_when: A cutoff-visible patch or concrete edit proposal changes database time-zone preparation behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements or specifies a minimal PostgreSQL-side classification that preserves named zones while retaining sign reversal for supported standalone offsets, without altering unrelated timezone APIs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A malformed or absent final diff, code that flips both signs sequentially, or code that changes the fixed-offset behavior caps credit at 2; preservation limited to only one literal example caps credit at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final repository diff or terminal unified diff outranks prose and scratch-script copies; a frozen empty git diff or later restoration contradicts claims that edits remain applied.
metadata.failure_mode: Overfitting to one timezone literal, changing timezone._get_timezone_name() globally, or treating every string containing '+' or '-' as a numeric offset.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a cutoff-visible production-code change that leaves Etc/GMT-10 and Etc/GMT+10 unchanged while still mapping standalone +10 to -10 and -10 to +10.
metadata.judge_focus: Cutoff-visible changes to django/db/backends/postgresql/operations.py, especially _prepare_tzname_delta(), and any directly necessary imports or helpers.
metadata.oracle_test: The production helper satisfies named-zone preservation and standalone-offset sign inversion, and Trunc()/Extract() continue to use that helper through PostgreSQL _convert_field_to_tz().

scale.1: No usable production-code change is visible, or the visible change is syntactically invalid or semantically opposite.
scale.2: A concrete change targets the right helper but is incomplete, contradicted by the cutoff state, or breaks standalone-offset conversion.
scale.3: A plausible PostgreSQL change preserves Etc/GMT names and retains basic offsets, but its classification is unnecessarily narrow, weakly justified, or misses supported offset forms.
scale.4: A focused, valid PostgreSQL change robustly distinguishes named zones from standalone offsets and preserves existing conversion behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise PostgreSQL implementation boundary

applies_when: The trajectory contains investigation or reasoning about why script-and-region language prefixes return 404.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that LocaleMiddleware reaches translation.get_language_from_path(), whose language_code_prefix_re in django/utils/translation/trans_real.py accepts only one optional hyphen/@ component and therefore fails before LocalePrefixPattern can resolve prefixes such as en-latn-us or en-Latn-US.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If visible evidence later shows the proposed cause does not reproduce, or the trajectory continues to attribute the failure primarily to LocalePrefixPattern, to_locale(), translation catalogs, or case normalization without reconciling that evidence, credit is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed repository source and executed reproductions outrank unsupported speculation; a full request-flow reproduction outranks regex-only intuition.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards broad i18n exploration or a plausible but downstream diagnosis as though it had isolated the actual parser boundary.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require locating language_code_prefix_re in trans_real.py and explaining that its single optional suffix is the causal limitation.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection, regex experiments, request-flow tracing, and conclusions connecting LocaleMiddleware, get_language_from_path(), and language_code_prefix_re.
metadata.oracle_test: The original prefix regex matches /en-us/ but not /en-latn-us/ or /en-Latn-US/; get_language_from_path() consequently returns no path language for the latter tags even when they are configured in LANGUAGES.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or the visible conclusion is materially wrong.
scale.2: Recognizes a language-prefix parsing or normalization problem but does not isolate the responsible function and regex, or retains conflicting explanations.
scale.3: Finds get_language_from_path() or language_code_prefix_re and notes multi-subtag failure, but does not clearly connect it to the middleware and i18n_patterns request flow.
scale.4: Correctly isolates the one-suffix regex limitation in trans_real.py and explains why both lowercase and BCP 47 case-form script-region paths fail.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis in anchor 4 and confirms it with visible before-change evidence at both the regex/function level and the configured request-language flow, while ruling out misleading alternatives.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly localizes the failure to URL language-prefix extraction

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or changes Django's extraction of language codes from locale-prefixed URL paths.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work applies a production change that extracts the complete configured language tag from only the first URL segment, preserves the parser's capture and delimiter contracts, and validates target, legacy, and route-boundary behavior with evidence connected to the changed Django code.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An applied edit that visibly returns the wrong capture, includes the leading slash, consumes later route content, rejects the reported configured script-and-region forms, or is proven to turn an unsupported route segment into a language through fallback scores 1. A failure caused only by missing dependencies, an invalid test target, stale imports, or settings that do not satisfy the assertion is not a behavioral contradiction. If the claimed edit differs from the latest visible file, score at most 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible repository content or git diff determines what is implemented. A passing focused repository test against that content outranks an execution importing the changed Django module, which outranks static inspection, which outranks a separately hard-coded regex demonstration or narrative claim. A failed ad hoc assertion is a product contradiction only when its settings, cache state, imported source, input, and expected result are visible and consistent with the repository contract.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding an intended edit as implemented work, treating hard-coded regex experiments as execution of Django, mistaking malformed test setup for a regression, overlooking capture or alternation errors, and assigning the same low score to an absent patch and a visibly destructive production patch.
metadata.hard_gate: Any score above 2 requires a visible applied production edit in the parser reached by get_language_from_path(). Score 4 additionally requires authoritative evidence against the actual changed code for both a script-and-region prefix and representative compatibility or boundary behavior. Score 5 requires a durable focused repository regression test and a passing relevant repository test command.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest production definition used by get_language_from_path(), its consumed and captured text, and checks that execute that definition. Confirm support for language-script-region tags and preservation of simple tags, language-region tags, slash/end boundaries, and unsupported route-segment behavior.
metadata.non_evidence: Repository browsing, RFC restatement, dependency installation, future plans, assertions without visible setup, hard-coded copies of the proposed regex, and test commands that fail before collecting or executing relevant behavior do not establish correctness.
metadata.oracle_test: Given a configured tag such as en-latn-us, the parser must supply that complete first segment to normal supported-language resolution for lowercase and conventional BCP 47 casing. It must still accept simple and language-region prefixes, terminate at the first slash or end of the path, preserve the capture consumed by get_language_from_path(), and avoid broad matching that makes unrelated route text resolve through a generic-language fallback.

scale.1: A production edit is visible and decisively violates the task contract: the target prefix remains unusable, the consumed or captured value is wrong, later path content can be consumed, or authoritative evidence establishes a legacy or unsupported-route regression.
scale.2: No usable production edit is visible in the latest repository state; the trajectory may localize the parser or propose a plausible change, but implementation credit is unavailable.
scale.3: A plausible production edit is visibly applied and has no decisive contract violation, but evidence against the actual changed Django code is absent or insufficient to establish both target behavior and compatibility or first-segment boundaries.
scale.4: A bounded, capture-preserving production edit is visible, and authoritative checks against the changed Django code establish the script-and-region behavior plus representative legacy or boundary behavior without a valid unresolved contradiction; focused durable regression coverage and a passing relevant repository test command are not both present.
scale.5: All score-4 requirements are met, and the repository visibly includes a focused regression test for script-and-region extraction with compatibility or negative-boundary coverage, with the relevant repository test command passing.

Cap at 2 when checks cover only F, inspect __module__, or merely compile the file. A passing syntax check cannot override a failing deconstruct assertion.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful focused repository tests or direct assertions on real Django expression classes outrank proposed assertions; concrete unexecuted test diffs outrank vague test plans; syntax checks, module-name prints, and import-only checks are indirect evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating compilation, dependency installation, module metadata, or vague future testing intent as proof of migration serialization behavior while still recognizing a concrete repository-specific test design before execution.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a concrete assertion or test change for at least one newly targeted class. Credit above 3 requires successful execution reaching a semantic deconstruct assertion. Credit 5 requires representative coverage across distinct expression families and preserved payload or reconstruction.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect existing deconstruction-test discovery, concrete expected-string updates, direct deconstruct tuple assertions, import resolution, reconstruction checks, focused test commands, and their visible results.
metadata.non_evidence: Generic statements that tests will be run, package installation, py_compile alone, printing class modules, toy deconstructible classes, and checks limited to the preexisting F behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Representative public expressions deconstruct to importable django.db.models names with unchanged args and kwargs, reconstruct equivalently, existing Value expectations are updated where applicable, and F continues to emit django.db.models.F.

scale.1: No concrete task-specific verification is visible, or the latest relevant check fails before exercising deconstruction behavior.
scale.2: Verification is only indirect or prospective, such as syntax checks, module inspection, F-only checks, or a vague test plan without concrete assertions.
scale.3: Concrete repository test edits or direct assertions are specified for newly targeted classes, but they are not successfully executed or cover only one narrow behavior.
scale.4: At least one focused semantic check succeeds for a newly targeted class and verifies the shortened path plus payload or importability, but representative family coverage is incomplete.
scale.5: Successful focused tests cover representative expression families, simplified importable paths, preserved args and kwargs, reconstruction or migration serialization, and continued F behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Expression deconstruction verification quality

applies_when: The trajectory edits or presents a concrete patch for expression deconstruction paths.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements valid, narrowly placed deconstruction-path changes so targeted public expressions return django.db.models.<ClassName> while preserving their constructors and runtime expression behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for malformed quoting, misplaced decorators, duplicated source, invalid indentation, or paths naming classes absent from django.db.models. Cap at 1 when a visible syntax/import failure remains unresolved at cutoff.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final visible diff and successful syntax/import evidence outrank stated intent, generated scripts, or earlier excerpts. Later restoration or correction supersedes earlier malformed edits.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents fixed-line sed corruption, escaped-quote artifacts, invalid decorators on internal classes, and superficially broad changes that leave expressions.py unimportable.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires syntactically valid source and evidence that decorators are attached to the intended classes rather than inserted inside methods or class bodies.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or file excerpts showing decorators or equivalent deconstruct logic immediately before the intended class definitions, with valid Python syntax and no unrelated class-body changes.
metadata.oracle_test: Calling deconstruct() on each supported public expression yields ('django.db.models.<ConcreteClass>', original_args, original_kwargs), and importing that path resolves to the same class; expression SQL and constructor semantics remain unchanged.

scale.1: No viable implementation is visible, or the latest source is demonstrably invalid and unrecovered.
scale.2: Some intended path edits are visible, but placement, syntax, class selection, or completeness has material defects.
scale.3: A valid narrow implementation covers at least one additional appropriate public expression but omits a substantial part of the task boundary.
scale.4: A valid implementation covers nearly all intended public expression classes with only a minor omission or unsupported edge.
scale.5: A clean, syntactically valid, minimal implementation covers the full public expression boundary, preserves F, avoids internal-only classes, and changes no unrelated behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Safe and precise expression-path implementation

applies_when: The task concerns shortening Django model-expression deconstruction paths to a public import location.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work correctly identifies and implements simplified deconstruction paths for the relevant expression classes exposed through django.db.models, while preserving constructor serialization and avoiding unsupported paths for internal-only classes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An explicit unrepaired parser, indentation, or import failure caused by the edits caps the score at 2. Visibly malformed quoting, misplaced decorators, duplicated source, or decorators inserted inside class bodies without an executed failure caps it at 3. A shortened path that is not actually importable from django.db.models prevents scores above 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed deconstruct assertions and focused tests outrank syntax-only checks; syntax or import checks outrank visual claims; the actual diff or displayed source outranks stated plans. Repository exports determine whether a shortened path is valid.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad but arbitrary decorator insertion, changing only Expression or the already-correct F precedent, treating an inventory as applied work, or accepting syntactically broken edits because the intended approach sounded plausible.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires applied source changes covering the task's public expression scope, not only a proposed list or a change to one precedent class. Credit of 5 additionally requires direct behavioral validation of representative paths and preservation of constructor arguments.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the discovered django.db.models exports, the deconstructible mechanism, concrete source edits, and any direct deconstruct(), import, syntax, or focused test evidence visible by the cutoff.
metadata.non_evidence: Repository browsing alone, repeated restatement of the ticket, unexecuted future plans, package installation, and class-name enumeration without tying classes to actual public exports or applied behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: For each targeted expression class publicly re-exported by django.db.models, deconstruct() should return django.db.models.<ClassName> with unchanged constructor args and kwargs, and that path must resolve to the same class; internal-only expression classes should not receive unsupported public paths.

scale.1: No task-causal mechanism is established, or the visible approach uses invalid paths, unrelated classes, or destructive edits with no coherent recoverable implementation.
scale.2: The simplified-path mechanism is recognized, but coverage is materially incomplete or indiscriminate; alternatively, relevant edits exist but an explicit unrepaired syntax, indentation, or import failure contradicts them.
scale.3: The public-expression scope and correct mechanism are substantially identified, with either a coherent complete plan or partial applied work, but implementation is incomplete, visibly malformed, or lacks enough evidence to establish correct coverage.
scale.4: A coherent implementation covers the relevant public expression classes with importable simplified paths and no visible source corruption, but comprehensive direct deconstruct behavior or regression validation is still absent.
scale.5: The relevant public expression set is implemented precisely, constructor serialization is preserved, internal-only classes are not given unsupported aliases, and focused executed checks or tests confirm the shortened paths and importability without regressions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Public expression deconstruction-path coverage

applies_when: The trajectory encounters failed edits, syntax errors, import failures, dependency failures, or conflicting evidence while implementing the change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Responds to contradictory evidence by isolating environmental failures from source defects, restoring corrupted edits when necessary, and re-establishing a clean, testable patch before proceeding.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the trajectory acknowledges a source corruption but continues without restoring and rechecking it. Cap at 1 when the last visible state has an unresolved parser/import error caused by the edits.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest successful syntax/import/test output and final diff supersede earlier mistakes. Explicit IndentationError, SyntaxError, or malformed-source excerpts remain authoritative until a later visible restoration and recheck.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding high confidence to trajectories that repeatedly generate malformed decorators, confuse dependency errors with implementation success, or abandon the repository in a broken state.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an observed contradiction followed by a concrete correction and successful revalidation, or—when no contradiction occurs—a clean diff plus successful validation showing preventive control.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible use of git diff/status, restoration of malformed source, syntax/import checks after edits, distinction between missing dependencies and code errors, and final confirmation that only intended source and test changes remain.
metadata.oracle_test: The final visible expressions.py compiles and imports, the focused deconstruction checks pass, and the final diff contains only intentional path and corresponding test expectation changes.

scale.1: Contradictory evidence is ignored and the latest visible source remains broken or unverifiable.
scale.2: Problems are noticed or partially repaired, but no successful post-repair validation establishes a sound state.
scale.3: The trajectory restores or corrects a significant mistake and obtains basic syntax or diff confirmation.
scale.4: It cleanly recovers, distinguishes environment issues from source defects, and obtains successful focused validation with a controlled diff.
scale.5: It demonstrates disciplined recovery or prevention throughout: malformed attempts are fully reverted, corrected changes are revalidated semantically, and the final visible diff is minimal and regression-safe.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression control and recovery from contradictory evidence

applies_when: The task concerns shortening deconstruction paths for expression classes available through django.db.models.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly derives the target expression boundary from public django.db.models exports and applies simplified deconstruction paths to that boundary without assigning unsupported public paths to internal-only classes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest source is visibly malformed, an explicit edit-caused syntax or import failure remains unresolved, or paths are assigned to names not available from django.db.models. Cap at 3 if work remains only an inventory or plan, or if applied coverage is limited to Expression, F, or one additional class.
metadata.evidence_authority: The repository's visible django.db.models exports determine public eligibility. The latest valid source or diff determines applied coverage and outranks inventories or plans. A successful import or deconstruct check outranks visual inference. Earlier edits cease to count after a visible restoration.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equating a broad class-name list with applied work, rewarding Expression-only changes as task-complete, or treating indiscriminate decoration of every class in expressions.py as correct public coverage.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a repository-backed mapping between public exports and intended path changes. Credit above 3 requires valid applied changes for multiple newly targeted public classes. Credit 5 requires the complete eligible public boundary to be applied and behaviorally checked.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible django.db.models expression imports or __all__, the exact-type behavior of the deconstructible path override, and the latest source showing which public classes actually received class-qualified django.db.models paths.
metadata.oracle_test: Each eligible expression class publicly re-exported by django.db.models deconstructs to django.db.models.<ConcreteClass> with unchanged constructor arguments; F remains correct, while internal-only expression classes are not given nonexistent public paths.

scale.1: No coherent public-scope model is visible, or the approach relies on invalid paths, unrelated classes, or unrecovered source corruption.
scale.2: The shortening mechanism is recognized, but scope is unsupported, limited to the existing F precedent or Expression alone, or indiscriminately includes internal classes.
scale.3: The public boundary is derived from repository exports and the required per-class behavior is substantially understood, but implementation is absent, covers only one newly targeted class, or remains incomplete.
scale.4: Valid applied changes cover multiple representative public expression families with class-qualified importable paths and no visible corruption, but one or more eligible public classes or direct behavioral checks remain missing.
scale.5: The complete eligible public expression boundary is implemented with importable django.db.models.<ConcreteClass> paths, F is preserved, internal-only classes are excluded, and representative deconstruct checks confirm the coverage.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Public expression scope and applied path coverage

applies_when: The trajectory evaluates side effects, existing behavior, or conflicting evidence after proposing a router-aware MigrationRecorder change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory preserves existing MigrationRecorder behavior when routers allow migration or express no opinion, avoids unrelated API and call-site changes, and responds correctly to failed or contradictory experiments.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for overwriting the module with malformed code, globally suppressing recorder behavior, changing constructors and all consumers without necessity, installing an unrelated Django version as validation, or claiming success while visible output still reports a created denied table or missing-table exception.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository diff, targeted existing-test results, and direct table/query observations outrank narrative assurances; later corrected evidence outranks earlier failed experiments only when the cause and correction are explicit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a narrow demonstration that solves the denied case by disabling normal migrations, destabilizing public internals, or ignoring contradictory runtime results.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an allowed/no-opinion regression check or a source-grounded argument preserving that path, plus no unresolved syntax/import/control-flow damage in the visible implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible evidence that no-router/None/True routing still creates and uses django_migrations, existing method contracts remain stable, changes are limited to relevant production and test files, and failed experiments lead to corrected hypotheses rather than unsupported success claims.
metadata.oracle_test: The patch changes only the router-denied behavior: absent routers and routers returning None or True continue to use django_migrations exactly as before, while False is safely honored.

scale.1: No compatibility consideration, or visible changes broadly break normal MigrationRecorder behavior.
scale.2: Mentions regressions but leaves major API churn, malformed code, or contradictory evidence unresolved.
scale.3: Keeps the main allowed path plausibly intact but lacks direct regression evidence or contains avoidable implementation churn.
scale.4: Shows a localized change, preserves allowed/no-opinion behavior, and handles failed experiments honestly, with only minor untested edge cases.
scale.5: Demonstrates minimal compatibility-preserving scope, credible allowed/no-opinion regression protection, and explicit recovery from any earlier contradictory or invalid evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility and regression protection

applies_when: The task concerns MigrationRecorder behavior under database-router migration restrictions.
The visible trajectory investigates or changes recorder schema, read, record, or call-site behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether cutoff-visible applied work coherently makes MigrationRecorder respect the configured migration router on the actual production call path without breaking recorder behavior on databases where migration is allowed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if visible execution after the change shows a denied database still receiving recorder schema or records, an allowed database losing normal recorder behavior, or an attributable syntax, import, or runtime failure. Also cap at 1 when the apparent fix is inert because its required router dependency is never supplied on the visible production call path.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current production-file contents or git diff outrank plans and narrated claims. Subsequent repository-backed executions outrank ad hoc assertions and printed expectations. An observed production-path failure outranks an earlier passing mock or isolated helper check. Installation output and failures caused solely by missing test-runner dependencies are not evidence about patch semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for proposed-only fixes, self-confirming scripts, checks disconnected from real callers, malformed broad rewrites, and denial guards that accidentally disable the allowed path.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a syntactically coherent applied production change whose router decision is reached by normal MigrationRecorder usage without relying on an optional object or argument that visible callers never provide. Credit of 5 additionally requires credible two-sided behavioral validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect production-file edits and subsequent file reads for the router decision, connection alias, Migration model or equivalent app/model hints, every affected recorder operation, and activation from ordinary callers. Inspect trustworthy executions for both a denied alias and an allowed alias.
metadata.oracle_test: With a router denying migration on one alias and allowing it on another, ordinary MigrationRecorder usage must avoid creating, reading, inserting, deleting, or flushing django_migrations on the denied alias as appropriate to the invoked operation, while retaining normal schema creation and record lifecycle behavior on the allowed alias.

scale.1: An applied change is visibly nonfunctional: it is malformed or inert on normal callers, or execution demonstrates denied-database mutation/access, broken allowed-database behavior, or another attributable runtime failure.
scale.2: An applied production change is active but has a concrete unresolved causal defect, such as inconsistent guards across operations, incorrect router inputs, or a caller contract that is only partially wired; no definitive execution establishes the complete intended behavior.
scale.3: The trajectory has a sound diagnosis or partial implementation with no cutoff-visible regression, but no complete active production fix is established; alternatively, a coherent applied fix remains materially unvalidated and has no concrete visible defect.
scale.4: A coherent production-path-active fix covers the relevant recorder operations and preserves the allowed path, with credible task-specific validation of at least one side and no visible contradiction, but complete two-sided or repository regression validation is absent.
scale.5: A coherent production-path-active fix is credibly validated on both denied and allowed aliases and by relevant repository regression tests, showing no recorder access where migration is denied and unchanged recorder lifecycle behavior where it is allowed.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: MigrationRecorder router fix is active, coherent, and behavior-preserving

applies_when: The trajectory creates, modifies, proposes, or runs tests for MigrationRecorder routing behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory supplies task-specific tests or runtime evidence that distinguish a router-denied connection from an allowed connection and directly observe both physical table state and recorder API behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if output shows django_migrations created on the denied database, an OperationalError such as 'no such table' after a denied operation, tests importing the wrong package, or assertions that contradict the printed physical table list.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing targeted test under tests/runtests.py against the modified checkout is strongest; a correctly configured isolated script importing the checkout is next; printed expectations, mocked permission values alone, or tests run against a separately installed Django release are weak.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents custom scripts from receiving strong credit when they only test the router itself, accidentally reuse a database containing an old table, import a pip-installed Django, or label contradictory output as success.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evidence for both a denied database and an allowed/default database, rather than merely printing router.allow_migrate results or checking a helper property.
metadata.judge_focus: Repository tests using DATABASE_ROUTERS or a correctly installed ConnectionRouter, separate database aliases, and assertions for table absence, empty applied_migrations(), harmless record_applied()/record_unapplied(), and normal creation/recording on an allowed database.
metadata.oracle_test: With a router returning False for the secondary alias, ensure_schema(), record_applied(), and record_unapplied() leave django_migrations absent and applied_migrations() empty; with permission True or no opinion, schema creation and applied/unapplied recording continue to work.

scale.1: No task-specific test or runtime evidence.
scale.2: Only checks router return values, importability, or a single superficial path; evidence is invalid or contradictory.
scale.3: Demonstrates one decisive denied-path outcome or supplies a credible focused regression test, but lacks the allowed-path control or complete recorder coverage.
scale.4: Credibly covers denied and allowed databases and checks table creation plus at least one recorder read/write behavior, with no unresolved contradiction.
scale.5: Provides or runs focused repository-quality regression coverage for denied schema creation, applied-state reads, applied/unapplied writes, and the allowed/default control, with clear passing evidence against the modified checkout.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive multi-database regression evidence

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes MigrationRecorder behavior under database-router migration restrictions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measure the severity of cutoff-visible defects that prevent a router-aware MigrationRecorder change from operating correctly through ordinary production callers.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assign the highest severity when an introduced syntax, import, name-resolution, or runtime error breaks an ordinary caller, or when the allowed recorder lifecycle visibly fails. Treat an optional router dependency that ordinary callers do not supply as an inert-guard defect, not as equivalent to an introduced caller crash. Treat an active guard followed by an unguarded schema or record operation as an operation-specific bypass. Do not infer defects from stale experiments or custom router mutation when current production source or later properly configured execution contradicts them.
metadata.evidence_authority: Complete current production-file reads or diffs together with visible ordinary callers have highest authority for activation and control flow. Repository-backed ordinary-path execution and direct table or record observations outrank custom scripts. A custom script is supporting evidence only when it imports the edited repository code, configures routing normally, and observes database state. Narration, printed expectations, dependency installation, test-discovery failures, and harness-only import or settings failures do not establish a production defect.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents neutral investigation from being penalized like broken code, prevents inert optional wiring from being mistaken for an active fix, and distinguishes partial denied-path access from more severe caller or allowed-path failures.
metadata.hard_gate: Severity above 2 requires a concrete cutoff-visible causal defect in applied production code or an attributable execution failure. An omitted patch, truncated source, unsuccessful test setup, or lack of regression coverage alone cannot establish such a defect.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect current production source and ordinary construction sites for whether the router decision is actually reached, whether denied control flow returns before every applicable schema or record query, and whether allowed or no-opinion behavior remains executable. Separate a proven defect from missing validation or proposal-only work.
metadata.oracle_test: Ordinary MigrationRecorder construction must consult the configured router using the active connection and appropriate Migration model information; denial must return before applicable django_migrations schema, read, insert, delete, or flush access, while allowance or no opinion must preserve the existing recorder lifecycle and caller contracts.

scale.1: No production-path defect is established: work is investigative or proposal-only, or the visible applied implementation has no concrete causal defect despite incomplete validation.
scale.2: Applied production work has unresolved viability risk, such as incomplete current source, uncertain ordinary-caller activation, or failed semantic validation, but no specific reachable defect is proven.
scale.3: A concrete localized defect is visible, such as one recorder operation bypassing an otherwise active denial, incomplete model hints, or denied control flow that can still reach a query.
scale.4: The intended guard is demonstrably ineffective on ordinary callers, including an optional router dependency that those callers do not provide, or several recorder operations remain causally incorrect.
scale.5: The change introduces an attributable syntax, import, name-resolution, or runtime failure on an ordinary caller, visibly mutates a denied database despite the active change, or makes the allowed or no-opinion recorder lifecycle unusable.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Production-path defects in the router-aware MigrationRecorder change

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates, implements, or attempts to validate MigrationRecorder behavior under database-router migration restrictions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the reliability of cutoff-visible evidence about the current implementation, distinguishing absent evidence, inconclusive validation attempts, direct semantic contradictions, and credible observations of denied and allowed recorder behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assign 1 when current applied source is definitely malformed or inert on ordinary callers, or post-change execution attributable to the implementation shows django_migrations access on a denied database, a missing-table exception caused by an unguarded denied operation, or failure of the allowed recorder lifecycle. An invalid harness alone cannot establish such a contradiction.
metadata.evidence_authority: An attributable execution through the edited checkout and ordinary MigrationRecorder construction outranks isolated helper output, narrated expectations, or earlier experiments. Direct table and record observations outrank printed router return values. Current source can establish definite syntax, control-flow, or inert-wiring defects. Dependency installation, test discovery failures, missing settings or helper modules, and executions against another installed Django version establish neither success nor semantic failure.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating no evidence as equivalent to disproving the fix, rewarding self-confirming router checks as database validation, or overlooking an allowed-path failure after a denied-path demonstration.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one trustworthy post-change behavioral observation against the edited checkout. Credit of 5 requires both a denied database and an allowed or no-opinion database, including physical table state and recorder API behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the current production source first, then executions performed after that source state. For denied routing, look for direct table introspection and harmless recorder reads or writes; for allowed or no-opinion routing, look for normal schema creation and applied/unapplied record lifecycle behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: With normal router configuration, a denied connection must not create or access django_migrations and its applied-state operations must remain harmless, while an allowed or no-opinion connection must create the table and preserve applied, unapplied, and read behavior.

scale.1: The current applied implementation is definitely malformed or inert, or trustworthy post-change execution directly contradicts required denied- or allowed-path behavior.
scale.2: Applied work has only an invalid, failed, or internally inconsistent validation attempt at cutoff, leaving its claimed behavior unresolved, but no trustworthy execution proves a semantic failure.
scale.3: No applied production change is established, or the current applied change is coherent but has no trustworthy task-specific behavioral result and no concrete visible contradiction.
scale.4: Trustworthy post-change evidence establishes one side of the router contract, or establishes both sides with incomplete recorder-operation coverage, and no stronger evidence contradicts it.
scale.5: Trustworthy validation against the edited checkout establishes denied and allowed or no-opinion behavior, directly observes table state and recorder reads and writes, and includes focused repository regression coverage with no contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reliability of MigrationRecorder router validation

applies_when: The visible trajectory addresses conditional MaxLengthValidator construction in model CharField initialization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible repository work applies the minimal conditional validator change and coherently demonstrates both the no-max-length and explicit-max-length behaviors without unresolved implementation contradictions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved syntax error, duplicate conditional, lost initialization statement, or unintended change to BinaryField caps the score at 2. If executed observations conflict with the claimed behavior and the conflict is not subsequently explained or corrected, cap at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Visible repository content, diffs, and executed command observations outrank plans, summaries, and assertions. A later verified restoration or correction supersedes an earlier accidental edit; otherwise the latest visible repository evidence controls.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents crediting a correct verbal diagnosis, a patch that was later reverted or corrupted, one-sided tests that miss explicit max_length behavior, or claims of success contradicted by visible execution.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a visibly applied conditional in CharField.__init__ that appends MaxLengthValidator only when self.max_length is not None. Score 5 additionally requires coherent executed validation of both branches and visible evidence that the relevant diff has no unintended neighboring change.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible edits or diffs to CharField.__init__, then inspect executed checks showing that CharField() or Value('text')._resolve_output_field() omits MaxLengthValidator while CharField(max_length=N) retains it and the no-length field can be cleaned without the reported TypeError.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended semantics are: Value('test')._resolve_output_field() yields a CharField with no MaxLengthValidator and does not raise the None-limit comparison TypeError during cleaning; CharField(max_length=N) still receives MaxLengthValidator(N); unrelated field initialization remains unchanged.
metadata.stage: implementation and validation at the visible cutoff

scale.1: No relevant applied change is visible, or the visible implementation clearly has the wrong behavior.
scale.2: A relevant edit is applied but is incorrect or remains structurally unsafe, such as an unresolved syntax error, duplicate logic, lost CharField setup, or unintended neighboring-field modification.
scale.3: The core conditional appears correctly applied, but validation is absent, materially incomplete, or contains an unresolved contradiction, so both required semantic branches are not established.
scale.4: The correct minimal conditional is visibly applied and executed evidence establishes the essential no-max-length and explicit-max-length behaviors, but clean-diff or broader coherence evidence remains incomplete or ambiguous.
scale.5: The correct minimal conditional is visibly applied; executed evidence coherently verifies omission for Value-derived or max_length=None CharField, preservation for explicit max_length, and absence of the reported cleaning failure; the visible relevant diff is clean and leaves neighboring behavior unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied CharField validator fix and validation coherence

applies_when: The trajectory contains or proposes runtime checks for Value string output-field resolution or CharField validator behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides decisive runtime evidence that implicit CharField instances created for string Value expressions omit MaxLengthValidator and no longer fail during cleaning, while explicit max_length CharFields still receive the validator.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A post-edit result showing MaxLengthValidator on the implicit Value output field, a TypeError from its clean path, or no validator for CharField(max_length=100) caps credit at 2 unless a later successful rerun visibly supersedes it.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful runtime output from the current edited source outranks assertions in thoughts or test scripts that did not run; later corrected tests override earlier malformed checks.
metadata.failure_mode: Avoids treating syntax checks, printed expectations, failing dependency setup, or incorrectly introspected validator attributes as proof of behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a successful executed check of the Value('test')._resolve_output_field() path after the current edit.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible command output for Value('test')._resolve_output_field(), validator lists or validator types, clean(), and CharField(max_length=positive_integer).
metadata.oracle_test: For `field = Value('test')._resolve_output_field()`, field is CharField, field.max_length is None, no MaxLengthValidator is present, and `field.clean('1', None)` does not raise the original int-versus-None TypeError; `CharField(max_length=100)` has a MaxLengthValidator with limit_value 100.

scale.1: No relevant runtime evidence is present, or the latest relevant execution contradicts the required semantics.
scale.2: Only failed setup, an unexecuted test, or a malformed test is visible, with no successful task-specific result.
scale.3: A successful executed check establishes only one required branch, such as omission for max_length=None or preservation for explicit max_length.
scale.4: Successful executed checks establish both omission for the Value/None case and preservation for explicit max_length.
scale.5: Successful executed checks establish both validator branches and directly demonstrate that the original Value output-field clean path no longer raises the TypeError.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific runtime semantics

applies_when: The visible trajectory implements or tests conditional MaxLengthValidator creation for model CharField.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Establishes that unbounded CharField instances used by string Value resolution omit MaxLengthValidator, explicitly bounded CharFields retain it, and the original invalid cleaning behavior is either directly disproved at runtime or the tested branches are corroborated by an exact current implementation diff.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest successful execution showing MaxLengthValidator on the unbounded Value/default CharField, no MaxLengthValidator on an explicitly bounded CharField, or the original int-versus-None TypeError caps credit at 2. Failed setup and malformed introspection are non-evidence unless they reveal a current production-code error.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful execution against the current edited source outranks prose, printed expectations, and unexecuted scripts. A later successful corrected check supersedes an earlier malformed check. A clean current diff may corroborate successful runtime checks but cannot by itself prove semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating branch-only printed output as equally decisive as end-to-end execution, while avoiding an unfair penalty when successful two-branch runtime checks are independently corroborated by the exact clean implementation diff.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires either successful runtime evidence for Value/default omission, explicit-max preservation, and the original clean path, or successful runtime evidence for both validator branches corroborated by a clean current diff showing only the exact CharField guard.
metadata.judge_focus: Successful post-edit executions inspecting Value('test')._resolve_output_field() or an equivalent default CharField, CharField(max_length=positive_integer), validator types and limits, and the original clean path; inspect a current diff only as corroboration for executed branch checks.
metadata.oracle_test: An unbounded `Value('test')._resolve_output_field()` is a CharField with max_length None and no MaxLengthValidator; `CharField(max_length=100)` has exactly the applicable MaxLengthValidator with limit_value 100; cleaning the unbounded Value output field does not raise the original TypeError.

scale.1: No successful relevant post-edit execution is visible, or the latest authoritative execution contradicts the required semantics.
scale.2: Only failed setup, malformed checks, unexecuted scripts, or runtime evidence exposing a current production-code error is visible.
scale.3: A successful post-edit execution establishes exactly one semantic branch: either omission for an unbounded Value/default CharField or preservation for an explicitly bounded CharField.
scale.4: Successful post-edit executions establish both omission for the Value/default case and preservation for explicit max_length, but neither the original clean path nor a clean exact current diff is visible.
scale.5: Either successful post-edit executions establish both validator branches and show the original Value clean path no longer raises, or successful executions establish both branches and a clean current diff independently corroborates the exact isolated CharField guard.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific semantic validation confidence

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains failed edits, accidental duplicate replacements, syntax errors, misleading tests, or other evidence requiring recovery.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Recognizes and fully repairs transient corruption or contradictory test evidence, then re-establishes a clean targeted source state with credible reruns or diff evidence.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Any latest visible syntax error, duplicate conditional, missing constructor statement, or unresolved collateral BinaryField change caps credit at 2; a clean source excerpt without a rerun can reach at most 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest current diff and successful reruns supersede earlier transient failures only when they visibly cover the affected code; unsupported statements that damage was repaired do not supersede observed corruption.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents an earlier correct intention or passing test from masking later file corruption, and prevents obsolete failed attempts from unfairly overriding demonstrated recovery.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible post-recovery evidence covering every production area known to have been accidentally modified, especially both CharField and BinaryField.
metadata.judge_focus: Chronology of failed edits and errors, restoration commands, later source excerpts, syntax/runtime reruns, and final diff scope.
