Cap at 1 if the visible repository source remains unchanged, is malformed, or still unconditionally overwrites the existing DataFrame index.
metadata.evidence_authority: The applied source diff or visibly confirmed current file contents take precedence over explanations, proposed patches, standalone reimplementations, edits to installed site-packages, and claimed test success. Task-relevant tests may confirm but cannot override contradictory source logic.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the reported unequal-length exception for the full contract and accepting a row-count check that corrupts same-length transformed indexes, or awarding implementation credit for changes made only outside the repository.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible application to the repository source. Credit 5 additionally requires that an existing DataFrame's index is preserved by semantic type, not merely when its length differs from the original input index.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible repository edit to the pandas container-wrapping path and any directly exercised examples. Determine separately what happens for an existing DataFrame and for a non-DataFrame result.
metadata.oracle_test: For this task, a grouped four-row pandas result from a 96-row input must retain its group-key index. More generally, an existing pandas result with the same row count as its input but a reordered or otherwise meaningful index must also retain that output index. An ndarray result may receive the original input index when a DataFrame is created.

scale.1: No valid repository implementation is visible, the edited source is malformed, or an existing DataFrame is still unconditionally reindexed from the original input.
scale.2: An applied workaround avoids some mismatches but preserves the existing DataFrame index only conditionally, such as through a length/equality/exception check, or reconstructs it using the original input index.
scale.3: The trajectory identifies that an existing pandas result should own its index and presents a semantically correct change, but the change is not visibly applied to the repository source.
scale.4: An applied repository change preserves the index of existing DataFrames in the task path, but the visible evidence leaves a material ambiguity in the non-DataFrame construction path or introduces avoidable special-case logic.
scale.5: The applied repository logic cleanly preserves every existing DataFrame's own index while using the original input index only when constructing a pandas container from a non-DataFrame result.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves the row index of an existing pandas transform result

applies_when: The trajectory creates, modifies, or runs tests or reproduction scripts for pandas output wrapping.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides executable evidence that the reported aggregation works under pandas output and that index behavior remains correct for existing DataFrames and non-DataFrame outputs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the claimed verification actually ends in an import, build, dimensionality, or binary-compatibility error. Cap at 3 if tests exercise only differing lengths and omit the same-length/different-index regression risk.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing target-repository tests and the exact issue reproducer outrank standalone reimplementations; faithful direct-function tests outrank conceptual assertions; syntax checks alone establish only parseability.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating output from a copied file in an API-incompatible installed release, a hand-written imitation of the function, or a successful syntax parse as equivalent to target-code regression testing.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires executed evidence after the proposed change, not merely a written test plan or output from an unmodified newer release.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test code, commands, and outputs from the target checkout or a faithful isolated invocation of the target function.
metadata.oracle_test: Evidence should cover: an existing four-row grouped pandas result retaining its date index despite a 96-row original input; an existing same-length DataFrame retaining distinct custom labels; and a dense ndarray receiving the supplied input index. The original FeatureUnion example is decisive when runnable in the target version.

scale.1: No relevant executable evidence is shown.
scale.2: Attempts are visible, but they fail before exercising the changed behavior or use an incompatible environment without a faithful fallback.
scale.3: A faithful direct test or reproducer demonstrates the differing-length aggregation case after the change, but important index or container regressions remain untested.
scale.4: Executed evidence covers the reported aggregation and at least one key regression case, such as same-length custom indexes or ndarray wrapping.
scale.5: Executed target-version evidence covers the exact FeatureUnion regression plus existing-DataFrame index preservation for both differing and equal row counts, non-DataFrame index assignment, and relevant existing tests without contradictory failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific runtime and regression evidence

applies_when: The visible trajectory analyzes the reported pandas-output failure or the output-container wrapping path
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judges whether the trajectory identifies the original-input-index reassignment as the cause of the failure, explains that an existing pandas transform result owns its row index independently of row-count equality, and remains consistent with that diagnosis in any visible repository change.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if applied repository logic assigns the original input index to an existing DataFrame under any length, equality, missing-index, or exception-based condition. Cap at 2 if it reconstructs an existing DataFrame with an incompatible input index, broadly suppresses the failure without preserving index ownership, or treats later FeatureUnion dimensionality validation as the cause of the supplied traceback.
metadata.evidence_authority: The supplied traceback and checked-out target source establish the reported cause. A visible applied repository diff takes precedence when deciding whether the trajectory's later action contradicts its diagnosis. Proposed code, standalone reimplementations, edits to installed packages, behavior from another scikit-learn version, and claimed test success cannot override contradictory repository logic.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding complete causal-diagnosis credit because the trajectory mentions the 96-versus-4 mismatch while its chosen fix still treats equal row counts, successful assignment, or absence heuristics as permission to overwrite a transformer-defined index.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an explicit semantic account that every existing pandas DataFrame retains its transformer-defined index regardless of length or label equality, with no visible applied repository change that can replace that index from the original input. Credit 5 additionally requires a visible repository implementation consistent with that account while retaining input-index construction for non-DataFrame output.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace the supplied original input index through `_wrap_data_with_container` into the existing-DataFrame branch of `_wrap_in_pandas_container`. Inspect whether the reasoning distinguishes an existing labeled pandas result from an unlabelled result that still requires DataFrame construction, and whether any applied repository logic agrees with that distinction.
metadata.oracle_test: The 96-row input index reaches the wrapper, but the already-created four-row grouped pandas result owns its date index and must retain it. The same ownership rule applies to a same-length reordered or relabeled DataFrame. Only an unlabelled array-like result should be newly constructed with the supplied input index.

scale.1: No causal diagnosis is visible, or the account is incompatible with the supplied traceback and target source.
scale.2: The trajectory locates pandas wrapping only generally, attributes the supplied failure primarily to FeatureUnion dimensionality or columns, or applies logic that can still reconstruct the existing pandas result with an incompatible original-input index.
scale.3: The trajectory recognizes the original-index assignment and reported row-count mismatch, but either fails to establish unconditional ownership of an existing DataFrame's index or applies repository logic that contradicts that ownership through a length, equality, missing-index, or exception-based condition.
scale.4: The trajectory completely explains that the existing pandas result owns its index regardless of row-count or label equality and distinguishes it from non-DataFrame construction; no contradictory repository edit is visible, but a conforming repository implementation is not visibly applied.
scale.5: The complete causal account in level 4 is demonstrated by a visible repository change that never replaces an existing DataFrame's index and still supplies the original input index when constructing a DataFrame from non-DataFrame output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Diagnoses transformer-owned index semantics consistently

applies_when: A visible patch or concrete implementation proposal changes pandas output-container handling.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the narrow pandas wrapping boundary so an output that is already a pandas DataFrame retains its own index, while column renaming remains supported and non-DataFrame outputs continue to be constructed with the supplied input index.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 for a length-equality guard because it still overwrites a same-length transformer-defined index with different labels. Cap at 2 if a mismatched index is used to reconstruct the same DataFrame, if only exceptions are swallowed, or if the patch can still raise the reported mismatch.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual source edits or a displayed unified diff take precedence over prose claiming a fix; semantic behavior takes precedence over the specific syntax used.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepting `len(data_to_wrap) == len(index)` as sufficient: equal row counts do not imply that the original input labels are semantically valid for transformed output.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a concrete implementation that never replaces an existing DataFrame's index merely because a supplied index has the same length.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible diff or exact proposed code in `sklearn/utils/_set_output.py`, especially the existing-DataFrame branch of `_wrap_in_pandas_container`.
metadata.oracle_test: For an existing DataFrame, retain `data_to_wrap.index` and optionally set valid output columns; for an ndarray or other supported dense output, create a DataFrame using the supplied `index` and `columns`. An equality check followed by a no-op assignment is semantically acceptable, though unnecessary.

scale.1: No concrete change reaches the index-overwrite path, or the change is syntactically invalid.
scale.2: The change targets the path but still assigns or reconstructs with an incompatible supplied index, broadly suppresses errors, or damages the return flow.
scale.3: The reported differing-length case is avoided, but same-length existing DataFrames can still have their transformer-defined index overwritten.
scale.4: Existing DataFrame indexes are preserved for all label and length relationships, while the surrounding path remains substantially intact.
scale.5: The implementation cleanly preserves every existing DataFrame index, retains column-renaming behavior, and leaves the non-DataFrame construction path using the supplied index and columns without unrelated changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserve the index of existing pandas transformer output

applies_when: Runtime reproduction, validation, or cross-version comparison of the reported IsolationForest warning
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces runtime evidence from the task checkout or a demonstrably equivalent affected version that isolates the feature-name warning to DataFrame fit with numeric contamination and distinguishes it from unrelated warnings or behavior in already-fixed releases.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A no-warning result from a newer external scikit-learn installation cannot establish absence of the bug and caps at 2 unless the provenance mistake is recognized and corrected; failed builds or missing imports alone do not count as reproduction.
metadata.evidence_authority: Runtime output from the task checkout is strongest; output from the reported affected release is secondary; output from a newer installed release is only comparative evidence. Exact warning-category and message filtering takes precedence over treating any warning as the target.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistakes environment failures, pandas deprecations, or behavior from a modern wheel for evidence about the frozen task checkout.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require successful execution against the task code or a compatible affected release and explicit isolation of the feature-name warning.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed warning-capture commands, imported module path and version, contamination cases, input container type, and exact warning filtering.
metadata.oracle_test: DataFrame input with string column 'a' and contamination=0.05 emits the target warning before the fix, while contamination='auto' does not; ndarray fit does not emit that feature-name warning.

scale.1: No executed task-relevant runtime evidence, or conclusions rely solely on unrelated failures.
scale.2: Attempts reproduction but uses an unverified or known-inapplicable environment, or does not isolate the target warning.
scale.3: Obtains one relevant runtime result from an affected environment, such as reproducing the exact warning, but lacks a control case or clear import provenance.
scale.4: Reproduces the exact warning in an affected environment and shows at least one decisive control such as contamination='auto' or ndarray input, with provenance visible.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and also runs the post-change case against the task checkout, demonstrating removal of only the target fit-time warning while control behavior remains correct.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-version reproduction and decisive runtime evidence

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the unexpected feature-name warning raised while fitting IsolationForest with named tabular input and non-auto contamination.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess how precisely the visible work establishes the task-specific mechanism: fit records feature names while validating the DataFrame, validation returns an array without those names, and the non-auto contamination branch sends that already-validated array through the public score_samples validation path with reset disabled, producing the spurious warning.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims the original DataFrame itself lacks valid names, attributes the warning to tree prediction without the redundant estimator validation, or persists in a mechanism contradicted by inspected source. Cap at 3 if it correctly names score_samples but never establishes the array conversion and stored feature_names_in_ mismatch.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful reproduction or runtime type trace in the task-relevant implementation is strongest; repository source that proves the complete call and data-conversion chain is next; unsupported narration, behavior from an unrelated installed version, and assumptions about predict are weaker and cannot override contradictory source evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad familiarity with feature-name warnings, repeated source browsing, or an incorrect claim that dtype conversion inside score_samples removes names before its feature-name check.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require explicit recognition that the X used for offset computation has already been validated and converted before the internal score_samples call; merely locating score_samples is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect repository-source reads, runtime traces, and reproductions that connect fit-time validation, loss of the DataFrame container, the contamination-specific offset calculation, score_samples, and the feature-name check.
metadata.oracle_test: The reference mechanism is: initial fit validation records DataFrame column names and returns numeric array-like X; only non-auto contamination computes offset_ from training scores; calling the public score_samples path on that converted X invokes reset=False feature-name checking and observes no names against stored names.

scale.1: The visible diagnosis is absent, materially wrong, or contradicts the inspected implementation.
scale.2: The trajectory notices a relationship among contamination, fit, and scoring or feature-name validation, but gives an incorrect or unsupported causal account.
scale.3: The trajectory localizes the warning to the non-auto offset calculation and score_samples validation, but does not clearly establish the already-validated array versus stored feature-name mismatch.
scale.4: The trajectory establishes the complete correct causal chain from DataFrame fit validation through array conversion and redundant reset=False score_samples validation, using repository source or a coherent trace.
scale.5: The complete causal chain is established and independently corroborated by a task-relevant reproduction, warning capture, runtime type trace, or equally direct evidence that also distinguishes the auto-contamination path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: IsolationForest feature-name warning causal diagnosis

applies_when: The trajectory performs or plans reproduction, testing, environment setup, or repository mutation for this bug.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible trajectory efficiently obtains reliable evidence for the reported warning and repair while preserving the repository and distinguishing tests of the checked-out implementation from tests of unrelated installed versions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the trajectory deletes or overwrites broad repository content, edits shared validation behavior without task-specific justification, or leaves known accidental corruption unresolved. Cap at 2 if it treats a different installed release as proof about the checked-out source. Cap at 3 if it reproduces only the warning but supplies no control for auto contamination or ordinary external feature-name checking.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository-local tests and runtime traces against the checked-out implementation are strongest; source-backed reasoning is next when compilation is unavailable; results from a separately installed newer release establish only environmental context. Final repository status and file readbacks override unsupported success claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding dependency churn, tests against the wrong package version, printed success messages without assertions, or destructive workspace manipulation.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require either direct task-relevant runtime evidence or a concrete repository-local regression-test design with explicit assertions and controls; package installation or generic source inspection alone is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect warning capture, contamination-path comparisons, DataFrame versus array controls, repository-local test selection, post-edit checks, dependency changes, failed build recovery, and workspace integrity.
metadata.oracle_test: Strong verification checks that fitting named DataFrame input with numeric contamination emits no feature-name warning, contrasts the auto path or array input, confirms score and offset behavior remains valid, and preserves legitimate warnings for external unnamed input after fitting with names.

scale.1: Verification is absent or unreliable, and the visible work materially damages or corrupts the repository or validation contract.
scale.2: The trajectory performs substantial setup or testing, but evidence comes from the wrong implementation, lacks warning-specific assertions, or is dominated by unresolved environment failures.
scale.3: The trajectory obtains one task-relevant result or gives a concrete test plan, but lacks important controls, post-change validation, or clear repository-local authority.
scale.4: The trajectory obtains reliable repository-relevant warning evidence or specifies a precise regression test with appropriate contamination and input-container controls while maintaining workspace integrity.
scale.5: The trajectory verifies the repaired behavior with warning-specific assertions and relevant controls, checks scoring or offset preservation and legitimate external validation behavior, and leaves the repository in a clean, reviewable state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-relevant verification with repository integrity

applies_when: Dependency installation, cross-version comparison, workspace mutation, or contradictory runtime evidence during the task
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Maintains a trustworthy task workspace and correctly reconciles evidence from local source, installed wheels, build failures, and newer versions without confusing external behavior with the frozen checkout.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Deleting or overwriting the repository package, editing site-packages as the purported solution, or leaving broad base.py changes caps at 1 unless visibly restored; continuing to rely on a newer wheel after identifying the version mismatch caps at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final git status and diff in the task checkout outrank narration; task-checkout source and execution outrank installed-wheel behavior; a documented restoration followed by a clean status resolves earlier accidental damage.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards apparent runtime success obtained from the wrong package version or a workspace damaged by dependency and copy operations.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require explicit provenance for decisive runtime evidence and no visible unresolved corruption or unrelated tracked-file changes.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible git status or diff, imported sklearn.__file__ and version, restoration actions after accidental changes, and explicit correction of conclusions after contradictory evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: The relevant behavior belongs to the frozen checkout or affected release, while a modern scikit-learn wheel may already contain the fix and therefore legitimately produce no warning.

scale.1: Visible unresolved workspace damage, broad unrelated edits, or purported validation performed only against modified site-packages.
scale.2: Environment provenance is unclear or contradictory evidence is noticed but not resolved; repository integrity is not demonstrated.
scale.3: Correctly identifies the provenance problem or restores an earlier mistake, but lacks a final clean status, diff, or task-checkout execution.
scale.4: Uses or clearly identifies the task checkout for decisive evidence, reconciles external-version results correctly, and shows no unresolved unrelated changes.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and demonstrates disciplined recovery with explicit import provenance, focused dependency handling, and a final diff limited to the intended IsolationForest code and tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence provenance and workspace integrity

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes, proposes, or applies a repair for the fit-time IsolationForest feature-name warning
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Develops or applies a narrowly scoped repair in IsolationForest that computes the contamination offset from already-validated training data without repeating public feature-name validation, while preserving score sign, sparse-input handling, and legitimate validation for external score_samples calls.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 for unresolved broad changes to shared feature-name validation, blanket warning suppression, syntactically broken code, an undefined scoring call, or workspace corruption. Cap at 2 if the edit revalidates with reset=True, removes legitimate public score_samples feature-name checks, uses the wrong score sign, or ignores a visibly required sparse conversion. Later source readbacks and diffs take precedence over earlier intentions.
metadata.evidence_authority: A readback or diff of the task-checkout edit is strongest for applied work; inspected task source supporting a concrete design is authoritative for unapplied work; narration and edits to installed packages are weaker. Visible code overrides claims that a fix was applied.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a correct diagnosis as though code were applied, speculative fixes that merely reset stored feature names, global changes to BaseEstimator warning behavior, malformed direct scorer calls, or edits that suppress the warning by weakening the public validation contract.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a coherent visible task-checkout edit in the IsolationForest implementation. Anchor 5 additionally requires a focused repository regression-test edit covering the fit-time warning. A proposal, planned command, or edit script not shown to have changed the repository cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Repository-source evidence and visible diffs showing the non-auto offset path, any private no-validation scoring path or equivalent direct computation, score negation, sparse-format handling, unchanged public score_samples validation, and the scope of all edited files.
metadata.oracle_test: The task-local repair should use the X already validated by fit to obtain the same negative score_samples values for percentile-based offset_ computation without invoking the public reset=False validation path a second time. A private no-validation scorer or semantically equivalent direct call is valid; public calls on unnamed external input after fitting with names must still retain the legitimate warning.

scale.1: The visible applied work is destructive or broadly weakens feature-name validation, or the repair is syntactically or semantically unusable and remains unresolved.
scale.2: No source-consistent task-local repair is established: work is limited to browsing or setup, or the proposed or applied mechanism would reset names, suppress legitimate public validation, compute the wrong scores, or otherwise fail the task contract.
scale.3: A concrete source-consistent task-local repair is derived, including bypass of only the redundant internal validation and preservation of public validation, but no coherent task-checkout edit is visibly applied.
scale.4: A coherent task-checkout IsolationForest edit is visibly applied and preserves score sign, required sparse handling, and the public score_samples validation boundary; no focused regression-test edit is yet visible.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and visibly adds a focused repository regression test that targets named DataFrame fit with numeric contamination while retaining a legitimate external feature-name validation control.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-local IsolationForest repair implementation

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a code change for SequentialFeatureSelector's cv handling.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses scikit-learn's existing check_cv abstraction once during fit, with classifier-aware semantics, and passes the resulting reusable local cv object through candidate scoring without mutating the constructor parameter or changing general cross-validation internals.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Calling check_cv separately for each candidate, changing only cross_validate, placing conversion inside an unrelated conditional, or leaving cross_val_score on self.cv caps credit at 2. Visible syntax or indentation breakage caps credit at 1 until repaired.
metadata.evidence_authority: A syntactically coherent repository diff takes precedence over prose. The established RFECV/check_cv pattern and target-repository APIs take precedence over ad hoc generator type checks or copied code from an incompatible release.
metadata.failure_mode: Applying list(self.cv) narrowly to GeneratorType, mutating self.cv during fit, repeatedly wrapping an already consumed iterator, or broadening a local estimator bug into a model_selection behavior change.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require visible applied edits that normalize cv once outside the candidate loops and use that normalized object in every cross_val_score call.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible edits or precise patch plans in sklearn/feature_selection/_sequential.py: imports of check_cv and is_classifier, one fit-time check_cv call, helper call/signature wiring, and cross_val_score receiving the local checked cv.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended boundary is equivalent to cv = check_cv(self.cv, y, classifier=is_classifier(self.estimator)) in fit, followed by passing cv to _get_best_new_feature_score and then cv=cv to cross_val_score.

scale.1: No relevant implementation, or visible edits are syntactically broken, unrelated, or alter the wrong subsystem.
scale.2: Suggests or applies ad hoc generator/list conversion, per-candidate check_cv, or another incomplete change that does not establish one reusable checked cv object.
scale.3: Presents a coherent exact plan, or a partial diff, to call check_cv once in fit and thread the result through scoring, but the complete applied wiring is not visible.
scale.4: Applies coherent fit-time check_cv normalization and passes the local cv through the helper to cross_val_score, with appropriate imports and no visible syntax errors.
scale.5: Applies a minimal, repository-consistent complete patch using check_cv and is_classifier, updates every required signature and call site, preserves self.cv as the constructor parameter, and avoids unrelated changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements CV normalization once at the SequentialFeatureSelector boundary

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why an iterable returned by a cross-validator's split method fails in SequentialFeatureSelector.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that SequentialFeatureSelector evaluates many candidate feature subsets by repeatedly calling cross_val_score with the same cv value, so a one-shot split iterator works once and is then exhausted, producing an empty results list and the reported IndexError.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claim that a fresh iterable is intrinsically unsupported by cross_val_score, or that cross_validate itself must globally materialize every splitter, caps credit at 2 unless visibly corrected with the repeated-use explanation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Target-repository source and a reproduction against the target version take precedence over behavior from a separately installed newer scikit-learn; a later explicit correction supported by source takes precedence over an earlier guess.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the downstream scores[0] IndexError for a scoring aggregation defect, or proposing a broad model_selection change instead of addressing reuse inside SequentialFeatureSelector.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires connecting iterator exhaustion to reuse across candidate-feature evaluations, not merely observing that cv is passed to cross_val_score.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tracing from SequentialFeatureSelector.fit through _get_best_new_feature_score to repeated cross_val_score calls, together with the behavior of check_cv and _CVIterableWrapper for iterables.
metadata.oracle_test: A fresh generator of valid (train, test) pairs yields folds on the first cross_val_score call but no folds on a later call; SequentialFeatureSelector invokes such scoring repeatedly, while a reusable list or _CVIterableWrapper continues yielding the same folds.

scale.1: No relevant causal account, or an account contradicted by the visible source, such as blaming scoring aggregation alone.
scale.2: Locates cv=self.cv or the empty-score traceback but gives only a vague iterable-handling explanation or asserts that cross_val_score cannot accept iterables at all.
scale.3: Correctly states that a generator is consumed by one scoring call and reused by later candidate evaluations, but does not trace the repository mechanism that makes a checked iterable reusable.
scale.4: Correctly traces repeated candidate scoring and explains that check_cv wraps a raw iterable by materializing it, so that validation must occur once before repeated use.
scale.5: Provides the complete trace with target-source or target-version evidence, distinguishes one-shot generators from reusable lists and splitter objects, and reconciles any contrary result from a newer or different installation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly diagnoses one-shot CV split exhaustion

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or changes SequentialFeatureSelector code that controls repeated use of cv.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Leaves a coherent target-checkout implementation that normalizes the supplied cv exactly once per fit with classifier-aware check_cv semantics and passes that local reusable object through every candidate-scoring path without mutating self.cv or changing shared model-selection code.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A surviving syntax or indentation error, a shared cross-validation-internals change used as the remedy, or normalization inside candidate scoring receives 1. A surviving generator-only conversion, mutation of self.cv, missing classifier awareness, missing helper propagation, or any remaining cv=self.cv scoring call cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The cutoff-visible target-checkout diff and repository status are authoritative for implementation credit. Earlier edits, terminal prose, hypothetical patches, and files later reverted do not count as implementation. Target source and neighboring estimator patterns determine API correctness; external installations are not evidence that the target edit persists.
metadata.failure_mode: Transient correct edits are mistaken for persisted work; detailed plans are credited as implementations; or list conversion, per-call wrapping, parameter mutation, and global validation changes are treated as equivalent to the local repository-consistent fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a surviving, syntactically coherent target diff containing the complete normalization-and-propagation chain. If the cutoff reports no changed target file or an empty diff, the score cannot exceed 3 regardless of earlier edit commands.
metadata.judge_focus: At the cutoff, inspect the target diff for the check_cv and is_classifier imports, one fit-local normalization, the helper call and signature receiving the local cv, and every relevant cross_val_score call using that local value.
metadata.oracle_test: The implementation should be structurally equivalent to computing cv = check_cv(self.cv, y, classifier=is_classifier(self.estimator)) once in fit, passing cv to _get_best_new_feature_score, and supplying cv=cv to cross_val_score while retaining the constructor value in self.cv.

scale.1: The surviving target change is malformed, changes shared model-selection behavior as the remedy, or normalizes cv within repeated candidate scoring where a one-shot iterator can already be exhausted.
scale.2: A surviving edit or active proposal is materially incomplete or incompatible, such as mutating self.cv, handling only generator objects, omitting classifier-aware check_cv, or leaving a scoring path on self.cv.
scale.3: No complete implementation survives at the cutoff, but the trajectory precisely specifies the full fit-local check_cv call and all required helper and scoring propagation; vague or partial plans remain at 2.
scale.4: A coherent surviving target diff performs classifier-aware normalization once in fit and threads the local cv through the helper into every relevant cross_val_score call without mutating self.cv.
scale.5: The surviving implementation satisfies anchor 4 and is minimal and repository-consistent, with all required imports and call sites updated and no unrelated production changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Persists the complete fit-local reusable CV wiring

applies_when: The trajectory considers compatibility of the fix with other accepted cv values or estimator lifecycle behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Keeps integer, None, reusable splitter objects, lists or tuples of splits, and one-shot iterables working under the documented cv contract, while preserving classifier-aware default splitting and avoiding mutation of the estimator's public cv parameter.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Mutating self.cv into a list, accepting only GeneratorType, converting splitter objects directly with list(...), or bypassing classifier-aware check_cv caps credit at 2 unless visibly replaced by a compatible design.
metadata.evidence_authority: The target cv documentation, parameter validation, check_cv implementation, and established neighboring estimator patterns take precedence over generator-specific heuristics.
metadata.failure_mode: Fixing only Python generator objects while regressing arbitrary iterable split containers, standard splitter objects, estimator cloning, repeated fitting, or stratified defaults.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires either code that naturally preserves all accepted forms through check_cv or explicit evidence covering more than the reported generator case.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, code, or tests covering accepted cv forms, classifier detection, list/tuple iterables, reusable splitter objects, repeated fit behavior, cloning, and get_params consistency.
metadata.oracle_test: After construction, get_params()['cv'] remains the supplied parameter; fit-time normalization accepts cv=5, None, a splitter object, a list or tuple of splits, and a fresh split generator, with classification defaults still selected through is_classifier.

scale.1: Visible approach breaks standard cv inputs or estimator construction semantics, with no recognition of the regression.
scale.2: Handles only the reported generator through a narrow type check or mutates self.cv, without protecting the broader documented contract.
scale.3: Recognizes the accepted cv forms and avoids an obvious regression, but compatibility reasoning or evidence is incomplete.
scale.4: Uses fit-local, classifier-aware check_cv normalization and explicitly preserves integer, None, splitter, and iterable behavior without mutating self.cv.
scale.5: In addition to the correct compatible design, supplies visible tests or source-backed evidence for multiple cv forms and estimator state or repeated-fit behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves the documented cv API and estimator parameter semantics

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or changes SequentialFeatureSelector handling of an iterable supplied through cv
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work correctly identifies one-shot split exhaustion across repeated candidate scoring and implements or precisely specifies a local, reusable CV object for the entire fit operation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if normalization occurs independently inside each repeated scoring call, after the original iterator can already be exhausted, or by broadly changing cross_validate instead of fixing SequentialFeatureSelector's reuse boundary. Cap at 3 for mutating self.cv or handling only generator objects when a local check_cv-style normalization is available. A malformed patch or testing only an unrelated installed package cannot receive implementation credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: Persisted repository diff and local test output outrank plans, comments, claimed success, comparisons with another installed version, and hypothetical snippets. When no patch persists, judge only the demonstrated diagnosis and proposed design.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for merely naming iterator exhaustion, wrapping the iterator anew after it has been consumed, applying a global validation-layer workaround, or reporting success from a different scikit-learn installation.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a coherent persisted implementation that normalizes cv once per fit and passes the reusable result through all repeated scoring calls; proposed or transient work cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the traced call structure, the proposed or applied normalization point, whether the normalized object is reused for every candidate and selection iteration, and any focused regression evidence using a one-shot iterable of train/test splits.
metadata.oracle_test: SequentialFeatureSelector evaluates many candidate feature subsets, invoking cross_val_score repeatedly. An iterable returned by splitter.split is one-shot, so fit must materialize or wrap it once—canonically with check_cv(self.cv, y, classifier=is_classifier(self.estimator))—and reuse that local CV object for every candidate. A regression should fit with a fresh iterable of explicit splits and exercise more than one candidate evaluation.

scale.1: The visible work has an incorrect causal model, makes an unrelated or malformed change, or would leave repeated scoring without usable splits.
scale.2: The work recognizes iterable exhaustion or repeated scoring, but the remedy is incorrectly scoped, applied too late or per call, changes global validation behavior, or is contradicted by visible code or test evidence.
scale.3: The work accurately explains that a one-shot split iterable must be normalized once and reused throughout fit, and gives a coherent local design, but no qualifying persisted implementation and focused local regression are visible.
scale.4: A coherent persisted implementation normalizes cv once per fit and reuses it across all candidate evaluations, with source-level inspection or limited local evidence supporting the change, but focused regression coverage is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: The persisted implementation correctly uses reusable CV normalization without mutating estimator parameters unnecessarily and includes a passing focused regression that exercises a fresh one-shot split iterable across multiple candidate evaluations while preserving ordinary integer or splitter-object cv behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly makes iterable CV splits reusable across candidate evaluations

applies_when: The trajectory encounters conflicting runtime results, an installed sklearn with different behavior, a failed build, a vacuous supplied assertion, or a proposed bounded fix that fails a counterexample.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Distinguishes repository evidence from external-version behavior, identifies misleading checks, and revises hypotheses or edits when counterexamples invalidate them rather than continuing to claim success.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the trajectory claims successful local testing after only running an external installation or simulation; cap at 2 if it notices a decision-score/equality failure but retains the contradicted bounded implementation.
metadata.evidence_authority: The checked-out source and tests are authoritative for implementation state; external releases may inform the solution but cannot prove the local patch; observed counterexamples override prior speculative conclusions.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing environment/version discrepancies with local behavior, or declaring victory despite evidence that a proposed fix breaks another accepted roc_curve input domain.
metadata.hard_gate: Higher anchors require explicitly acknowledging at least one contradiction and updating the conclusion or implementation accordingly.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible responses to inf outputs from another sklearn version, build/import failures, failed edge cases, malformed assertions, and restoration or revision of incorrect edits.
metadata.oracle_test: Seeing np.inf in a newer installed sklearn is useful precedent for the intended sentinel, while the local old source still requires a patch; a failure of threshold=1 at y_score==1 decisively rejects that finite sentinel.

scale.1: Ignores contradictions, misattributes external output to the checkout, or claims tests passed when they did not exercise modified code.
scale.2: Notices conflicting evidence but retains a refuted implementation or repeats unreliable checks.
scale.3: Correctly separates some external and local evidence or retracts one bad approach, but the recovered conclusion remains incomplete or weakly supported.
