reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-grounded validation and recovery from failed experiments

applies_when: The trajectory adds, edits, runs, or concretely specifies tests for KMeans reproducibility across job counts.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides a regression test that exercises multiple stochastic initializations with a fixed random_state and demonstrates that effective single-job and multi-job KMeans choose equivalent results.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A test using n_init=1, explicit deterministic centers only, a modern KMeans version without n_jobs, or merely comparing fabricated random numbers cannot establish the regression and caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A repository regression test and its actual test output outrank ad hoc scripts; an ad hoc run of the reported dataset outranks seed-only simulations or textual assurances.
metadata.failure_mode: Testing general determinism across repeated fits without crossing the serial/parallel branch, or treating a standalone seed demonstration as a KMeans regression test.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible repository test that compares n_jobs=1 with a genuinely parallel value using fixed random_state and n_init greater than one.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible changes or commands involving sklearn/cluster/tests/test_k_means.py or an equivalent repository test, including n_init, random_state, n_jobs values, and assertions on KMeans outputs.
metadata.oracle_test: On identical input and fixed random_state with multiple initializations, n_jobs=1 and n_jobs>1 must yield equal inertia and compatible fitted clustering outputs; the test must exercise the branch whose seed derivation changed.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence or test design is visible.
scale.2: Only a generic reproduction, seed simulation, or unsuitable test configuration is visible.
scale.3: A concrete and semantically relevant regression-test design is shown, but it is not visibly added to the repository or omits an important branch condition or assertion.
scale.4: A focused repository regression test visibly compares serial and parallel KMeans with fixed randomness and multiple initializations, but successful execution is not shown.
scale.5: The focused repository regression test is visible and has successful targeted execution, with assertions covering inertia and at least one fitted clustering output such as labels or centers.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression coverage across n_jobs

applies_when: The task concerns fixed-random-state KMeans results differing between effective single-job and multi-job n_init execution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Accurately traces the serial-versus-parallel initialization-stream mismatch and makes observable progress toward having both branches derive and consume the same ordered per-run integer seeds.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Visibly unresolved source corruption, such as code inserted outside the KMeans branch or syntactically merged statements, forces score 1. A latest account based on job ordering, scheduling arithmetic, repeated reset to an identical serial initialization, or shared mutable RandomState use across workers caps credit at 2 unless later corrected. A correctly directed partial edit that draws seeds but has not yet replaced the serial call is incomplete rather than contradictory and may receive score 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest source readback or repository diff is strongest. An exact, unambiguous edit command targeting the relevant branch is evidence that the stated operation was applied unless later source evidence contradicts it. Source-grounded reasoning can establish diagnosis and repair readiness but not a complete intervention. Synthetic random-number scripts, unrelated installed package behavior, staging or patch-summary artifacts, and unsupported success claims do not establish checkout behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating partial progress with a malformed remedy, rewarding confident but incorrect random-state explanations, or accepting mock simulations and unrelated installations as proof that the repository now has branch-invariant seeding.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires visible evidence that both required operations are applied coherently in the target source: drawing an n_init-sized integer seed sequence from the normalized fit-level RandomState and passing one corresponding scalar seed to each serial single-run call. A correct diagnosis, an exact unapplied plan, or a non-destructive edit establishing only one operation cannot exceed 3. Score 5 additionally requires focused task-specific verification against the modified checkout.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest account of the effective_n_jobs split and the visible KMeans orchestration work. Distinguish an evolving shared RandomState in the serial loop from independently seeded parallel runs, then assess separately whether the trajectory establishes the n_init seed draw and whether it passes corresponding scalar seeds to serial Lloyd or Elkan calls while preserving best-result selection.
metadata.oracle_test: From one normalized fit-level RandomState, both execution modes derive the same ordered n_init integer seeds, invoke the selected single-run implementation once per seed, and select the minimum-inertia candidate; execution mode changes scheduling and storage but not the candidate initializations.

scale.1: The latest visible target source is unusable or corrupted, or no relevant causal investigation is present.
scale.2: The relevant branches are inspected, but the latest mechanism or remedy remains materially wrong, contradictory, or unsafe and no correctly directed source progress is established.
scale.3: The evolving-shared-generator versus per-run-seed mismatch and exact two-part repair are correctly specified without complete application, or a non-destructive repository intervention visibly establishes only part of that repair.
scale.4: Visible source evidence coherently establishes both the n_init integer-seed draw and corresponding scalar-seed use in every serial single-run call while preserving the parallel path, algorithm choice, serial storage optimization, and best-result bookkeeping; focused behavioral verification is absent.
scale.5: Meets score 4 and includes successful focused execution or a repository regression test showing equivalent fixed-random-state KMeans results across serial and parallel job counts with multiple initialization runs.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: KMeans seed-parity diagnosis and intervention progress

applies_when: Production reader source, a runtime diff, or execution of the reader is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the latest operative implementation selects file content, dedents that selected content, and only then inserts unchanged prepend and append text.

metadata.failure_mode: Synthetic text is transformed, dedent precedes selection, or no relevant runtime behavior is implemented
metadata.judge_focus: Latest operative runtime semantics

scale.1: The operative behavior is absent or clearly transforms synthetic text, leaves it inside dedent, or dedents before selection.
scale.2: A runtime edit targets parsing, rendering, warning suppression, or another mechanism without establishing the required boundary.
scale.3: An indirect isolation approach may work in common cases but has concrete ambiguity around empty options, empty selections, matching, markers, or automatic dedent.
scale.4: The visible production pipeline performs selection, then dedent, then unchanged synthetic insertion.
scale.5: The correct boundary is retained in the latest source and visible behavior also preserves insertion placement, absent options, line state, and the separate diff path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Operative transformation semantics

applies_when: A production edit, direct source view, git diff, git status, patch payload, or restoration command is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether a focused, applicable production change implementing the literalinclude transformation boundary remains operative in the latest directly observed repository state.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest direct evidence shows the production edit was restored, lost, malformed, or replaced by a rewrite utility. Cap at 3 when an edit was shown but its latest retention or applicability is genuinely unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest direct production-source view and git diff take precedence over earlier edits, prose claims, simulations, terminal-state labels, and coarse workspace summaries. A later checkout, restore, clean diff, or source view showing the old implementation overrides an earlier patch.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking an attempted or simulated fix for retained integration, or disregarding a visible retained diff merely because the trajectory is nonterminal or a summary omits changed files.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a syntactically valid retained production edit that applies dedent after selection and before unchanged prepend and append insertion; tests, documentation, temporary scripts, or proposed commands cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest direct source or diff for a valid production-path change in LiteralIncludeReader.read(), then determine whether later commands retained, replaced, malformed, or restored it.
metadata.oracle_test: The evaluator-facing source must retain the equivalent of pyobject/start/end/lines selection, then dedent, then prepend/append, without changing the separate diff branch.

scale.1: Latest authoritative evidence shows no production edit, the original pipeline, or an explicitly restored change.
scale.2: Only tests, prose, simulations, documentation, or a rewrite utility remain, or the visible production edit is malformed or implements the wrong mechanism.
scale.3: A relevant production edit was visibly applied, but its latest retention, syntactic validity, or evaluator applicability is unresolved.
scale.4: Latest authoritative evidence retains a focused, syntactically valid production edit implementing selection, then dedent, then unchanged synthetic insertion.
scale.5: Anchor 4 is satisfied, and the retained artifact also contains a focused repository-conventional regression test plus a coherent final diff or status review.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Retained runtime integration

applies_when: Investigation or explanatory reasoning is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether reasoning correctly separates selected file content, dedent processing, and synthetic insertion, without allowing prose to outweigh code and execution.

metadata.failure_mode: Blaming rendering or parsing, suppressing warnings, or inferring synthetic indentation
metadata.judge_focus: Accurate causal model

scale.1: Reasoning is absent or centered on an unrelated mechanism.
scale.2: Relevant code is found, but the proposed model strips, pads, parses, or otherwise changes synthetic text.
scale.3: The filter interaction is recognized, but selection scope or warning causality remains incomplete.
scale.4: The reasoning correctly identifies selection before dedent and synthetic insertion afterward.
scale.5: The explanation also accurately covers numeric and automatic dedent, absent options, warning causality, line state, and the separate diff path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific causal understanding

applies_when: A final diff, tracked-file list, submitted patch, or repository-state summary is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures repository defects according to their demonstrated ability to interfere with applying, importing, collecting, packaging, or evaluating the operative change.

metadata.failure_mode: Malformed submitted code, truncated runtime source, or utilities replacing the actual fix
metadata.judge_focus: Material evaluator impact rather than cosmetic cleanliness

scale.1: The visible artifact is focused and valid, or no evaluator-impacting defect is shown.
scale.2: A harmless focused auxiliary file, patch-display file, or backup is present without affecting runtime or test execution.
scale.3: Multiple diagnostics or unexplained files create meaningful uncertainty, but the operative patch remains applicable and executable.
scale.4: Malformed nonessential submitted code, a full duplicate runtime file, or substantial pollution can interfere with collection, packaging, or review.
scale.5: The patch is malformed, production source is truncated or syntactically invalid, or a rewrite utility substitutes for the required runtime edit.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-impacting artifact defects

applies_when: A test, reader invocation, documentation build, rendered-output inspection, or execution failure is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether valid execution of the operative Sphinx production path demonstrates that selected file lines are dedented while prepend and append text remain unchanged.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A valid unresolved failure of the combined production case caps the score at 1. A wrong constructor, missing dependency, malformed RST fixture, wrong imported source, or incorrect expectation is non-evidence unless repaired or causally connected. Correct output from an implementation that rewrites synthetic text caps at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: An exact LiteralIncludeReader assertion against the operative source is strongest, followed by a warning-free repository build whose underlying literal content is inspected, then relevant repository tests. Copied filter logic, manually sequenced helpers, or highlighted HTML without recoverable text cannot override a valid production-path failure.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding validation credit for simulations, standalone cases that passed before the fix, visually inspected highlighting, or environment failures that never exercised the modified reader.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require execution of the operative production implementation with selection, dedent, prepend, and append all present and exact complete content checked. The runtime source must also implement the required boundary.
metadata.judge_focus: Verify the executed code is the operative repository implementation, the fixture combines selection with dedent and synthetic insertion, and the observed content checks exact whitespace and newlines rather than visual similarity alone.
metadata.oracle_test:
For lines 9-11 with dedent 2, prepend 'class Foo:', and append '# comment', the exact reader result is 'class Foo:
  def baz():
      pass

# comment
'; both synthetic strings are unchanged and only selected file-derived lines are dedented.

scale.1: A valid combined production-path case fails against the operative implementation, or repeated relevant execution exposes unresolved incorrect content or warnings.
scale.2: No valid discriminative production execution succeeds; evidence consists only of source inspection, copied logic, standalone cases, visual rendering, invalid fixtures, or environment-blocked attempts.
scale.3: A valid operative production execution or relevant repository tests support part of the behavior, but the complete selection-dedent-prepend-append interaction is not exactly asserted.
scale.4: The operative production reader passes an exact complete-content check combining selection, dedent, prepend, and append, with both synthetic strings unchanged.
scale.5: Anchor 4 is satisfied and nearby reader tests for ordinary inclusion, selection, standalone dedent, prepend/append, tab handling, and the separate diff behavior also pass or any failures are causally baseline-diagnosed.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative production-path validation

applies_when: The task concerns autoclass displaying a constructor-derived return type under description-style autodoc type hints.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible repository change precisely prevents constructor-derived return annotations from becoming class-level return-type documentation without suppressing valid parameter types or function and method return types.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the change skips all type-hint merging for classes, suppresses every None return annotation, restricts return handling to an incomplete callable whitelist, uses the wrong objtype value, or visibly leaves malformed code. Cap at 3 if preservation of method or function return types is not demonstrated.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final visible diff or latest file contents take precedence over earlier proposed snippets and verbal claims. Successful tool output produced after the latest edit supports, but does not override, the actual code. Reverted edits receive no implementation credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the constructor signature's return annotation for a semantic return value of the class, or fixing the symptom by disabling unrelated type-hint behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied, syntactically coherent repository change whose scope preserves return-type handling for non-class callables.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible implementation in the autodoc signature-recording or description-merging path. Determine whether it distinguishes a class description from functions and methods and whether the edit is syntactically coherent.
metadata.oracle_test: For autoclass of a class whose __init__(width: int, height: int) is annotated -> None, description-mode output retains width and height type documentation but has no class-level Return type: None; a normal method or function annotated -> int still documents int as its return type.

scale.1: No surviving relevant implementation, or the latest visible edit is malformed, reverted, or causally unrelated.
scale.2: A surviving change targets the symptom but is visibly overbroad or uses an incorrect object-type or annotation rule that can suppress valid documentation.
scale.3: A surviving, plausible class-specific change removes the constructor-derived class return annotation, but preservation of adjacent behavior is not visibly established.
scale.4: A targeted surviving change is accompanied by visible evidence that the class-level return field disappears while constructor parameter types and at least one ordinary callable return type remain correct.
scale.5: The targeted change satisfies the level-4 behavior and is integrated with a focused repository regression test covering the class case and a non-class return-type control.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Targeted class return-type fix

applies_when: The trajectory selects, revises, or applies a rule intended to prevent constructor-derived return metadata from appearing on a top-level class description.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the trajectory selects the return-only class boundary supported by the visible object-type and annotation flow, distinguishes top-level class output from separately documented members, and calibrates its conclusion when source, generated output, syntax, or repository tests contradict the attempted rule. Correctly retracting a malformed or overbroad edit receives design credit, while an exact applied implementation receives credit only when its latest source and scoped effects are visible.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when the latest relevant code is malformed and the trajectory neither retracts nor repairs it. Cap at 2 when the selected rule bypasses all class type-hint merging, globally filters a return value such as `None`, uses an object-type value contradicted by visible source, checks a constructor suffix while processing a class fullname, or claims success after scoped output still shows the defect. Cap at 3 when the exact latest edit is not visible, when validation cannot distinguish a top-level class field from a nested member field, or when a relevant focused test fails and the trajectory continues to claim completion without qualifying or revising the boundary. A reverted bad edit is judged by the final stated boundary, not as a surviving implementation.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible file contents or diff outrank descriptions of an edit. Source or runtime evidence for the event object type and annotation flow outranks guessed names. Generated output is authoritative only when enough of the enclosing class, constructor, method, or function section is shown to attribute each field correctly. Focused repository tests outrank broad build success. A later evidence-based retraction or narrowed conclusion outranks an earlier malformed or overconfident attempt.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing a nested method return field with a class field; treating a successful build or broad grep as proof of semantic scope; rewarding class-wide early returns, global `None` suppression, constructor-name heuristics applied to class metadata, wrong object-type strings, reverted edits as surviving code, or claims of completion that ignore a focused test conflict.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a source-supported class-only and return-only rule, or an equivalent filter, with parameter processing and non-class return handling explicitly left reachable. Credit above 3 requires either a syntactically coherent latest edit shown in context with section-scoped behavioral evidence, or a focused contradictory repository test that causes an explicit retraction, qualification, or concrete revision of the selected boundary. Credit at 5 requires both a surviving narrow edit and reconciled focused repository coverage.
metadata.judge_focus: First identify the final selected condition and whether it is actually present in the latest source. Then inspect surrounding control flow to ensure only top-level class return metadata is excluded while constructor parameters remain recorded. Attribute generated fields to their enclosing descriptions rather than relying on unscoped searches. Finally, check whether syntax errors, failed reproductions, persistent output, or existing tests caused the trajectory to retract, narrow, or qualify its conclusion.
metadata.oracle_test: The selected rule uses the source-supported class object type at return recording or an equivalently precise merge filter. For a class whose inspected constructor-derived signature supplies typed parameters and `-> None`, description output keeps the class parameters but omits only the top-level class return field. A separately documented member and an ordinary function or method remain on their normal return-annotation paths, and any conflicting existing expectation is explicitly examined and reconciled rather than ignored.

scale.1: No coherent class-return boundary is selected, or the trajectory ends with unretracted malformed code, a contradicted rule, or a class-wide/value-wide suppression presented as successful.
scale.2: The trajectory locates relevant code but selects an unsupported or overbroad rule, or merely proposes a plausible filter without establishing the actual object type, surrounding parameter flow, or attribution of generated fields.
scale.3: A source-supported class-only, return-only boundary is selected and adjacent parameter and non-class paths are correctly preserved in the reasoning, but the edit is absent, reverted, not visible in final source, or validated only by ambiguous output. Responsible retraction of a malformed or overbroad attempt can reach this level.
scale.4: The exact narrow boundary is visible in coherent latest source and is supported by section-scoped evidence for retained class parameters and a non-class return control; alternatively, a focused source or test contradiction causes an explicit, technically correct retraction or concrete boundary revision rather than an unsupported success claim.
scale.5: The level-4 narrow implementation survives and is covered by focused repository evidence that distinguishes the top-level class from a separately documented constructor or member, preserves an ordinary callable return type, and reconciles any pre-existing conflicting expectation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-calibrated selection of the class-return suppression boundary

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why an autoclass description acquires a return-type field from an annotated constructor.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies the task-specific data flow: a class is callable, inspection of its constructor-derived class signature exposes `__init__` annotations including `-> None`, `record_typehints` stores that annotation as `return`, and description merging later renders it as the class-level `rtype`.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the trajectory attributes the defect solely to HTML rendering, caching, or the generic `force_rtype` condition despite visible evidence that the class return annotation is recorded earlier, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A focused experiment with the task's class plus the actual `record_typehints` and `merge_typehints` source flow outranks speculation based only on function names or HTML appearance.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents fixes aimed at presentation code without understanding why constructor return metadata is associated with the class.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require distinguishing the top-level class description from separately documented methods such as `__init__`.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection, focused signature experiments, or generated output that connects class signature inspection, recorded annotations, and the class-level field list.
metadata.oracle_test: For `class Square` whose `__init__(width: int, height: int) -> None`, class signature inspection supplies constructor parameters and a `None` return annotation; only the latter is semantically invalid as a class return type.

scale.1: No causal account, or an account incompatible with the observed class-level `Return type: None`.
scale.2: Recognizes that `__init__ -> None` is involved but does not trace how it becomes class annotation metadata and then an `rtype` field.
scale.3: Correctly identifies either the recording stage or the merge/render stage and explains that the unwanted field belongs to the class, not a nested method.
scale.4: Correctly traces the class-callable inspection through recorded `return` metadata into description merging, supported by visible source or signature evidence.
scale.5: Provides the complete supported trace and explicitly separates valid constructor parameter annotations and member return annotations from the invalid top-level class return annotation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of the class return-type leak

applies_when: Existing autodoc tests or observed outputs conflict with the task's expected no-return-type behavior for classes.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Recognizes that an existing expected `Return type: None` for the class may encode the reported bug, updates only that stale class-level expectation, and protects unrelated type-hint behavior through targeted and broader regression runs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Treating every existing failure as irrelevant, or changing broad expected output without explaining which class-level assertion is obsolete, caps at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The task's explicit class semantics plus a scoped regression test outrank a stale expectation that preserves the bug; genuine failures in unrelated function/method behavior outrank claims that the old test is merely stale.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents abandoning a semantically correct direction merely because a regression test encodes the old bug, and prevents indiscriminate test rewriting to hide real regressions.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require correctly separating the obsolete class-level expectation from still-valid expectations for an explicitly documented `__init__`, methods, functions, and parameter types.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspection of existing `test_ext_autodoc_configs.py` class/`__init__` cases, interpretation of failures, expected-output edits, and targeted or broader pytest results.
metadata.oracle_test: A test formerly expecting a return field in the top-level autoclass block should be adjusted, while any separately rendered `__init__` or ordinary callable block and its intended annotations remain governed by their own expectations.

scale.1: Does not inspect relevant existing tests or accepts contradictory output without analysis.
scale.2: Notices a failing or stale test but either abandons the task semantics or dismisses the whole test without isolating the obsolete assertion.
scale.3: Correctly explains that a class-level `Return type: None` expectation must change, but shows no precise expected-output adjustment or regression run.
scale.4: Shows a precise update or plan that removes only the stale class-level return expectation while preserving valid parameter and member expectations.
scale.5: Shows the precise expectation recovery together with passing targeted regression evidence and broader relevant autodoc/type-hint tests, with any remaining failures accurately classified.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from stale expectations and regression protection

applies_when: The trajectory selects or attempts a repository code boundary for excluding constructor-derived return metadata from a top-level class description.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the strongest visibly established implementation state for a class-only, return-only suppression boundary: whether the boundary is actually applied and effective, whether class parameter processing and non-class return handling remain reachable, and whether observed output or tests support rather than contradict those effects.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score at most 1 when the latest relevant source is malformed, the attempted edit was explicitly reverted without replacement, or scoped post-edit output still shows the defect while success is claimed. Score at most 2 when the applied rule skips all class type-hint merging, globally filters `None`, uses an object-type value contradicted by visible source, relies on a constructor suffix while processing a class fullname, or changes a path not shown to affect the task. Score at most 3 when a narrow edit is present but its effect is supported only by unattributed output, or when a genuine focused regression in parameter or non-class return handling remains unresolved. A focused failure consisting solely of the formerly expected top-level class return field is not by itself a regression contradiction, but it prevents level 5 until the expectation is deliberately reconciled.
metadata.evidence_authority: An explicitly shown latest file section or diff outranks prose, edit-command success messages, and generic workspace summaries. An explicit later checkout, restore, malformed replacement, or newer file view outranks an earlier valid snippet. Section-scoped output from a clean build demonstrably using the edited checkout may establish behavior even before a final diff is printed; output from an installed or otherwise unproven copy cannot establish the edit's effect. Focused tests outrank broad suites for behavior they directly exercise.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating a correct proposal with applied code; equating failed edit commands or reverted code with a surviving boundary; rewarding class-wide early returns, global value suppression, wrong object-type strings, or ineffective fullname heuristics; treating an obsolete assertion for the reported bug as equivalent to a genuine adjacent-behavior regression; or accepting output without establishing that it came from the edited checkout.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a syntactically coherent applied class-only and return-only condition using a source-supported object identity, or an equivalently precise applied filter. Credit above 3 requires attributable evidence after that edit that the top-level class return field is absent while typed class parameters remain and at least one ordinary callable return is still documented. Credit at 5 additionally requires focused repository coverage and reconciliation of affected existing expectations.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest directly visible relevant source or diff, including the return-recording and description-merging control flow. Classify separately: no applied edit, an applied but ineffective or overbroad rule, a coherent narrow rule, and a narrow rule whose three required effects are shown in attributable output. Check whether any test failure reflects the obsolete top-level class return expectation or a real regression in parameters, members, functions, or methods.
metadata.oracle_test: With description-style type hints, a class whose constructor supplies typed width and height parameters and a `None` return annotation retains those parameter types but has no top-level return-type field. A separately documented member and an ordinary function or method with an integer return annotation retain their normal return documentation. The effective rule uses the actual class object identity and does not bypass unrelated class merging.

scale.1: No usable applied boundary survives: edits fail or are reverted, the latest code is malformed or unrelated, or attributable post-edit output still shows the unwanted class return field under a claimed fix.
scale.2: There is investigation, a proposal, or an applied symptom-directed rule, but no coherent effective narrow implementation is established; this includes class-wide bypasses, global `None` filtering, wrong object-type values, ineffective fullname checks, and edits whose resulting source is never shown.
scale.3: A coherent applied class-only, return-only boundary is visible and leaves parameter and non-class paths reachable in source, but edited-checkout behavioral evidence is incomplete or ambiguous, or a genuine adjacent-behavior regression remains unresolved.
scale.4: The narrow applied boundary is visible or otherwise firmly established, and attributable post-edit evidence shows all three required effects: retained typed class parameters, no top-level class return field, and a preserved ordinary callable return type. A focused failure may remain only when it clearly encodes the obsolete class-level expectation rather than a behavioral regression.
scale.5: Level 4 is satisfied, and focused repository tests cover the top-level class case plus a separately documented member or ordinary callable control; stale class-level expectations are precisely updated or otherwise reconciled, and relevant tests pass after the final edit.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied and behaviorally supported class-return boundary

applies_when: A concrete change, predicate, regex, lookahead, or executable proposal for the leading field scan is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible corrective rule is a task-causal and usable next step for recognizing genuine leading fields without classifying interpreted-role title text as docinfo, independently of whether the rule has already been committed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A candidate that visibly leaves the reported title broken or still classifies its literal role syntax as docinfo cannot exceed 2. Malformed logic or a rule that demonstrably rejects common fields such as `:title: value` is score 1. A narrower exclusion that fixes exercised roles but visibly mishandles a legitimate uncommon field body is capped at 4 rather than treated as absence of a solution.
metadata.evidence_authority: The current inspected source and results executed against that source outrank standalone proposed snippets; an exact proposed predicate with direct example checks outranks narrative intent. A successful HTML build proves only the exercised role spelling unless broader matcher or insertion checks are also visible. Repository summaries do not erase source edits or proposals visible in the prefix.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating implementation status with semantic quality, awarding narration without an inspectable rule, treating one successful rendered role as complete grammar coverage, or scoring an unapplied but directly checked corrective predicate as if no candidate existed.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 or higher requires a concrete rule whose visible logic and direct checks accept representative genuine fields and reject literal interpreted-role syntax. Score 5 additionally requires the rule to be applied and behaviorally verified across simple and qualified roles, genuine or mixed docinfo, and title/underline insertion semantics.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact current or proposed predicate and its demonstrated behavior on ordinary fields, empty-body fields when exercised, literal simple roles, and domain-qualified roles; distinguish proposed logic from applied source.
metadata.oracle_test: A valid field marker ends at its closing field-name colon and has the Docutils-allowed boundary or body; role content continues immediately as interpreted text, including forms such as `:mod:`name`` and `:py:class:`Name``. The correction must stop the prolog scan before those role-title lines while retaining genuine leading fields.

scale.1: A concrete candidate is malformed, uses the wrong grammar, or demonstrably destroys common genuine-field handling.
scale.2: A concrete candidate targets the area but visibly leaves the reported role-title failure, covers only an contradicted special case, or has no usable rule behind the proposal.
scale.3: No concrete discriminator is visible, or a candidate is only plausible narration with insufficient exact logic or checks to establish field-versus-role behavior.
scale.4: A concrete current or proposed rule directly accepts representative genuine fields and rejects literal simple and qualified roles, with no demonstrated core regression; application or broader mixed-document validation may remain incomplete.
scale.5: The applied rule has complete field-marker semantics or an observably equivalent boundary and passes direct checks for genuine and empty-body fields, simple and qualified roles, mixed docinfo, and preserved title/underline insertion behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Corrective readiness of the field-versus-role discriminator

applies_when: The current source state, repository diff, validation failure, or absence of a source edit is observable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates only present, observable harm in the current repository state; unfinished status alone is neither a flaw nor a clean-patch bonus.

metadata.failure_mode: Malformed source, known semantic regression, unsafe indexing, missing required source change in a purported patch, tracked backup, escaped fixture, or contaminated artifact.
metadata.judge_focus: Current syntax, safety, regressions, provenance, and artifact cleanliness
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect current source, known failing checks, complete diff, backups, generated files, and fixture bytes.

scale.1: A visible current implementation is syntactically valid, semantically safe on the exercised cases, and cleanly scoped.
scale.2: Only minor harmless noise is visible, with no known semantic, syntax, provenance, or applicability defect.
scale.3: No implementation is present, or the observable state is neutral and contains no current source defect to assess.
scale.4: A serious but recoverable current defect is visible, such as incomplete role coverage, an unsafe workaround, a conflicting focused check, or repository contamination.
scale.5: The current source is syntactically malformed, retains or introduces a demonstrated core regression, or combines known semantic failure with evaluator-facing artifact defects.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current implementation or repository harm

applies_when: The prefix investigates the reported failure or explains where `rst_prolog` is inserted.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the prefix observably connects the leading field scan to insertion between a literal role-bearing title and its adornment, rather than attributing the defect to downstream rendering.

metadata.failure_mode: The prefix remains speculative, uses altered role syntax, or pursues downstream components despite observable evidence that the input was split.
metadata.judge_focus: Root cause and exact pre-parse structure
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect matcher results and the complete `StringList` ordering around the first title and underline.

scale.1: The explanation is materially wrong or remains focused on downstream rendering without locating the input mutation.
scale.2: The prefix suspects prolog placement but does not establish the field-versus-role false match or title/underline split.
scale.3: The overbroad leading matcher is identified, but the structural consequence is asserted rather than directly demonstrated.
scale.4: The prefix shows matcher or insertion evidence connecting role misclassification to the broken title.
scale.5: Literal role syntax, exact insertion ordering, title/underline adjacency requirements, and the rendered or toctree consequence are all connected by direct evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal localization of the title split

applies_when: The prefix contains at least two investigation, reproduction, editing, or validation commands whose outputs can be compared.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether successive visible experiments use faithful inputs, recover from execution errors, narrow the causal hypothesis, and support only conclusions warranted by their outputs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An altered role spelling, wrong output path, unloaded edited source, or failed command presented as successful evidence caps the score at 2. Repeated source corruption or unsupported claims contradicted by visible output forces score 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Literal command output, file contents, and exit status outrank narration. Results from a faithful Sphinx build outrank isolated Docutils parsing without Sphinx role registration. Post-edit output is candidate evidence only when the current edited source was actually loaded.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding command volume, accepting invalid fixtures, confusing a successful process exit with correct heading behavior, or treating pre-edit output as validation of a later candidate.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 or higher requires a faithful reproduction or equivalent structural experiment, correction of material command errors, and at least one source or input-state observation that narrows the cause. Score 5 requires a clean baseline-versus-candidate comparison.
metadata.judge_focus: Compare fixtures with the reported literal role syntax, check command exit status and inspected paths, determine whether failures are corrected, and verify that each causal turn follows from the immediately preceding output.
metadata.oracle_test: Reliable convergence should move from the exact `:role:`text`` title and enabled prolog to the leading-field scan and resulting title/underline ordering; downstream title collectors or role registration are not causal unless visible input ordering remains intact.

scale.1: Visible experiments are dominated by uncorrected malformed commands, corrupted source or fixtures, or conclusions contradicted by their outputs.
scale.2: A reproduction or inspection is attempted, but material execution errors, altered inputs, wrong paths, or unsupported causal turns remain unresolved.
scale.3: Some faithful evidence is obtained, but the sequence mixes useful observations with unresolved failures or speculation and does not yet converge on a supported causal mechanism.
scale.4: The reported input is reproduced faithfully, material errors are corrected, and successive source or structural checks narrow the defect without overstating what has been shown.
scale.5: The investigation cleanly separates baseline from candidate evidence and every material conclusion is supported by faithful source, structure, matcher, or rendered-output observations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Experimental reliability and causal convergence

applies_when: Parent HTML, a parent doctree, or a concrete propagation implementation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores only whether listener-modified included RST becomes input to the parent parser and appears in the parent result.

metadata.failure_mode: The original included token remains or only standalone output changes
metadata.judge_focus: Parent-consumed text rather than event occurrence

scale.1: No transformed included text is visibly consumed by the parent parser, or the parent result remains unfixed.
scale.2: A plausible reinsertion mechanism is described but not concretely implemented or observed.
scale.3: A concrete data flow appears capable of reinsertion, but parent consumption is untested or ambiguous.
scale.4: A clean normal-include parent result visibly consumes the mutation.
scale.5: Normal and nested parent results consume the mutation, with no original token remaining in the focused reproduction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Parent parser propagation

applies_when: The prefix runs a build, test, output inspection, or makes a correctness claim.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores observed evidence that distinguishes baseline reproduction, causal diagnosis, and an actual post-edit fix.

metadata.failure_mode: Failed tooling, event logs, stale output, or a nonexistent output path used as proof
metadata.judge_focus: Commands that ran and outputs that were inspected

scale.1: No valid task-specific result is observed, or the claimed result relies on a failed command, wrong path, or contradicted output.
scale.2: A valid baseline parent-output reproduction is observed, but no post-edit semantic check passes.
scale.3: One valid post-edit parent-output or focused include check passes.
scale.4: Normal and nested propagation plus a clipping or literal boundary check pass.
scale.5: The exact reproduction, nested propagation, clipping, literal exclusion, and relevant existing tests visibly pass.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific validation

applies_when: Select this rubric only when a task-specific build, focused test, generated parent-output inspection, or execution-based propagation claim is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores the strongest reliable execution evidence about whether listener-modified included text reaches the parent parser, distinguishing incomplete execution, an isolated baseline reproduction, a baseline connected to the active include-input boundary, and a verified post-edit fix.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A materially misread artifact, stale or wrong output path, or success claim contradicted by inspected parent output caps the score at 1. A valid post-edit parent result that still contains the focused original token caps the score at 2 unless a later valid rerun passes.
metadata.evidence_authority: Fresh parent HTML, parent-doctree assertions, and focused semantic test results outrank build-success messages, event logs, debug prints, standalone included-document output, summaries, and unsupported claims. The latest valid check relevant to the current implementation controls; an earlier failed command is superseded by a later successful rerun, while a later failing parent check supersedes an earlier success.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting generic build success, standalone output, repeated event invocation, ambiguous grep output, reproduction debris in production paths, or speculative cache explanations as proof that the parent consumed modified include text.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires a completed task-specific execution and unambiguous inspection of the generated parent result. A score above 3 requires a relevant production edit followed by a passing parent semantic check.
metadata.judge_focus: Command completion, isolation of reproduction artifacts, freshness and path of the parent result, exact escaped-original versus replacement semantics, and whether observed data flow reaches the parent parser rather than only standalone document processing.
metadata.oracle_test: In the focused reproduction, baseline parent HTML contains the escaped original token from included text and the replacement from parent text. Stronger pre-fix evidence also connects docutils' direct include read to the parser-input insertion boundary. A passing post-edit result contains the expected replacements in the parent and no focused original token; event invocation or standalone included-document output alone does not pass.
metadata.stage: reproduction, causal execution evidence, and post-edit validation

scale.1: No trustworthy task-specific result is established: relevant commands remain failed without a later valid rerun, the artifact or path is wrong or materially misread, a success claim contradicts inspected output, or workspace contamination makes the evidence unreliable.
scale.2: Usable but limited evidence is visible: setup advances after an earlier failure, a build completes without unambiguous parent inspection, or a clean parent baseline is shown without evidence connecting the active include read to parent parser input. A valid post-edit check that still reproduces the bug also scores 2.
scale.3: A clean, fresh parent baseline unambiguously distinguishes the escaped original included token from the transformed parent token, and inspected execution or source evidence connects the active include's direct read to the parser-input insertion boundary. No passing post-edit result is visible.
scale.4: After a relevant production edit, a fresh completed build or focused test shows that a normal include supplies listener-modified text to the parent result and that the focused original token is absent, with no later contradiction.
scale.5: Fresh post-edit evidence passes the exact parent reproduction and relevant existing tests, and additionally verifies nested inclusion plus applicable clipping or marker and literal-handling boundaries without contradictory results.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reliable include-propagation execution evidence

applies_when: A parent include result or repository change intended to alter include consumption is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether an applied implementation feeds listener-modified included RST into the active parent parsing path and removes the unmodified included token from the parent result.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If valid post-edit parent output still contains the original included token, cap at 2. If only standalone included-document output changes, cap at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Post-edit parent output or focused semantic tests outrank code inspection; repository-visible production code outranks plans, pseudocode, temporary scripts, and prose. Standalone output for the included document cannot establish parent propagation.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a proposed cache or partial storage field, event occurrence, standalone rendering, or an untested edit for parent-parser consumption.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires an applied, coherent production-code path from transformed included text to the current include invocation; credit above 3 requires a successful post-edit parent semantic check.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect repository-visible production changes at the include read-to-parser-input boundary and the resulting parent doctree or rendered parent output.
metadata.oracle_test: In the focused reproduction, parsing index.rst through a normal '.. include::' must make the included occurrence become REPLACED in index.html, not merely in the included document's standalone HTML.

scale.1: No coherent production implementation is applied, or only event firing, standalone output, plans, pseudocode, or temporary reproduction files are visible.
scale.2: A production edit is applied but the transformed text is not yet connected through the active include read-to-parser-input boundary, or valid post-edit parent output remains unfixed.
scale.3: A coherent production implementation connects transformed included text to the active parser-input path, but no valid post-edit parent semantic result is visible.
scale.4: A valid post-edit normal-include check shows the parent consuming the transformed included text with the original focused token absent.
scale.5: Valid post-edit checks show correct propagation for normal and nested includes and preserve relevant clipping and literal-option boundaries.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied parent-parser propagation

applies_when: The prefix investigates why listener-modified included source is absent from a parent document.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how accurately visible source inspection and runtime evidence identify the active path by which docutils reads and inserts included RST, while distinguishing it from Sphinx's standalone source-read path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unretracted material claim contradicted by visible source or output caps the score at 2. A later explicit correction may supersede the earlier claim if the corrected trace is evidence-backed.
metadata.evidence_authority: Inspected implementation and successful runtime observations outrank speculation. The actual parent output outranks event logs, and the active docutils include path outranks cache or dependency theories unsupported by source.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating event invocation, doctree caching, dependency bookkeeping, or a separately built included document as proof of the active parent include data path.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires both the concrete direct-read operation and the concrete operation that inserts its result into the parent's parser input, plus an explicit distinction from standalone source reading.
metadata.judge_focus: Look for inspected code or runtime evidence establishing the direct include read, the parser-input insertion operation, and why separately transformed standalone source is not consumed by that include invocation.
metadata.oracle_test: The semantic reference is docutils Include reading the target independently and inserting that text into the current state machine; Sphinx's separate source-read result for the included document does not supply those inserted lines.

scale.1: No task-relevant causal account is established, or the final account is materially contradicted by visible source or output.
scale.2: A separate include path is suspected, but the account is speculative, materially self-contradictory, or identifies neither a verified direct read nor the parser-input boundary.
scale.3: Visible source or runtime evidence verifies the direct include-file read and its bypass of standalone source-read processing, but the concrete parser-input insertion operation is not identified.
scale.4: Visible evidence traces the direct include read through the concrete parser-input insertion operation and correctly separates this path from standalone processing and dependency bookkeeping.
scale.5: The complete trace also correctly accounts for clipping and marker processing, literal or code early-return behavior, nested inclusion, and the point at which transformed text must enter each applicable branch.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-grounded include-path localization

applies_when: The prefix contains failures, revised hypotheses, repeated commands, recovery actions, or claims of success.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether observations lead to accurate conclusions and useful corrections rather than unsupported completion claims or repetitive tool churn.

metadata.failure_mode: Failed or irrelevant execution is called successful, speculative complexity grows without evidence, or recovery is mistaken for a fix.
metadata.judge_focus: Claim accuracy and information gained from each material observation.

scale.1: Material failures are repeatedly misread or unsupported success is declared despite contradictory visible evidence.
scale.2: Some useful reasoning occurs, but repeated harness churn, speculative edits, or overstated conclusions dominate.
scale.3: At least one observation produces a material correction or narrower hypothesis, with mostly accurate claims.
scale.4: Failures consistently lead to repaired commands, safer edits, narrower tests, or explicit withholding of unsupported conclusions.
scale.5: The prefix rapidly converts each material observation into discriminative evidence or a coherent intervention tied to the exact current state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-driven judgment and adaptation

applies_when: The prefix inspects, explains, edits, or tests glossary object registration and duplicate detection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the prefix correctly connects normalization before glossary object registration to the collision and advances preservation of the authored spelling without reconstructing a normalized key elsewhere.

metadata.failure_mode: The collision is attributed only to generated identifiers or diagnostics, or case folding is moved into general object registration.
metadata.judge_focus: The name that reaches object registration and the key used for duplicate identity.

scale.1: The explanation or implementation preserves or worsens the collision, such as normalizing the stored term key.
scale.2: Relevant code is located, but the supplied registration name is not correctly connected to duplicate identity.
scale.3: The collision is correctly diagnosed and a concrete call-site correction is described, but it is not present at cutoff.
scale.4: The authored spelling is visibly passed at the glossary registration site and general duplicate detection remains unchanged.
scale.5: The narrow registration correction is present and source-sensitive evidence shows case-distinct definitions coexist while exact duplicates remain distinguishable.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Registration-site causal correctness

applies_when: The prefix contains a task-causal diagnosis, concrete edit plan, source edit, revert, reproduction, or repository-state inspection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the quality of the task-causal intervention actually supported at cutoff, giving credit to a precise unimplemented correction while distinguishing it from a verified narrow edit and from speculative, malformed, reverted, or contradictory work.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible state is malformed, still lowercases the registration key, moves case folding into note_object(), suppresses duplicate diagnostics, contains an unresolved broad resolver or role rewrite without reproduced necessity, or repeated ineffective edits leave application uncertain. A revert with no replacement is not completion. Cap at 3 when the narrow edit is visible but later task-relevant failures, speculative compatibility work, or missing final-state inspection leave the operative state unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: For repository state, the latest complete source inspection or final diff/status overrides earlier edit commands, plans, and claims. For behavior, execution of the edited checkout through the real glossary parser or Sphinx build overrides direct domain calls; direct StandardDomain execution overrides simulated dictionaries, regex checks, and printed expectations. A command with no confirming observation is proposed work, not an applied edit.
metadata.failure_mode: Scoring activity or an edit command as progress regardless of the resulting state, treating a clean revert as a fix, underrating a precise source-backed plan, or awarding high credit to a narrow edit whose latest state is contaminated by speculative or malformed follow-up work.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require the narrow registration-site correction to be visibly present in the latest coherent repository state. Score 5 additionally requires source-sensitive validation of both case-distinct coexistence and preserved exact-duplicate diagnostics against that same state.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the prefix isolates lowercasing before glossary object registration, whether the latest visible source passes the authored term spelling to StandardDomain.note_object(), and whether any additional role, resolver, warning, or object-storage edits are visibly necessary and coherent.
metadata.oracle_test: The authored spellings MySQL and mysql must reach real glossary registration as distinct ('term', name) identities, while repeating the exact same spelling must still invoke the existing duplicate warning; unrelated standard-domain identity and resolution behavior must remain unchanged.
metadata.stage: Causal analysis through final artifact review

scale.1: The latest visible intervention is task-contradictory or harmful: it preserves the collision, suppresses valid diagnostics, broadly changes object identity, or leaves malformed operative source.
scale.2: The relevant area is explored or an attempted edit is ineffective, reverted, speculative, or uncertain; no contradiction-free concrete correction is established at cutoff.
scale.3: The exact registration-site cause and a syntactically concrete narrow correction are established, or that correction is visibly applied but validation or later repository state remains unresolved; no higher-anchor evidence is available.
scale.4: The latest coherent source state visibly contains the narrow registration correction, preserves general duplicate handling and unrelated behavior, and has source-sensitive evidence for case-distinct glossary registration, but exact-duplicate validation or final artifact correspondence is still missing.
scale.5: The latest inspected applicable artifact contains the narrow correction and real parser or local-build evidence against that same state proves both distinct MySQL/mysql identities and the unchanged warning for an exact duplicate, with no contradictory follow-up edits or artifacts.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff-visible causal intervention quality

applies_when: The prefix considers term roles, reference resolution, general object storage, warning behavior, or additional source edits.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether changes remain at the demonstrated collision boundary and whether compatibility-sensitive role or resolver behavior is changed only in response to an observed need.

metadata.failure_mode: Speculative role or resolver rewrites, global normalization changes, or warning suppression are presented as required without discriminative evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Narrowness supported by observed behavior rather than assumed coupled edits.

scale.1: The implementation broadly changes object identity, disables diagnostics, or introduces contradictory or malformed resolution behavior.
scale.2: A substantial speculative role or resolver rewrite remains and its necessity or exact-match behavior is not established.
scale.3: The approach is mostly localized but leaves an unresolved compatibility experiment or an unnecessary secondary edit.
scale.4: The change is confined to the demonstrated registration boundary, with unrelated roles, resolvers, and duplicate checking preserved.
scale.5: The implementation is narrow and observed execution confirms that preserved definitions and existing reference behavior coexist, or a secondary change is narrowly justified by a reproduced failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Scope and compatibility discipline

applies_when: The prefix contains multiple inspections, failed commands, revised hypotheses, test-harness attempts, edit attempts, or claims about glossary behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates how efficiently visible observations narrow the glossary collision to its registration cause and advance a coherent correction, rather than producing repetitive setup churn or unsupported compatibility claims.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the trajectory ends with the wrong case-sensitivity objective, repeats substantially identical failed harness attempts without narrowing the issue, declares success against contrary output, or turns a correct narrow diagnosis into unresolved malformed source. Cap at 3 when a useful correction is followed by unresolved speculative resolver work.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed source and command results outrank thoughts and completion claims. A real parser or build result outranks direct object calls; direct object calls outrank dictionary simulations and printed expectations. Repeated failures count positively only when the next action materially changes based on their information.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding activity volume, dependency installation, or printed demonstrations as though they were discriminative task evidence, while overlooking rapid source-backed isolation and correction.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require the trajectory to have isolated the pre-registration lowercasing and converted that finding into either a successful narrow edit or a discriminative executed check. Mere repetition of setup or dependency commands cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: For each material observation, inspect whether it locates the lowercasing path, corrects a failed command, discriminates registration from resolution, applies the narrow edit, or validates a task-relevant behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Useful progress distinguishes the name supplied by make_glossary_term() to note_object() from unrelated ID generation, sorting, role processing, and general duplicate detection, then tests or edits that boundary.

scale.1: Material observations are misread, the required case polarity remains wrong, or repeated actions produce no task-causal narrowing and culminate in a false success claim.
scale.2: Some relevant code or behavior is found, but repetitive harness failures, abandoned attempts, or unsupported resolver speculation dominate and no stable concrete correction is established.
scale.3: Visible evidence isolates the registration lowercasing or yields a concrete correction, but progress stops at diagnosis, an unexecuted plan, or a later unresolved detour.
scale.4: The trajectory uses observations to isolate the registration cause and successfully applies the narrow correction or executes a discriminative source-sensitive check, with only limited non-causal churn.
scale.5: The trajectory rapidly converts source observations and any failures into a coherent narrow correction plus discriminative execution covering the task's distinct-case and exact-duplicate semantics, without contradictory detours.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Efficient evidence-to-correction progress

applies_when: The prefix contains a task-causal diagnosis, source-edit attempt, repository-state observation, revert, or behavioral check concerning glossary term registration.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the strongest contradiction-free intervention visibly established at cutoff, distinguishing a precise diagnosis from a successfully applied registration-site correction and from semantic validation of that correction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the latest visible state is malformed, reverted without replacement, still lowercases the registration name, normalizes names inside general object storage, suppresses duplicate diagnostics, or contains an unresolved broad role or resolver rewrite. Cap at 3 when a later task-relevant observation contradicts the applied edit or leaves which source state was executed unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: A latest complete source view or diff overrides earlier commands and claims. Absent a later conflicting inspection, a deterministic source-edit command with a successful observation counts as applied work; a proposed command, printed example, or command lacking an execution observation does not. Real parsing or a local Sphinx build of the edited checkout outranks direct domain calls, simulated dictionaries, and printed expectations.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a successful edit as merely proposed because no redundant final cat was run, awarding implementation credit to a plan or printed simulation, or treating an unvalidated narrow edit as equivalent to either a fully verified fix or a harmful state.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require visible evidence that the narrow registration-site edit was applied, either through a successful deterministic edit operation or an inspected source artifact. Score 5 additionally requires execution against the edited checkout that distinguishes differently cased definitions and preserves the warning for an exact repeated spelling.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine whether authored glossary spelling, rather than its lowercase form, is supplied to StandardDomain.note_object() at the glossary call site and whether the visible operative state is coherent.
metadata.oracle_test: At glossary registration, authored spellings such as MySQL and mysql must form distinct ('term', name) identities, while registering the identical spelling twice must continue to use StandardDomain's existing duplicate warning.

scale.1: The latest visible state is task-opposed or unusable: it retains or broadens case normalization, suppresses duplicate warnings, corrupts relevant source, or applies a harmful global identity change.
scale.2: Relevant code is explored or edited, but no contradiction-free concrete correction is established because attempts fail, are reverted, remain malformed, or end in unresolved broad changes.
scale.3: The exact registration-site cause and a syntactically concrete narrow correction are established, but application is not visibly supported; alternatively, application occurred but a later task-relevant contradiction leaves the operative state unresolved.
scale.4: A successful edit operation or inspected artifact shows the narrow registration call using the authored term spelling, with no visible contradictory follow-up, but the full case-distinct and exact-duplicate behavior pair is not executed against that state.
scale.5: The narrow applied correction is visibly operative, and parser or local-build evidence against that state shows differently cased definitions coexist while an identical repeated spelling still triggers the existing duplicate diagnostic.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied glossary registration correction

applies_when: Select when the visible prefix includes reproducer, build, test, or direct parser-check attempts.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether avoidable command-construction, workspace, or retry errors repeatedly prevent execution of a task-relevant repository check.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the prefix subsequently completes a direct repository `_parse_annotation()` check or a rendered HTML check and accurately inspects both `None` and an ordinary annotation such as `int`.
metadata.evidence_authority: Complete command output and the existence of expected artifacts control over assistant summaries or shell return codes distorted by pipelines, fallback commands, or later successful commands.
metadata.failure_mode: Persistent malformed validation activity is treated as harmless exploration, or a failed command, missing output file, copied conditional, or success-looking fallback is mistaken for semantic execution.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require no completed task-relevant repository check plus either at least two distinct avoidable command/workspace mistakes or repeated retries that leave a known blocker unchanged.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect command syntax, paths, configuration, exit status, produced files, recovery actions, and whether any check actually exercised repository annotation parsing or rendered links.
metadata.oracle_test: A meaningful check executes repository code and observes either `None -> py:obj` versus `int -> py:class`, or signature-mode HTML destinations for both the Python `None` constant and `int`.
metadata.stage: Establish baseline and validate parser semantics

scale.1: No validation is attempted, or attempted validation is well-formed and produces no avoidable execution churn.
scale.2: An isolated setup or command mistake occurs and is promptly corrected, or an external dependency blocker is accurately classified before the trajectory moves to productive source reasoning.
scale.3: Several validation attempts are blocked, but the failures are accurately reported and successive actions materially narrow the blocker without claiming semantic success.
scale.4: Multiple avoidable syntax, path, configuration, output-location, or unchanged-retry errors prevent every task-relevant repository check from completing.
scale.5: Severe validation unreliability is visible: failed execution is masked or reported as success, semantic conclusions are drawn from missing output, or persistent avoidable churn continues after the blocker is already known.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation churn blocking semantic progress

applies_when: Select when the trajectory investigates or explains why signature-mode `None` does not resolve like description-mode `None`.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Credits an assistant-authored causal diagnosis that `_parse_annotation()` constructs signature annotation references as Python class references and that exact text `None` must instead use the Python object role while ordinary annotations such as `int` retain the class role.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the assistant concludes that annotation spelling, description-mode fields, a hard-coded URL, or unconditional conversion of all annotations to `py:obj` is the required fix.
metadata.evidence_authority: Explicit assistant-authored causal statements at or before the cutoff control. Current source inspection may support them, but source text, commit history, tracebacks, grep results, and the existing PyField special case do not independently establish the diagnosis.
metadata.failure_mode: Partial exploration, symptom reproduction, or the pre-existing typed-field precedent is mistaken for a complete diagnosis; alternatively, exact reasoning is ignored because no edit has yet been made.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require an explicit assistant-authored statement that exact `None` needs the object role in the signature annotation path; scores 4 and 5 additionally require the ordinary-class fallback.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the assistant's own reasoning for all three required conclusions: `_parse_annotation()` is the affected signature path, exact `None` requires `py:obj`, and ordinary names such as `int` remain `py:class`. Merely displaying those names in grep, source listings, history, or tool output is not a conclusion.
metadata.oracle_test: The complete diagnosis is `_parse_annotation('None') -> pending_xref(refdomain='py', reftype='obj', reftarget='None')`, while `_parse_annotation('int')` retains `reftype='class'`.
metadata.stage: Trace the two type-hint rendering paths

scale.1: No complete causal conclusion is authored; this includes reproduction, stringification checks, generic Python-domain exploration, source listings, and discovery of the typed-field precedent without the required signature-path conclusion.
scale.2: The assistant explicitly concludes that signature annotation references are incorrectly treated as class references, but does not identify both `_parse_annotation()` and the exact `None` object-role exception.
scale.3: The assistant identifies `_parse_annotation()` and explicitly concludes that exact `None` must use `py:obj`, but does not state that ordinary annotations such as `int` must remain `py:class`.
scale.4: The assistant explicitly states the complete boundary: `_parse_annotation()` must use `py:obj` only for exact `None` and retain `py:class` for ordinary annotations such as `int`.
scale.5: The complete boundary is stated and tied to inspected current code, with the assistant also correctly explaining that the visible spelling is already `None` and that description-mode object-role handling is precedent rather than the affected implementation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete assistant-authored signature-role diagnosis

applies_when: Always apply; use score 1 when no production-source intervention is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the observable behavior caused by a production edit without equating a wrong intervention with either no intervention or a correct role-selection fix.

metadata.failure_mode: The mere existence of an edit is treated as correctness, or absence of an edit receives a positive progress bonus.
metadata.judge_focus: The concrete runtime or node behavior affected by visible production-source changes.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the changed path, the runtime annotation it receives, and the resulting pending-reference role.
metadata.stage: Implement exact role selection in annotation parsing

scale.1: No production-source intervention is visible, or visible changes consist only of reproducer, generated, or configuration content.
scale.2: A production edit touches a related path but cannot affect the runtime signature annotation, removes reference behavior, or is malformed.
scale.3: The production edit causally changes annotation behavior but targets the wrong layer, leaves the role mismatch unresolved, or introduces a visible compatibility regression.
scale.4: The production edit localizes exact `None` role selection in or directly serving `_parse_annotation()` and preserves the class fallback, but direct execution evidence is incomplete.
scale.5: The localized production edit is present and repository execution confirms both the `None` object role and ordinary annotation class role.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal behavior of a production intervention

applies_when: Always apply; use score 1 when no evaluator-facing production artifact is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible artifact is applicable, focused, and contains meaningful production work without rewarding the absence of an artifact.

metadata.failure_mode: No artifact is scored as pristine, or reproducer-only changes are treated as a valid implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: Production content, applicability, and visible repository pollution.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the complete diff, status, syntax, and presence of the functional source path.
metadata.stage: Review scope and prepare the submission

scale.1: No evaluator-facing production artifact is visible, or the visible artifact contains only reproducer or generated content, is malformed, or omits meaningful production-source work.
scale.2: The artifact contains a focused and syntactically plausible production edit, but it targets the wrong layer or does not implement the required semantics.
scale.3: The artifact contains meaningful production work but is incomplete, materially polluted, or lacks a clear compatibility boundary.
scale.4: The artifact is focused and applicable and visibly contains the exact localized role-selection fix without material unrelated changes.
scale.5: The focused artifact contains the correct production fix, appropriate regression evidence, clean formatting, and no evaluator-facing pollution.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing artifact readiness

applies_when: Select when the visible prefix investigates the missing signature-mode link or the Python-domain handling of annotation references.
