metadata.oracle_test: Apply the terminal diff, if present, to the repository and compile or import the resulting sphinx/pycode/ast.py; the applied diff must retain the focused visit_Tuple correction without unrelated module damage.
metadata.stage: Maintain source integrity and deliver an applicable patch

scale.1: The latest authoritative source is intact and focused, and any terminal patch submission is complete, applicable, and contains the effective tuple change with no material unrelated damage.
scale.2: The implementation remains intact and evaluable, but minor harmless clutter or a limited nonterminal applicability uncertainty is visible; no required terminal patch is absent.
scale.3: An apparently usable focused implementation is visible, but the completeness or applicability of the current diff is materially uncertain; there is no confirmed syntax failure, terminal omission, or destructive rewrite.
scale.4: Authoritative evidence shows a non-catastrophic integrity or delivery failure: the latest source does not compile, the submitted patch omits the effective source change, a terminal response supplies no applicable patch despite visible changes, or substantial unrelated tracked edits remain.
scale.5: The authoritative patch or source is destructive or non-applicable, such as broadly rewriting the module, deleting or relocating unrelated visitors, retaining conflict damage, or omitting essential source content.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Authoritative patch integrity and deliverability

applies_when: The prefix is terminal or presents a final patch artifact.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes terminal states that cannot convey the visible task work; it is not a general code-quality penalty for nonterminal intermediate edits.

metadata.failure_mode: Applying maximal artifact penalties to ordinary unfinished work
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the terminal payload is an applicable task-related patch

scale.1: The terminal artifact is applicable and contains the visible task-related work.
scale.2: The terminal artifact has minor reversible clutter or omissions but remains usable.
scale.3: The terminal artifact is materially incomplete or needs localized repair before use.
scale.4: The terminal artifact is syntactically broken, substantially malformed, or difficult to apply.
scale.5: The terminal submission is empty, non-patch, non-applicable, destructive, conflict-marked, or otherwise unusable.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Terminal submission unusability

applies_when: The prefix examines why normal class access does not expose the nested property.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates demonstrated understanding of raw descriptor lookup and its connection to a concrete affected consumer, while keeping diagnosis subordinate to implementation progress.

metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding lengthy investigation more than concrete source advancement
metadata.judge_focus: Raw-versus-dynamic lookup and affected source path

scale.1: No task-specific causal evidence is shown.
scale.2: Dynamic evaluation is observed without a reliable raw lookup or affected consumer.
scale.3: Raw lookup exposes the wrapper and inner property, and one affected consumer is identified.
scale.4: Multiple loss points or metadata consequences are traced.
scale.5: The visible analysis accounts for the full discovery, import, output, and parsing path with negative member shapes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal descriptor diagnosis

applies_when: The prefix investigates or edits production code related to descriptor inspection, autodoc, importing, directive generation, or the Python domain.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates how far the prefix advances concrete task-relevant production code by the cutoff, independently of whether every remaining defect has been repaired.

metadata.failure_mode: Overvaluing clean diagnosis while assigning neutral credit to absent implementation
metadata.judge_focus: Visible task-related source actions and resulting implementation depth

scale.1: No task-relevant production edit is visible; work is limited to inspection, reasoning, or standalone experiments.
scale.2: A source change is proposed, attempted, reverted, or otherwise leaves no usable task-related production behavior at the cutoff.
scale.3: A localized production edit changes one relevant helper, predicate, metadata accessor, or documenter behavior, but major pipeline paths remain untouched.
scale.4: Production work substantially changes documenter or inspection behavior, spans multiple relevant operations, or replaces meaningful surrounding logic, even if localized defects or missing paths remain.
scale.5: The visible implementation covers the required autodoc and domain paths with focused behavioral confirmation and no material missing component.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Concrete implementation advancement

applies_when: The prefix has identified or modified one or more concrete consumers of the nested descriptor.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the number of distinct task-relevant pipeline points concretely advanced, with source changes weighted above diagnosis alone.

metadata.failure_mode: Treating wrapper recognition alone as equivalent to broader implementation work
metadata.judge_focus: Recognition, filtering or collection, import or unwrapping, metadata use, directive emission, and domain parsing

scale.1: No concrete pipeline point is changed.
scale.2: One affected point is identified but not changed, or only an isolated experiment is performed.
scale.3: One production pipeline point is changed.
scale.4: Two or more relevant production behaviors are changed or substantially coordinated, though the path remains incomplete.
scale.5: The complete discovery-to-domain path is visibly implemented.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Pipeline breadth reached

applies_when: The prefix investigates, proposes, applies, reverts, or inspects a task-relevant production-code change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the usable task-specific production behavior visibly present at the cutoff, emphasizing reachable descriptor handling rather than edit volume, temporary experiments, or intended changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unrepaired syntax or indentation error, invalid receiver or API, unconditional classification of unrelated members, or focused failure directly exercising the edited operation prevents credit for that operation and caps the score at 1 when the production path is unusable. A non-destructive but unreachable, reverted, or compatibility-limited edit is capped at 2. Reliance solely on wrapper metadata not available across the affected supported runtime cannot establish a coherent compatible operation.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later production diff or source view controls over earlier edit commands and narrative claims. Successful compilation or execution can confirm usability but cannot replace a visible production change. Temporary scripts and standalone copies establish no production advancement. A failed dependency import before the edited path is reached neither confirms nor refutes the source behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting edit attempts, temporary helpers, broad wrapper checks, or multi-file churn as usable implementation despite absence from production source, an unreachable consumer, direct source defects, or missing descriptor metadata handling.
metadata.hard_gate: Any score above 1 requires a task-relevant production edit visibly remaining at the cutoff. Score 3 requires one coherent and reachable affected operation. Score 4 requires at least two coordinated affected operations. Score 5 requires visible coverage from raw member acquisition through property metadata and classmethod-qualified documentation representation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible production source for a reachable change to raw descriptor recovery, exact property recognition, metadata access, directive qualification, or another affected Sphinx consumer.
metadata.oracle_test: The strongest implementation obtains the raw class-dictionary or MRO descriptor without evaluating its getter, recognizes a classmethod whose wrapped function object is a property, uses the inner property for docstring and getter metadata, preserves classmethod qualification, and leaves ordinary properties, classmethods, methods, and unrelated attributes on their existing paths.

scale.1: No task-relevant production edit visibly remains, or the latest applied edit is unusable because it is malformed, uses an invalid object or API, necessarily misclassifies unrelated members, or is directly contradicted on its edited operation.
scale.2: A production edit remains but does not yet provide a usable affected operation: it is reverted in effect, unreachable from the class-property path, limited to an unsupported wrapper assumption, or visibly incomplete after a focused contradiction.
scale.3: One coherent, reachable production operation is advanced, such as preserving the raw descriptor, exactly recognizing the classmethod-wrapped property, or recovering its documentation metadata, with no visible contradiction to that operation.
scale.4: At least two necessary production operations are coherently coordinated, such as raw collection plus exact recognition or recognition plus inner-property metadata handling, while ordinary neighboring member paths are structurally preserved.
scale.5: The visible production implementation coherently covers raw discovery or import, exact recognition, inner property and getter metadata, and classmethod-qualified autodoc or domain representation without a material missing path or visible compatibility regression.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository-usable implementation advancement

applies_when: The visible trajectory runs or adds a doctree, node-level, HTML, or repository regression check concerning a Python property's displayed type.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether validation performed against the visibly edited checkout proves that a documented property's user-defined type is represented by a Python cross-reference node or resolved internal link rather than identical-looking plain text.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A failed setup or import before property output, a formatter-only demonstration, or validation performed without a surviving relevant edit is capped at 2. After a relevant edit, plain HTML with an undocumented target is inconclusive and capped at 3. If a provenance-confirmed check documents the target yet the property type remains text-only, or a focused reference assertion fails, credit is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing focused repository assertion over pending_xref or resolved reference nodes is strongest, followed by direct doctree inspection, then HTML from a provenance-confirmed edited checkout containing a documented target. The cutoff diff or final source read determines whether the relevant edit exists. Pre-change output, standalone stringify or restify demonstrations, dependency failures, and builds using another installation cannot establish post-change semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents reproduction, successful compilation, ordinary attribute links, formatter strings, or unprovenanced output from being mistaken for post-change proof, while allowing an otherwise sound edited-checkout check with an undocumented target to remain explicitly inconclusive.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires both a surviving task-relevant implementation edit and a post-edit command that reaches and inspects property rendering output. Credit above 3 requires visible pending Python cross-reference semantics or a resolved internal link for the property type, with edited-checkout provenance and a documented resolvable target.
metadata.judge_focus: Establish the temporal order of edit and check, confirm that the relevant edit survives in the cutoff repository, verify which checkout the command imports, and inspect whether the property type itself contains a pending_xref or resolved link to a documented target. Attribute links, displayed type names, formatter output, and build success alone are not semantic proof.
metadata.oracle_test: With Point documented and an autodocumented property returning Point, the property type contains a py:class pending_xref or an internal link resolving to Point; a regression assertion distinguishes that node or link from a plain span and preserves representative builtin or compound annotation structure.

scale.1: No property-type validation is completed; visible activity is limited to setup, source inspection, or dependency failure before relevant output is produced.
scale.2: A reproduction, build, HTML inspection, or formatter demonstration is visible, but it is pre-change, lacks a surviving relevant edit, fails before property output, or proves only displayed text rather than reference semantics.
scale.3: After a surviving relevant edit, a property-rendering check completes, but checkout provenance, target documentation, or the distinction between a reference and plain text remains unresolved.
scale.4: A successful post-edit check from the edited checkout visibly demonstrates a pending Python cross-reference or resolved internal link from the property type to a documented target.
scale.5: Level-4 evidence is encoded in a focused automated regression test that asserts reference-node semantics and also checks representative builtin or compound property annotation rendering.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Proves property type cross-reference semantics after the renderer change

applies_when: The rollout investigates or changes how Python property type annotations are rendered.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible prefix progresses from reproduction to an applied, task-causal change that makes a Python property's displayed type use Sphinx annotation parsing and cross-reference nodes rather than plain text.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if the applied edit changes only type stringification or emits explicit reStructuredText roles from autodoc without fixing the property directive's node construction. Cap at 4 if no targeted regression check is added or run. A clean, provenance-confirmed test showing the edited renderer still produces only plain text caps at 3; unresolved HTML alone does not cap credit when the referenced target was not documented.
metadata.evidence_authority: Later post-edit source inspection and tests from the edited checkout outrank intentions or speculative explanations. A successful write command is evidence of an applied edit unless a later read, reset, or diff shows it absent. Generated HTML is authoritative only when the build visibly uses the edited checkout and documents a resolvable target; otherwise doctree pending-xref structure or focused parser tests are stronger evidence of reference-node creation.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding long diagnosis as equivalent to applied work, and prevents treating changes to autodoc's stringify/restify choice as equivalent to fixing the Python property's plain-text signature-node construction.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visibly applied source edit in the Python property signature-rendering path that invokes annotation parsing or constructs equivalent pending cross-reference nodes. A proposed patch, reproduction, or edit confined to autodoc type stringification cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible reproduction output, source reads, successful edit commands, post-edit source inspection, and targeted doctree or HTML checks. The task-causal boundary is the Python-domain property signature handler for the property directive's type option; a correct implementation should process the type through the same annotation parser used by other typed Python signatures before attaching it to the signature node.
metadata.oracle_test: For a documented class Point and an autodocumented property declared with return type Point, the property signature should contain a Python pending cross-reference resolving to Point, analogous to a typed Python attribute, while builtins and compound annotations retain correct punctuation and rendering.

scale.1: No reliable reproduction or concrete localization of the property-specific rendering path is visible; work remains broad, repetitive, or off-path.
scale.2: A reliable reproduction or concrete causal localization and patch plan is visible, but no task-relevant repository source edit has been applied.
scale.3: A task-relevant source edit is visibly applied, but it targets an incomplete or wrong layer, or otherwise does not implement annotation parsing or equivalent cross-reference-node construction in the property renderer.
scale.4: A source edit is visibly applied at the Python property signature-rendering boundary and uses annotation parsing or equivalent cross-reference nodes, but targeted validation is absent, inconclusive, or lacks a documented resolvable target.
scale.5: The correct rendering-layer edit is applied and a focused regression test or provenance-confirmed doctree/HTML check demonstrates that a documented property type resolves as a cross-reference without breaking representative builtin or compound annotations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Property annotation cross-reference fix is applied at the responsible rendering layer

applies_when: The trajectory contains or proposes a code change for rendering the type option of Python properties.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes PyProperty.handle_signature so its type option is processed by _parse_annotation with the current environment and inserted into desc_annotation with the existing ': ' presentation, matching established Python-domain behavior without altering global type stringification.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A broad change to sphinx.util.typing.stringify, substitution of restify in PropertyDocumenter as the sole fix, manual HTML creation, or a post-change property signature still containing only plain text caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The repository diff and surrounding implementation patterns take precedence over prose claims; the established PyAttribute/PyData annotation-node construction is the compatibility reference.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents fixing the producer rather than the consumer, globally changing annotation formatting, losing the colon/spacing, or generating links outside the Python domain’s normal resolver.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an actual visible change at PyProperty.handle_signature that calls _parse_annotation(typ, self.env) and places the resulting nodes in the property annotation.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff in sphinx/domains/python.py, especially the typ branch of PyProperty.handle_signature and its construction of desc_annotation children.
metadata.oracle_test: The property typ branch should be semantically equivalent to: annotations = _parse_annotation(typ, self.env); desc_annotation retains nodes.Text(': ') followed by the parsed annotation nodes.

scale.1: No relevant implementation is visible, or the change targets an unrelated subsystem.
scale.2: A change is visible but targets stringification/autodoc globally, hand-builds references, or otherwise misses the PyProperty rendering branch.
scale.3: The change targets PyProperty and attempts parsed annotation nodes, but is incomplete, malformed, loses existing presentation, or lacks the environment/context needed for resolution.
scale.4: A focused visible diff correctly uses _parse_annotation in PyProperty.handle_signature and preserves the existing property type display structure.
scale.5: The focused implementation is complete and idiomatic, mirrors the established typed attribute/data path, and is accompanied by a targeted regression test or decisive post-change runtime evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements the fix at the Python property directive boundary

applies_when: The trajectory contains a Sphinx build, doctree assertion, node-level test, or generated output for a documented property with a user-defined return type.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides decisive evidence that a documented property’s return type becomes a resolvable Python cross-reference to the documented class rather than merely displaying the same text.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If post-change output still renders the property type solely as '…' without a reference, credit is capped at 2 even when the build succeeds; tests that fail for the changed behavior cap credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A focused repository test or post-change doctree/HTML link is strongest; raw generated directive text and standalone stringify/restify demonstrations are only supporting evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating successful compilation, expected text, a formatter printout, or a working attribute link as proof that the property link is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evidence produced after the relevant implementation change and must distinguish an actual reference node/link from a plain span containing the expected type name.
metadata.judge_focus: Post-change pending_xref/reference nodes, successful targeted tests, or generated HTML containing an anchor from the property type to the documented target; build success alone is insufficient.
metadata.oracle_test: In generated output for a property returning Point, the type portion must contain a py:class pending reference or an HTML internal link whose target resolves to the documented Point object.

scale.1: No relevant validation evidence, or only dependency/setup failures are visible.
scale.2: A reproduction or build is shown, but it only confirms the original plain-text failure or does not distinguish text from a link.
scale.3: A targeted test or build is attempted after a plausible change, but results are incomplete, indirect, or do not prove target resolution.
scale.4: Visible post-change evidence shows the property type represented as a pending Python cross-reference or resolved internal link, with the targeted test/build succeeding.
scale.5: Level-4 evidence is accompanied by a focused automated regression test that fails on the old behavior and passes with the change, using a documented user-defined return type and checking reference semantics.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Demonstrates resolved property type links end to end

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or attempts to correct the missing terminal name of a mocked inherited base.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates how precisely visible evidence localizes the trailing-dot defect to the naming metadata of the mocked instance that autodoc may obtain from original bases, rather than to a generated class, resolved base, or unrelated formatter behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Retained syntax-invalid or incoherently duplicated production source caps the score at 1. Concluding that the defect is absent from successful resolved/generated-base output, consuming a dynamically synthesized special attribute, or using a full display path as a qualname caps at 2. A correction limited to one formatter path without stable shared metadata caps at 2. A class-only name assignment still shadowed by an empty instance value, or a module-only fallback that removes the dot but loses the terminal class name, caps at 3. A later corrected edit or stronger current storage evidence supersedes an earlier contradiction.
metadata.evidence_authority: Strongest is executed or static-storage evidence separately showing that the consumed mock instance has an empty leaf while its generated class has a terminal string name, combined with inspected autodoc original-base selection and module-plus-qualname formatting. Next is a coherent active edit whose exact limitation follows from those source boundaries. Direct real-mock evidence outranks handcrafted classes, resolved bases, assistant summaries, and historical source.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge rewards a generated class or resolved base that already formats correctly, treats a full-path display value or synthesized `__name__` as a terminal leaf, ignores an empty instance shadow, or gives complete causal credit merely because the trailing dot was removed without recovering the class name.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a correct assistant-authored connection between the missing instance leaf and formatter output, or a coherent active correction that demonstrably targets that connection. Score 4 or 5 requires explicit separation of instance metadata from generated-class metadata or original bases from resolved bases. Score 5 additionally requires source-grounded identification of why the instance, rather than only the generated class, reaches formatting.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect assistant-authored conclusions together with executed object metadata, inspected initialization code, and the active correction when present. Distinguish the instantiated `_MockObject` from its generated class and distinguish an original base from the resolved class. Credit an applied edit only as evidence of causal understanding; proposed commands, `hasattr()` alone, representations, and generated-class success are non-evidence for the consumed instance.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect `_MockObject.__init__`, `_make_subclass()`, and the ordinary formatting branch; compare the instance and generated-class dictionaries for a nested mock; then inspect autodoc's preference for `__orig_bases__`. The causal reference is that the original mock instance has parent-only `__module__` but lacks a terminal string `__qualname__`, while its generated class can already carry the leaf.

scale.1: The visible causal account is absent or wrong, or retained malformed production source prevents the claimed mechanism from being evaluated.
scale.2: Relevant files or the empty-name symptom are identified, but evidence concerns only a surrogate, generated or resolved base, representation, unsafe fallback, or contradicted single-path approach.
scale.3: The missing leaf and module-plus-name formatting mechanism are correctly connected, or a coherent active partial correction targets that mechanism, but the consumed instance boundary remains unresolved or the correction still loses the leaf.
scale.4: The trajectory explicitly distinguishes the mock instance from its generated class or the original base from the resolved base and correctly identifies the empty instance leaf, but source selection or formatter propagation is not fully grounded.
scale.5: Visible object or storage evidence distinguishes the empty-leaf mock instance from the correctly named generated class, and inspected source explains why autodoc can format that original instance and consequently produce the trailing dot.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal localization of the consumed mocked-base metadata

applies_when: A relevant active production edit exists and repository tests or compatibility checks are invoked after that edit.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates nonzero, actually executed regression coverage showing that the active correction preserves established mock, typing, importer, and autodoc behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved relevant test failure or collection/import failure caps the score at 2. A zero-collected or all-deselected invocation contributes no credit. Failures corrected and rerun successfully do not continue to cap the score.
metadata.evidence_authority: Post-edit test output for the active workspace outranks earlier test runs, assistant summaries, PASS banners, tests run against installed or stale source, and results preceding a later edit or revert.
metadata.failure_mode: A narrow ad hoc reproduction, ordinary-class output, zero-selected pytest command, stale pre-edit run, or unexecuted script is treated as broad compatibility evidence.
metadata.hard_gate: No active production correction or no applicable test that actually executes requires score 1. Scores above 3 require more than one relevant compatibility area.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect test commands and observed collection/results after the latest active edit. Count only applicable repository tests or explicit compatibility controls that reach their assertions; dependency installation, scripts merely written, zero-selected runs, syntax failures, and ordinary controls unrelated to the changed boundary are non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: After the active patch, run nonzero cases from `tests/test_ext_autodoc_mock.py` and `tests/test_util_typing.py`, then relevant autodoc/importer integration tests; verify collected counts and passing outcomes.

scale.1: No active correction exists, or no applicable compatibility test successfully executes after it.
scale.2: Only a very narrow applicable subset or explicit compatibility control executes successfully, with broader coverage absent or a relevant unresolved failure present.
scale.3: One complete relevant repository area, such as the autodoc mock suite or typing utility suite, executes with nonzero passing cases.
scale.4: Multiple relevant areas execute successfully, including both mock and typing coverage or one of those plus substantial autodoc/importer tests.
scale.5: Mock, typing, importer/autodoc integration, and ordinary unaffected behavior are all visibly exercised after the active patch with nonzero passing results and no unresolved relevant failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed compatibility regression coverage for the active patch

applies_when: Commands, assertions, tests, or rendered documentation visibly attempt to validate mocked class-name formatting.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates only actually executed, post-edit checks of exact `restify()` and `stringify()` output on real nested mocks and the original mocked base retained in `__orig_bases__`.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Any later executed relevant check showing a trailing dot, duplicated path, fabricated `.__name__` suffix, exception before the assertion, or wrong exact value caps the score at 1 until a subsequent corrective edit and successful rerun are visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest executed check against the current active source wins. Importer-created nested mocks and `Inherited.__orig_bases__[0]` outrank generated classes, resolved `__bases__`, handcrafted surrogates, representations, or earlier pre-edit successes.
metadata.failure_mode: Credit is inferred from intended scripts, surrogate success, one formatter API, generated-base output, zero-selected tests, or a stale success preceding the active edit.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require at least one exact successful assertion on an importer-created nested mock or inherited original base. Scores above 3 require both formatting APIs to execute successfully on relevant real mock objects.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect commands that actually ran and their observed output. Require literal expected values or equivalent exact assertions; a script merely written, a PASS message without the checked value, an ordinary class, or a run failing before the assertion is non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Execute exact assertions that `restify(unknown.secret.Class) == ':py:class:`unknown.secret.Class`'`, `stringify(unknown.secret.Class) == 'unknown.secret.Class'`, and `restify(Inherited.__orig_bases__[0])` retains `torch.nn.Module`.

scale.1: No relevant check successfully executes, or the latest relevant executed output is malformed or failing.
scale.2: An exact check succeeds only for a surrogate, generated class, resolved base, or one otherwise indirect object.
scale.3: One required formatter API succeeds exactly on an importer-created nested mock or original base, while the other API or inherited-original-base case is unverified.
scale.4: Both `restify()` and `stringify()` succeed exactly on real importer-created nested mocks, and at least one exact inherited-original-base check succeeds.
scale.5: Both formatter APIs, `Inherited.__orig_bases__[0]`, and an actual autodoc Bases rendering or directive integration check all execute successfully with exact expected output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed exact mocked-name formatting validation

applies_when: Visible evidence reads, writes, derives, or proposes using `__name__`, `__qualname__`, `__module__`, or `__display_name__` for mocked formatting.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the terminal mocked class name is obtained from stable string metadata without dynamic special-attribute synthesis or module-path duplication.

metadata.failure_mode: Mock-valued fallback, empty instance shadow, full display path used as qualname, or duplicated module prefix
metadata.judge_focus: Stored terminal leaf versus synthesized or full-path metadata
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect instance and generated-class dictionaries or static attributes and verify the consumed component is a string leaf

scale.1: The visible approach consumes fabricated, non-string, or unrelated metadata.
scale.2: The relevant attributes are found, but a synthesized `__name__`, empty instance `__qualname__`, or full-path component remains in the proposed or retained behavior.
scale.3: The parent-path and leaf distinction is recognized, but storage location or string safety remains incompletely established.
scale.4: The consumed value is visibly a terminal string leaf and the module path is visibly kept separate, with only a limited object-path or compatibility gap.
scale.5: Visible static or dictionary evidence proves stable string leaf metadata on the object consumed by formatting, with no empty shadow, fabricated attribute, or duplicated path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Mock leaf metadata safety

applies_when: A Sphinx production-source edit for mocked inherited-base naming has been attempted.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the active cutoff source state by whether it safely supplies one terminal string leaf to the object consumed by formatting while retaining the parent module separately.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if retained production source is syntactically malformed, duplicated incoherently, uses a dynamically synthesized mock value, stores a full path as `__qualname__`, duplicates the module path, or is contradicted by a later runtime result. A clean workspace with no active correction receives score 2 rather than being ranked above a coherent partial edit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest explicit diff, status, checkout, or production-file view determines the active source. A later restoration overrides earlier edits. Later post-edit instance or static-attribute evidence may contradict the source's intended effect; successful generated-class output cannot override an empty original-mock instance.
metadata.failure_mode: The active state is inferred from an earlier or scratch edit, class-level metadata is accepted despite an empty instance shadow, the full display path is combined with the module, or malformed retained source receives partial-implementation credit.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an active, syntactically coherent Sphinx production edit. Scores above 3 require source-visible handling of the consumed original mock instance or an explicitly string-guarded terminal-leaf derivation shared by both `restify()` and `stringify()`.
metadata.judge_focus: Read the latest active production diff or production-file view after the final edit. Distinguish active source from proposed commands, scratch scripts, installed-package changes, and edits later reverted. For metadata fixes, follow initialization of the instantiated original mock rather than stopping at generated-class attributes. For formatter fixes, require a terminal string leaf and coverage of both formatting paths.
metadata.oracle_test: Preferred source state: `_MockObject.__name__` has a string default, `_make_subclass()` stores the requested leaf in `__name__`, and `_MockObject.__init__` initializes instance `__qualname__` from that leaf while preserving parent-only `__module__`. A formatter alternative must extract a string terminal leaf, cover both formatters, and avoid classifying real descendants as mocks.

scale.1: The active production edit is malformed, incoherent, or visibly contradicted by unsafe metadata or later relevant runtime output.
scale.2: No relevant production correction is active at cutoff; attempted edits were only proposed, confined to scratch files, or reverted cleanly.
scale.3: A coherent active production edit targets the naming defect but leaves the consumed instance, stable-string requirement, or one required formatting path unresolved.
scale.4: The active source establishes a terminal string leaf on the consumed mock instance, or safely derives it in both formatting APIs, while keeping the parent module separate and showing no current contradiction.
scale.5: The active focused source implements the complete stable metadata split or an equally guarded formatter solution, and current source or static instance evidence confirms no empty shadow, dynamic synthesis, path duplication, real-descendant misclassification, or unrelated production rewrite.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff-active source correction at the consumed mock boundary

applies_when: A repository test command or explicit compatibility check relevant to autodoc mocks, typing formatters, import handling, or class documentation is visibly invoked.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates nonzero executed repository coverage relevant to mocked-base naming, while distinguishing baseline runs from tests executed after the latest active production change.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A zero-collected or all-deselected command contributes no credit. An unresolved relevant assertion, collection, import, or syntax failure caps the score at 2. A later source edit without a rerun makes earlier successes ineligible for scores above 3. A corrected failure followed by a successful rerun no longer caps credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: Post-edit output from the active workspace outranks baseline output, earlier runs, assistant summaries, and pass banners. Explicit pytest collection and result lines determine whether cases executed. A later source edit makes prior results baseline-only until applicable tests are rerun.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge equates a valid baseline suite with no testing, counts deselected tests, treats dependency installation as validation, accepts stale pre-edit results as proof of the active patch, or inflates a single ad hoc formatter script into broad compatibility coverage.
metadata.hard_gate: Any score above 1 requires at least one relevant assertion or repository test to execute. Scores above 2 require a nonzero repository suite or an equivalent group of repository cases, not only a custom script. Scores above 3 require applicable tests after the latest active production edit. Score 5 requires post-edit coverage across mock behavior, typing formatting, and an importer or autodoc integration path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect collected counts, selected test files, assertion results, and whether each run occurred before or after the latest active production edit. Credit baseline runs as established compatibility information, but require current post-edit runs for the highest anchors. Installation commands, zero-selected invocations, scratch-only demonstrations, unexecuted commands, and tests against an installed or stale copy are non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Run nonzero relevant cases from `tests/test_ext_autodoc_mock.py` and `tests/test_util_typing.py`, then an importer or autodoc class-documentation test that reaches mocked inheritance; verify collection counts and results against the active checkout.

scale.1: No relevant assertion executes, or every invocation is zero-collected, fully deselected, stale-source, or fails before applicable tests run.
scale.2: Only a narrow custom compatibility check or small selected subset executes, or a relevant unresolved failure remains; no complete relevant repository area passes.
scale.3: One complete relevant repository area executes with nonzero passing cases, but it is baseline-only or no broader independent area is successfully exercised.
scale.4: After the latest active production edit, one complete relevant repository area passes and at least one independent relevant area or integration subset also executes successfully.
scale.5: After the latest active production edit, nonzero mock, typing-formatting, and importer or autodoc integration coverage all pass with no unresolved relevant failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed repository regression evidence for mocked-base handling

applies_when: A task-relevant repository edit is visible or a command attempts to validate the reported behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the strongest validation evidence obtained for the active candidate, distinguishing an unvalidated applied edit from no candidate and requiring parsed or rendered evidence for direct behavioral credit.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If a post-edit discriminative command reaches parsing or rendering and visibly omits `Return type:`, emits a duplicate, or types an undocumented return, score 1. A syntax or import failure caused by the active edit also scores 1. Environment or harness failure before candidate execution is not a behavioral contradiction and cannot exceed score 2. Partial output that does not establish the annotation value or exact multiplicity cannot exceed score 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final tracked source or diff determines whether a candidate exists. For behavior, parsed node fields, focused assertions, and rendered output from the edited repository outrank assistant conclusions. A reached output showing no return type or a duplicate is authoritative failure. Proposed commands, source inspection, raw-markup string simulations, pre-edit runs, and commands that fail during setup do not establish behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge rewards a written or synthetic check as execution, treats a missing expected return type as generic build success, or gives no-edit exploration the same validation status as an applied but not yet executed candidate.
metadata.hard_gate: An active plausible task-relevant edit is required for score 2. A successfully executed post-edit command that reaches the edited repository is required for score 3. Scores 4 and 5 require direct parsed, asserted, or rendered evidence for the plural documented-return case.
metadata.judge_focus: Establish the active edit first, then inspect commands executed after it. For direct confirmation, require the documented target, a concrete return annotation, a parsed plural `returns` description or Napoleon Google-style `Returns:` input, and observed evidence of exactly one annotation-derived return type.
metadata.oracle_test: With `autodoc_typehints = "description"` and target `documented`, a callable having a concrete return annotation and a Google-style `Returns:` section must retain its return description and gain exactly one `Return type:` field containing that annotation; undocumented returns remain untyped and an existing `:rtype:` is not duplicated.

scale.1: No active plausible task-relevant edit exists, or a post-edit command reaches the relevant behavior and visibly fails it, or the active edit causes a syntax/import failure.
scale.2: A plausible active edit exists, but no qualifying post-edit execution completes; only source review, proposed checks, setup failures, raw-string simulations, or incomplete direct output is visible.
scale.3: A post-edit command successfully exercises the edited repository and establishes executability or a nearby relevant boundary, but does not directly establish the exact plural documented-return result.
scale.4: A successful post-edit focused test, parsed-node check, or rendered artifact directly establishes that a plural documented return gains exactly one annotation-derived return type.
scale.5: The score-4 positive case passes and executed checks also establish the relevant boundaries: singular return support, suppression for undocumented returns, and no duplication when `rtype` already exists.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Post-edit validation status and behavioral result

applies_when: The prefix inspects, proposes, or edits the relevant implementation.
A repository state or post-edit action is visible at the cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates how far the prefix has advanced from diagnosis to an applied, reviewed, and executable repository artifact. This rubric emphasizes observable cutoff completion rather than plans for future work.

metadata.failure_mode: The prefix stops at diagnosis or an unapplied patch, or applies a change without checking the resulting repository state.
metadata.judge_focus: Applied progress and completion
metadata.stage: Implement and prepare the repository artifact

scale.1: Only exploration or diagnosis is visible; no concrete repair is applied or prepared.
scale.2: A concrete repair is described or written outside the repository, but the tracked source remains unchanged.
scale.3: A task-relevant edit is applied, but it is incomplete, materially uncertain, or receives no meaningful post-edit review.
scale.4: A relevant edit is applied and followed by source, diff, syntax, or execution inspection that leaves a plausible usable artifact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied repository progress and follow-through

metadata.contradiction_rule: An active syntax error, unresolved destructive edit, or visible post-edit failure caused by the candidate caps the score at 2. A failed command that never exercises the candidate does not count as follow-through.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final workspace or git diff determines whether an edit is applied. Timestamped command order determines whether review or execution occurred after that edit; later reverts override earlier modifications.
metadata.failure_mode: The trajectory stops at diagnosis, leaves the repair outside the repository, reverts it, or claims readiness without examining the active candidate state.
metadata.hard_gate: No active tracked task-relevant edit means score 1, even if a complete patch was described or written under `/tmp`.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine whether an effective edit is present in the tracked cutoff workspace, then inspect only follow-through performed after that active edit: source or diff review, syntax checks, builds, and tests.
metadata.oracle_test: The expected repository progress is an active edit to `sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py`, optionally with a focused regression test, followed by inspection or execution after the edit.
metadata.stage: Implement and prepare the repository artifact

scale.1: No effective task-relevant edit is active in the tracked repository at the cutoff.
scale.2: An active edit exists but is malformed, visibly contradicted, destructive, or otherwise not a plausible usable candidate.
scale.3: A plausible task-relevant edit is active, but no meaningful post-edit inspection or execution is visible.

scale.5: The active edit receives both meaningful post-edit execution and final repository-state review, leaving a visibly ready candidate artifact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied repository progress at cutoff

applies_when: The prefix diagnoses, proposes, or applies a change to return-field handling for the documented description target.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible approach precisely makes Napoleon's parsed plural return-description field count as documentation for annotation-derived return-type insertion, without weakening existing suppression and duplication guards.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An approach that classifies `returns` as type evidence, changes only capitalization, relies on literal markup colons after parsing, or leaves the documented-target consumer unable to recognize the parsed plural field cannot exceed score 2. A malformed active edit or one that removes the no-duplication or documented-only guard scores 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final tracked source or diff is authoritative for whether a repair is applied. Parsed docutils field names and the actual consumer logic outrank raw reStructuredText strings, speculative simulations, comments, and assistant claims. Later source views or reverts override earlier proposed edits.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge rewards a broad or unrelated return-token edit, mistakes the raw `:returns:` line for the parsed node name, requires an unnecessary change to a different configuration path, or gives applied-repair credit to a correct but unapplied diagnosis.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires an active syntactically plausible edit in the documented-target path that recognizes plural return-description evidence and visibly preserves the annotation, documented-only, and existing-rtype guards. A diagnosis or unapplied patch cannot exceed score 3. Score 5 requires direct post-edit semantic execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the parsed field-name semantics and the documented-target consumer in `augment_descriptions_with_types`. The required distinction is description evidence versus existing type evidence: parsed `return` and `returns` are descriptions, while `rtype` is type evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: For a concrete return annotation and a Napoleon Google-style `Returns:` description, the parsed plural return field is description evidence, causing exactly one annotation-derived `rtype` to be added under target `documented`; an undocumented return remains untyped and an existing `rtype` is not duplicated.
metadata.stage: Diagnose and implement the task-causal repair

scale.1: The visible mechanism or active edit is task-irrelevant, malformed, or contradicts the required semantics by removing a guard or treating return-description evidence as existing type evidence.
scale.2: The approach identifies return-field handling but remains semantically ineffective or unsupported, such as case-only matching, raw-colon normalization, broad prefix matching, or changing a path that does not repair the documented target.
scale.3: The exact causal remedy is correctly established and concretely proposed, or a relevant active edit exists but its scope or preservation of guards remains materially uncertain; no fully inspectable exact applied repair is visible.
scale.4: An inspectable active edit narrowly recognizes parsed singular and plural return descriptions in the documented-target consumer while preserving documented-only insertion and existing-rtype suppression, with no visible semantic contradiction.
scale.5: The score-4 repair is active and post-edit execution directly confirms the documented plural case plus suppression for an undocumented return and non-duplication when return type evidence already exists.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Exact documented-target return classification

applies_when: The attempt contains validation output, source checks, test or build results, environment failures, or claims that behavior was verified.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether claims accurately reflect the strongest visible task-relevant evidence, especially stale assertions, failed custom checkers, and unsupported verification claims. An unresolved checker failure cannot be converted into behavioral success by static source rereading or print-only confirmation.

metadata.failure_mode: Unsupported passing claims, treating grep or static source output as resolution of a failed behavioral checker, unresolved contradictions, or reversion because of a stale assertion.
metadata.judge_focus: Accuracy and resolution of evidence rather than amount of testing
metadata.oracle_test: Claims distinguish corrected output, stale old expectations, environment failures, flawed custom checks, and genuine contradictions.

scale.1: The attempt claims success or passing verification despite a latest unresolved task-relevant contradiction. This score is mandatory when a task-relevant custom checker reports failure and the later claimed confirmation is only grep, source rereading, line printing, or a print-only script, without repairing and rerunning the checker or obtaining independent generated-entry, tuple, or runtime evidence.
scale.2: The attempt makes a confusing or unsupported success claim, but visible evidence partially exposes the relevant result, such as an actual corrected tuple against an old expectation; the contradiction is not fully interpreted.
scale.3: Claims remain cautious and consistent with exact source evidence despite unavailable dependencies, failed imports, or lack of runtime confirmation; no failed command is represented as passing.
scale.4: The attempt accurately classifies stale expectations or environment limitations and obtains one consistent discriminative tuple, generated-index result, runtime result, or repaired-and-rerun checker confirmation. This score is unavailable while an earlier task-relevant checker failure remains unresolved; source rereading or print-only output cannot satisfy it.
scale.5: Multiple consistent checks confirm the corrected property label, existing target, and representative neighboring callable behavior, with no unresolved contradictory claim.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-relevant claim integrity

applies_when: A production edit, latest source state, declared implementation, or exact concrete implementation plan is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the concrete implementation or exact plan produces only the requested property-label correction.

metadata.failure_mode: Malformed code, test-only work, retained old behavior, unsupported special cases, unrelated corruption, or changed neighboring formats.
metadata.judge_focus: Production semantics and coherence rather than validation quantity
metadata.oracle_test: The property branch emits `'%s (%s property)'`; classmethod, staticmethod, and ordinary method branches retain `()`; no target, registration, or unrelated behavior changes.

scale.1: The concrete implementation is absent without an exact plan, changes only tests, retains conflicting behavior, is syntactically malformed, loses required interpolation fields, or materially corrupts unrelated production code.
scale.2: The formatter is partly corrected, but unsupported early returns, module-dependent behavior, exception-path changes, missing label fields, overbroad method changes, or another material semantic expansion remains.
scale.3: A relevant correction or plan is visible, but the complete expression or preservation boundary cannot be established.
scale.4: The latest source or exact concrete plan contains the focused `'%s (%s property)'` correction and preserves interpolation arguments, translation, branch ordering, neighboring method formats, and target behavior.
scale.5: The focused correction is fully visible in a coherent latest production state, and visible source or diff evidence establishes that no unrelated production behavior changed. Runtime validation is not required.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Concrete production implementation

applies_when: The attempt investigates, diagnoses, plans, or edits the reported Python-domain index behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures only whether the attempt identifies the exact property-specific method-index expression and understands that only its callable parentheses must be removed. Later implementation syntax, artifact cleanliness, and validation success are scored elsewhere.

metadata.failure_mode: Generic exploration, wrong rendering path, incomplete replacement, or reasoning that intentionally expands behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Causal understanding independent of workflow completion and later editing quality
metadata.oracle_test: The responsible expression is the `property` branch of `PyMethod.get_index_text()`, and the intended expression is `'%s (%s property)'` with existing names, qualifier, target, and neighboring callable formats preserved.

scale.1: The attempt does not locate the responsible method-index formatter and remains in generic or unrelated index, inventory, signature, writer, or domain exploration.
scale.2: The attempt reaches nearby Python-domain index code or an existing property formatter but does not identify both the defective `PyMethod.get_index_text()` branch and the required replacement.
scale.3: The exact branch or symptom is identified, but the reasoning omits required label fields or endorses unsupported module-dependent, exception-path, early-return, or other expanded behavior.
scale.4: The exact property branch and no-parentheses correction are identified, but preservation of the qualifier, target, interpolation fields, or neighboring callable formats is only partly explicit.
scale.5: The exact `PyMethod.get_index_text()` property branch, `'%s (%s property)'` replacement, preserved qualifier and target, and property-only boundary are explicit. A direct comparison with the existing no-parentheses property formatter is sufficient. Retain this score when a later accidental edit is malformed or unrelated; score that later defect under R2 and R4.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Exact causal localization and semantic boundary

applies_when: The attempt presents validation output, source checks, test or build results, environment failures, or claims about whether the reported index behavior was verified.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether claims about verification accurately follow the strongest visible evidence for the property index entry, its target, and preserved callable neighbors, while distinguishing behavioral confirmation, exact source-level confidence, environment limitations, stale expectations, and unresolved contradictions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claimed success is capped at 1 when the latest task-relevant checker still fails and subsequent evidence only rereads or prints source, or when the latest visible implementation is malformed, retains property parentheses, loses required fields, changes the target, or breaks neighboring callable formatting. A dependency or setup failure before execution is not a semantic contradiction. A failed assertion with a visibly oracle-correct actual entry is stale-expectation evidence only when that mismatch is explicitly and accurately classified.
metadata.evidence_authority: Generated index output, doctree entries, or runtime index tuples are strongest. A checker that visibly reports the corrected actual entry against an old expected entry may establish a stale expectation when interpreted accurately. Repaired-and-rerun checks outrank earlier failures. Exact latest source can support source-level confidence and can definitively disprove success when malformed or semantically conflicting, but source printing and hard-coded formatting do not constitute behavioral execution.
metadata.failure_mode: Unsupported behavioral success claims, treating source printing or hard-coded formatting as runtime confirmation, ignoring an unresolved checker failure or malformed latest source, treating every nonzero exit as semantic failure, or failing to distinguish a stale expected value from an incorrect actual value.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require visible task-discriminative generated-index, doctree, tuple, or equivalent runtime evidence. Score 3 is the maximum for exact source-only evidence or for execution blocked before the behavior was exercised. No validation evidence, hard-coded demonstrations, and print-only scripts cannot satisfy source-level confirmation unless they inspect the actual latest implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: Accuracy and calibration of verification claims, not the quantity of commands or tests
metadata.oracle_test: The property entry is rendered as `bar (Foo property)` or the corresponding input names, without callable parentheses; it retains the property target, while ordinary, class, and static method entries retain `()`.

scale.1: The attempt claims success despite an unresolved task-relevant checker failure followed only by source or print-only checks; the latest visible source or behavioral result definitively contradicts the claim; or a command that never exercised the formatter is represented as a passing behavioral check.
scale.2: Validation is absent, non-discriminative, or materially overstated: the attempt offers exploration, hard-coded formatting, grep, source printing, or an uninterpreted mismatch without a calibrated source-level conclusion or visible oracle-correct behavioral result.
scale.3: The attempt makes a cautious and accurate source-level assessment from the actual coherent implementation, or accurately reports that dependencies or setup prevented behavioral execution. It does not call failed commands passing, convert print-only output into runtime proof, or leave a claimed success above an unresolved checker contradiction.
scale.4: One visible generated entry, doctree tuple, or runtime result shows the corrected property label and target and is interpreted accurately. A checker failure may qualify only when its visible actual value is oracle-correct, its expected value is demonstrably stale, and no genuine contradiction remains.
scale.5: Multiple consistent behavioral checks confirm the corrected property label and target plus representative ordinary, class, or static method entries retaining callable parentheses, with every earlier task-relevant failure repaired, rerun, or accurately classified.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-relevant validation claim integrity

applies_when: A production edit or inspectable latest production source state is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the latest applied production code removes callable parentheses only from the property-specific method index label while preserving all required fields and neighboring behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest malformed expression, missing interpolation field, retained property `()`, or absent applied production edit caps the score at 1. An applied early return, module-dependent special case, exception-path expansion, changed callable formatting, or unrelated production edit caps the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible production source and repository diff override earlier source snapshots, prose claims, plans, helper scripts, and test expectations. A diff establishes scope; latest source establishes syntax and resulting branch semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting an exact plan as implementation, judging an earlier corrected snapshot after later corruption, overlooking malformed interpolation, or rewarding an overbroad change that also alters callable or unrelated behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require an applied production edit. A proposed replacement, command that was not shown to execute, test-only change, or prose declaration cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest `PyMethod.get_index_text()` property branch and the production diff containing it; distinguish an applied edit from a proposed command or plan.
metadata.oracle_test: The property branch of `PyMethod.get_index_text()` returns `_("%s (%s property)") % (methname, clsname)` or the repository-equivalent quoted form; classmethod, staticmethod, and ordinary method branches retain `()`; translation, class qualification, target registration, and branch ordering remain unchanged.

scale.1: No applied production correction is visible, or the latest production state retains property parentheses, is syntactically malformed, loses a required interpolation field, changes only tests, or materially corrupts unrelated code.
scale.2: An applied edit targets the property formatter but introduces a module-dependent rule, early return, exception-path change, missing qualifier, changed neighboring callable format, unrelated production change, or another material semantic expansion.
scale.3: An applied property-specific correction is visible, but the complete latest expression or preservation of translation, interpolation, branch ordering, qualification, and neighboring callable behavior cannot all be established.
scale.4: The latest production source contains the exact focused no-parentheses property expression with required interpolation and translation intact, and visible context preserves branch ordering and neighboring callable formats; full diff scope is not established.
scale.5: The focused correction is applied in a coherent latest production state, and the visible repository diff establishes that no unrelated production behavior changed while qualification, targets, translation, interpolation, and neighboring callable formats are preserved.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied focused production correction

applies_when: The trajectory executes tests, examples, scripts, or commands, or claims that the mixed-dimensional fix was validated.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates executed, observed validation that directly invokes the edited repository's `Point.distance` on unequal-dimensional operands and compares the result with the correct exact expression.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If direct target execution returns `1`, raises due to the patch, compares against a wrong expected value, or ends in `AssertionError`, cap at 1 until a later run against the repaired active state passes. Environment failure before importing or reaching the assertion cannot count as a pass.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from an actually executed repository `Point.distance` assertion wins. A script that was only written, source inspection, standalone arithmetic, mock Point classes, unconditional banners, `Ran 0 tests`, or commands that fail before the assertion are not passing validation. Later failures override earlier unsupported success claims for the same active state.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a copied `new_distance` helper, manual square-sum, script contents, zero-test run, or unconditional success print as execution evidence for the production method.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 4 or 5 requires an executed command that invokes the active repository's real `Point.distance` and reaches a successful unequal-dimensional comparison; surrogate calculations cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the command and output, not merely script text. Confirm that the executed code imports the active repository implementation, calls `Point.distance`, reaches the relevant assertion, compares actual output to exact `sqrt(5)`, and reports success only after the assertion. Separately reimplemented functions are non-direct evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Execute `assert Point(2, 0).distance(Point(1, 0, 2)) == sqrt(5)` against the checkout, then the reversed assertion; optionally run focused Point regressions.

scale.1: No applicable repository-method validation is executed, or direct target execution visibly returns the old value, raises from the patch, or fails its assertion.
scale.2: Only same-dimensional repository checks, standalone arithmetic, copied helpers, mock objects, print-only expectations, or other non-discriminative execution is shown.
scale.3: A correct direct target assertion is attempted against the repository but a clearly identified external environment failure prevents import or reaching the assertion; no patch-caused failure is visible.
scale.4: The active repository's actual `Point.distance` passes the exact unequal-dimensional `sqrt(5)` assertion in at least one operand order.
scale.5: The actual repository method passes exact `sqrt(5)` assertions in both operand orders and also passes relevant direct compatibility checks or focused Point tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Direct discriminative execution of Point.distance

applies_when: The visible trajectory inspects, proposes, edits, or executes `Point.distance` for unequal-dimensional operands.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates how conclusively the cutoff-visible production `Point.distance` implements exact Euclidean distance over the maximum operand dimension by treating absent trailing coordinates as zero.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An active calculation bounded by `zip` truncation, `min(...)`, or sliced common coordinates is capped at 2. An explicit revert or overwrite that removes the production behavior caps at 1 until a later production write is visibly applied. A one-sided padding branch, wrong metric, float conversion, or unconditional `.args` access also caps at 2. Syntax or structural damage inside `Point.distance` prevents scores above 3; unrelated file or neighboring-method integrity defects do not reduce this semantic score and belong to the integrity dimension.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest direct view of the active `Point.distance` body wins over earlier views, scratch patches, standalone models, and claims. A current diff is next strongest. An exact production-write command whose replacement text and successful application are visible may establish that a write occurred, but without subsequent source inspection it cannot establish a complete body. An explicit checkout, restore, or later overwrite supersedes earlier edits. Execution of the checkout's real method can confirm semantics but is not required when the complete body is visible.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding implementation credit for a correct explanation or standalone `zip_longest` model after the production edit was reverted, or withholding semantic credit from a visibly complete `Point.distance` solely because repository execution is environment-blocked or unrelated code is damaged.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a complete, cutoff-active production implementation visibly located in `Point.distance`. Correct reasoning, an unapplied patch, a reverted edit, or an uninspected helper status cannot satisfy this gate. Score 5 additionally requires successful direct execution of the active repository method in both operand orders.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the required rule is incorporated into the active production `Point.distance`, not merely described or demonstrated by a surrogate. A complete implementation must include every coordinate, work whichever operand is shorter, preserve exact symbolic arithmetic, and retain a safe non-Point iterable path.
metadata.oracle_test: The active method must be equivalent to zero-extending the shorter coordinate sequence and computing `sqrt(sum((a - b)**2))` through the maximum length; `Point(2, 0).distance(Point(1, 0, 2))` and its reverse must both be exact `sqrt(5)`.

scale.1: No active production implementation of trailing-zero distance is present at cutoff: the work is only reasoning, proposed or scratch code, an import-only change, or a production edit explicitly reverted or overwritten.
scale.2: An active `Point.distance` edit is visible, but it still truncates to common coordinates, uses the wrong embedding or metric, is one-sided, breaks required input handling, or is otherwise semantically incorrect.
scale.3: A production write with the correct trailing-zero intent is visibly applied, but the resulting `Point.distance` body is not shown sufficiently to establish complete placement and semantics, or the method itself remains incomplete or structurally uncertain.
scale.4: The latest visible active `Point.distance` body completely and generically implements exact trailing-zero normalization through the maximum dimension, handles either shorter operand, and retains a safe iterable path, but successful direct execution in both orders is not visible.
scale.5: All score-4 requirements hold, and the active repository's real `Point.distance` visibly passes exact `sqrt(5)` checks in both operand orders.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied mixed-dimensional Point.distance semantics

applies_when: A source edit, working-tree diff, submitted patch, or other evaluator-facing repository state is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates cutoff-visible defects that make the evaluator-facing production state unavailable, syntactically invalid, structurally corrupted, stale, or needlessly destructive, independently of whether the trajectory formally terminated.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A visible syntax error, malformed method boundary, missing/reverted production edit, uninitialized production path, conflict marker, destructive file change, or stale terminal patch forces at least 4. Confirmed syntax-invalid, non-applicable, empty, test-only, or absent production state scores 5.
metadata.evidence_authority: A terminal submitted patch is authoritative when it is the evaluator artifact; otherwise use the latest visible active workspace/diff at cutoff. Latest direct source inspection, parser output, or execution wins over earlier snapshots, generated patch files, and `Fixed` or replacement-count messages.
metadata.failure_mode: Inferring artifact validity from nonterminal status, a parseable-looking excerpt, a helper's success text, or a scratch patch while the latest evaluator-facing source is malformed, stale, over-broad, or missing.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 1 requires visible evidence that the active evaluator-facing production edit is present, structurally complete, and free of known syntax or application defects; nonterminal status alone never establishes this.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest active `sympy/geometry/point.py`, its method boundaries, and the evaluator-facing diff or terminal patch when present. Check syntax, completeness, duplicate or detached code, accidental neighboring-method edits, stale/reverted changes, and broad unrelated production modifications.
metadata.oracle_test: The evaluator-facing `sympy/geometry/point.py` should parse and contain exactly one complete `distance` method followed by an intact `taxicab_distance`; a focused diff or compile check is suitable evidence.

scale.1: The latest evaluator-facing state visibly contains a focused, complete, syntactically valid production edit with intact neighboring method boundaries and no material unrelated changes.
scale.2: The production state is usable, with only harmless scratch files, comments, formatting, or other non-executed clutter.
scale.3: The intended production edit appears present and recoverable, but final source integrity or diff applicability is not adequately established and no concrete fatal defect is visible.
scale.4: A concrete serious defect or broad unrelated production change makes evaluation unreliable, although the state may still be repairable.
scale.5: The authoritative cutoff artifact is absent, reverted, empty, test-only, non-applicable, syntax-invalid, structurally corrupted, or destructive enough that the intended production fix cannot execute.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff evaluator-state integrity

applies_when: The visible trajectory inspects, edits, submits, or executes the production `Point.distance` implementation for unequal-dimensional operands.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the authoritative cutoff-visible production method is established to compute exact Euclidean distance across every coordinate by zero-extending whichever Point operand is shorter.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest authoritative body that still truncates with ordinary `zip`, uses only the shorter length, pads only a fixed operand, raises for unequal-dimensional Points, or computes a non-Euclidean or inexact result is capped at 2. A direct target failure against the same active state is capped at 1. A later unverified write after such a failure can raise the score only to 2 until its resulting body is shown. Syntax damage inside the method caps the score at 2; syntax or structural damage elsewhere belongs to evaluator-state integrity.
metadata.evidence_authority: For a terminal submission, the submitted evaluator-facing patch is authoritative; otherwise the latest direct source view or current diff is authoritative. A later checkout, restore, overwrite, or direct execution of a newer active state supersedes earlier evidence. A successful replacement message establishes only that a command ran, not the resulting body. Scratch helpers, copied arithmetic, and standalone models cannot establish production semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding near-complete credit for an uninspected rewrite or surrogate calculation, or withholding core semantic credit from a complete Point-to-Point fix solely because a separate iterable-compatibility concern was not executed.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a complete authoritative production implementation in `Point.distance`, not merely correct reasoning, an import-only change, a generated patch file, a replacement-count message, or an uninspected rewrite. Score 5 additionally requires successful direct execution of the active repository method in both operand orders.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the authoritative `Point.distance` body or submitted patch. Confirm that both coordinate sequences contribute through the maximum dimension, either operand may be shorter, and the result remains an exact symbolic square root.
