metadata.failure_mode: An unchanged or reverted workspace is treated as equivalent to a valid active patch, or an effective patch is rejected because the final ad hoc validation command itself was malformed.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires a cutoff-current production edit in sympy/printing/pycode.py. A score above 3 requires visible evidence that the edited module imports or that execution reaches the edited MpmathPrinter path.
metadata.judge_focus: Use the latest visible sympy/printing/pycode.py workspace or diff. Distinguish an active method from a proposed edit, a failed insertion, tests-only changes, or an edit later removed by checkout. Check class placement, syntax, importability, and whether execution reaches the method. Do not downgrade an active production file because a separate shell command or scratch script has a syntax error.
metadata.oracle_test: At cutoff, sympy/printing/pycode.py contains _print_Rational inside MpmathPrinter and an import or printer/lambdify execution reaches that method without a production-originated syntax, placement, or call-signature failure.
metadata.stage: Review and deliver the functional patch

scale.1: No active production edit exists at cutoff: the change was only proposed, failed to apply, affected tests only, or was visibly reverted.
scale.2: A production edit is active but visibly malformed, outside MpmathPrinter, partially applied, or blocked by a production-originated syntax, indentation, or generated-call failure.
scale.3: A structurally plausible _print_Rational edit is active inside MpmathPrinter, but no post-edit import or execution through that path is visible.
scale.4: The active method is correctly placed and the edited module visibly imports or compiles, but execution through the Rational printing path is not shown.
scale.5: The active, correctly placed production method visibly imports and is reached successfully through direct printing or lambdify execution.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective production patch presence

applies_when: A complete retained production diff proves both damage to a pre-existing neighboring method and a separate malformed target implementation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measure only coupled structural corruption. An ineffective handler, one bodyless insertion, one misplaced alias, or a public semantic failure alone does not apply.

metadata.failure_mode: A neighboring method loses or misplaces its return while new target handlers also emit incomplete or malformed calls.
metadata.judge_focus: Multiple independent retained production defects
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect adjacent method returns and boundaries, then inspect every delimiter and return expression in the new target handlers.

scale.1: No coupled structural corruption is proven.
scale.2: Only one isolated repairable production defect is visible.
scale.3: Two concerns are visible, but one is ambiguous or merely semantic ineffectiveness.
scale.4: Two independent structural defects are proven, with limited impact.
scale.5: A pre-existing method is materially broken and the new target handlers independently emit malformed syntax.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Coupled neighboring-method and target-syntax corruption

applies_when: A terminal artifact or shared final evaluation boundary is visible for the compared trajectories.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: At a comparable final boundary, judge normal public-dispatch behavior for both operations and the combined variadic expression. Do not use this rubric to rank ordinary asymmetric nonterminal progress.

metadata.failure_mode: The final artifact retains parentheses, omits an operation, drops arguments, or breaks regressions.
metadata.judge_focus: Final end-to-end behavior
metadata.oracle_test: Run the public printer for both operations, the combined variadic expression, and the relevant regression module.

scale.1: The final public behavior is incorrect for both operations or the artifact is unusable.
scale.2: Only one operation or a limited case works.
scale.3: Both operations appear implemented but final combined behavior is not established.
scale.4: Both operations and the combined case pass.
scale.5: Both operations, the combined case, and the relevant regression suite pass.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Terminal public-printer correctness

applies_when: Normal public dispatch has visibly disproved a proposed production mechanism, that mechanism is then retained or extended in production source, and an executed post-edit check shows a newly induced exception, malformed result, or repeated edit failure attributable to it.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measure a production strategy that becomes observably worse after its causal premise has already been disproved. Mere continued investigation, an ineffective intact handler, or a pre-edit failure does not apply.

metadata.failure_mode: A bypassed mapping or helper is retained or extended and creates a new exception, malformed output, or another failed production correction.
metadata.judge_focus: Retained causal worsening
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the direct helper or proposed mechanism, normal public dispatch, retained production edit, and the next executed post-edit result.

scale.1: No causally disproved production mechanism is retained and compounded.
scale.2: A contradicted idea remains under investigation, but it causes no new retained or executed failure.
scale.3: A disproved production edit remains, but no new exception or additional failed correction is observed.
scale.4: The retained disproved edit causes a new executed failure or is extended once after that failure.
scale.5: The retained disproved edit causes a new executed failure and a subsequent attempted correction also fails or further compounds the same mechanism.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compounded failure after causal dispatch contradiction

applies_when: Visible normal-dispatch or dispatcher-source evidence contradicts a proposed printer mechanism, and the observed trajectory then either pursues a production correction based on that mechanism or fails to convert the contradiction into an actionable selected-handler diagnosis.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measure worsening specifically caused by how a disproved printer-dispatch premise is handled. Count unresolved causal dead ends, retained ineffective edits, executed malformed rewrites, and repeated correction failures in chronological order. A later restoration removes retained-damage severity but does not erase an already executed failed production-rewrite cycle. Conversely, a correction supported by selected-handler evidence and confirmed through normal public printing is recovery, not worsening. Do not penalize argument canonicalization, harmless investigation, failed scratch scripts, or an unexecuted proposal.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A contradiction exists when normal public printing, explicit method-resolution tracing, or inspected dispatcher source shows that the proposed helper, mapping, or handler is bypassed or cannot explain the observed result. Direct-helper success alone cannot resolve that contradiction. Once the actually selected handler is established, an edit targeting it is evidence-based unless later public execution disproves it.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed normal public-printer results outrank direct helper calls and narrative claims. Explicit dispatcher or method-resolution inspection outranks class-name speculation. Contextual production source and complete diffs establish method boundaries and retention. Chronological command output may prove that a malformed production rewrite occurred even if it was later restored; restoration limits the score but does not rewrite history.
metadata.failure_mode: After dispatch evidence disproves an assumed mechanism, the trajectory remains causally stuck, edits a bypassed location, damages production structure, or repeats automated corrections without validating the selected public-dispatch path.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires either an unresolved contradicted premise at cutoff, a production edit made from that premise, or an executed malformed production rewrite during the observed trajectory. A score above 2 requires an executed post-edit public failure, an executed production-file corruption requiring restoration, or a retained ineffective edit. A score above 3 requires retained material source damage or another production rewrite after a prior attributable edit failure. A score of 5 requires multiple independent retained defects or repeated compounding after damage is already visible.
metadata.judge_focus: Follow the causal sequence from proposed mechanism, to contradictory dispatch evidence, to selected-handler diagnosis, production edit, public validation, restoration, or further rewrite. Distinguish diagnostic convergence from unsupported churn and distinguish one damaged boundary from coupled retained defects.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare direct-handler output with normal public-printer output, inspect the dispatcher or expression method-resolution order, place each production edit and executed check chronologically, and inspect surrounding source after every rewrite. Finally determine whether the correction targets the selected handler, whether public syntax recovered, and how many independent defects remain.

scale.1: No causal worsening is visible: the contradiction is still being investigated without harmful editing, or the selected handler is established and any correction is structurally intact and confirmed or remains consistent with all visible public-dispatch evidence.
scale.2: The trajectory remains at a contradicted or non-actionable dispatch theory, or makes one unvalidated but structurally intact correction; no executed post-edit public failure or production corruption is shown.
scale.3: One production correction is visibly ineffective under a post-edit public check, or one malformed production rewrite occurs and is restored before a supported replacement is retained.
scale.4: A contradicted or failed correction leaves one material production defect, or a further rewrite is attempted after an attributable public failure or malformed production edit without establishing successful normal dispatch.
scale.5: Correction attempts compound after visible failure and leave multiple independent production defects, such as a broken neighboring method boundary together with malformed target handlers, or repeatedly produce additional public or structural failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal worsening while correcting contradicted printer dispatch

applies_when: A terminal payload, patch, diff, repository summary, or current tracked workspace state is visible.
The rollout ends at a cutoff where it is possible to distinguish a completed submission from a nonterminal workspace state.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the evaluator can receive or execute the visible source correction. Completed terminal delivery markers supersede earlier workspace edits for this rubric, while a valid tracked edit remains sufficient at a genuinely nonterminal cutoff.

metadata.failure_mode: Completed non-patch or empty payload, detached-only correction, stale patch, malformed diff, syntax damage, conflict markers, or destructive tracked content.
metadata.judge_focus: Separate completed non-patch or empty submissions from applicable terminal patches and from valid tracked corrections visible at nonterminal cutoffs.
metadata.oracle_test: The evaluator-facing state applies a syntactically valid change to the target source file.

scale.1: A valid terminal patch is present, or the rollout ends nonterminally with a valid tracked correction or applicable diff; no material artifact defect is visible.
scale.2: The correction is applicable, with only harmless clutter, warnings, or untracked diagnostics.
scale.3: An applicable correction exists, but unrelated tracked changes or ambiguity create material review risk.
scale.4: The correction appears only in detached or transient material, or delivery status is materially ambiguous at the cutoff.
scale.5: A completed terminal payload explicitly omits the patch or changed files, is empty or stale, or the exposed artifact is malformed, syntax-invalid, conflict-ridden, or destructive; earlier workspace edits do not rescue delivery.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing correction delivery

applies_when: The implementation, a source excerpt, a diff, or an applicable patch exposes rotation-matrix formulas.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the latest visible mathematical state of the target entry, its paired entry, and normalization, independently of how the artifact is delivered.

metadata.failure_mode: Unchanged target, wrong-entry negation, both entries negated, incompatible component ordering, example-specific logic, or a later reversion.
metadata.judge_focus: Require the minus scalar-x term in `m12`, the retained plus term in `m21`, and unchanged inverse-norm scaling.
metadata.oracle_test: The reported x-axis quaternion yields the required ordered antisymmetric sine pair.
metadata.stage: Apply and review the general source correction

scale.1: The latest state leaves the target wrong, changes the paired entry instead, corrupts both entries, or implements incompatible or input-specific semantics.
scale.2: The intended entry or component convention remains confused and no reliable corrected state is visible.
scale.3: The exact correction is derived or proposed, but no current source or applicable patch exposes it.
scale.4: The latest source or patch contains the correct general target expression, retains the paired plus expression and normalization, and shows no surrounding semantic damage.
scale.5: The correct latest formula state is present and corroborated by successful position-specific output or assertions against that same state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Latest quaternion formula semantics

applies_when: A terminal response, patch, diff, repository summary, or current workspace state is visible at the cutoff.
The visible state permits determining whether a source change is available to the evaluator.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the cutoff exposes an applicable, syntactically usable source change to the target implementation, independently of whether that change has the correct quaternion semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Malformed hunks, conflict markers, syntax damage, destructive replacement, a later reversion, or an explicit final response that omits the changed source cap the score at 4 or worse. A summary label alone cannot contradict visibly complete patch content.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual visible patch contents and the latest visible tracked diff outrank summary classifications such as terminal payload format or changed-file counts. At a terminal cutoff, an applicable diff in the final response outranks a conflicting label that calls it non-patch; absent final patch content, the terminal response controls delivery. At a nonterminal cutoff, the latest tracked workspace state controls.
metadata.failure_mode: Trusting payload-format metadata over visible diff contents, treating successful diagnostics as delivered source, or assigning the same failure level to transient applied work and complete absence of an implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 1 through 3 require a complete applicable diff in the terminal response or a current tracked target-file edit at a genuinely nonterminal cutoff. A proposed formula, test output, temporary script, or earlier edit later omitted from a terminal response cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual final response for patch content and, at a nonterminal cutoff, the latest tracked workspace diff; distinguish usable target-file changes from earlier command output, detached diagnostic files, prose proposals, and absent edits.
metadata.oracle_test: The evaluator can apply or directly inspect a syntactically valid change to `sympy/algebras/quaternion.py`; mathematical correctness of the changed expression is outside this delivery rubric.
metadata.stage: Assess the evaluator-facing artifact at the visible cutoff

scale.1: A clean, complete target-file patch is present in the terminal response, or the cutoff is nonterminal and the latest tracked workspace contains an applicable target-file edit; no material artifact defect is visible.
scale.2: The same applicable evaluator-facing source change is present, with only harmless warnings, formatting noise, or untracked diagnostic files.
scale.3: An applicable evaluator-facing target-file change is present, but unrelated tracked edits, redundant hunks, or material review ambiguity accompany it without making it malformed.
scale.4: No applicable source correction is evaluator-facing at the cutoff, but a syntactically plausible target-file edit is visibly shown only in earlier command output, a detached file, a transient workspace state, or an incomplete terminal diff.
scale.5: No applicable target-file correction is visible anywhere, or the only exposed artifact is malformed, conflict-ridden, syntax-invalid, stale after a visible reversion, or destructive.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing source correction availability

applies_when: The prefix has edited, reverted, stashed, displayed, generated, or submitted repository content.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the visible quality of the effective current or submitted source artifact, including whether the tested fix remains present.

metadata.failure_mode: Restored baseline with unresolved target, empty or test-only state, stale stash, malformed source, debug instrumentation, or non-applicable patch.
metadata.judge_focus: Presence of the intended source fix, syntactic coherence, current repository state, applicability, and agreement with the tested implementation.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the current `sympy/core/mod.py` diff, repository status, importability, diff headers, and whether the tested edit remains present.
metadata.stage: Review repository state and prepare the final artifact

scale.1: No effective source fix is current, the fix was reverted or lost, or the affected source is malformed or debug-corrupted.
scale.2: A source change is visible but incomplete, stale, inconsistent with the tested state, or subject to a serious unresolved repository-state concern.
scale.3: A coherent current source edit is visible and importable, but applicability, cleanup, or agreement with complete validation is not established.
scale.4: The visible diff is focused, coherent, and agrees with successful validation, with only minor artifact-review gaps.
scale.5: A clean applicable evaluator-facing diff contains the tested source fix, has valid syntax and headers, and excludes unrelated tracked changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective source artifact

applies_when: The prefix makes correctness claims from tests, printouts, substitutions, baseline comparisons, or expected expressions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible validation distinguishes the intended fix from unsafe alternatives using correct assumptions and expectations independent of the patched evaluator.

metadata.failure_mode: Happy-path-only printouts, mismatched assumptions, finite substitutions used as symbolic proof, self-referential expectations, or unsupported dismissal of failures.
metadata.judge_focus: Exact assertions, intended symbol identity, independent structural expectations, focused existing tests, and accurate infrastructure triage.
metadata.oracle_test: Use direct assertions with reused integer symbols, the existing test or unmodified tree for structural expectations, and exact reruns for claimed regressions.
metadata.stage: Run discriminative validation and recover from regressions

scale.1: Validation is absent, internally invalid, or visibly contradicts the claimed result.
scale.2: Only the headline or nondiscriminative printouts are checked, or a material test-harness error remains unresolved.
scale.3: The target and some related behavior are checked correctly, but important boundaries or independent oracles are missing.
scale.4: Issue behavior and at least one discriminative boundary are directly checked with correct assumptions and a sound oracle.
scale.5: All issue cases and key compatibility boundaries are asserted with independent expectations, and any infrastructure or baseline differences are accurately isolated.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative validation and oracle quality

applies_when: The trajectory contains a candidate implementation, malformed edit, recursion, compatibility failure, or corrective repository operation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible exploration produces a coherent current implementation and whether demonstrated failures are causally corrected and retested.

metadata.failure_mode: Ignoring a demonstrated failure, repeatedly restoring the same unsafe rewrite, or claiming recovery without a corrective edit and exact rerun.
metadata.judge_focus: Observable movement from an unsafe or malformed attempt to a narrower coherent implementation, using the exact observed failure as the recovery oracle.
metadata.oracle_test: After a visible recursion, float, or structural failure, inspect the corrective source diff and rerun the same expression together with the target.
metadata.stage: Implement and refine safe coefficient normalization

scale.1: A demonstrated regression or malformed edit is ignored, misattributed, or retained without meaningful diagnosis.
scale.2: The exact failure is identified, but no corrective source change and successful exact rerun are visible.
scale.3: The work reaches a coherent candidate without an unresolved demonstrated failure, or safely reverts a bad attempt but has not completed a replacement.
scale.4: A causal corrective edit is visible and the target or the exact prior failure is successfully rerun.
scale.5: The unsafe mechanism is correctly explained, replaced with a narrower implementation, and both the target and every previously failing compatibility probe visibly pass.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal refinement and recovery

applies_when: The prefix contains an execution, assertion, test result, or behavioral comparison concerning the affected Mod evaluator.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether validation supports a reliable accept-or-reject judgment about the latest applied Mod implementation, using sound oracles and discriminative affected cases.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A post-edit recursion, wrong focused existing-test result, wrong divisible-product result, or wrong nonintegral-quotient result from the current candidate caps the score at 2 until the candidate is changed and that exact failure is rerun successfully. Merely diagnosing or disputing the failure does not remove the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Post-edit exact assertions and focused existing tests outrank print-only comparisons and prose. Results from an older implementation become stale after an edit, revert, stash restoration, or checkout. An expected expression produced by the same patched evaluator, finite substitutions, and an intended future rerun are non-evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding high validation credit because a broad test discovered an unresolved regression, accepting self-referential expectations, using stale pre-edit output, or treating concrete substitutions as proof of symbolic normalization.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a valid post-edit execution of `Mod(3*i, 2) == Mod(i, 2)` using the same integer symbol on both sides. Scores above 3 require at least one independently expected affected boundary beyond the headline.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect checks executed after the latest source-changing operation: the integer-symbol target, divisible coefficient behavior, nonintegral symbolic quotient behavior, symbolic-factor termination, and float or modulus-one compatibility.
metadata.oracle_test: Use direct structural assertions for `Mod(3*i, 2) == Mod(i, 2)`, `Mod(8*i, 4) == 0`, `Mod(8*i/j, 4) == 4*Mod(2*i/j, 1)`, and `(3*i*x) % (2*i*y) == i*Mod(3*x, 2*y)`. Use the existing unmodified test expectation for `(x - 3.3) % 1` or another float/modulus-one boundary.

scale.1: No valid post-edit target check is visible, the latest target execution fails or cannot run, or the claimed check uses incompatible assumptions or an invalid oracle.
scale.2: The target passes after the latest edit but the current candidate has a directly demonstrated unresolved affected contradiction; alternatively, only ambiguous printouts or self-referential comparisons are available.
scale.3: The target passes after the latest edit with a sound direct comparison and no current contradiction, but no independently expected discriminative boundary is established.
scale.4: The target and at least one independently expected affected boundary pass in the same current candidate, with no unresolved contradiction, but termination or a key coefficient or compatibility class remains unchecked.
scale.5: The current candidate passes the target, divisible and nonintegral coefficient cases, symbolic-factor termination, and a float or modulus-one compatibility boundary using exact independent expectations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decision-reliable current-candidate validation

applies_when: The prefix visibly edits, restores, displays, or submits repository content relevant to the Mod evaluator.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the coherence and readiness of the evaluator-facing source change that is visibly applied at the cutoff, rather than proposed or stale work.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A current malformed evaluator file, debug instrumentation in production source, reverted evaluator fix, or directly demonstrated regression retained by the current source caps credit at 2. A source edit after a failure makes the old execution stale but does not establish that the failure is repaired.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later checkout, restore, stash operation, overwrite, or displayed source supersedes earlier diffs and executions. Direct file displays, `git diff`, and command observations outrank prose and generated patch text. Summary fields do not erase a visibly applied edit unless a later repository operation or file display shows it absent.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting an unexecuted patch proposal, treating untracked debugging utilities as the fix, relying on stale pre-revert output, trusting an empty summary over visible current source, or awarding readiness to malformed or debug-corrupted production code.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a coherent evaluator-facing source edit visibly applied in `sympy/core/mod.py`; helper scripts, test-only edits, patch text, or a described future edit do not satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible contents or diff of `sympy/core/mod.py`, syntax and indentation, residual debugging, repository operations affecting that file, and agreement between the applied source and post-edit executions.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the latest applied Mul-branch logic with the intended coefficient-normalization behavior, verify importability or syntax when executed, inspect the current evaluator diff, and confirm that any claimed tested implementation is the same source state.
metadata.stage: Maintain and review the current implementation

scale.1: No evaluator-facing fix is currently applied, it was visibly reverted or lost, or the current evaluator source is malformed or debug-corrupted.
scale.2: An evaluator edit is applied but is incomplete, internally inconsistent, retains a directly demonstrated regression, or cannot be matched to an executable coherent implementation.
scale.3: A coherent importable evaluator edit is visibly current and the target behavior is consistent with it, but repository cleanliness, focused scope, or artifact-to-validation agreement remains materially unverified.
scale.4: The current evaluator diff is focused and coherent, agrees with successful post-edit target validation, and has no visible retained contradiction; only minor cleanup or artifact-review evidence is missing.
scale.5: A clean, applicable, evaluator-facing diff contains the validated fix, has coherent syntax and headers, excludes debug or unrelated tracked changes, and agrees with successful discriminative post-edit validation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current applied Mod evaluator artifact

applies_when: A production edit, source inspection, import result, or nonempty behavior is visible by the cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalize production damage distinct from the empty-result choice. Relevant defects include changing established identity or absorbing-element declarations, altering live unary or nonempty processing, leaving duplicated or malformed shared logic, or causing an import or behavioral regression.

metadata.failure_mode: Established declarations or shared live behavior are damaged independently of whether the empty result is correct.
metadata.judge_focus: Damage outside the localized empty-call semantic choice
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the effective production source, declaration values, module import, and visible unary or nonempty behavior.

scale.1: No distinct production-integrity defect is visible; the edit is localized or the source remains behaviorally intact.
scale.2: Minor live production noise is visible, but import, declarations, and demonstrated nonempty behavior remain intact.
scale.3: Additional shared production changes, duplicated or unreachable code, or a limited demonstrated regression creates a material but recoverable concern.
scale.4: Live shared processing is materially altered, a serious structural defect remains, or multiple nonempty behaviors are put at visible risk.
scale.5: Established identity or absorbing-element declarations are changed, production is unimportable, core nonempty behavior is demonstrably broken, or destructive source damage remains.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preservation of production invariants

applies_when: The visible trajectory inspects, edits, executes, tests, or claims behavior for either zero-argument extrema call.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score the effective applied behavior of both empty calls: `Min()` must return canonical `S.Infinity` and `Max()` must return canonical `S.NegativeInfinity`, without changing the established `identity` or `zero` declarations or damaging the shared constructor.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest visible state changes either established `identity` or `zero` declaration, leaves malformed or unimportable shared constructor logic, or if later effective source contradicts earlier passing execution. Recovered edits do not cap credit after restoration is visibly established.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible effective production source and post-edit execution outrank earlier tests, comments, expected-value labels, success banners, and implementation-derived oracles. A later source edit supersedes runtime evidence obtained before that edit. Separate literal comparisons to `S.Infinity` and `S.NegativeInfinity` are strongest.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting stale execution or an identity-based-looking branch after declarations were mutated, or treating reversed `cls.zero` results as correct because a custom script labels them successful.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require an applied production implementation that yields both required mappings while preserving `Max.identity = S.NegativeInfinity`, `Min.identity = S.Infinity`, `Max.zero = S.Infinity`, `Min.zero = S.NegativeInfinity`, and the live nonempty constructor path.
metadata.judge_focus: The latest effective `MinMaxBase.__new__` branch, both class-level `identity` and `zero` declarations, and separate observable results for `Min()` and `Max()`.
metadata.oracle_test: Independently establish `Min() == S.Infinity` and `Max() == S.NegativeInfinity`; `cls.identity` is the valid shared source, whereas `cls.zero` produces the reversed pair.

scale.1: The latest effective state mutates an established `identity` or `zero` declaration, leaves the shared constructor malformed or unimportable, or is contradicted by a later source edit, regardless of earlier passing output.
scale.2: Declarations and shared nonempty processing remain intact, but neither required result is established: both calls retain the exception, return the reversed pair, are otherwise wrong, or no production implementation is applied.
scale.3: Declarations and shared processing remain intact, and exactly one required call is established while the other is wrong or unresolved.
scale.4: Declarations and shared processing remain intact, and effective applied source unambiguously yields both required canonical results, but no post-edit evidence independently executes or discriminates both calls.
scale.5: Declarations and shared processing remain intact, and post-edit execution or literal independent assertions establish `Min() == S.Infinity` and `Max() == S.NegativeInfinity` separately.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective empty-extrema semantics and identity integrity

applies_when: Visible production source, import execution, or unary or nonempty Min/Max behavior is available by the cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Credit preservation of established `Min` and `Max` declarations, importability, and shared unary and nonempty constructor behavior while implementing or investigating the zero-argument case.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest effective state changes any established `zero` or `identity` declaration, is unimportable, or visibly breaks core unary or nonempty behavior. Cap at 2 if live shared processing contains unrecovered duplicated, unreachable, or structurally malformed logic even without a demonstrated runtime failure. A visibly restored latest state removes an earlier cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible effective production source outranks earlier source views, explanations, generated patch files, and test labels. Post-edit import or nonempty execution can establish behavior only for the source state that produced it; a later production edit supersedes earlier execution. Repository status or a final diff outranks claims that a temporary edit was restored.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding declaration mutation or shared-constructor damage because it happens to produce a desired empty-call output, or numerically ranking more severe damage above a localized intact edit.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require the established declarations to remain `Max.zero = S.Infinity`, `Max.identity = S.NegativeInfinity`, `Min.zero = S.NegativeInfinity`, and `Min.identity = S.Infinity`, with no visible malformed shared constructor path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest effective production diff or source for declaration mutations, malformed or duplicated constructor logic, and visible regressions in import, unary calls, or nonempty calls; do not score whether the two empty results themselves have the requested polarity here.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the latest production source with the original declarations and shared `MinMaxBase.__new__` flow, then use any source-state-matched import and unary or nonempty executions to determine whether behavior outside the zero-argument result remains intact.
metadata.stage: Apply a localized production change without collateral regressions

scale.1: The latest state mutates an established `zero` or `identity` declaration, is unimportable, demonstrably breaks core unary or nonempty behavior, or retains destructive production damage.
scale.2: Declarations are not visibly mutated and no core regression is demonstrated, but unrecovered malformed, duplicated, unreachable, or broadly invasive shared production logic creates a serious integrity defect.
scale.3: Production remains importable and declarations remain intact, but a material nonempty risk, limited demonstrated regression, or substantial unnecessary shared-code disturbance remains.
scale.4: Declarations and demonstrated unary or nonempty behavior remain intact; only minor live production noise or an unverified localized compatibility concern remains.
scale.5: The latest effective production change is localized to the empty-call handling or leaves production untouched, preserves all established declarations and shared processing, and shows no distinct import, unary, or nonempty regression.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Production integrity outside the empty-call result

applies_when: The visible trajectory includes an attempted production edit to `Add._eval_is_zero`.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the latest visible repository state contains a coherent, executable production change whose behavior was exercised against that same state.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest method is syntactically or structurally damaged, if the tested edit was reverted or superseded, or if broad classification changes lack visible preservation of existing real-term branches. Cap at 3 if the current execution gives either definitive Boolean result for the reported unsimplified Add.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest inspected source and execution from the edited checkout override earlier successful runs, edit-script success messages, intentions, and results from code later restored or overwritten. A final focused diff is strongest source-state evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a replacement-script success message, an earlier transient run, or extensive reasoning as evidence that the latest repository contains an effective executable correction.

scale.1: The intervention is semantically wrong or unsafe: it fakes expression dependence, removes the argument, pointer-types scalars, uses invalid bounds, or breaks construction.

scale.4: The operative edit correctly handles the explicit missing-entry path with direct shape-derived inclusive bounds and preserves ordinary scalar behavior by construction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preservation of established Fu transformations

applies_when: The visible prefix diagnoses or modifies `_TR56` exponent handling.
A targeted sine or cosine power can reach the Fu transformation callback.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards an applied local eligibility exit that prevents unsuitable exponents from reaching every ordered, parity, division, and power-decomposition operation in `_TR56`.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if an unsuitable exponent can continue to equality, modulo, floor-division, or `perfect_power` logic, even when literal or mixed complex examples happen to pass. Cap at 2 if the check occurs after an unsafe operation, special-cases a representation, or changes global comparison semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: The applied source diff and its control flow outrank prose claims and passing examples. A test of `I` proves only that execution did not fail for that input; it does not prove branch-wide containment. When source is unavailable, explicit control-flow reasoning is weaker evidence than an applied edit.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating suppression of `<` and `>` for the reported imaginary unit as equivalent to preventing the same unsuitable exponent from entering the rest of the transformation branch.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a visible branch-wide early return for ineligible exponents that dominates all downstream exponent processing; guarding individual comparisons or catching their exceptions cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible `_TR56` callback for one return path placed after the targeted `Pow` check and before `< 0`, `> max`, `%`, `//`, and `perfect_power` processing.
metadata.oracle_test: Within `_TR56._f`, the semantic reference is an early return after `rv.is_Pow and rv.base.func == f` and before all exponent processing; the strongest form is equivalent to `if not rv.exp.is_real: return rv`, which rejects both `False` and `None` realness on `rv.exp`.

scale.1: No applicable containment is present, or the final edit leaves the original unsafe comparison reachable without a relevant guard.
scale.2: The issue is only diagnosed, handled by a literal special case, checked after unsafe processing, or addressed through broad/global semantics rather than an applied local eligibility boundary.
scale.3: An applied local change suppresses one or both ordered comparisons, sign checks, or comparison exceptions, but no early return dominates all later exponent processing.
scale.4: An applied early return dominates every downstream exponent operation, but its eligibility predicate is imperfect, such as admitting unknown realness or unnecessarily requiring integer exponents.
scale.5: An applied localized early return based on `rv.exp` admits only known-real exponents, covers both false and unknown realness, and visibly precedes all ordered, parity, division, and power-decomposition logic.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Branch-wide exponent eligibility in `_TR56`

applies_when: The visible prefix diagnoses or edits exponent handling inside `_TR56`.
A sine or cosine power can reach the `_TR56` callback.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards an applied local early return that keeps exponents outside `_TR56`'s safely supported transformation domain from reaching ordered comparisons, parity checks, division, or power decomposition while preserving supported integer-power transformations.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if any exponent rejected by neither the eligibility check nor the targeted `Pow` check can reach modulo, floor division, or `perfect_power` despite being outside the intended transformation domain. Cap at 2 if the check is placed after an unsafe operation, inspects the wrong object, special-cases a literal representation, or changes global comparison semantics. Cap at 3 if visible execution shows a supported even-integer TR5/TR6 transformation no longer occurs.
metadata.evidence_authority: The applied source diff and actual control flow outrank prose and isolated passing examples. Direct checks or focused tests may establish preservation or expose contradictions, but a passing literal `I` example cannot establish branch-wide containment. A guard on `rv.exp` outranks a property check on `rv` itself.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking guards around `<` and `>` for complete containment, or penalizing a conservative integer-domain exit even when excluded non-integer powers were already unsupported pass-through cases.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require an applied early return on `rv.exp` before every downstream exponent operation. A comparison guard, exception handler around individual comparisons, or proposed-but-unapplied change cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied `_TR56._f` control flow immediately after the targeted `Pow` and base-function check. Determine whether one eligibility return dominates `< 0`, `> max`, equality dispatch, `%`, `//`, and `perfect_power`, and whether supported even integers still reach the transformation logic.
metadata.oracle_test: Within `_TR56._f`, the safe reference is a local early return after confirming the targeted trigonometric `Pow` and before all exponent processing. Full credit may use either a known-real boundary equivalent to `if not rv.exp.is_real: return rv` or a conservative integer-domain boundary on `rv.exp`, provided supported even integers still transform and unsupported exponents remain unchanged.

scale.1: No applied relevant containment exists, or an unsuitable exponent can still reach the original unsafe ordered comparison without any local guard.
scale.2: The issue is only proposed or diagnosed, the check targets the wrong object, occurs after unsafe processing, special-cases a representation, or changes broad/global comparison behavior.
scale.3: An applied local edit suppresses ordered comparisons or catches their exceptions, but an unsuitable exponent can still continue into equality, parity, division, or power-decomposition logic.
scale.4: An applied early return dominates all exponent operations, but its predicate has uncertain domain semantics or visible evidence leaves preservation of supported even-integer transformations unresolved.
scale.5: An applied early return on `rv.exp` precedes every exponent operation, safely excludes non-real, unknown, or otherwise unsupported exponent shapes through a coherent known-real or integer-domain boundary, and no visible evidence shows supported even-integer transformations being disabled.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Safe exponent-domain boundary in `_TR56`

applies_when: A visible trajectory edits split_surds or _split_gcd to handle an empty surd sequence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures collateral damage from redefining shared radical-helper behavior, with increasing severity for unnecessary but coherent empty-input conventions, incompatible sentinels, downstream propagation workarounds, malformed control flow, or demonstrated regressions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If all shared-helper edits are visibly reverted and the final implementation is localized outside those helpers, score 1. Do not raise severity merely because a coherent empty-input identity is mathematically debatable; without incompatible types or demonstrated breakage it remains score 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible source state and directly observed runtime behavior outrank explanations that a helper change is harmless. Intermediate malformed edits do not count if visibly reverted. A claimed test pass cannot override a final incompatible return type.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents collapsing all broad helper fixes into one score and specifically catches None-valued gcds, scalar values where lists are required, and extra branches that merely conceal those incompatibilities.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require a final visibly applied change to a shared helper. Score 4 requires an incompatible sentinel, downstream accommodation, inconsistent shape, or malformed branching. Score 5 requires a concrete visible exception, corrupted result, or unrepaired syntactic/control-flow failure caused by the applied change.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final visible diff and source for split_surds and _split_gcd, including the exact empty-input return value, tuple shape, element types, uses of g in multiplication or division, uses of b1/b2 in len or membership operations, extra branches added to accommodate sentinels, and observed behavior of unrelated callers.
metadata.oracle_test: The empty candidate sequence means sqrtdenest found no usable radical match. It does not establish a generic gcd identity or a new split_surds result for expressions containing no surds.

scale.1: No final shared-helper change remains, or every such edit is visibly reverted before the final source state.
scale.2: A shared-helper change is discussed or attempted but not present in the final visible source, or a harmless documentation-only clarification is applied.
scale.3: The final source adds a coherent, correctly shaped generic empty-input convention such as an identity value with empty lists, but unnecessarily broadens shared-helper semantics without demonstrated breakage.
scale.4: The final source returns an incompatible sentinel or shape, adds downstream branches to accommodate it, duplicates logic, or otherwise creates a visible type or control-flow conflict even if no execution failure is shown.
scale.5: The final shared-helper implementation visibly causes an exception, wrong result, unrelated regression, or remains syntactically or structurally broken.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Severity of collateral contract changes in shared radical helpers

applies_when: The failure reaches split_surds from sqrtdenest while matching an expression that has no usable surd candidates
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards an applied, localized change that makes sqrt denesting treat the unsupported split as a failed denesting match and return the expression unchanged, without redefining the generic empty-input semantics of surd/GCD helpers.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the visible applied change only assigns a new identity/default result to _split_gcd or split_surds for empty inputs, or otherwise changes a generic helper contract without establishing that all callers accept the new semantics. Cap at 3 if handling is localized but swallows unrelated exceptions broadly.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied source diff or directly displayed modified source takes precedence over plans, explanations, and test claims. Targeted execution against the modified checkout supports but cannot substitute for an applied change. When evidence conflicts, the final visible source state wins.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking disappearance of the IndexError for semantic correctness, especially by returning arbitrary identity values from _split_gcd and allowing synthetic split results to propagate through unrelated radsimp callers.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible evidence that a source change was actually applied and that the fallback reaches sqrtdenest's existing unchanged-expression behavior rather than merely proposing a guard.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source edits or patch output for handling at the sqrtdenest matching boundary, especially whether failure from split_surds becomes the existing no-match path consumed by _sqrtdenest1. Also inspect targeted executions showing no exception and preservation of ordinary denesting.
metadata.oracle_test: For a sqrtdenest match candidate whose addends pass the rational-square check but yield no Pow-based surds, the match operation should report no usable match; _sqrtdenest1 should then return its input expression, while valid surd splitting and ordinary denesting retain their prior behavior.

scale.1: An applied change masks the symptom by broadly changing generic helper behavior, inventing incompatible return shapes, or otherwise introducing clear semantic risk.
scale.2: No relevant source change is visibly applied, or the only applied change is an unvalidated empty-input default in _split_gcd/split_surds that does not preserve the caller contract.
scale.3: A relevant localized source change is applied, but its fallback is overly broad, incompletely connected to the existing no-match path, or lacks convincing task-specific validation.
scale.4: An applied change at the sqrtdenest matching boundary converts the unsupported split into the existing no-match/unchanged-expression path while leaving generic helper contracts intact; visible validation is limited but relevant.
scale.5: The localized no-match fix is visibly applied, the failing structural case is exercised without exception, unchanged fallback semantics are checked, and representative previously denestable inputs or existing tests are shown to remain correct.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves helper contracts while handling non-denestable inputs locally

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates the reported sqrtdenest IndexError or the split_surds/_split_gcd call chain.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly identifies that _sqrt_match can send an additive expression whose terms have rational squares but no qualifying Pow terms to split_surds, producing an empty surds sequence that makes _split_gcd access a[0].

metadata.contradiction_rule: If visible evidence shows the trajectory continues to assert that the reported public expression directly reproduces the fault after it has visibly simplified to I without entering the failing path, cap at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: A reproduced traceback or instrumented call path using repository code outranks narrative inference; inspected source outranks assumptions based only on the issue text.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for locating the final stack frame without understanding why the sequence is empty or how sqrtdenest reaches it.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require explicit recognition that the IndexError is caused by an empty argument sequence, not merely a statement that _split_gcd raises IndexError.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection, traces, or controlled probes connecting _sqrt_match, split_surds, the empty surds sequence, and _split_gcd's a[0] access.
metadata.oracle_test: The causal semantic reference is: _sqrt_match evaluates the rational-square condition, split_surds finds no x[1].is_Pow terms, _split_gcd receives no arguments, and a[0] raises IndexError.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by the inspected code.
scale.2: Locates sqrtdenest, split_surds, or _split_gcd but does not establish the empty-input cause.
scale.3: Identifies that _split_gcd receives no arguments and a[0] fails, but does not connect this to the _sqrt_match classification path.
scale.4: Explains the complete call chain and the empty-surds condition with source-based evidence, but lacks a decisive reproduction of that path.
scale.5: Establishes the complete causal chain with source inspection plus a controlled reproduction or instrumentation of the empty-surds path, while distinguishing it from eager simplification of the public example.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-causal diagnosis of the empty-surds failure

applies_when: The visible trajectory reaches or changes the sqrtdenest matching path associated with an empty surd-candidate sequence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards a source-proven, task-local conversion of an unsupported empty-surds match into the established falsy result consumed by the denester's unchanged-input fallback, while distinguishing coherent but misplaced helper defaults from incompatible or mixed implementations.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if local handling coexists with a shared-helper workaround that prevents the intended exception or condition from reaching the local no-match path, or if any final return has incompatible types, inconsistent shape, malformed control flow, or a fabricated truthy match. Score 2 when the only final change is a coherent, correctly shaped generic empty-input default in a shared helper. Cap at 3 when local handling catches arbitrary exceptions, covers substantially more than the split operation, or leaves the route to the falsy result source-ambiguous.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final visible source or a final unified diff outranks narrated intent, intermediate edits, and claimed tests. Direct execution is supporting evidence only when the shown construction reaches the empty-surds branch in the modified source. A public expression already reduced to a simpler object before entering the denester does not establish this routing.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents disappearance of the original exception from being mistaken for correct fallback semantics, especially when an incompatible sentinel or generic helper default changes shared behavior, bypasses the local guard, or creates a truthy synthetic match.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require visibly applied task-local code whose final control flow unambiguously produces the established falsy no-match value without any retained behavioral change to shared surd or GCD helpers. Score 5 additionally requires visible execution connecting that branch to unchanged return by the enclosing denester and evidence that an ordinary denestable case still works.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final visible source around the split operation in the square-root matcher, the exact exception or precondition scope, the value and control-flow path used for no match, the enclosing falsy-match fallback, and any remaining behavioral edits to shared surd or GCD helpers. Determine whether a shared edit prevents the local exceptional path from running or fabricates a truthy match.
metadata.oracle_test: For an additive match candidate whose terms satisfy the matcher's rational-square classification but produce no qualifying radical powers, the matching operation must yield its normal falsy no-match value. The existing caller must then return that candidate unchanged, while successful radical matches retain their prior tuple-derived result.

scale.1: The final implementation is malformed or type-incompatible, fabricates an active match, visibly produces a wrong result or exception, or combines local handling with a shared-helper edit that defeats or contradicts the local no-match route.
scale.2: No task-local implementation is visibly applied, or the final implementation consists only of a coherent and correctly shaped generic empty-input convention in a shared surd or GCD helper.
scale.3: Task-local handling is visibly applied, but its exception scope is broad, its path to the established falsy result is ambiguous, or source evidence does not establish that later matching logic cannot reinterpret the unsupported case.
scale.4: Final source narrowly handles the empty-surds failure at the matching boundary, unambiguously reaches the established falsy no-match path, preserves successful-match control flow, and leaves shared helper behavior unchanged; decisive end-to-end structural validation is absent.
scale.5: The clean task-local route is visibly applied, a controlled structure reaches the empty-surds branch and is returned unchanged by the enclosing denester, and representative ordinary denesting or relevant existing tests visibly retain prior behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Sound local no-match routing for empty surd candidates

applies_when: The visible trajectory applies or attempts a behavioral change to split_surds or _split_gcd for an empty surd sequence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the visible semantic and control-flow risk introduced by retained changes to shared radical helpers, including unnecessary generic defaults, redundant dual handling, incompatible return shapes, and demonstrated downstream failures.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if every behavioral shared-helper edit is visibly absent or reverted in the final source. A correctly shaped generic identity default by itself is score 3, not 4 or 5. If such a default remains even though a task-local no-match guard also handles the same condition, score 4 because the generic contract expansion is visibly unnecessary and overlapping. Demonstrated exceptions or wrong results override claims that a sentinel is harmless.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final visible source or a final unified diff outranks earlier edits and narrative claims. Direct execution against that source outranks claimed test success. Reverted helper edits are non-evidence; merely discussing or testing an empty-input convention does not establish a retained contract change.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents ties between a single coherent but overbroad workaround and a patch that both handles the condition locally and still redefines shared helpers, while preserving the stronger distinction for incompatible scalar sentinels and observed regressions.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require a behavioral shared-helper change in the final visible source. Score 4 requires redundant dual handling, a return value incompatible with downstream list or arithmetic operations, inconsistent tuple shape, or another concrete source-level contract conflict. Score 5 requires a visible failure caused by that retained change or malformed final control flow.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final visible source of split_surds and _split_gcd, the exact empty-input tuple and element types, all retained task-local guards, downstream len, membership, multiplication, and division uses, and executions that directly expose consequences of the helper change.
metadata.oracle_test: An empty surd-candidate sequence in this call chain means sqrtdenest found no usable match; it does not require split_surds or _split_gcd to acquire a generic empty-input arithmetic contract.

scale.1: No behavioral shared-helper change is present in the final visible source; any attempted change was reverted.
scale.2: A shared-helper change is only proposed, tested, or attempted without remaining applied, or the final change is documentation-only.
scale.3: The final source adds only a coherent, correctly shaped generic empty-input convention, such as an identity with two empty lists, with no retained task-local duplicate and no visible downstream conflict.
scale.4: The final source retains both a task-local handler and an unnecessary shared-helper convention for the same condition, or returns an incompatible type or tuple shape, requires downstream accommodation, or creates another concrete contract or control-flow conflict without a demonstrated runtime failure.
scale.5: The retained shared-helper change visibly causes an exception, wrong result, unrelated regression, or leaves syntactically or structurally broken control flow.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Collateral severity of retained shared radical-helper changes

applies_when: A task-relevant Add expression, block product, block collapse, or equivalent semantic check is executed
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score only behavior visibly produced by the current checkout: preservation of matrix type and dimensions through core Add and repeated block multiplication.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Any current repeated multiplication that raises or produces scalar zero blocks caps the score at 2. If only an unrelated installed version passes, current-checkout credit is capped at 1. An unexecuted edit cannot raise the score. Printed `0` without type or shape evidence cannot satisfy a higher anchor.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executions after the latest source edit outrank earlier runs. Explicit checkout import paths outrank installed-package results. Type-and-shape output outranks textual display or assistant claims. A later failing execution supersedes an earlier success for the same invariant unless another edit and successful rerun follow.
metadata.failure_mode: A first product that merely prints correctly, operator addition instead of core Add, or a passing external version is mistaken for repaired checkout behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require repeated multiplication to complete in the current checkout with matrix-valued zero blocks. Scores above 3 additionally require direct core Add of compatible ZeroMatrix operands to be visibly matrix-valued and shaped.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect actual result types, matrix predicates, rows, columns, shapes, exceptions, and equality for direct core Add, first block multiplication, triple collapse, and chained _blockmul.
metadata.oracle_test: For compatible ZeroMatrix operands, inspect Add(z,z), block_collapse(b*b), block_collapse(b*b*b), and b._blockmul(b)._blockmul(b), including the type and shape of every zero result block; use partition-derived rectangular or symbolic dimensions for the highest anchor.

scale.1: Current-checkout executions fail before establishing a valid first product, expose scalar zero blocks, or only a different installed version is shown succeeding.
scale.2: A first product or isolated operation succeeds, but repeated block multiplication is failing, unrun, or lacks matrix-type evidence for its zero blocks.
scale.3: Triple collapse and chained _blockmul visibly succeed in the current checkout, and their zero blocks are shown matrix-valued with concrete shapes, but direct core Add is absent or still scalar.
scale.4: Repeated block operations and direct core Add visibly succeed in the current checkout with type, shape, and expected-result evidence, but generic dimension behavior is not demonstrated.
scale.5: All level-4 behavior succeeds together with inspection of every zero output block and a compatible rectangular, nonuniform, or symbolic-dimension case.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable zero-matrix preservation behavior

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or explains where matrix-valued zero products become scalar zero.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the assistant visibly identifies the first type-losing operation as additive construction over matrix-valued terms and, at higher levels, traces it to scalar identity injection in the MatrixExpr Add postprocessor.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If visible direct checks show individual products remain ZeroMatrix but the assistant continues to claim multiplication itself creates scalar Zero, cap at 2. If no assistant-authored causal conclusion is present, names appearing only in tool output cannot raise the score above 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed type-and-shape comparisons of individual product terms and their exact accumulated Add outrank speculation about BlockMatrix validation or dense storage; inspected local postprocessor source outranks an external patch description.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied and retained production correction

applies_when: A production change affecting Subs LaTeX parenthesization is active or has been attempted in the cutoff workspace.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the active production implementation unconditionally places exact scalable parentheses around the rendered body of every `Subs` inside the evaluation bar, including additive and multiplicative bodies.

metadata.contradiction_rule: No active production edit, a reverted edit, or malformed active Python forces score 1. An active generic `_needs_mul_brackets` change that wraps the complete Subs notation, or an ineffective call that receives already-rendered text, caps the score at 2. Conditional wrapping, plain parentheses, spaces inside `\left(` or `\right)`, or visible omission for `x*y` caps the score at 3. A latest applicable output from the active source overrides contrary assumptions about what the code should emit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active production source at cutoff is primary. A later restoration or checkout overrides an earlier edit. A latest command executed from that active source may contradict an optimistic source interpretation. Viewed source, proposed patches, helper scripts, untracked backups, failed edit commands, and reverted implementations are non-evidence for an active fix.
metadata.failure_mode: Absent or reverted production change, wrong parenthesization boundary, ineffective rendered-text helper use, conditional body selection, non-scalable delimiters, or exact-spacing defects.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires an active production edit. A score above 2 requires the edit to affect the Subs body inside the evaluation bar. A score above 3 requires source logic that applies to every Subs body without a precedence, Add, sign, first-character, coefficient, or surrounding-Mul condition. A score of 5 requires the visible active source to conclusively encode the exact inner `\left(%s\right)` form.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff source or diff that determines Subs rendering. Determine whether the body itself is always emitted as `\left(%s\right)` inside `\left. ... \right|`, without spaces inside the delimiters. Check the implementation against the exact body classes `-x+y` and `x*y`; output for `x*y+z`, another Add, or the motivating case alone does not establish multiplicative-body behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: The active semantics must yield body fragments `\left(- x + y\right)` and `\left(x y\right)` inside the evaluation bar for `3*Subs(-x+y, (x,), (1,))` and `Subs(x*y, (x, y), (1, 2))` respectively.

scale.1: No active production edit exists at cutoff, or the attempted edit is reverted, malformed, test-only, or otherwise absent from production behavior.
scale.2: An active edit exists but targets the complete Subs notation or generic Mul bracketing, passes rendered text to an ineffective helper, or visibly leaves the motivating body unparenthesized.
scale.3: The active edit parenthesizes the body for some cases, but uses plain or incorrectly spaced delimiters, or conditions wrapping on precedence, expression type, sign, coefficient, text prefix, or surrounding context so `x*y` is not guaranteed.
scale.4: The active source visibly places scalable parentheses around every Subs body at the correct inner boundary, but one exact delimiter, spacing, or all-body detail is not conclusively visible and no applicable output resolves it.
scale.5: The active source conclusively and unconditionally emits the exact `\left(%s\right)` body form inside the evaluation bar for both additive and multiplicative bodies, with no visible current-state contradiction.

metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source or unified diff overrides earlier edit commands, intended snippets, summaries, and verbal claims.

metadata.evidence_authority: Observed source definitions and runtime output take precedence over narrative descriptions; the printer dispatch convention `_print_<type name>` takes precedence over guessed method names.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of srepr container dispatch failure

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or explains why built-in Python dict or set objects are not recursively rendered by srepr.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Accurately identifies the missing lowercase ReprPrinter dispatch paths and maintains that causal model consistently through subsequent task-directed inspection, edits, interpretation of output, and any rollback.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Using or endorsing uppercase-only handlers for built-in containers, accepting raw `x`/`y` output as recursively printed, constructing dictionary output from printed item tuples or quoted rendered pairs, recursing on the whole set, or leaving a visibly malformed causal edit caps the score at 2 unless the mistake is explicitly recognized and then visibly corrected or cleanly rolled back.
metadata.evidence_authority: Runtime output and inspected source or diff outrank narrative claims. Later visible evidence outranks an earlier diagnosis. A visibly applied or rolled-back source state outranks a proposed edit, while successful same-state execution of both requested examples is the strongest confirmation.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full diagnostic credit for an early correct observation even though later edits or success claims reveal that the operative causal model is wrong, or denying diagnostic coherence to a deliberate rollback that removes a recognized bad edit.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a precise lowercase dispatch-and-fallback diagnosis supported by visible source or runtime evidence, with no unresolved later task-directed action that contradicts it. Score 5 additionally requires same-state successful execution of both requested nonempty examples.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the stated cause together with later task-directed behavior: recognition of lowercase `_print_dict` and `_print_set`, fallback to ordinary container rendering, recursive treatment of set elements and separate dictionary keys and values, and whether subsequent edits or output interpretations remain consistent with those facts.

Latest visible file contents or diff determine whether a correction was actually applied; proposed edits and intermediate commands are not implementations.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating ambiguous text as a malformed parse, counting simplification as proof of faithful rendering, crediting raw source listings as authored diagnosis, or accepting parser evaluation changes that erase the structure to be printed.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires an explicit assistant-authored conclusion, supported by visible structural evidence or a parser-independent reproduction, that the reciprocal-of-reciprocal tree is preserved and ordinary string rendering is defective. A score above 3 additionally requires tracing StrPrinter._print_Mul denominator extraction and the existing guarded parenthesization path. A score of 5 requires a visible effective localized source edit.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executed srepr, args, direct unevaluated Mul/Pow probes, exact displayed strings, assistant-authored causal conclusions, and any visible source inspection or edit. Distinguish evidence that the tree is mathematically intended from a mere simplification result, and distinguish inspecting _print_Mul from only naming StrPrinter.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended tree contains an outer inverse whose base is the complete inner reciprocal; for example, Mul(x, Pow(1/y, -1, evaluate=False), evaluate=False) must retain that structure and should be rendered by StrPrinter as x/(1/y). The relevant source mechanism is _print_Mul extracting the negative-Pow base into its denominator list while the existing guarded pow_paren handling covers suitable Mul bases but misses Pow bases.
metadata.stage: Reproduce, classify, and localize the defect

scale.1: No executed structural or semantic evidence advances classification; investigation remains setup-oriented, grammar-oriented, or causally unsupported.
scale.2: Executed evidence provides a useful partial distinction—such as mathematical equivalence, nested-Pow clues, args inspection, or a representation concern—but the latest diagnosis remains unresolved, parser-directed, semantically contradictory, or unsupported as a printer conclusion.
scale.3: The assistant explicitly and consistently concludes, from visible structural evidence or the direct unevaluated reproduction, that the reciprocal tree is preserved and ordinary string rendering is the defect, but does not trace the exact _print_Mul grouping mechanism.
scale.4: In addition to the supported printer diagnosis, the trajectory traces negative-Pow denominator extraction in _print_Mul and explains that the reciprocal Pow base is missed by the existing guarded Mul-only parenthesization path; no effective correction is yet visible.
scale.5: The complete level-4 causal account is accompanied by a visible, syntactically valid, localized source correction that extends the relevant denominator-parenthesization behavior to the reciprocal Pow case without evaluating the structure away.

applies_when: The cutoff state exposes an active repository diff, changed-file summary, or tracked file contents.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Removal or reversion shown by later cutoff evidence cancels the corresponding penalty. Conversely, successful mathematical output does not excuse an active change that evaluates away the required reciprocal structure or corrupts generated artifacts.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible git diff and cutoff file contents override earlier edit commands, assistant claims, and intermediate source listings. An empty or clean cutoff diff establishes that earlier experiments are no longer active.
metadata.failure_mode: Inferring damage from discussion or intermediate commands rather than the active diff, or treating all scratch files and absent implementations as equivalent to semantic source corruption.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires an active tracked change with task-causal compatibility or evaluator risk. Missing implementation, unfinished status, and an unchanged repository are not damage.
metadata.judge_focus: Use only changes visibly active at cutoff. Distinguish tracked core-source or generated-file damage from harmless exploratory scripts, dependency installation outside the repository, proposed edits, failed commands that changed nothing, and edits later reverted.
metadata.oracle_test: The active workspace must not replace convert_frac's unevaluated Mul/Pow construction with ordinary division or simplification, alter serialized ANTLR payloads, leave malformed Python in core files, or track a failed download containing only an error body.

scale.1: No harmful active tracked change is visible; the workspace is clean or contains only the intended localized printer/test work.
scale.2: Only minor tracked exploratory clutter is active, such as valid task-related scripts, with no parser semantic rewrite, generated-file change, malformed artifact, or core compatibility risk.
scale.3: A broad or poorly justified active source change creates concrete compatibility risk, but no required structure is visibly erased and core source remains syntactically usable.

metadata.failure_mode: Inferring a malformed parse tree from the ambiguous displayed string or treating raw tool output as an authored printer diagnosis.
